a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, ouston. Go ahead with backup voice check. [No answer.]

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Go ahead with backup voice check. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Go ahead with backup voice check. Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Anders
a08_0012852.text: Roger, Mike. I gave you a count. I'll give you another one. Are you standing by?

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Roger. Standing by.

a08_0012852.speaker: Anders
a08_0012852.text: Roger. This is Apollo 8 through backup voice: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Roger, Bill. Reading you weak but clear.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Go ahead with Normal S-band voice check.

a08_0012852.speaker: Anders
a08_0012852.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0012852.speaker: Anders
a08_0012852.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8 on Normal S-band: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. How do you read? Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Reading you loud and clear Normal S-band. How me? [No answer.]

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Reading you loud and clear on Normal S-band. How me? Over. [No answer.]

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Anders
a08_0012852.text: Roger, Houston. This is Apollo 8. Reading you loud and clear on Normal.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Roger. Reading you loud and clear on Normal S-band. How me?

a08_0012852.speaker: Anders
a08_0012852.text: Clear. [Pause.]

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Anders
a08_0012852.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. How do you read on VHF? Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Reading you loud and clear. We are also reading you loud and clear on S-band Normal. How me? Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Anders
a08_0012852.text: Roger. I'm reading you loud and clear. I'll give you another count on S-band Normal: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. How do you read me?

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Roger. That's loud and clear, Bill. California, would you enable the VHF downlink, please?

a08_0012852.speaker: Comm Tech
a08_0012852.text: California enabled. [Long pause.]

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Borman
a08_0012852.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Roger. We are going to rewind your tape recorder, and we have the TLI plus 90 and TLI plus 4-hour PADs at your convenience. Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Borman
a08_0012852.text: Roger. Ready to copy.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Roger. TLI plus 90, SPS/G&N, 63531; minus 1.64 plus 1.29. Are you with me so far? Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0012852.text: Roger. We're with you.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Okay. 004:17:42.65; minus 0440.2, minus 0000.1, plus 4838.7; 178, 169, 359; not applicable, plus 0018.5; 4858.7, 6:03, 4838.3; 06, 202.7, 25.0; Earth center, 0123 - correction - down 12.3; I say again, down 12.3, right 2.2; plus 11.23, minus 030.00; 1231.3, 34494, 017:47:39, north set stars; roll, 068; pitch, 097; yaw, 356; ullage none; other: high speed procedure not required. Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0012852.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. We missed a portion of that maneuver PAD. Can you start with H P and go down to boresight star? Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Roger. I say again. H P plus 0018.5. Are you with me?

a08_0012852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0012852.text: Roger. We're with you.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: 4858.7, 6:03, 4838,3; 06, 202.7, 25.0; and the boresight star is Earth's center. Over.

a08_0012852.speaker: Collins
a08_0012852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Did you copy?

a08_0012852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0012852.text: Roger, Houston. This is a TLI plus 90 as follows: minus - the weight will be plus 63531; minus 1.64, plus 1.29; 004:17:42.65; minus 0440.2, minus 000.1, plus 4838.7; 178, 169, 359; plus 0018.5; 4858.7, 6:03, 4838.3. We'll have to get the sextant information later; 123 minus 030.

a08_0012900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0012900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston here; 1 hour, 29 minutes into the flight. And the first call from Mike Collins to Apollo 8, has gone out as yet without response.

a08_0012900-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0012900-pao.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. (No answer.)

a08_0012900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0012900-pao.text: This will be - this pass across the States this time - should last 15 or 20 minutes - will be a major checkpoint on all the systems, particularly that guidance and navigation system. Jim Lovell will be a very busy boy and so will Frank Borman and - ensuring that all the checks are accurate. In the course of it, Bill Anders is to perform a backup communications check, switching to alternate channels should anything develop or go wrong in the primary communications mode. And as the spacecraft moves across the Atlantic, the crew then will proceed into their Translunar Injection checklist in prepa

a08_0012900-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0012900-pao.text: Apollo 8, Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0012900-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0012900-pao.text: Roger. How do you read? [No answer.]

a08_0013600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0013600-pao.text: The information that Mike Collins is passing to Jim Lovell is procedural numbers and angles should abort become necessary at two discrete periods after the Translunar Injection burn. Ninety minutes after and then 4 hours after. And we should hear quite a few numbers.

a08_0014700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0014700-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control, Houston here. While we are still in communication by the Vanguard, I wanted to pass on to you some real-time telemetry we're getting on a few cabin functions. The cabin pressure has been holding at a rock steady 5.2 pounds per square inch since launch. We've switched now to the biomed, switched the biomed harness over to Jim Lovell, on the center couch. And his heart has been running around 69 to 70 beats per minute. He's breathing at a very steady 25 - 20 to 25 respirations per minute. He's been doing a lot of talking, a lot of writing down there, trying to copy al

a08_0014700-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0014700-pao.text: Very good. That's all correct, and I have a TLI PAD for you whenever you're ready to copy it.

a08_0014700-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0014700-pao.text: Okay. Your computer PAD is in and verified. You can go to Block, and we're going to have LOS here in about 45 seconds. I'll start on the TLI PAD anyway. Time base 6 p[redict], 2:41:36; roll, 179; pitch, 045; yaw, 001; burn time, 5 plus 15; Delta V C prime, 10519.6; V I 35569; roll, 357; pitch, 091; yaw, 001. Comments: TLI plus 10 minutes; abort attitude is 199 degrees, and I don't believe you've got time to read that back. We'll see you over Canaries at 1:50 GET. Adios.

a08_0014700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0014700-pao.text: You heard Mike Collins. After a conversation that started at 1 hour and 25 minutes into the mission, is now 1 hour and fort - nearly 1 hour and 50 minutes, to give you some understanding of the extraordinarily long periods that we can hold the spacecraft during these Stateside passes, and Mike bobbed that conversation off with an 'Adios' and said we'd pick them up in 1 minute over the Canaries. So essentially we've got, well let's say, on the order of 40 - 35 to 40 minutes of continuous communication starting with Guaymus and running through the Canary station. Let's just leave the circuit up.

a08_0015000-pao.speaker: Lovell
a08_0015000-pao.text: Roger. Houston, Apollo 8. Reading you loud and clear. TLI planned 2:41:36; 179, 045, 001; 5:15 10519.6, 35569; 357, 091, 001; TLI plus 10, abort attitude 199 on the pitch.

a08_0015200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0015200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. The Flight Director has just advised the room that the booster, the S-IVB, all consumable sources, every bit of data we have looked at and examined indicate we should proceed with the TLI burn. (We) go back to the crew.

a08_0015600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0015600-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. That will apparently wrap it up via Canary Islands. Tananarive, we are due to acquire at 2 hours and 9 minutes into the flight, about 15 minutes from now. You heard on the tag end of that conversation a fairly relaxed Borman commenting on the fact that it looked very much like it did three years ago when he and Jim Lovell were flying Gemini VII , and he also reported that inadvertently a Mae West had been inflated. We're not just sure whose Mae West it was, but the supposition here is that one tank or one side of the life jacket on the Command Pilot might have

a08_0021407.speaker: Collins
a08_0021407.text: Roger. Gemini 8, Houston. We'd like to bring you up to date on the comm situation while we've got some quiet time here. We'll be LOS Tananarive in another 2 minutes; we'll be picking you up over Carnarvon at 2 hours, 25 minutes and 22 seconds. LOS Carnarvon will be 02:31:55; then we've got ARIA number 1 coming in at about 02:37:30; and after that, we have a hand-off to Mercury to Hawaii to Goldstone, and we should have continuous comm. Over.

a08_0021407.speaker: Borman
a08_0021407.text: Very good. That's very good. Thank you.

a08_0021500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0021500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 2 hours, 15 minutes into the flight. We have had a chat with the crew over Tananarive and among other things, Frank Borman reported that this - that he was Gemini VIII , which was a cause for a few smiles. Some wag finally added, 'remember now, you're Gemini 7, not Gemini 8.' And here's how the conversation went.

a08_0021500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0021500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 2 hours, 26 minutes into the flight. We have just acquired via Carnarvon, and here is how that conversation is going.

a08_0022600-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0022600-pao.text: Roger. Loud and clear. We'd like to take your tape recorder for a minute, please.

a08_0022800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0022800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston, running through an unusually quiet pass across Carnarvon with very little more than establishing call signs. Our orbital digitals, which we're reading out from Australian sites, show that the present velocity is 25,569 feet per second [7,793 m/s], showing an apogee of 105.5 nautical miles [195.4 km]; and our Translunar Injection burn will have the effect - Here's some comm going up, let's catch up with it.

a08_0023126.speaker: Collins
a08_0023126.text: Roger. We'll have LOS in about 30 seconds, and we'll pick you up over ARIA 1 at 02:37 and a half.

a08_0023200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0023200-pao.text: Apollo Control back here. The TLI burn will add 10,500 feet per second - perhaps a foot or two more per second than that, but that's pretty close - 10,500 feet per second to the present 25,570. And the duration of the burn'll be slightly more than 5 minutes. It is to occur at 2 hours and 50 minutes into the flight. Now, a combination of stations will be seeing it. The ship Mercury will see it. It's parked about 8, 9 - about a thousand miles southwest of Hawaii. Hawaii also should see it. And in a very few minutes, as the spacecraft starts away from the Earth, the big dish in Goldstone, Califor

a08_0024200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0024200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 2 hours, 42 minutes into the flight. We attempted to establish some communication a minute or two ago through one of our instrumentation aircraft. We heard them, they heard us, but it was just barely. And we are now awaiting contact, which we should have in about 2 minutes, [for communications] through the good ship Mercury. It is entirely appropriate that the ship Mercury should be the relay point for this historic burn, which is planned for in about 6 - 6 minutes from now. Flight Director has just advised that we should standby to receive Mercury data and tha

a08_0024200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0024200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 2 hours, 45 minutes into the flight. And we now are getting data from the ship Mercury and everything looks good. The Booster has advised that the tanks have repressurized properly and here goes the first call up to Apollo 8.

a08_0024500-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0024500-pao.text: Good; you're loud and clear through the Mercury, and you're looking good down here. Everything looks good.

a08_0024512.speaker: Collins
a08_0024512.text: Good; you're loud and clear through the Mercury, and you're looking good down here. Everything looks good.

a08_0024512.speaker: Borman
a08_0024512.text: Roger. Understand. Our O 2 flow is a little bit higher than I thought, but Bill says that it's just about what he expected.

a08_0024512.speaker: Collins
a08_0024512.text: Your O 2 flow looks good down here.

a08_0024800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0024800-pao.text: Here in the Control Center, two big charts dominate the front of the room, and two of the walls. One of them will present the data as it climbs. It's a plot of velocity versus altitude, so we will be able to track that for you. The other plots show the angle of the burn - is following. And still another shows the ever-so-slight out of plane maneuver. Stand by one.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Okay. Start your watch [garble] see what time it says.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Okay, 42 is S-II Sep light, Off.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Okay, you're in EMS Mode, Auto?

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0024917-onboard.text: We're past 42. That was when our light...

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Go ahead. Boy, it's going off in yaw.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Okay, the DAP [Digital AutoPilot] is fine over here.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Okay, align yourself in attitude, we got plus or minus 5 degrees.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Things are looking good over here.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Okay, cut-off at 02:55:51. Okay, we're coming up on 28,000 (fps).

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Shouldn't have that goddamn high flow rate up there.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Coming up on 29,000 [fps, 8,840 m/s]. Okay, our yaw should be coming off now a little bit.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0024917-onboard.text: You should have about 8 degrees of yaw yet, compared to what - 35? A weak 35, now 37. Alright, it was what - 9 degrees?

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Hey, that O 2 is pegged high, Bill.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Yes, I know. It's just a little warmer up here. I'd - I'm looking at the Delta-P here. The surge tank in the tank 1 [garble] nothing else to worry about.

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0024917-onboard.text: What time [garble, probably asking for the cut-off time]?

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0024917-onboard.text: 30 seconds to go. 34,000 [fps, 10,360 m/s]. You got the card?

a08_0024917-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0024917-onboard.text: Did you see the card, Bill?

a08_0024940-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0024940-pao.text: Immediately following the burn, we should get a detailed report on it from Frank Borman. And meanwhile, Bill Anders, and during the course of the burn, will operate the onboard flight recorder and on which any various comments from the various crewmembers will be recorded. And we will undoubtedly hear some comments from them during the course of the burn. Immediately following the burn, Jim Lovell is to start stowing the many items of camera gear, lenses, mirrors, cables, all manner of camera equipment, including a spotmeter. And the - Apollo 8's been advised once again that they look good for

a08_0024940-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0024940-pao.text: Apollo 8, coming up on 20 seconds to ignition. Mark it, and you're looking very good.

a08_0024940-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0024940-pao.text: And Mike Collins gives them a mark 20 seconds to ignition.

a08_0024940-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0024940-pao.text: Now he [probably Flight Director] is counting, 4 - 2, we see ignition.

a08_0024940-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0024940-pao.text: Lovell confirms ignition and the thrust is okay, Booster says.

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0025000-pao.text: Apollo 8, coming up on 20 seconds to ignition. Mark it, and you're looking very good.

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025000-pao.text: And Mike Collins gives them a mark 20 seconds to ignition.

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025000-pao.text: Now he [probably Flight Director] is counting, 4 - 2, we see ignition.

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025000-pao.text: Lovell confirms ignition and the thrust is okay, Booster says.

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025000-pao.text: Flight Dynamics says we look good, Flight - watching this thrust build. Trajectory, Guidance, Flight Dynamics, everybody in the front, what's called the front trench of this Control Center, says they're happy. That includes the Booster.

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0025000-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You're looking good. [Long pause.]

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025000-pao.text: Two hours, 51 minutes and 30 seconds, that would put us about a minute into the burn. Apogee now 800 [nautical] miles [1,500 km] and climbing.

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0025000-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Trajectory and guidance look good. Over.

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0025000-pao.text: Roger. Apollo 8, looks good here. [Long pause.]

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025000-pao.text: Hawaii confirms that they've got a very solid lock and Borman almost nonchalantly says 'Roger, we look good here,' at 2 hours, 52 minutes.

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0025000-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're predicting cut-off, 02:55:58, and it looks exactly nominal here.

a08_0025000-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0025000-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. That predicted cut-off, 02:55:52, 52, and that's exactly as it should be.

a08_0025454.speaker: Collins
a08_0025454.text: Apollo 8. Houston. You're looking good, right down the old center line.

a08_0025454.speaker: Borman
a08_0025454.text: Okay. We got SECO right on the money.

a08_0025500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025500-pao.text: Flight Dynamics says we're exactly nominal. And cut-off is now predicted; 2 hours, 55 minutes and 58 seconds; 2 hours, 55 minutes and 58 seconds. The crew's been advised that they look - all values look exactly nominal or just exactly what we'd hoped they'd be. Their present altitude is now about 3,000 miles and we're Go and these three crewmembers are traveling faster than man has ever flown before. There is very little conversation with the crew, but let's cut now to the crew and see what we can pick up.

a08_0025500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025500-pao.text: Their velocity now is about 32,000 feet per second, 32,000 feet per second. Velocity is now 33,000 feet per second. And from Hawaii, we are getting a visual report that people in Hawaii are observing the burn from on the ground.

a08_0025500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025500-pao.text: We're about 40 seconds away from cut-off here. The spacecraft moving at nearly 35,000 feet per second. Cut-off in 30 seconds.

a08_0025500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025500-pao.text: Present altitude [means apogee], 35,000 [nautical] miles [55,500 km]. 60,000 [nautical] miles [111,000 km] we're approaching. We have passed the 60,000 miles and we are very nearly...

a08_0025520-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025520-pao.text: Present altitude [means apogee], 35,000 [nautical] miles [55,500 km]. 60,000 [nautical] miles [111,000 km] we're approaching. We have passed the 60,000 miles and we are very nearly...

a08_0025520-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0025520-pao.text: Okay. We got SECO right on the money.

a08_0025520-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025520-pao.text: ... And Borman says we got SECO. Cut-off was right on the second.

a08_0025622-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0025622-onboard.text: S-IVB will maneuver to orb-rate, heads down at 0.3 of a degree per second.

a08_0025622-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0025622-onboard.text: I'll give it to you. V I was 34 - 35452.

a08_0025622-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0025622-onboard.text: Let's not go out of there. You leave it like it is.

a08_0025622-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0025622-onboard.text: I've got to go to my Key Release [garble].

a08_0025622-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0025622-onboard.text: The Flight Recorder is Off; Tape Recorder is stopped...

a08_0025700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0025700-pao.text: At 2 hours and 57 minutes here, just - all the sources again are being looked at, compared. They all are exactly what we'd hoped to see and more than once we've heard Chris Kraft, the Director of Flight Operations say, 'You're on your way. You're really on your way now.' We don't have an exact cut-off - cut-off figure yet in feet per second, but we should be getting it very soon from the Flight Dynamics Officer.

a08_0025700-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0025700-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Looks like a good cut-off. Everything's looking real good down here. [Pause.]

a08_0025727.speaker: Collins
a08_0025727.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Looks like a good cut-off. Everything's looking real good down here. [Pause.]

a08_0025727.speaker: Collins
a08_0025727.text: Your cut-off looked very good down here. We got a whole room full of people that say you look good.

a08_0025727.speaker: Borman
a08_0025727.text: Roger. Thank you. The only situation we have here is the O 2 flow is pegged high, O 2 flow pegged high.

a08_0025727.speaker: Lovell
a08_0025727.text: We'll get you the burn status report here shortly.

a08_0025727.speaker: Collins
a08_0025727.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Your booster is configured normally, and we're not concerned with the O 2 high flow. We think its normal.

a08_0025727.speaker: Lovell
a08_0025727.text: Roger. The Delta-T IG looked like it was right on. Burn time appeared to us to be about 2 seconds longer, 517. V GX was reading 95485 when we got it. The attitude was nominal. V I was reading 35452 at cut-off, H-dot 04552, and H is 01791. Delta-V C on the EMS was minus 20.6.

a08_0025727.speaker: Collins
a08_0025727.text: Alright, we copy that, Jim, and I've got some times here for you.

a08_0025727.speaker: Collins
a08_0025727.text: Booster begins maneuver to Sep[aration] attitude at 03:10:55. Takes 5 minutes, so it arrives at 03:15:55, and Sep time, 03:20:55. Your Sep attitude, the gimbal angles on the PAD remain good.

a08_0025727.speaker: Lovell
a08_0025727.text: Roger. I have those times. The Sep time will be 03:20:55.

a08_0030000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0030000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. We - we're getting a post-TLI report from the crew. I apologize. I quoted some erroneous figures during the course of the burn. Our present altitude is about 240 [nautical] miles [444 kilometres] and very shortly we'll get a more precise fix on that. I believe in the course of the burn I quoted some features in thousands of miles which should have been in thousands of feet [in fact he was reporting the current apogee]. I apologize. Our new displays are getting a good workout and some of the people reading those new displays are getting a very good workout.

a08_0030000-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0030000-pao.text: Alright, we copy that, Jim, and I've got some times here for you.

a08_0030000-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0030000-pao.text: Booster begins maneuver to Sep[aration] attitude at 03:10:55. Takes 5 minutes, so it arrives at 03:15:55, and Sep time, 03:20:55. Your Sep attitude, the gimbal angles on the PAD remain good.

a08_0030200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0030200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control here. We're watching the altitude plot now. Now it's a good solid trace coming to us through Goldstone. We're up to 879 [nautical] miles. Our present Ground Elapsed Time into the flight is 3 hours, 3 minutes. At the same time we're already beginning to see the velocity begin to recede slightly. It's now 32,418 feet per second, and we'll continue to see that slight lowering in the velocity reading and a constant elevation of the apogee [means altitude]. Now 934, 961, and every 10 seconds it seems to be adding about 30 to 40 miles. That spacecraft right now, in relation to

a08_0030200-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0030200-pao.text: Roger. Going to start charging battery B.

a08_0030200-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0030200-pao.text: And would you keep a special eye on the surge tank and cryo O 2 tank 1 Delta-P for us since our flowmeter is pegged out, we got no warning on O 2 high flow.

a08_0030200-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0030200-pao.text: Roger, Bill. We'll do that for you.

a08_0030308.speaker: Anders
a08_0030308.text: Roger. Going to start charging battery B.

a08_0030308.speaker: Anders
a08_0030308.text: And would you keep a special eye on the surge tank and cryo O 2 tank 1 Delta-P for us since our flowmeter is pegged out, we got no warning on O 2 high flow.

a08_0030308.speaker: Collins
a08_0030308.text: Roger, Bill. We'll do that for you.

a08_0031108.speaker: Borman
a08_0031108.text: Okay. Maneuver's started to separation attitude.

a08_0031108.speaker: Borman
a08_0031108.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0031108.speaker: Collins
a08_0031108.text: Yeah, reading you loud and clear, Frank. Understand you've started the maneuver to Sep attitude.

a08_0031108.speaker: Collins
a08_0031108.text: Are you reading us all right?

a08_0031200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0031200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We estimate another 7 or 8 minutes before the spacecraft will separate from the S-IVB. We have not heard from the crew in the last few minutes, they're busy with doing their post TLI duties and we're looking at data here and everything we see is quite comforting. That's the next major event, separation from the booster. For now, we've - the pool has asked us to replay the communication during Translunar injection, which you heard live. Here it is.

a08_0031416.speaker: Collins
a08_0031416.text: Okay. Coming up on 3 hours and 15 minutes as per Flight Plan; we have you Go.

a08_0031416.speaker: Borman
a08_0031416.text: You got any reading on this O 2 flow?

a08_0031416.speaker: Collins
a08_0031416.text: We're reading about the same as we were before on that oxygen flow. The reason that it's that high is due to the cabin gas changeover. According to Apollo 7, if your data repeats theirs, you can expect it to be high for another few hours.

a08_0031416.speaker: Collins
a08_0031416.text: You can expect that the S-IVB will be 10 degrees off in pitch at Sep attitude; however, that is Go. There is no problem involved.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Okay, turn controller counterclockwise, plus X, and hold at zero.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Let me attempt to turn it Off. Give me a 10-second warning on the flight recorder.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Okay, I'm coming up on 15 seconds to Sep.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Okay, at zero, turn Hand Controller counterclockwise, plus-X, and hold.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: 3 seconds, Launch Vehicle Tank Pressure indicator, zero; CM/LV Sep; Translational Contr, Neutral; plus-X, Off; TVC Servo Power 1, Off.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Okay, desired gimbal angles and proceed.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Okay, you're notched up by 30 seconds so a minus-X of 2½.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Okay, you put your other - you're not around by 30 seconds, so minus-X is your roll.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Why can't you call it yaw?

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Because we're not - see, we're not...

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Man, where's the S-IVB? Anybody see it, now?

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Right in the middle. Right in the middle of my window. There's not a panel around.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Well, we've got some still pictures we can take...

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Could you pitch a little more?

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: We haven't got in here, yet.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Could you pitch just a little more or [garble].

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Pitch up, pitch up a little more.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0031957-onboard.text: I don't see the [garble]. Maybe I can get it in a minute.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Don't you think that's enough pictures of it?

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0031957-onboard.text: How far away do you think it is?

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Let me switch the antenna here.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0031957-onboard.text: I'm not going to fly around the damn thing. I don't think there's any - do you?

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: You read him loud and clear? I don't...

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Turn your VHF up and your [garble].

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Okay, let's make sure we've done everything here. Get that Flight Recorder, Off.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: Off. Okay, about 23:50, I want it Off.

a08_0031957-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0031957-onboard.text: At 35:50, I turn it back On. [Garble] 23:50 [garble].

a08_0032026.speaker: Collins
a08_0032026.text: Roger. We have you about 30 seconds prior to separation, and everything's looking good.

a08_0032026.speaker: Anders
a08_0032026.text: We've Sep'd Houston. We got the IVB, right in sight.

a08_0032026.speaker: Borman
a08_0032026.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8 on VHF and S-band. How do you read?

a08_0032026.speaker: Collins
a08_0032026.text: Hear loud and clear, Bill. How me?

a08_0032026.speaker: Borman
a08_0032026.text: Read you loud and clear. We've Sep'd and looking good.

a08_0032200-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0032200-pao.text: We've Sep'd Houston. We got the IVB, right in sight.

a08_0032200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0032200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 3 hours, 22 minutes into the flight. Exactly 1 minute ago we observed separation from the S-IVB. The crew immediately turned around and had a look at the S-IVB and we're watching that pitch - pitch attitude right now and telemetry coming through over the Eastern Test Range. And as the vehicle climbs, it will - from a flat map projection appear to swing to the south and west which, of course is a little unusual for our usu - for our past flight, the Earth orbital tracks which invariably take us to the east. But we will observe a swing down starting across the At

a08_0032500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0032500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control here. No additional communications from the crew, but while we've been sitting here in the last few minutes, the Mission Control Center has gone to what we call the translunar phase map. It's a new display. Those of you watching in the News Center will observe a long, elongated figure 8 map which shows the Earth-Moon transit and it also shows the numbers, the small flashing light now being portrayed to us in black and white. And we would estimate our distance at something on the order of 3,000 - 3,500 [nautical] miles [6,200 km] from Earth. It will carry us out in increm

a08_0032823.speaker: Borman
a08_0032823.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0032823.speaker: Collins
a08_0032823.text: Read you loud and clear, Frank. How us?

a08_0032823.speaker: Borman
a08_0032823.text: Roger. We're loud and clear. We're taking pictures of the S-IVB; the post-separation sequence is completed, and we seem to have a High Gain [Antenna].

a08_0033038.speaker: Collins
a08_0033038.text: Roger. Is Bill ready for his VHF test? We can configure any time he is.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Rog. We would like to ask whether you did a Verb 66 Enter to transfer the state vector from CSM to LM slot. We didn't copy that down here.

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: We did not.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Okay.

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: Do you want us to do that now?

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: At your convenience.

a08_0033521.speaker: Lovell
a08_0033521.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: We see the Earth now, almost as a disk.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Good show. Get a picture of it.

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: We are.

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: Tell Conrad he lost his record.

a08_0033521.speaker: Lovell
a08_0033521.text: We have a beautiful view of Florida now. We can see the Cape, just the point.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Roger.

a08_0033521.speaker: Lovell
a08_0033521.text: And at the same time, we can see Africa. West Africa is beautiful. I can also see Gibraltar at the same time I'm looking at Florida.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Sounds good. Get a picture of it. What window are you looking out?

a08_0033521.speaker: Lovell
a08_0033521.text: The center window.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Rog. [Pause.]

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Are your windows clear so far? [Long pause.]

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: How about this VHF check? We would like to get that done before you get too much further away.

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: Roger, we're listening on VHF Alpha Simplex.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Say again.

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: We're listening for VHF Alpha Simplex.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Okay, good. Thank you. VHF Alpha Simplex, and we will get configured for it; and in between times, give us a clue as to what it looks like from way up there.

a08_0033521.speaker: Lovell
a08_0033521.text: Roger. Well, Mike, I can see the entire Earth now out of the center window. I can see Florida, Cuba, Central America, the whole northern half of Central America, in fact, all the way down through Argentina and down through Chile.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: They picked a good day for it.

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: Stand by. We're going through the separation maneuver checklist here.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Roger. Standing by. [Long pause.]

a08_0033521.speaker: Borman
a08_0033521.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. We've lost sight of the S-IVB here. The separation maneuver may be delayed slightly, or else we'll go ahead and make it without having her in sight.

a08_0033521.speaker: Collins
a08_0033521.text: Roger. Understand, Frank.

a08_0033700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0033700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. The crew seems to be pretty well settled down in their translunar - after their Translunar Injection burn and they're - they're getting some time on the window. We just heard Jim Lovell report he could see Florida perfectly. By the way, they're out about 6,500 [nautical] miles [12,000 km] above the Earth now. He said he had a beautiful view of Florida and then he - his gaze roamed a little bit to the other side of the window and he said he could also see Gibraltar. The crew reminded the Control Center here that Pete Conrad and Dick Gordon would have to step asi

a08_0033700-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0033700-pao.text: How about this VHF check? We would like to get that done before you get too much further away.

a08_0033700-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0033700-pao.text: Roger, we're listening on VHF Alpha Simplex.

a08_0033700-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0033700-pao.text: We're listening for VHF Alpha Simplex.

a08_0033700-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0033700-pao.text: Okay, good. Thank you. VHF Alpha Simplex, and we will get configured for it; and in between times, give us a clue as to what it looks like from way up there.

a08_0034158.speaker: Borman
a08_0034158.text: When does the S-IVB do their blowdown maneuver?

a08_0034158.speaker: Collins
a08_0034158.text: Your blowdown will be 1 hour from now, a little over 1 hour from now.

a08_0034158.speaker: Borman
a08_0034158.text: Roger. We have the S-IVB in sight again now, and we've done the separation maneuver.

a08_0034158.speaker: Collins
a08_0034158.text: We'd like to take control of the DSE for a while, Bill.

a08_0034158.speaker: Collins
a08_0034158.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We'd like to get an approximate GET of your Sep maneuver to use for our ephemeris tracking data.

a08_0034158.speaker: Borman
a08_0034158.text: Roger. It was 3 hours, 40 minutes, zero seconds.

a08_0034158.speaker: Collins
a08_0034158.text: Good, 03:40 and a foot and a half - feet per second. Right?

a08_0034158.speaker: Borman
a08_0034158.text: We have the - Mike, we have the exact call-out here for you and a burn status report.

a08_0034158.speaker: Borman
a08_0034158.text: Alright, Delta-V X minus 00011, Delta-V Y plus 0002, Delta-V Z minus 0002; roll, 0; pitch, 180; yaw, 0. Over.

a08_0034625.speaker: Collins
a08_0034625.text: Roger. At your convenience, would you please go P00 and Accept? We're going to update to your W-matrix.

a08_0034625.speaker: Borman
a08_0034625.text: They all departed, and it worked fine.

a08_0034625.speaker: Borman
a08_0034625.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Will you give us the information when you want us to stop the venting and so on?

a08_0035039.speaker: Collins
a08_0035039.text: Rog. Which venting information are you inquiring about: the O 2 flow high out through the waste tank or waste compartment, or are you talking about your evaporator?

a08_0035039.speaker: Borman
a08_0035039.text: Evaporator. We're configuring now to stop boiling.

a08_0035039.speaker: Collins
a08_0035039.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You can go back to Block. We've gotten in the load to the W-matrix update.

a08_0035039.speaker: Borman
a08_0035039.text: Houston, Apollo 8. The back pressure valve is closed, and the water flow (to the evaporator) is Off.

a08_0035039.speaker: Collins
a08_0035039.text: Back pressure valve, Closed, and water flow, Off. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0035039.speaker: Borman
a08_0035039.text: Roger. It looks like I might have to do a couple more small maneuvers to stay away from the front of this S-IVB, the way we're ending up now. Do you want me to do these with a P47 if we have to do them?

a08_0035039.speaker: Collins
a08_0035039.text: That's affirmative, Frank, on the P47.

a08_0035039.speaker: Borman
a08_0035039.text: Okay. And give me the time again when it [the S-IVB] starts to dump [its LOX], please.

a08_0035039.speaker: Collins
a08_0035039.text: Roger. [Pause.] We're working on an exact GET [Ground Elapsed Time] of that, Frank.

a08_0035454.speaker: Collins
a08_0035454.text: I'd like to give you some idea about your trajectory. It looks like a midcourse correction number 1, projected out to TLI plus 6 hours, would be only 7 feet per second. So, of course, any further maneuvers you do would add to that, which is probably good.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: I just want to stay from away from in front of this thing.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Rog. We concur. Looks like it is chasing you, huh?

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Yeah. [Long pause.]

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Omni-D. [Pause.]

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Boy, it's starting to vent now, blowing down.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Say again.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: The S-IVB is really venting.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Rog. Understand; that is supposedly a nonpropulsive vent. The big blowdown maneuver, it starts maneuvering to blowdown attitude at 04:44:55, and the vent occurs at 05:07:55.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Roger.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: That is the nonpropulsive vent, but it's pretty spectacular. It's spewing out from all sides like a huge water sprinkler.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Rog. Get some pictures of it.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: We are. [Long pause.]

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Say again that big vent time, so I can write it down please, Houston.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Rog. Big vent time: 05:07:55, and it will be maneuvering to vent attitude beginning at 04:44:55. And Bill's got the tape recorder back.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Thank you. Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: We're receiving VHF music now, Houston. Thank you.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Yeah, you took the words right out of my mouth, Frank, and we would like to know also how far away from the S-IVB you are now.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: I guess we're between 500 to 1,000 feet.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Herb Alpert seems pretty good.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Rog.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. I believe we're going to have to vent or thrust away from this thing; we seem to be getting closer.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Rog. Understand, Frank; go ahead whenever - just give us some idea of when you did it and how much.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Could you stand by one? We're working on something here.

a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0035500-pao-press-conference.text: Okay.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [Pause.]

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: You're loud and clear, Mike. Go ahead.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Okay, Frank. On your additional separation maneuver, we recommend that you make a radial burn, point your plus-X axis toward the Earth and thrust minus-X for 3 feet per second. Over.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: I don't want to do that; I'll lose sight of the S-IVB.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Okay. The reason we want a radial burn is to increase your midcourse correction so we can use the SPS. Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Apollo 8. Houston.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Go ahead.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: How close to a radial burn can you get without losing sight of the S-IVB, Frank?

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Well, I don't know because I can't see the Earth now, Mike.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: We can pitch down some. Jim has the Earth in the optics so we could pitch some and get pretty close to one (a radial burn), I guess. [Long pause.]

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: We can give you a pitch gimbal angle on the radial direction if that would be a help. It's 181 degrees; pitch gimbal angle would be exactly radial at 4 hours and 10 minutes. I don't know whether that solves your visibility problem or not.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: That's affirmative.

a08_0040510.speaker: MCC
a08_0040510.text: Go ahead, SPAN.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Well, that zero would be just as good, wouldn't it?

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Frank, if you use zero, then make the Sep if possible with the plus-X thrusters. That's the direction of the burn we'd like.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Well, I can't do that. I'll thrust right square into that S-IVB.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Yeah, okay, understand,

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: What it is - what will he [the S-IVB] maneuver to, as far as the gimbal angle for this blowdown? [Long pause.]

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Apollo 8, Houston. At blowdown, that S-IVB should be oriented to perform a retrograde blowdown along the local horizontal.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Okay.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Is it still chasing? Does it look like it is closing on you, Frank?

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: It is about the same. The trouble is it is pointed at us pretty well.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Rog. Understand. [Long pause.]

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Frank, what we want to do is get a radial upward burn; and as long as you can, through the optics or some other means out the window, figure out where the Earth is, then use the appropriate thrusters to thrust upward, radially upward for 3 feet per second. That's what we are looking for, for trajectory reasons.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Okay. Understand. I just - as I say, I just can't very well do that now. I don't want to lose sight of this S-IVB.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Rog. We concur with that. I just thought perhaps Jim, through his optics, or you could get some feel for where the Earth is. That's what we want to do, is radially upward.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Okay. As soon as we find the Earth, we'll do it.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Houston. The venting on the S-IVB is terminated.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Roger. Thank you.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Rog. Frank, do you think you are going to be able to do this burn radially? We would like to add to its magnitude if you are going to make it in some other direction. Over.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Well, I'm - I'm not even sure we're going to do it yet, Mike. If I can get - we seem to be drifting away from this thing a little bit, although it is still pointing at us quite closer than I'd like.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Roger. Understand. [Pause.]

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We would like you to do some additional maneuver; it's just a question of how much and in which direction.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Okay. Well, right now, our gimbal angles are about - roll's about 190 and pitch is about 320 and yaw is about 340. We could certainly do it in this position. That would be alright.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Stand by. We'll check those.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Rog, Frank. You could help us out if you would explain where you are relative to the booster. In other words, with respect to the Earth and the radius vector, are you above or below or to one side, or where exactly is the booster relative to you?

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Well, the trouble is, as I said before, we can't definitely find the Earth. I think we are in front and a little bit above - a little bit above the - almost in front of the - directly in the front of the booster.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Roger. Understand; almost directly in front of the booster.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Perhaps a little bit horizontally displaced toward the - let's see...

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Houston, to help you, we're looking right directly above the S-IVB with - the Sun is - it's on the right side of the S-IVB and on our - coming in our left number 1 window.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Okay. Understand; the Sun is on the right side of the S-IVB and coming in your number 1 window. And are you - when you give us those angles, that means that your plus-X axis is pointed at it with those angles. Is that affirm?

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Rog.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: The Earth is in our plus-Y, plus-Z direction now, Mike.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Thank you. Earth is plus-Y, plus-Z.

a08_0040510.speaker: Borman
a08_0040510.text: Right, and a little minus-X.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Okay.

a08_0040510.speaker: Lovell
a08_0040510.text: Houston, for information, I'm looking through the scanning telescope now, and I see millions of stars; most of them - the venting from the S-IVB.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Right. Are you having any trouble telling which are the stars and which are the S-IVB particles?

a08_0040510.speaker: Lovell
a08_0040510.text: Oh yeah, definitely. We are in sunlight, and it looks like they are all S-IVB, but we don't know. I am going to attempt a P52 realign at this time and see what I can do.

a08_0040510.speaker: Collins
a08_0040510.text: Understand you.

a08_0042100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0042100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 4 hours, 21 minutes into the flight. In the last half an hour, we've had a very interesting interchange with the crew. They've given us a good description of what has been going on; but more than that, we've been occupied with trying to understand what a proper maneuver would be to give us added separation from the S-IVB. Borman reported some 15 to 20 minutes ago, that he thought the S-IVB was staying a little bit to close for comfort. He estimated that its distance from the spacecraft, 500 to 1,000 feet, and he said he was viewing quite a lot of venting, not

a08_0042100-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0042100-pao.text: Right. Are you having any trouble telling which are the stars and which are the S-IVB particles?

a08_0042100-pao.speaker: Lovell
a08_0042100-pao.text: Oh yeah, definitely. We are in sunlight, and it looks like they are all S-IVB, but we don't know. I am going to attempt a P52 realign at this time and see what I can do.

a08_0042637.speaker: Borman
a08_0042637.text: Mike, anything more on this separation maneuver you're on?

a08_0042637.speaker: Collins
a08_0042637.text: We are working on it, Frank. We're trying to compute what radially outward will be in close terms. Now, you still have the Earth - as I understand plus-Y and plus-Z quadrant. In other words, it's down below you on your right and slightly to your rear? Is that still true?

a08_0042637.speaker: Borman
a08_0042637.text: That's right. Quite a bit to our rear and down below us. Off to the right.

a08_0042637.speaker: Collins
a08_0042637.text: Okay. Well, we - of course, in that attitude, you want to burn some upward and some to the left, and we are trying to be more precise than that. [Pause.] Frank, is it still about the same distance away? Are you opening or closing?

a08_0042637.speaker: Borman
a08_0042637.text: It sure is staying close to us.

a08_0042637.speaker: Borman
a08_0042637.text: Mike, can you just tell us which way the S-IVB pitches and how far it'll pitch to the sling shot maneuver attitude?

a08_0042637.speaker: Collins
a08_0042637.text: Frank, your S-IVB is within 10 degrees of its final attitude at this time.

a08_0042637.speaker: Anders
a08_0042637.text: Houston, you ready to copy the IMU align information?

a08_0042637.speaker: Anders
a08_0042637.text: Alright. Star ID is 03, and star 36, star angle difference 0.01, torquing angle; X, minus 00034; Y, minus 0027; Z, plus 00100. Over.

a08_0042637.speaker: Collins
a08_0042637.text: Okay. Thank you. For Y, I just got four digits here: 0027.

a08_0042637.speaker: Lovell
a08_0042637.text: And Houston, we're going to have to hold up on the cislunar navigation until after this next little maneuver.

a08_0043120.speaker: Collins
a08_0043120.text: Could you give us an updated read-out of your gimbal angles. When your plus-X axis is pointed toward the booster, please?

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Could you give us those gimbal angles, Frank, when you have a chance?

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: I'm getting the COAS right on it now so it'll be accurate.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: Okay. With the COAS right on the S-IVB, the roll reads 105, the pitch is 275, and the yaw is about 325.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Roger. Copy roll 105, pitch 275, and yaw 325.

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: Roger. That should be 115 for the roll.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Thank you. 115 roll. [Long pause.]

a08_0043408.speaker: Anders
a08_0043408.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Go ahead.

a08_0043408.speaker: Anders
a08_0043408.text: Roger. If it will help you any, Mike, the Earth is plus-Y about 45 degrees in a minus-X. I can see it out my side window, and it's a beautiful view with numerous cloud vortex.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Roger, Bill. Thank you. Understand; plus-X 45 degrees between - halfway between plus-Y and plus-Z and slightly minus-X.

a08_0043408.speaker: Anders
a08_0043408.text: Negative. It's 45 degrees in the plus-Y, in the X-Y plane towards minus-X. Over.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Rog. Understand in the X-Y plane, toward X, 45 degrees.

a08_0043408.speaker: Anders
a08_0043408.text: Forty-five degrees from plus-Y to minus-X.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Roger. Thank you.

a08_0043408.speaker: Anders
a08_0043408.text: It's behind us to the right, if that'll help.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: I can still see the Cape and isthmus of Central America.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Rog. Understand. Frank, what we want on this burn is 8 feet per second now, 8 feet per second. We want it radially upward, and we want you to use whatever thrusters are required to burn radially upward at 8 feet per second.

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: Why do you want to use - do so much, Mike?

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Because of the separation distance we would like to achieve between now and the time of S-IVB blowdown.

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: Okay.

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: Mike, do you want me to go ahead and try to do this, or are you going to give us some gimbal angles?

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Apollo 8, Houston. If you can go ahead and do it without gimbal angles, if you can do that. Over.

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: Okay. I don't understand why you want so many feet per second on it, but I think I can - with just a little maneuvering, I can get away from it a lot simpler than that.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Well, we'd like the radial upward for trajectory reasons, and the magnitude we'd like because of the separation distance which we're predicting you will have at S-IVB blowdown.

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0043408.speaker: Borman
a08_0043408.text: VHF sounds good.

a08_0043408.speaker: Collins
a08_0043408.text: Roger. On the VHF.

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Omni-B.

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Understand; Omni-B Baker. [Long pause.]

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0044125.speaker: Anders
a08_0044125.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Rog. About 12 minutes before your big blowdown, there is a small continuous vent which opens at a GET of 04:55:55. You may notice that on the booster, 12- or 15-pound thrust.

a08_0044125.speaker: Anders
a08_0044125.text: Okay.

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: And, Apollo 8, could you give us your burn information whenever you have it?

a08_0044125.speaker: Anders
a08_0044125.text: Roger. We're maneuvering to the attitude now.

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Okay. Houston. I understand you want 8 feet per second burn, is that right?

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Right. Eight feet per second, radially upward.

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Well, we are as close to being radially upward as we can determine.

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Are you going to use P47 to monitor the burn?

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Yeah, Roger. We're putting it in now.

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Maneuvering now.

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Houston, we made the burn at 7.7 plus-X, plus 00001 Y, and Z's are all zeros. The gimbal angles: roll, 180; pitch, 310; and yaw, 020.

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Rog. I copy plus-X, 7.7; Y, 0.1; and roll, pitch, and yaw 180, 310, and 20.

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Did you get that information, Houston?

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. How are you reading?

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Read you loud and clear. Did you get the information?

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: That's affirmative. I say again, we copied plus-X, 7.7; one-tenth in Y, no Z; roll, pitch, and yaw; 180, 310, 020.

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Roger. [Pause.] The burn was made at - initiated at 04:45.

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Roger. Copy 04:45 T IG . [Long pause.]

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Okay. Do you want us to transfer that to the CS - to the LM state vector or just leave it alone, Houston?

a08_0044125.speaker: Collins
a08_0044125.text: Affirmative, Frank. We'd like you to transfer from the CSM to the LM state vector.

a08_0044125.speaker: Borman
a08_0044125.text: Roger.

a08_0044900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0044900-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control. That brings us up to the live action at 4 hours, 49 minutes into the flight. You heard Jim Lovell say we'd have to postpone his navigation - cislunar navigation task which involved plotting several stars, which had been planned during this last half hour and in its place went the separation maneuver, an 8-foot-per-second separation maneuver to ensure adequate separation from the S-IVB. In the course of the last half hour, we lost, the ground lost lock with the beacon on the S-IVB. That was a VHF beacon. Our present altitude, their distance from Earth is 17,200 [naut

a08_0044900-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0044900-pao.text: Roger. Understand; 90 degrees from its X-axis and about 1,000 feet and separating.

a08_0044900-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0044900-pao.text: How's that booster looking now? Is it drifting away rapidly, or how does it look?

a08_0044900-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0044900-pao.text: Bill's the only one that can see it. Just a minute.

a08_0044900-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0044900-pao.text: We're 90 degrees from its X-axis, and we must be out 1,000 feet [300 metres] and moving out.

a08_0044900-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0044900-pao.text: Plus or minus a couple of thousand.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Roger. Understand; 90 degrees from its X-axis and about 1,000 feet and separating.

a08_0045033.speaker: Borman
a08_0045033.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: How's that booster looking now? Is it drifting away rapidly, or how does it look?

a08_0045033.speaker: Borman
a08_0045033.text: Bill's the only one that can see it. Just a minute.

a08_0045033.speaker: Borman
a08_0045033.text: We're 90 degrees from its X-axis, and we must be out 1,000 feet [300 metres] and moving out.

a08_0045033.speaker: Anders
a08_0045033.text: Plus or minus a couple of thousand.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Understand. [Long pause.]

a08_0045033.speaker: Borman
a08_0045033.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. I think we've got clearance now; we got a little behind on our P23s , but I suggest we go ahead and start those now.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Roger. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a08_0045033.speaker: Borman
a08_0045033.text: We're well clear of the S-IVB now, Houston.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Roger, Bill. Thank you, and at your convenience, could you give us the PRD reading?

a08_0045033.speaker: Lovell
a08_0045033.text: Roger. We'll start P23.

a08_0045033.speaker: Anders
a08_0045033.text: Houston. Apollo 8 with a PRD reading.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Go ahead.

a08_0045033.speaker: Anders
a08_0045033.text: Roger. At 4 hours, 4 minutes; Commander is 0, CMP 0.64, LMP 0.02.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Got that. Copy left to right: 0, 0.64, and 0.02 at 4 hours and 4 minutes. Thank you.

a08_0045033.speaker: Anders
a08_0045033.text: Roger. At 04:53, it was 0.01, 0.64, 0.03, and negligible on the survey meter.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Roger. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0045033.speaker: Borman
a08_0045033.text: I have a beautiful view of the S-IVB and the Earth here in one. I'll try and get a picture for you.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Hope so. [Pause.]

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We've got you about a minute away from the Continuous Vent, Open, and 14 minutes away from the big dump, and we'd like an estimate on your distance now if you can give it.

a08_0045033.speaker: Borman
a08_0045033.text: Stand by. Our distance is about 3,000 feet [900 metres] we'd estimate.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0045033.speaker: Borman
a08_0045033.text: And we can see the vent.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Apollo 8. Houston. Say again.

a08_0045033.speaker: Borman
a08_0045033.text: We can see the vent.

a08_0045033.speaker: Collins
a08_0045033.text: Rog. Thank you.

a08_0045831.speaker: Lovell
a08_0045831.text: Boy, it's really hard to describe what this Earth looks like. I'm looking out my center window, which is a round window, and the window is bigger than the Earth is right now. I can clearly see the terminator. I can see most of South America, all the way up through Central America, Yucatan, and the peninsula of Florida. There is a big swirling motion just off the East Coast, and then going on over toward the east, I can still see West Africa, which has few clouds right now. We can see all the way down to Cape Horn in South America.

a08_0045831.speaker: Collins
a08_0045831.text: Good grief, that must be quite a view.

a08_0045831.speaker: Borman
a08_0045831.text: Yeah. Tell the people in Tierra Del Fuego to put on their raincoats; looks like a storm is out there.

a08_0045831.speaker: Collins
a08_0045831.text: Rog. Will do. Do you care to give them a 24-hour forecast?

a08_0045831.speaker: Borman
a08_0045831.text: Probably as good as any other.

a08_0050300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0050300-pao.text: Apollo Control here. As we started to say, the distance from Earth, 17,400 [nautical] miles [32,200 km]. Our velocity now has slowed in relation to the Earth down to 14,384 feet per second [4,384 m/s] and constantly slowing. We just heard from the Command Pilot [means Commander] and he says they will resume the Flight Plan now with their navigation tasks. At 4 hours and 52 minutes into the flight, this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0050300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0050300-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 5 hours, 3 minutes into the flight. The spacecraft is 18 - nearly 19,000 [nautical] miles [35,000 km] from Earth nearing the synchronous point, which it'll just dart on through, of course. Velocity continues to slow, it's now 13,860 feet per second [4,225 m/s]. In the last 10 minutes, we got another beautiful view type statement from the crew. We heard from both Lovell and Frank Borman, and the view indeed must be extraordinary. They described the cloud cover over Africa, over all of South America, and the effects over much of North America. Frank Borman issued

a08_0050513.speaker: Borman
a08_0050513.text: Rog. You might be interested to know the center window is pretty well fogged up, but the other four seem to be in pretty good shape.

a08_0050513.speaker: Collins
a08_0050513.text: Glad to hear you've got four out of five [windows], and your big dump will be coming up in 2 minutes or so.

a08_0050513.speaker: Borman
a08_0050513.text: The S-IVB has started [to] dump. [Long pause.]

a08_0050513.speaker: Lovell
a08_0050513.text: Roger. Mike, did you say star 14 was good till about 05:30 or something?

a08_0050513.speaker: Collins
a08_0050513.text: Yeah. Stand by while I give you that time again. Star number 14 should be good for about another 8 minutes, Jim - 7 minutes.

a08_0050513.speaker: Lovell
a08_0050513.text: Okay. Now be advised, the optics calibration is very difficult to do because of all the other little stars floating around here. I'm going to [garble] bypass it and do it at the end of this.

a08_0050513.speaker: Collins
a08_0050513.text: You should have the LOX dump now, Apollo 8. [Pause.]

a08_0050513.speaker: Lovell
a08_0050513.text: Houston, this is 8. I'm looking through the scanning telescope and that LOX dump just blanked out completely the entire scanning telescope.

a08_0050513.speaker: Borman
a08_0050513.text: It's a fantastic sight, Bill. Looks like the S-IVB, [made] a small attitude excursion while it's dumping.

a08_0050900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0050900-pao.text: Apollo Control here. And we're 5 hours, 9 minutes into the flight and we, as you heard the crew record, the S-IVB is doing its propulsive vent. Now we should see a pretty dramatic separation between the two vehicles. The S-IVB will remain on a path which will take it essentially, if you consider the Moon straight ahead of you for analogy purposes, it will take the S-IVB to the right of the Moon while the spacecraft will veer into the left and slightly ahead of the Moon. Earlier in that conversation you heard Anders reporting his PRD readings. That's the Personal Radiation Dosimeter, and perhap

a08_0051131.speaker: Collins
a08_0051131.text: Rog. I've got a Flight Plan update for Bill if he's ready to copy.

a08_0051131.speaker: Collins
a08_0051131.text: Okay. We're about 05:10 GET where we will record the block data, TLI plus four and TLI plus 11. The TLI plus four PAD that we gave you before is perfectly all right. We will not require that one, and we'll have the TLI plus 11 hour PAD for you shortly. Then at 05:45 or 6 hours on that High Gain Antenna checkout. Roger. Standing by.

a08_0051131.speaker: Anders
a08_0051131.text: We are on Omni-D, and we heard - we lost you after - TLI plus four was okay.

a08_0051131.speaker: Collins
a08_0051131.text: Okay. The TLI plus 4-hour PAD is okay. We'll have the TLI plus 11-hour PAD for you shortly, and at 05:50, for your High Gain Antenna checkout, we'd like you to leave that switch in Wide Beam with reference to our conversation the other day; leave it in Wide.

a08_0051131.speaker: Anders
a08_0051131.text: Roger. Don't want to zap your receivers.

a08_0051131.speaker: Collins
a08_0051131.text: No, it has to do with some loss of tracking data, so it is better to leave it Wide.

a08_0051641.speaker: Lovell
a08_0051641.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Are you recording what we're getting out of (P)23?

a08_0051641.speaker: Collins
a08_0051641.text: Stand by one, Jim; I'll check. [Long pause.]

a08_0051641.speaker: Collins
a08_0051641.text: That's affirmative, Jim; we are copying your P23.

a08_0051641.speaker: Collins
a08_0051641.text: Well, we think that's because you bypassed the trunnion check.

a08_0052218.speaker: Lovell
a08_0052218.text: Houston, we are getting some really big numbers in Delta-R and Delta-V.

a08_0052218.speaker: Lovell
a08_0052218.text: Suggest, do you want us to proceed with this, or should we just leave them alone?

a08_0052218.speaker: Lovell
a08_0052218.text: Do you want us to accept these, or should we leave them alone?

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Roger. We do not wish you to accept those marks. This is due to the fact that in bypassing the trunnion bias check, you still have big numbers left in those registers, so if you go ahead when you - after you do the trunnion bias check, then those numbers will become small later, but do not accept them right now.

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: And we have a TLI plus 11-hour update for you when you're ready to copy.

a08_0052218.speaker: Anders
a08_0052218.text: Roger. Ready to copy TLI plus 11.

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Roger, Bill. TLI plus 11, and this assumes no midcourse correction number 1: it's an SPS/G&N; 63330; minus 1.63, plus 1.29. Are you with me so far?

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Okay. Plus 11.97, minus 165.00; 1268.1, 35608, 050:46:53; GDC Align, north set stars; roll, 068; pitch, 097; yaw, 356; ullage none; other: one, fast return, P37, Delta-V equals 7,900 for Indian Ocean; number 2, high-speed procedure not required; number 3, assumes no midcourse corrections number 1. Over.

a08_0052218.speaker: Anders
a08_0052218.text: Roger. TLI plus 11. SPS/G&N; 63330; minus 1.63, plus 1.29; 013:56:47.59; minus 0048.9, plus 0000, plus 4725.0. You copy so far?

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Yeah, I'm with you so far. [Pause.]

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Apollo 8, Houston, affirmative. I'm with you.

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Yeah, I'm with you so far, Bill; go ahead.

a08_0052218.speaker: Anders
a08_0052218.text: Plus 11.97, minus 165.00; 1268.1, 35608, 050:6 - correction - 050:46:53; north set, 068, 097, 356; zero ullage. Note one: fast return, P37, Delta-V 7900 Indian Ocean; two, high-speed procedure not required; three, PAD assumes no MCC-1. Over.

a08_0052218.speaker: Lovell
a08_0052218.text: Roger, Mike. I might give some comments on P23 data. The auto maneuver was quite accurate. Looks like we got some substellar point in the maneuver; auto optics put Canopus straight where it should be; minimum impulse control worked as advertised.

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Roger, Apollo 8. We copied that, and we'd like for you to do that trunnion check, that calibration, prior to your next set of sightings.

a08_0052218.speaker: Lovell
a08_0052218.text: Roger. Will do. Canopus just disappeared from view, and maybe when we get a little time here, I'll try to get a calibration the first time.

a08_0052218.speaker: Anders
a08_0052218.text: And, Houston. We've rewound the [DSE] tape; you can dump it at your convenience.

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Roger, Bill. Thank you. Are you still picking up anything on the VHF?

a08_0052218.speaker: Anders
a08_0052218.text: No, I'm not picking anything up.

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Give or take a thousand feet.

a08_0052218.speaker: Anders
a08_0052218.text: I'll go ahead and turn VHF-A off and High Gain.

a08_0052218.speaker: Anders
a08_0052218.text: That was some pretty nice music while it lasted.

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: We're going to have to wait until we get the High Gain Antenna locked on again to dump the tape.

a08_0052218.speaker: Borman
a08_0052218.text: Okay. And you about ready for us to go to the PTC attitude?

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: We'd like to hold off on the PTC and get some more P23 information. We'll have some more details of that for you shortly.

a08_0052218.speaker: Lovell
a08_0052218.text: Mike, what I'm doing now, I'm going over to the star Sirius [garble].

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You faded out completely on that, Jim. I heard Frank, but it faded when you began talking. Say again.

a08_0052218.speaker: Lovell
a08_0052218.text: Roger. I have switched to Sirius, the second star in the first set, to see if I can't get an optics calibration on it, at least.

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Roger. That's fine. We'll have some more good words for you shortly.

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Jim, on your P23, we'd like you to go ahead and do the calibration and then use star number 15 and take three sets, followed by star number 16, two sets. Over.

a08_0052218.speaker: Lovell
a08_0052218.text: Roger, Houston. That's what we're trying to do. I'm trying to get [star] 15 for an optics cal. It's was very difficult with the bright Earth to find a star that we can get into the sextant. I'm trying to use the auto optics in P23 to get the star. We have that now; we're trying to maneuver the spacecraft to bring the trunnion to zero so we can get the landmark line of sight.

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Roger. Understand. And I also have your PTC attitude, which is different than you have. I'll give that to you whenever you get a free moment. [Pause.]

a08_0052218.speaker: Collins
a08_0052218.text: Alright. PTC attitude will be pitch, 242; yaw is 020. Over.

a08_0053300-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0053300-pao.text: And, Houston. We've rewound the [DSE] tape; you can dump it at your convenience.

a08_0053300-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0053300-pao.text: Roger, Bill. Thank you. Are you still picking up anything on the VHF?

a08_0053300-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0053300-pao.text: No, I'm not picking anything up.

a08_0053300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0053300-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 5 hours, 33 minutes into the flight. We are now 22,500 [nautical] miles [41,700 km] from Earth, our velocity 12,700 feet per second [3,870 m/s]. In the - in the course of his recent remarks, Jim Lovell said that it was - he had a lot of difficulty in finding the proper stars during his star checks from - because of the competition of the S-IVB venting. Apparently that's setting off big splashes of light, which drown out the stars; however, they should be separating. At the last reading they were 3,000 feet [900 metres] from the S-IVB, and that distance should b

a08_0053300-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0053300-pao.text: Give or take a thousand feet.

a08_0053300-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0053300-pao.text: I'll go ahead and turn VHF-A off and High Gain.

a08_0053300-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0053300-pao.text: That was some pretty nice music while it lasted.

a08_0055056.speaker: Anders
a08_0055056.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Over.

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Go ahead.

a08_0055056.speaker: Anders
a08_0055056.text: Roger. We'll hold up on the High-Gain check until we get out of P23.

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: Roger, Bill. Thank you. [Pause.]

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: You may have to delay your lunch a little bit. Are you hungry?

a08_0055056.speaker: Anders
a08_0055056.text: No.

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: First time I ever heard you say that. [Long pause.]

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0055056.speaker: Borman
a08_0055056.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: Rog. It looks to us like the S-IVB is behaving completely normally in regard to all the blowdowns and other sequential events that take place. It looks good.

a08_0055056.speaker: Borman
