a08_0055056.text: Roger. How far away is it from us now?

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: We were going to ask you.

a08_0055056.speaker: Borman
a08_0055056.text: (Laughter) Okay.

a08_0055056.speaker: Anders
a08_0055056.text: Fifty miles.

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: Roger. Copy.

a08_0055056.speaker: Anders
a08_0055056.text: Let's make that 80 kilometers, since there are some international aspects to this flight.

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: Roger.

a08_0055056.speaker: Lovell
a08_0055056.text: Okay, Houston. We did an optics calibration; we get zeros all the time.

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: Roger. Understand; optics calibration and zeros all the time. Good.

a08_0055056.speaker: Lovell
a08_0055056.text: It takes a lot longer to do it, though. I had to go to a star like Sirius to finally see it.

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: Rog. Understand. We're real glad you got that so we can get a horizon calibration to put in the computer. [Long pause.]

a08_0055056.speaker: Borman
a08_0055056.text: Looks like the number 5 window is starting to fog up, Houston.

a08_0055056.speaker: Collins
a08_0055056.text: Roger, Houston. Understand it's the number 5 that's fogging up. [Long pause.]

a08_0055200-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0055200-pao.text: Rog. It looks to us like the S-IVB is behaving completely normally in regard to all the blowdowns and other sequential events that take place. It looks good.

a08_0055200-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0055200-pao.text: Roger. How far away is it from us now?

a08_0055200-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0055200-pao.text: We were going to ask you.

a08_0055200-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0055200-pao.text: Let's make that 80 kilometers, since there are some international aspects to this flight.

a08_0055200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0055200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 5 hours, 52 minutes into the flight. You undoubtedly heard Frank Borman say that they would delay temporarily the checkout of the High Gain Antenna. And that - we just got an estimate from the crew on the distance of the S-IVB. Frank Borman estimates 50 miles, about 50 miles away. And then he corrected it and said in view of the international aspects of this flight, let's make it 80 kilometers. Meanwhile, Lovell is checking his navigational programs and assuring that he can see the - making sure that his optics are operating properly. At 5 hours - the High Gain

a08_0055848.speaker: Lovell
a08_0055848.text: Houston, P23 coming through with Sirius.

a08_0055848.speaker: Lovell
a08_0055848.text: A little better, these numbers are a little better.

a08_0060716.speaker: Borman
a08_0060716.text: Houston, how do you read? Apollo 8.

a08_0060716.speaker: Borman
a08_0060716.text: Roger. Have you been getting the downlink on the P23?

a08_0060716.speaker: Borman
a08_0060716.text: Okay. Now how much longer do you want us to hold off going to PTC?

a08_0060800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0060800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 6 hours, 8 minutes into the flight. We've pretty well settled here in the Control Center on the first midcourse correction, which is presently planned as an SPS burn. Purposely wanted to get some early indication of its performance, the Service Propulsion System, and fortunately, the other events seemed to have worked in their favor. Presently planning an SPS burn of 2 to 3 seconds duration. We'll be putting 24 feet per second into the overall velocity. And this event is presently scheduled to occur at about 9 hours into the flight. And, let's see, beyond tha

a08_0061316.speaker: Lovell
a08_0061316.text: Roger. Are you recording all of the data from 23, or do you want some read down to you?

a08_0061316.speaker: Collins
a08_0061316.text: Stand by, Jim. We think we're getting it all. We're confirming now. That is affirmative, Jim. We are getting all that's coming down. How is it going?

a08_0061316.speaker: Lovell
a08_0061316.text: It's working very nicely. I finished - one set was Sirius, three stars [means marks], and one set with Procyon, or two sightings; three sightings with Sirius and two with Procyon.

a08_0061316.speaker: Borman
a08_0061316.text: Okay, Houston. This is Apollo 8. We are ready to go to the PTC attitude.

a08_0061316.speaker: Collins
a08_0061316.text: Roger, Frank. Understand. And we understand you've completed all five sets, three on one and two on another in P23. Is that right?

a08_0061316.speaker: Borman
a08_0061316.text: That's affirmative. But we've finished the five sightings, three on [star] 15 and two on [star] 16.

a08_0061618.speaker: Collins
a08_0061618.text: Rog, Frank. What we're doing down here is this. We'd really like, for horizon calibration, we'd like a total of 15 marks; you know, three sets on one star, two on the other. On the other hand, we're balancing that with the need to go to PTC, and we're not losing sight of the fact that you want to go to PTC right away. So if you'll bear with us another couple of minutes, we are trying to decide whether to ask you to go back and do some more of P23 or whether to clear you at this time to go to PTC. Over.

a08_0061618.speaker: Borman
a08_0061618.text: Okay. We started maneuvering to PTC. We're getting kind of far behind, is one thing I'm concerned about, Mike. Jim is now taking off his pressure suit.

a08_0061618.speaker: Collins
a08_0061618.text: Roger. Understand. How about you and Bill?

a08_0061618.speaker: Borman
a08_0061618.text: Well, we're standing by till he gets through.

a08_0061618.speaker: Collins
a08_0061618.text: Understand. And you are maneuvering to PTC. That's fine.

a08_0061618.speaker: Borman
a08_0061618.text: Well, I would prefer to do that, but we will...

a08_0062212.speaker: Collins
a08_0062212.text: Roger. We would like to hold off on the Passive Thermal Control until 7 hours GET and, in the meantime, to get as many more P23 marks as Lovell can give us, starting again with the first star and doing two sets of three marks each, and then going to the second star we gave you. And concurrent with that, if possible, we'd like Bill to run this High Gain Antenna check-out if Lovell's attitude is compatible with that. Over.

a08_0062212.speaker: Borman
a08_0062212.text: Okay. But they have not been to date. We are almost to the Passive Thermal Control attitude now, and Jim is just half way through taking his suit off.

a08_0062212.speaker: Borman
a08_0062212.text: We'll have to hold off for a minute here. [Pause.]

a08_0062212.speaker: Collins
a08_0062212.text: Roger, Frank. And the reason for this, of course, is the horizon calibration requires a number of points to give you good data for the onboard Nav coming on.

a08_0062212.speaker: Borman
a08_0062212.text: Roger. We understand. We'll be right back with you; just - just have to wait a minute here.

a08_0062212.speaker: Borman
a08_0062212.text: That failing to separate from the S-IVB kind of fouled us up a little.

a08_0062721.speaker: Borman
a08_0062721.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0062721.speaker: Borman
a08_0062721.text: Roger. We're standing by. Are you about ready for the High Gain Antenna trial?

a08_0062721.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0062721.text: Okay. Just a second; we will check on that. Then are you in a position where you can go back to the star sightings?

a08_0062721.speaker: Borman
a08_0062721.text: Well, we will be, but we can't until Jim gets ready.

a08_0062721.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0062721.text: Okay. We'll stand by, and you give us a mark on that. In just a second, I will check on the antenna. Okay. It looks like we are ready to go on the High Gain Antenna check. And we can either go with commands called out from the ground, and you can monitor it, or you can be talked through it, whichever you prefer.

a08_0062721.speaker: Borman
a08_0062721.text: Well, stand by. I guess we're not quite in a proper attitude yet.

a08_0062900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0062900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 6 hours, 29 minutes into the flight. At the present time, here in Mission Control Center, we're in the process of changing shifts. Flight Director Milton Windler and his Maroon Team of flight controllers coming on to relieve Flight Director Clifford Charlesworth and the Green Team.

a08_0063242.speaker: Borman
a08_0063242.text: Roger. There is the High Gain Antenna on Wide, Auto.

a08_0063500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0063500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. At the present time the spacecraft is nearing 30,000 miles altitude. The displays here in Mission Control Center show our current altitude at about 29,228 nautical miles [54,130 km]. This is Apollo Control at 6 hours, 35 minutes into the flight.

a08_0063521.speaker: Borman
a08_0063521.text: Are you getting the results you want from our High Gain Antenna? [Long pause.]

a08_0063521.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0063521.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Affirmative. We are getting your data, and we may have a beamwidth change but stand by on that.

a08_0063521.speaker: Borman
a08_0063521.text: Alright. We're standing by. Jim's about ready to go back to the P23s.

a08_0063521.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0063521.text: Roger. We have a Go until 7 hours on the start of the PTC.

a08_0063521.speaker: Borman
a08_0063521.text: We're in a PTC mode now waiting for Jim, and I noticed that out my window now I can see Orion very clearly, even though the win - the Sun is bright in the other window.

a08_0063521.speaker: Borman
a08_0063521.text: It almost pained me to say that, but it's true.

a08_0063521.speaker: Borman
a08_0063521.text: Speaking of the windows, the number 5 window is getting pretty well obscured and the number 3 window is unusable.

a08_0063521.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0063521.text: Roger. Understand; number 3 is unusable and number 5 is obscured. Can you make out any definition at all, or do you have a target to look at?

a08_0063521.speaker: Borman
a08_0063521.text: Well, I can see the Sun. Wait till it comes around the Earth, and I'll give you a better hack on that.

a08_0063521.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0063521.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're going to go ahead and try to dump your tape right now. The circuit margins aren't too good at our present configuration. We're going to take a look at it. If it doesn't work, we may have to dump it again at a later configuration.

a08_0064257.speaker: Borman
a08_0064257.text: Houston, Apollo 8. We're maneuvering back now to do another P23.

a08_0064257.speaker: Lovell
a08_0064257.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. I'll do two more sets on [star] 15, and then we'll do one set on [star] 16.

a08_0064257.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0064257.text: Okay, Apollo 8. I'd like to fill you in on things we're thinking about doing in the next couple of hours, first chance you get there.

a08_0064257.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0064257.text: Okay. In relationship to the midcourse correction, we'd like to put that one off until about 11 hours, and it'll be approximately a 25-foot-per-second burn. The reason we're delaying the burn time is to allow for better tracking as a result of the 7½-foot-per-second you put in on the separation. Why, we'd like to take little more time to look at the tracking data. And the dispersions in your correction aren't going to be growing very fast here. What we'll do then is to delete the Nav sightings that occur about 09 plus 10 in the Flight Plan, and this will be getting us back on to the nor

a08_0064500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0064500-pao-press-conference.text: Is due to the what, you say?

a08_0064500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0064500-pao-press-conference.text: The 7 hours on the P23 problem is due to the fact that we want to get these sightings in at a certain range. Over.

a08_0064500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0064500-pao-press-conference.text: If you have any comments on that proposal, why, go ahead and pass them down, and we'll feed them in.

a08_0064500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0064500-pao-press-conference.text: No. I think that's fine. We need to get out of the suits and get something to eat here too.

a08_0064500-pao-press-conference.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0064500-pao-press-conference.text: Rog. Looks like we'll be back on the Flight Plan by 11 hours. We'll be holding up on the updates and PADs because of the later burn.

a08_0064735.speaker: Lovell
a08_0064735.text: Roger. I believe we have the S-IVB in sight. It's - it would appear to be tumbling, and every once in a while, we are getting very bright reflections from it off the star - off the Sun.

a08_0065000.speaker: Lovell
a08_0065000.text: Houston, 8. Are you getting the data from the P23?

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0070013.speaker: Borman
a08_0070013.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Rog. We're copying your P23 progress, and FAO advises that it looks like you are finishing your first star, and we'll need one more set on the second star, and this 7-hour cut-off isn't that firm, so we'd like for you to go ahead and complete the second star if you can. And...

a08_0070013.speaker: Borman
a08_0070013.text: We're on the last setting of the second star right now.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Okay. Real fine. And we've got a - it's about time for a cryo fan cycle.

a08_0070013.speaker: Borman
a08_0070013.text: Okay. We'll do them one at the time for about 4 minutes on each of them.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a08_0070013.speaker: Anders
a08_0070013.text: We've got the cryo fan on in H 2 tank number 1.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Rog, Bill.

a08_0070013.speaker: Lovell
a08_0070013.text: Houston, Apollo 8. We've just got finished taking two sets, six sightings on Sirius, and one set [three sightings] on Procyon.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Roger. Understand that's six on Sirius and one on Procyon.

a08_0070013.speaker: Lovell
a08_0070013.text: Two sets on Sirius, one set on Procyon.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0070013.speaker: Borman
a08_0070013.text: And we're maneuvering now to PTC attitude.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Oh. Roger, Apollo 8. [Long pause.]

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Apollo 8, when you get a chance down in the Lower Equipment Bay, it looks like you're using the floodlights in the Dim 2 position, and that one is a time-limited item. We'd like for you to do your standard running in the Dim 1 position. Over.

a08_0070013.speaker: Borman
a08_0070013.text: Roger. Just turned them off.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Okay. Any time you have them on, running Dim 1 position is preferred for the LEB.

a08_0070013.speaker: Borman
a08_0070013.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0070013.speaker: Anders
a08_0070013.text: Houston. We have the cryo fan on - the number 1 H 2 tank was on at 07:01. You can give us a hack when you want it - when you're ready for it to be turned off.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Wilco. [Pause.]

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Okay, Apollo 8. You can terminate that one and go to the other tank.

a08_0070013.speaker: Anders
a08_0070013.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0070013.speaker: Anders
a08_0070013.text: Okay. H 2 number 2 is On.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Rog.

a08_0070013.speaker: Borman
a08_0070013.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Go ahead.

a08_0070013.speaker: Borman
a08_0070013.text: Are you having any problem on the ground with your comm?

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Negative. You're coming in loud and clear.

a08_0070013.speaker: Borman
a08_0070013.text: Okay. We seem to be breaking lock intermittently up here once in a while.

a08_0070013.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070013.text: Rog. We'll keep our eye on it. It sounds good though.

a08_0070846.speaker: Borman
a08_0070846.text: Okay. Houston, Apollo 8. We've initiated the PTC.

a08_0070846.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0070846.text: Okay. Apollo 8, you can terminate the fans in the hydrogen, and we're ready to start on the oxygen tanks.

a08_0071100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0071100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 7 hours, 11 minutes now into the flight. During the change of shift press conference, we've had a very quiet period relatively quiet period here in Mission Control Center. Astronaut Tom Mattingly now acting as Capsule Communicator and we had some communications with the Apollo 8 crew primarily concerning some minor modifications to their Flight Plan to get them back on flight - back on the Flight Plan. Frank Borman also reported that the S-IVB appeared to be tumbling. That observation was confirmed from the ground and we appear to be getting good data from th

a08_0071100-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0071100-pao.text: Apollo 8, we're through with the dump; you can have the tape recorder back.

a08_0071510.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0071510.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're ready to go to the [stirring of the] second O 2 tank.

a08_0071510.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0071510.text: And for your information, it's Cleveland 24 to 10, and what we plan to do...

a08_0071510.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0071510.text: That's Cleveland 24 to 10, not over yet. [Pause.]

a08_0072049.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0072049.text: Okay, Apollo 8. Looks like you can terminate your cryo fans now, and we're going to leave you alone for a while. Let you get caught up. Things we have on board; the High Gain Antenna check - comm mode check that you have listed at 7 hours, we'll put off and do whenever you are ready for it. So that's at your convenience. During the High Gain dump that we performed using the wide band, we were still getting real good data at 36K, which is a little bit further than circuit margins that were predicted for you. And we've got our SPS [Service Propulsion System] burn coming up somewhere around 11 ho

a08_0072049.speaker: Borman
a08_0072049.text: We're doing the program 21 now, determining ground track for LOI that we did not make at 5 hours.

a08_0072500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0072500-pao.text: During that conversation with the crew, you heard Frank Borman refer to the windows on the spacecraft clouding up. He mentioned that the number 3 window was completely clouded over and that the number 5 window was partially clouded. Those windows, as seen from the inside of the spacecraft, number from 1 to 5 beginning with the Commander's side window, left hand side of the Commander's couch. Number 2 window would be the docking window above the Commander's position. The number 3 window is the hatch window, and number 4 would be the docking window above the Command Module - or rather Lunar Modu

a08_0072720.speaker: Borman
a08_0072720.text: Okay. We just broke lock on S-band High Gain. We're on Omni D now.

a08_0072720.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0072720.text: Apollo 8, Is that Bravo or Delta?

a08_0072720.speaker: Borman
a08_0072720.text: We can't get the Program 21 to integrate up to LOI. It just stalled out around 61 hours and 2 minutes.

a08_0072720.speaker: Borman
a08_0072720.text: Roger. Do you want us to stop the integration via Verb 96? Over.

a08_0075651.speaker: Borman
a08_0075651.text: Rog. Do you want us to hold off on this P52 realignment, also?

a08_0075651.speaker: Speaker - Mission Control
a08_0075651.text: Yeah, that's affirmative, CapCom. We want to do that a couple of hours when it is related to the maneuver, midcourse.

a08_0075651.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0075651.text: That's affirmative, Apollo 8. That's tied to the maneuver and we will hold off and do that all in normal pre-maneuver sequence. And - We have got a score here [in the Cleveland-Dallas football game] - in the fourth quarter, 31 to 13. And I've got some words on your P21 discrepancy any time you're interested. And I'd like to confirm...

a08_0075651.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0075651.text: Okay. Before I get off on that one, I'd like to confirm that you use the Verb 37 procedure to go to P00.

a08_0075651.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0075651.text: Okay. On P21, the thinking runs that you had a slight error in your state vector at the time you started, and when that was integrated out, it intercepted the lunar surface where it locked up and this is contained in a fairly recent program note.

a08_0075651.speaker: Borman
a08_0075651.text: Okay. Now, we've closed the - the waste vent, so we should see this O 2 come down now.

a08_0075651.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0075651.text: Okay. Understand you closed the waste vent, and how about the lithium change? Have you done that one?

a08_0075651.speaker: Flight Director
a08_0075651.text: EECOM, Flight. Did you copy that?

a08_0075651.speaker: Borman
a08_0075651.text: This conference communication is great. We won't have to have any debriefing.

a08_0080100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0080100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 8 hours, 1 minute into the flight. The crew has been involved in some housekeeping chores aboard the spacecraft. Changing out the lithium hydroxide canister and we had a brief conversation with them during which the ground passed up the score of the - the fourth quarter score of the Cleveland-Dallas game and we'll play back that conversation for you now and then stand by for any further comment from the spacecraft.

a08_0080100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0080100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. At the present time, the spacecraft altitude is 37,749 nautical miles [69,911 km] and our velocity now down to 9,800 feet per second [2,987 m/s]. We don't hear any more conversation from the crew at this point. We'll stand by to pick up again should any communication develop between the ground and the spacecraft. This is Apollo Control at 8 hours, 04 minutes.

a08_0081339.speaker: Borman
a08_0081339.text: Roger. With the delay in burn, do you mind if we have a urine dump the - before the burn? Will that foul your tracking up?

a08_0081339.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0081339.text: Okay. Standby. Let me run that one by. [Long pause.]

a08_0081339.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0081339.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We don't have any objections to going ahead with the urine dump now. And for your information, the waste water dump - our schedule, we plan to put it off until about 11:30, and this will get you up to approximately 90 percent in your waste tank. It's a little higher than normal, but we wanted to put this off until after the burn was completed.

a08_0081339.speaker: Anders
a08_0081339.text: Houston, how do the circuit margins on the S-band look as compared to your pre-flight calculations? [Long pause.]

a08_0081339.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0081339.text: Okay, Apollo 8. It's a little bit early to give you any real numbers on your comm performance. Looks like it's working as good as predicted, and everything else seems to be doing better, so this may be doing better, too. After we've done our next comm checks and some of these other things, we'll have a better hack on it; I can give you a quantitative answer to your question.

a08_0082423.speaker: Anders
a08_0082423.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0082423.speaker: Anders
a08_0082423.text: Roger. Sure got a nice view of the Earth from here. We can see Baja California and about where San Diego ought to be.

a08_0082423.speaker: Anders
a08_0082423.text: I can't see my dad's flag pole, out there today, though.

a08_0082423.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0082423.text: We'll tell the doctors about that.

a08_0083000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0083000-pao.text: This is Apollo control at 8 hours, 30 minutes into the mission. We continue to have a very quiet period here in Mission Control Center. On board the spacecraft, the crew also getting a bit of a chance to relax and get out of their spacesuits. We also anticipate they will be getting something to eat at this period. The midcourse correction maneuver, the first run of the Service Propulsion System engine, which is anticipated to be about 2 to 3 seconds in duration, is currently scheduled for about 11 hours Ground Elapsed Time. That's about 2 hours later than it was originally planned in the Fligh

a08_0083000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0083000-pao.text: And that is the extent of that bit of communication with the crew. At the present time the spacecraft is approaching 40,000 [nautical] miles [74,080 km] in altitude. We're about 39,500 [73,150 km] and the velocity continuing to drop off, down now to about 9,600 feet per second [2,930 m/s]. At 8 hours, 35 minutes into the mission, this is Apollo Control.

a08_0084840.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0084840.text: Okay. We dropped off of High Gain on the Omni there for a bit and went to a low bit rate, and we're getting ready to command you back to high bit rate. Do you want us to keep you posted every time we change tape speeds?

a08_0084840.speaker: Borman
a08_0084840.text: We're not recording now anyway, Houston.

a08_0084840.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0084840.text: Rog. Understand; but when we go to high bit rate, do you want to be kept informed every time we transfer? We hadn't planned on it.

a08_0084840.speaker: Borman
a08_0084840.text: If we think if we need to record, we'll ask you on that deal.

a08_0090000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0090000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 9 hours into the mission. At the present time the spacecraft has covered about 42 - almost 43 thousand [about 78,000 km] of the some 200 thousand [nautical] miles separating Earth and Moon. It's now traveling at a speed of about 9,200 feet per second or about 6,200 miles an hour [2,800 m/s]. Up to now the mission has gone extremely well. The spacecraft is performing nominally in all respects, and we continue to have a relatively quiet period, both here on the ground and in terms of communications with the astronauts on the spacecraft. We did have one brief communicati

a08_0090000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0090000-pao.text: At the present time the Flight Plan, the updated Flight Plan, shows the crew in an eat period and are interspersed with that activity for Bill Anders, he will also be doing some checks on the monitoring equipment onboard the spacecraft to observe the Service Propulsion System midcourse correction burn. That will be occurring in just a little less than 2 hours from now as currently planned. At 9 hours, 3 minutes; this is Apollo Control.

a08_0090934.speaker: Borman
a08_0090934.text: Roger. How does your tracking look on us?

a08_0090934.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0090934.text: Apollo 8, tracking still in progress and a little too soon to give you a firm answer on the results, but everything looks nominal so far.

a08_0091205.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0091205.text: Okay. Sometime when it's convenient for you now, I would like to see an oxygen fuel cell purge. And do you have any estimate on when you might be getting around to this comm test?

a08_0091205.speaker: Anders
a08_0091205.text: Right now we're right in the middle of trying to get something to eat, Ken. We can - I guess we can do the fuel cell purge.

a08_0091205.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0091205.text: Okay, Apollo 8, there's no rush. Just didn't know what you were doing at the time and - Give us a call when you have a free moment; we'll pick up.

a08_0091205.speaker: Anders
a08_0091205.text: We can start the O 2 purge now, if you wish.

a08_0091205.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0091205.text: Okay. That'd be fine, and I'll keep track of the time for you.

a08_0091205.speaker: Anders
a08_0091205.text: Okay. That'd be good. Now I'll turn on O 2 now on fuel cell 1.

a08_0091541.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0091541.text: Apollo 8, Houston. That's about 2 minutes on your first fuel cell.

a08_0091541.speaker: Anders
a08_0091541.text: Roger. It's up, and number 2 is on now.

a08_0091731.speaker: Lovell
a08_0091731.text: While I'm waiting for my turn at the water gun, I might give some comments on the optics. There seems to be quite a band of light that goes all across the scanning telescope anywhere in the vicinity of the Sun. Just a little while ago we were in the position where I could pick up the Moon in the scanning telescope. And then I looked at it in the sextant and the sky - the space around the Moon was a very light blue, just about as light blue as we have it back on Earth. And it's not black - that Sun angle with the Moon.

a08_0091731.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0091731.text: Understand. This light blue was - showed up in the sextant.

a08_0091731.speaker: Lovell
a08_0091731.text: That's affirmative. I maneuvered the optics so I could pick up the Moon in the sextant, and the - the space around the Moon is a light blue.

a08_0091731.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0091731.text: Rog. Can you make any kind of estimate about the proportion of the radius, how far out that seems to extend?

a08_0091731.speaker: Lovell
a08_0091731.text: Well, it extends the full length of the sextant. Actually, I could see us coming as we moved across, because the band of light in the scanning telescope cut across where the Moon was, and it moved in this area. I believe it's caused by the refractional light inside the optics themselves.

a08_0091731.speaker: Lovell
a08_0091731.text: Also, I've been occasionally looking out to see if I could see stars at various Sun angles, and at this particular altitude, it's very difficult. In the scanning telescope the Sun is very bright and the Earth is very bright, And if I looked at the Earth and try to look for stars, I lose my dark adaptation very quickly.

a08_0091731.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0091731.text: Roger. Do you have any problem seeing the Moon?

a08_0091731.speaker: Lovell
a08_0091731.text: No problem seeing the Moon. When I looked in the star/landmark line-of-sight, I - It's a very thin crescent, but it vas very visible.

a08_0091731.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0091731.text: Rog. Does the area illuminated in Earthshine show up?

a08_0091731.speaker: Lovell
a08_0091731.text: Not at this altitude, and that's strange. I thought I could see that. At this altitude, the refraction of the light in the optics themselves, due to the reflection of the sunlight I suspect, or Earth's light, completely blanked out the dark side of the Moon to this altitude.

a08_0091731.speaker: Lovell
a08_0091731.text: Maybe we have an atmosphere around the Moon. [Long pause.]

a08_0091731.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0091731.text: Okay, Apollo 8. Looks like that ought to terminate the fuel cell purging.

a08_0092400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0092400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 9 hours, 24 minutes. The spacecraft at this time is about 45,000 nautical miles [83,300 km] from Earth. The velocity currently about 8,900 feet per second [2,700 m/s]. We just had a rather brief communication with the spacecraft. Astronaut Lovell reported on the optics, the onboard system to assist in navigation - midcourse navigation, and reported that the sky around the Moon, when viewed through the sextant, the 28-power optical device on the spacecraft, appeared to be a light blue rather than black as he had expected. Lovell also reported that he was not able to se

a08_0092400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0092400-pao.text: This is Mission Control, Houston. Some very interesting comments there from astronaut James Lovell on the optical system for the Guidance and Navigation system aboard the spacecraft. The assessment here in Mission Control Center is that there is no problem associated with the minor anomalies that Lovell mentioned. And this, of course, is verified by the fact that the crew has been able use the optics aboard the spacecraft to do the sightings that have been required. At 9 hours, 32 minutes into the mission, the Apollo 8 spacecraft is now some 45,686 nautical miles [84,610 km] in altitude. The v

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Go ahead, Apollo 8.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Do you want to get started here around 10 hours? Is that what you said?

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Well, what we had planned was to use the 10- to 11-hour period as your pre-burn preparation just as we would have done normally, and...

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: That's fine. We can go ahead and do that.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: ...and if you can work in this comm check before that, it would be desirable, but that's not a constraint.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: What do you want in the way of a comm check, George?

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Again, what do you want?

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay. What we've got here is a couple of DTO [Detailed Test Objective] comm checks. We'll be switching around to five different modes, and only one of them will interrupt your activities. In that case, we'll be switching to the uplink backup voice, and that's the one time that you might lose temporary uplink voice comm. You'll have downlink voice comm throughout the entire procedure, and it ought to take you, I guess, 10 to 15 minutes max., the only requirement being that we should stay on a High Gain Antenna.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Why don't we go ahead and start now then?

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay. That sounds pretty good.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: ...whenever.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay, Apollo 8. Another couple of minutes, we'll be ready to go into our - our comm check. And, for your information, looks like the signal strength is 3 to 4 dB better than expected on the wide range, on the wide beam mode, and approximately that gives you 1.4 increase in your range.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Roger. Let's not increase it by 1.4, though.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Something else you might take a look at, as you go through the PTC, we have some people who would like to know if you can see any detectable effect on the windows in the form of their fogging. Particularly, does the Sun seem to vary the fog intensity or does it increase it or decrease it or make it go in patches or anything like that that you might be able to notice?

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: The Sun doesn't seem to change it much; however, the different incidences of the Sun's rays magnify the - the fogging, or at least change it.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay, Apollo 8. I'm sorry. Would you say again, please?

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: The Sun doesn't seem to have any effect on the windows themselves, but the different incidence - angles of incidence of the Sun rays change the relative amount of obscuration caused by the fogging.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We're ready to go into the comm check now, and it's your option. We can call out the switches and let you position them, or we can command it from the ground. In either event, there'll be a couple of switches that you'll have to throw for us.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: We'll have you command them, and we'll throw [the switches] what we have - what you want.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay. And I'll keep you posted on what we're doing. The first test is an uplink voice and ranging with full downlink voice which is essentially what you're doing right now, is to be used for a baseline.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay. We're starting on test number 1, and if you would verify that the S-band Normal mode switch is in Voice.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Roger. We're in Voice.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: [Garble] Charlie. [Pause.]

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: And the Up Telemetry Data to Data.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Roger. Data. [Long pause.]

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay. And Up Telemetry Command to Normal.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Normal.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Roger. How about High Gain Antenna Track to Auto.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: We're on Omni D now; we've got to wait 'til we get around the other way.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay. What's your estimate? [Pause.]

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: We're at 15 minutes from it.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Maybe we'd better hold the comm check off till after the midcourse, because we'd better get started here at 10 [hours] if we want to burn at 9 [means 11 hours].

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: That's affirm. We're reviewing that right now.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: ... means we want to burn at eleven [hours].

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We're gonna postpone the comm test until after the burn.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Thank you.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Are you ready to go - for us to go through with the P52 now?

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: That's negative, Apollo 8. We'd like to update things first, and we're going to give you a LM state vector and then an external Delta-V.

a08_0094440.speaker: Borman
a08_0094440.text: Roger.

a08_0094440.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0094440.text: And with P00 and Accept, why, we'll go ahead and work on that.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0095718.speaker: Lovell
a08_0095718.text: Go ahead.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Okay. We've got your PADs. We're ready to read up to you. And we're standing by to uplink your state vector and external Delta-V whenever you're ready to give us Accept.

a08_0095718.speaker: Lovell
a08_0095718.text: Roger. Just stand by one, and we'll get the PAD from you. [Pause.]

a08_0095718.speaker: Lovell
a08_0095718.text: And we'll put it in TM [Telemetry] and Accept now - at this time.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a08_0095718.speaker: Anders
a08_0095718.text: We're ready to copy the PAD. [Pause.]

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Okay, Apollo 8. I didn't copy that last one. We are sending your state vector up now.

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Roger. We say we are ready to copy the PAD.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Okay. The first PAD will be a maneuver PAD, MCC-1: and this will be an SPS/G&N, beginning with the weight; 63295; minus 1.63, plus 1.29; 010:59:58.30; plus 0013.6, minus 0004.5, plus 0020.2; 345, 188, 343; 99999; plus 0168.5; 0024.8, 0:02, 0018.6; 23, 201.3, 16.4; 012, up 27.6, left 0.4; November Alpha for the remainder of that column. In the comments: north stars; 068, 097, 356; a no ullage start, and a single bank burn on bank Alpha. Over.

a08_0095718.speaker: Lovell
a08_0095718.text: Houston, Apollo 8. MCC-1 maneuvers: SPS/G&N; 63295; minus 1.63, plus 1.29; 010:59;58.30; plus 0013.6, minus 0004.5, plus 0020.2; 345, 188, 343; all 9's; plus 0168.5; 0024.8, 0:02, 0018.6; 23, 201.3, 16.4; 012, up 27.6, left 0.4; November Alpha for the remainder. North set stars; roll, 068; pitch, 097; yaw, 356; no ullage, single bank - bank Alpha.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Roger, Apollo 8. That's correct. And I have a TLI plus - 11 PAD for you. [Long pause.]

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Roger. Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Go ahead.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Roger, Apollo 8. Loud and clear now. Are you ready to copy?

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Roger. Ready to copy.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Okay. This is a TLI plus 11, SPS/G&N. This assumes a midcourse correction number 1: 63140; minus 1.63, plus 1.29; 013:56:48.97; minus 0059.9, plus 00000, plus 4701.6; 177, 143, 000; November Alpha, plus 0019.7; 4702.0, 5:51, 4681.8; 12, 128.3, 25.7; 023, up 26.3, left 1.7; plus 11.95, minus 165.00; 1268.3, 35608, 050:47:05; north stars; 068, 097, 356; no ullage. For the fast return P37 Delta-V, 7900 for the Indian Ocean, high speed procedure not required for the MS. This assumes midcourse correction 1. Over.

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Stand by.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Houston, Apollo 8. For the readback, are you ready?

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Go ahead.

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: TLI plus 11; SPS/G&N; 63140; minus 1.63, plus 1.29; 13:56:48.97; minus 0059.9, plus 00000, and I believe it's plus 4701.6.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Affirmative. [Pause.]

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: 177, 143, 000; N/A, plus 0019.7; 4702.0, 5:51, 4681.8; 12, 128.3, 25.7; 023, up 26.3, left 1.7; plus 11.95, minus 165.00; plus 1262.3, 35608, 050:47:05. [Pause.] The north set; roll, 68; pitch, 97; yaw, 356; no ullage, P37 high speed, 7900 Indian Ocean, and high speed procedures for the MS are not required; assumed MCC-1.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Roger, Apollo 8. Two corrections on the GETI. The hour's 013. Range to go EMS.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Roger. Copy that and the range-to-go in the EMS 1268.3. Over.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: That's correct.

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. Be advised that we doubted that it would be possible to use the stars to get our backup alignment. We haven't been able to see any stars through the scanning telescope yet.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Okay. And another comment for you, Apollo 8; like for you to use Verb 37 to select P00 and then wait for your computer activity light to go off prior to unzap of the LM NAV to CSM slots.

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Roger. You ready for us to do that now?

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: That's affirm. [Long pause.]

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8.

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Go ahead.

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Okay. Now we'll go ahead and start back towards the Flight Plan around 8 hours here of P52, right?

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: That's affirm.

a08_0095718.speaker: Borman
a08_0095718.text: Well, we - we've transferred - wait - we've transferred the state vector to the LM slots already before we did a 52. So we're going to do the 52 now. [Pause.]

a08_0095718.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0095718.text: Okay, Apollo 8. That's good procedure and...

a08_0100000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0100000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 10 hours into the mission. At the present time activity here in Mission Control is beginning to pick up as we prepare for the first operation of the spacecraft Service Propulsion System engine, and matching that activity here on the ground is also heightened activity in the spacecraft. At the present time the crew is involved in making preparations for that burn scheduled to be a 2.4-second burn of the Service Propulsion System engine. That will occur in just about an hour from now. Scheduled to occur at 11 hours Ground Elapsed Time. During the next hour the crew will

a08_0100000-pao.text: Houston, Apollo 8. a08_0101500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0101500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. During that lengthy string of numbers, which was read up to the crew from the ground; included in that information was the data that they would need to return to Earth should that be necessary at a point following the mid-course correction and assuming that they were unable to communicate with the ground. This type of information is passed up routinely to the crew during the course of the mission at specified intervals and is kept by the crew for use should it become necessary because of some contingency to return to Earth.

a08_0101613.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0101613.text: Roger. Will you check your Up Telemetry switch to Block, please?

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Well, no. We got to get a DAP load in here to make sure they check first, right? Okay? Okay, it's... You got the DAP to where you want it?

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0101938-onboard.text: I'm going to get it right now.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0101938-onboard.text: I know, but don't you want to do - Before you do P30, don't you want to look at the DAP?

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0101938-onboard.text: No, no, that comes way down along the line.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Alright, Alright, excuse me; go ahead.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Okay? I like it. Do you like it?

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Okay, 136, good; minus three balls 45 is good; plus 00202, good. I like it. Proceed.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Okay, 1685 [garble]. Okay, I'll - Okay, that's good.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Let's see, might as well have a countdown for this one, huh?

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Well, all our stuff is counting up though, isn't it?

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0101938-onboard.text: I got mine; I can figure it - I've got 6 seconds to go or some - 6 minutes to go, 5 minutes to go either way, so you can suit yourself.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Why don't you count down? I can call it out to you.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Okay, we don't have too much time. We've got to get a boresight star and all that stuff, too.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Just stand by, I don't haven't started yet.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Okay, we did a P52. Now we go to P00. Is that what we're doing?

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0101938-onboard.text: You know you ought to go to P00 to maneuver to the burn attitude.

a08_0101938-onboard.text: Yeah, I will; I got it.

a08_0101938-onboard.text: Okay, P30. You got your optics power Off, by the way? Oh, you're going to be using them, are you?

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0101938-onboard.text: Yeah, I got to use them.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0101938-onboard.text: ISS, On. SCS, operating; test the Caution/Warning lights.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0101938-onboard.text: You guys can go on; I'll get this.

a08_0101938-onboard.text: SCS - SPS thrust light On and Off in 10 seconds.

a08_0101938-onboard.text: Good, minus 19.5. Good set; it's okay.

a08_0101938-onboard.text: Okay. Nonessential bus is going to Main B.

a08_0101938-onboard.speaker: Anders

a08_0102900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0102900-pao.text: At the present time, the mission is proceeding nominally. The - all the spacecraft systems are functioning very well and we have no problems to speak of at the present time. The crew is very heavily involved at this time and preparing for that mid-course correction, the first use of the Service Propulsion System engine. That is scheduled to occur at 11 hours Ground Elapsed Time or about 33 minutes from now. That burn is a planned as a 2½-second burn - a very short ignition of the 20,500-pound-thrust SPS engine. It will give them a velocity change of about 24 or 25 feet per second. At th

a08_0102900-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0102900-pao.text: Okay. We've got a telescope alignment if you'd like to give it a try. Your sextant star is still good, but if you had problems with that, folks have worked out that if you look through the telescope at 10:35, we have a shaft and trunnion that should point you at the center of the Earth, if you would like to give that one a try.

a08_0102930.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0102930.text: Okay. We've got a telescope alignment if you'd like to give it a try. Your sextant star is still good, but if you had problems with that, folks have worked out that if you look through the telescope at 10:35, we have a shaft and trunnion that should point you at the center of the Earth, if you would like to give that one a try.

a08_0103238.speaker: Anders
a08_0103238.text: Roger. I've already given 2 minutes on H 2 1 and 2 and O 2 1, and I've just started O 2 2.

a08_0103238.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0103238.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We'd like to dump your tape prior to the burn.

a08_0103238.speaker: Anders
a08_0103238.text: Roger. It's only been running here about 15 minutes. [Long pause.]

a08_0103238.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0103238.text: Okay, Apollo 8. That's - that's correct. You're on high bit rate, and we're afraid you may run out before the burn, so we'd like to dump it, and give it back to you with a full load before the burn.

a08_0103238.speaker: Anders
a08_0103238.text: Roger. And give us a comment on the voice quality.

a08_0103640.speaker: Anders
a08_0103640.text: Roger. We plan to stop charging battery B about another 5 minutes. You concur?

a08_0104308.speaker: Lovell
a08_0104308.text: Go ahead, Houston. You were cut out.

a08_0104308.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0104308.text: Okay, Apollo 8. All your systems are Go, and we were about to tell you, you could go ahead and terminate the battery charge, and you beat us to the punch.

a08_0104308.speaker: Borman
a08_0104308.text: I read your mind, and it's showing 37 volts right now.

a08_0104500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0104500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 10 hours, 45 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. At the present time, our spacecraft is at an altitude of 51,595 nautical miles [95,554 km], traveling at a velocity of about 8,300 feet per second [2,530 m/s]. Flight Director Milton Windler has just gone around the room here in Mission Control Center. Reviewed the status of the spacecraft and our flight for the first midcourse correction burn and we've passed up a Go to the crew for that maneuver, scheduled to occur in just about 15 minutes from now at 11 hours Ground Elapsed Time. That burn will be a very short one,

a08_0104500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0104500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. We had a relatively quiet period for the last few minutes between the ground and the spacecraft and we imagine that the crew is rather actively involved in getting - making final preparations for their first midcourse correction en route to the Moon. That ignition - engine ignition is now scheduled to occur about 2½ minutes. Correction: about 6½ minutes from now at 11 hours Ground Elapsed Time. The batteries aboard the spacecraft have been fully charged up and they will be brought on the line during preparation and during the burn, to assist in carrying th

a08_0105357.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0105357.text: Apollo 8, Houston. If you'll go high bit rate, we'll give you a tape recorder back to your command. [Long pause.]

a08_0105357.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0105357.text: Apollo 8, Houston. If you'll put your high bit rate on, we'll give you the tape recorder back.

a08_0105500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0105500-pao.text: Here in Mission Control, the Guidance Officer has just advised the Flight Director that the spacecraft gimbal motors positioning the SPS engine are in the proper attitude and everything looks Go for the burn scheduled to occur now in about 3 minutes. We'll continue to monitor for conversation with the crew.

a08_0105650.speaker: Borman
a08_0105650.text: Houston, did you give us a tape back? Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0105650.speaker: Borman
a08_0105650.text: Apollo 8's Command Reset to get tape motion. We're now in Normal.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0105730-onboard.text: You heard me, didn't you? I [garbled]. Not if you do a real quickly.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Okay, 2 minutes. Delta-V Thrust A, Normal.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Tape recorder is Record, High bit rate, and Forward.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Okay, stand by for DSKY blanking.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0105730-onboard.text: What happened to EMS, Auto? Bill?

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: I don't see how Wally did this [garble].

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Okay, at 30 seconds, get EMS Mode, Auto.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: EMS Mode, Auto; average g is On.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Stop. At 10:02, it has to be Off.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0105730-onboard.text: It's holding; let's go, let's go through the checklist.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Okay, okay, you got that; SPS Thrust light, On, Okay, Delta-V Thrust A, Off.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Okay, verify Thrust is Off. I verify it over here.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: SPS Pitch and Yaw circuit breakers, Closed.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Okay, turn them Off: Gimbal Motors.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Flight Recorder's Off; Main Bus ties going Off.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Okay, proceed. You've got your [garbled, probably referring to having the residual velocities to be gained displayed on the DSKY].

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Got them? Do I null them?

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Okay - Okay. Null residuals.... residuals are nulled.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0105730-onboard.text: Okay, record Delta-V Counter and residuals.

a08_0105730-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0105730-onboard.text: You can turn this off before...

a08_0105830-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0105830-pao.text: We're now 30 seconds from ignition of the SPS engine for that 2.4-second burn. That maneuver will be primarily to control the altitude of the spacecraft as it goes around the back side of the Moon at perigee. Targeting for there is 60 nautical miles [111 km].

a08_0105830-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0105830-pao.text: Apollo 8, stand by for a mark at 1 minute.

a08_0105830-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0105830-pao.text: And we have confirmation of SPS ignition. Thrust looks nominal says the Flight Dynamics Officer. And we should have shutdown also, we'll have confirmation of that shortly.

a08_0105830-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0105830-pao.text: And the Guidance and Control Officer advises the Flight Director the burn time was 2.4 seconds exactly nominal, just what was planned. That should have given us a velocity increase of about 24 or 25 feet per second. We've now taken the batteries off the line, their job done in assisting in carrying the heavy - heavier than normal electrical loads during a major maneuver of this sort, even though a very short maneuver. They will then be recharged to bring them up to full charge for the next maneuver or use of the SPS system. The initial indication was that the Service Propulsion System engine w

a08_0105842.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0105842.text: Apollo 8, stand by for a mark at 1 minute.

a08_0110243.speaker: Lovell
a08_0110243.text: Roger. The burn time was on time - about 2 seconds; we had residual 4.4 in X. We burned it out to 0.2. Attitudes are nominal. The Delta-V C , before the residuals were taken out, was a minus 2.4. I have transferred the state vector to the LM slot in Verb 66.

a08_0110243.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0110243.text: Roger. Copy 4.4 for X and 2.4 on C. And negative residual on Y prior to the trim. Is that affirm?

a08_0110243.speaker: Borman
a08_0110243.text: That's affirmative, and we took out the 4.4 residual down to 0.2.

a08_0110243.speaker: Anders
a08_0110243.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Do you want us to start charging battery A, now?

a08_0110243.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0110243.text: Apollo 8. Let's go back to battery Bravo, and we'll finish that one off before we start in on Alpha.

a08_0110243.speaker: Borman
a08_0110243.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Do you want us to maneuver to any particular attitude for a water dump, or do you want us to go to PTC attitude?

a08_0110243.speaker: Borman
a08_0110243.text: And give me the angles please. [Long pause.]

a08_0110243.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0110243.text: Okay, Apollo 8. Let's do the same angles we had before: that's pitch 242 and yaw 20 on the PTC attitude.

a08_0110750.speaker: Borman
a08_0110750.text: Houston, we're preparing to dump our waste water now.

a08_0110800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0110800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 11 hours, 8 minutes and we've just gotten a preliminary assessment of the performance of the SPS engine from here in the Mission Control Center. And from the indications of the burn, the SPS looks to be completely Go on the words of the Guidance Officer, and the other flight controllers also concur. The burn was completely nominal in all respects. We also had a post-burn report from Astronaut Jim Lovell aboard the spacecraft and we'll play that back for you now and then stand by for any further communications with the spacecraft.

a08_0110800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0110800-pao.text: During that conversation you heard Jim Lovell refer to the residuals. Now this is the amount of velocity remaining to be added or taken out of the trajectory following the ignition of the SPS engine and we normally expect a small residual. We did have residuals of about 4.4 feet according to Lovell, and as per the normal procedure, these were removed by burning the Reaction Control System thrusters. A very short duration burn on those to, in effect, peak up the effects of the burn and put the spacecraft velocity right on the pre-planned [value].

a08_0111041.speaker: Borman
a08_0111041.text: We've noticed on our system test battery vent pressure that when we opened the battery vent valve, we get an immediate drop-off to pressure which nulls out at about two-tenths of a - to three-tenths of a volt. And we think this is zero in the battery manifold. Do you concur?

a08_0111041.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0111041.text: Okay. Stand by. [Garble] stand by, and let's check it out.

a08_0111041.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0111041.text: Apollo 8, I cut you out there. What did you say on the last one?

a08_0111041.speaker: Borman
a08_0111041.text: It looks like probably the - that zero psi corresponds to about three-tenths of a volt on the test meter. We've had it happen a couple of times, where the pressure would drop rapidly to this setting, as if it was zero. Over.

a08_0111041.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0111041.text: Rog. We'll look at our data here and let you know what we see. Are you going ahead with the water dump now?

a08_0111041.speaker: Borman
a08_0111041.text: Roger. We'd - we're pausing here on the water dump, though, just to verify that the battery vent - the line is clear as indicated by a battery vent pressure of zero.

a08_0112010.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0112010.text: Okay. Number one on the list of things is that the Flight Plan shows CDR should hit the sack. Number two, kind of a summary of your burn. All your SPS and systems look Go. The trajectory shows that you have a CPA with a mode of 69.67 [nautical] miles and the time of pericynthion is 69 plus 10. You do have a capture on a good free return. It's a little bit early to completely evaluate the trajectory for corridor control.

a08_0112010.speaker: Borman
a08_0112010.text: Thank you very much. That was a very fine resume you just sent in. We're right now in the process of trying to dump out the water and the UCTAs and so on and so we'll get with you on the High Gain as soon as we can.

a08_0112010.speaker: Borman
a08_0112010.text: Houston, what do you want to dump the waste tank down to? [Long pause.]

a08_0112010.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0112010.text: Apollo 8, I'd like for you to dump the waste tank to 25 percent.

a08_0112707.speaker: Anders
a08_0112707.text: We finally got some stars to see.

a08_0113000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0113000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control; 11 hours, 30 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. We have some further refinements on the results of that Service Propulsion System midcourse correction, the first midcourse correction planned en route to the Moon. The effect of the burn was to give us a peri - pericynthion or low point, closest approach to the Moon of 69 nautical miles. We've been targeting for about 60 nautical miles. This information of course will be evaluated further and refined. This is the preliminary Flight Dynamics Officer analysis of the effects of the burn, and we would expect some update to

a08_0113200.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0113200.text: Rog. Do you folks have your water quantity switch in the potable or the waste water tank position now?

a08_0113200.speaker: Borman
a08_0113200.text: We're in the waste tank position now, and we're dumping UTCAs [means UCTAs] first, Houston.

a08_0113200.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0113200.text: Okay. We weren't watching any waste quantity decrease, and it looked like the nozzle temps indicated that something was going on, and we were trying to dope out what was going on.

a08_0113200.speaker: Borman
a08_0113200.text: Well, there's a lot of stuff going out I'll tell you. How do nozzle temps look?

a08_0113200.speaker: Borman
a08_0113200.text: Okay. We'll keep on going then.

a08_0113900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0113900-pao.text: Communications continues to be excellent with the spacecraft. We're continuing to track with the 85-foot dish antenna at Goldstone - Goldstone, California. The crew reported earlier that the signal strength indication that we had was above normal, above what they would expect. And up to this point, we have had extremely good results from the unified S-band communications system. Spacecraft is presently about 50,000 nautical miles [93,000 km] from Earth as shown on the large plot board here in the front center of Mission Control Center. We expect the crew will begin a series of relatively relax

a08_0114037.speaker: Anders
a08_0114037.text: Okay, Houston. We're going to dump the waste tank on down to about 25 percent.

a08_0114037.speaker: Anders
a08_0114037.text: Okay. Tell EECOM to wake up and keep an eye on the waste tank servicing. [Pause.]

a08_0114037.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0114037.text: It'll take a minute to think of something appropriate. [Pause.]

a08_0114653.speaker: Anders
a08_0114653.text: How're the nozzle temperatures looking, Houston?

a08_0114916.speaker: Anders
a08_0114916.text: Man, you're looking pretty small down there now, Houston. [Pause.]

a08_0114916.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0114916.text: We're carrying a big stick, though.

a08_0114916.speaker: Anders
a08_0114916.text: Just barely make out Clear Lake. [Pause.]

a08_0114916.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0114916.text: And your nozzle temperatures, Bill, have dropped from about 94 to around 66.

a08_0114916.speaker: Anders
a08_0114916.text: Okay. I'm showing just a little bit above 50 percent here, and we'll keep on going, and if it looks too cold, give us a call.

a08_0114916.speaker: Anders
a08_0114916.text: Houston, we had a momentary O 2 high flow, but we think it's due to all the purging of the water lines we're doing here in the cabin.

a08_0115320.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115320.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We show you down to 25 percent of your waste water.

a08_0115320.speaker: Anders
a08_0115320.text: Okay, I'm about 28, Houston. Stand by just a bit. [Long pause.]

a08_0115320.speaker: Anders
a08_0115320.text: Okay. Waste dump stopped and then purge again.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Houston, we're on a High Gain, and it might be a good time to try your comm check. [Long pause.]

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Apollo 8, we're going to go ahead and crank up for a comm test now, and we will be a little bit late on your update for 12 hours.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Okay.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Do you still want our - have us command as much as we can on the ground, or would you like to move the switches yourself?

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Oh, you can have the fun of doing it.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Sounds like you're dragging there.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: [Garble] you suggest a [garble] We're using 1/250 on at f:11 on CEX and C mags for Earth shots. Do you verify? Over.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Okay. You got going before I got my pencil up. How about saying it again?

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: f:11 - f:11 and 1/250 for CEX 16-mm and C 70-mm.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Okay. Thank you.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: How about running it by the back room boys. My light meter doesn't seem to be helping out too much.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We're starting in - setting up for our first comm test. This is going to be an uplink voice, ranging, and full downlink, which is not anything really different than what you have on board. I'd like for you to verify that the S-band Normal Mode Voice switch is in Voice.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Roger. Voice.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Okay. And the Uptelemetry Data to Data.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Roger. Data.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Uptelemetry Command in Normal.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Roger. Normal.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: High Gain Antenna to Auto Track.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Correction. That's...

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Auto.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: We're in Auto, Wide Beam, and you can go ahead and dump the tape.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Okay. I'd like for you to go to Narrow Beam.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Okay. Going to Narrow Beam now.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Rog. [Pause.]

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: And I'll give you a call when we get ready to work on the tape.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Okay. We're still in PTC, so you're only going to have it for about 10 or 15 minutes.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Okay. We've had some problems with our displays, and I think they're straightened out now, but you may have to keep us advised if we run out of limits in case we lose our display again.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Say, while we're standing by here, Apollo 8, the Service Module quantities that we had listed - we're going to try to update them, if you want to call out your quantities. Have you checked them with your charts?

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Negative. I haven't gotten around to that. Stand by.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Okay. There's no hurry on that. Just wondered if you had done it; we'll check it against what we've got on our nomogram. [Long pause.]

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: I'm showing a SPS helium pressure, about 3,570, indicated on board.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Rog.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: And fuel/ox[idizer] tank pressures are 177 and 176, respectively.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Okay.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: And our back room tells you that you've got the right f-stop.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Okay. I will keep using it.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: This PTC attitude really isn't the greatest for taking pictures of the Earth.

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Rog.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Or of the Moon. [Pause.]

a08_0115950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0115950.text: Apollo 8, kinda stand by for a burst of noise, as we change configurations on the ground. We're going into test 1; You'll still have up and downlink, and we'll be in this mode for 2 minutes, but you may hear some burst of noise as we change.

a08_0115950.speaker: Anders
a08_0115950.text: Roger.

a08_0120400-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0120400-pao.text: And I'll give you a call when we get ready to work on the tape.

a08_0120400-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0120400-pao.text: Okay. We're still in PTC, so you're only going to have it for about 10 or 15 minutes.

a08_0120400-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0120400-pao.text: Okay. We've had some problems with our displays, and I think they're straightened out now, but you may have to keep us advised if we run out of limits in case we lose our display again.

a08_0120400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0120400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 12 hours, 4 minutes into the mission. The flight of Apollo 8 continues to progress very smoothly at this point. Both here in the Mission Control Center and in the spacecraft, things have quieted down considerably since that mid-course correction maneuver. At the present time, Commander Frank Borman is scheduled to begin a 7-hour sleep period, and his fellow crewmen, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders, are presently involved, primarily, in some housekeeping functions aboard the spacecraft, managing the systems. And also apparently, from the communications with the - with the g

a08_0120400-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0120400-pao.text: Say, while we're standing by here, Apollo 8, the Service Module quantities that we had listed - we're going to try to update them, if you want to call out your quantities. Have you checked them with your charts?

a08_0120846.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0120846.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We're in the middle of our first test, and how about giving me a voice check.

a08_0120846.speaker: Anders
a08_0120846.text: Roger, Houston. This is Apollo 8. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Apollo 8, out.

a08_0120846.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0120846.text: Rog. And read you loud and clear. This comm is unbelievably good.

a08_0120846.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0120846.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We've finished the first test, and we're now going to change the uplink mode to Uplink Command and Ranging, and we'll be going without upvoice. We'll be in this mode for 2½ minutes and will be sending a test message. It'll have no effect on either your computer or your panel switch configuration. What you might see will be the S-band noise that's associated with the break lock. However, you should still have a good signal on your power meter. This is not a loss of signal, but rather just a loss of the voice modulation, and I'll do you a mark just before we do that so tha

a08_0120846.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0120846.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're about to disable the voice modulation on uplink, and we'll be back up no later than 12:13.

a08_0121400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0121400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 12 hours, 14 minutes into the mission now. Apollo 8 is presently some 57,000 - rather 58,000 nautical miles from Earth, 58,334 [108,034 km] according to our displays here in Mission Control Center, and the spacecraft is traveling at a velocity of 7,700 feet per second [2,347 m/s]. We do expect, probably for the rest of the night, we'll have a rather quiet period here in Mission Control Center. The Commander Frank Borman is in his 7-hour sleep period now. He should be about one hour along. Following that we'll have sleep periods for Command Module Pilot Jim Lovell and

a08_0121400-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0121400-pao.text: Roger, Houston. Read you loud and clear. How me?

a08_0121400-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0121400-pao.text: Okay, loud and clear. We're back up with you. Completed our second test.

a08_0121400-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0121400-pao.text: Okay. Our next test will be a test of the uplink voice and ranging with downlink voice, ranging and low bit rate, so we'll be changing bit rate on you, and we'll be making a voice check in the middle.

a08_0121400-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0121400-pao.text: Okay. You've about had it on the High Gain. You might try to get it in, but it's going to hit the scan limit at any second. [Long pause.]

a08_0121400-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0121400-pao.text: Okay, Apollo 8. Looks like we'll get our information before we lose the High Gain.

a08_0121426.speaker: Anders
a08_0121426.text: Roger, Houston. Read you loud and clear. How me?

a08_0121426.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0121426.text: Okay, loud and clear. We're back up with you. Completed our second test.

a08_0121426.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0121426.text: Okay. Our next test will be a test of the uplink voice and ranging with downlink voice, ranging and low bit rate, so we'll be changing bit rate on you, and we'll be making a voice check in the middle.

a08_0121426.speaker: Anders
a08_0121426.text: Okay. You've about had it on the High Gain. You might try to get it in, but it's going to hit the scan limit at any second. [Long pause.]

a08_0121426.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0121426.text: Okay, Apollo 8. Looks like we'll get our information before we lose the High Gain.

a08_0121426.speaker: Anders
a08_0121426.text: Okay. We'll just leave it go.

a08_0121426.speaker: Anders
a08_0121426.text: They got the scan limit. We'll let it go, Houston, until it breaks lock. [Pause.]

a08_0121426.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0121426.text: Okay, Apollo 8. Go ahead and switch to the Omni.

a08_0121426.speaker: Anders
a08_0121426.text: How're you doing with your test?

a08_0121426.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0121426.text: Okay. We've got three-fifths of the test. We'll have to pick up the rest next time we get a look at the High Gain.

a08_0122656.speaker: Lovell
a08_0122656.text: Roger. Running out P21 at - to 69:10 indicates a parallel of about 67.4 [nautical] miles [124.8 km]. I guess we concur here.

a08_0122656.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0122656.text: You guys are getting pretty good.

a08_0122656.speaker: Lovell
a08_0122656.text: That's a lot better than our first answer.

a08_0122656.speaker: Anders
a08_0122656.text: We don't care if we're right, just so MPAD is right.

a08_0123820.speaker: Lovell
a08_0123820.text: Roger. I'd like to ask a question about this TLI plus 11 maneuver that we copied. In the remarks, you have P37, Delta-V 790.0. Is this the Delta-V that we would use with P37?

a08_0123820.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0123820.text: Okay. That's the option that you use with minimum time.

a08_0123820.speaker: Lovell
a08_0123820.text: Roger. What I'd like to do is check on our P37 with your TLI maneuver update.

a08_0123820.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0123820.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We'd like to make sure that we don't have a misunderstanding that this 790.0 feet per second is the Delta-V. It's not associated with the high speed proced - workaround procedure. This is just a standard P37 Delta-V.

a08_0123820.speaker: Lovell
a08_0123820.text: Roger. But was that the Delta-V that you used to give us the TLI plus 11 PAD? Okay, I see. Never mind.

a08_0123820.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0123820.text: Okay. That's not the one that the maneuver PAD was based on. That's the number you put in for the minimum time.

a08_0123820.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0123820.text: Okay. Sounds like a good idea if you want to go ahead and check out the 37. And we're standing by to work on comm as soon as that High Gain's available.

a08_0124454.speaker: Anders
a08_0124454.text: Okay. Houston, you got the High Gain.

a08_0124454.speaker: Anders
a08_0124454.text: Houston, do you read? Apollo 8. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0124454.speaker: Anders
a08_0124454.text: Roger. The High Gain is yours.

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: Okay. And if you're ready, why, we'll go ahead with our comm checks.

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: We're starting in now on our fourth test. [Pause.] Like for you to put your Telemetry Input switch to PCM High.

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: Okay. And now we're going to switch uplink to the upvoice backup for about 2 minutes, and it may take a couple of seconds when you hear the upvoice lost. So you can place your Uptelemetry Data switch to Upvoice Backup, and in the event that all of this doesn't work out too well, I'm reading 12:47 on my clock now, and let's meet back in our present configuration no later than 12:50.

a08_0124454.speaker: Anders
a08_0124454.text: Roger, Houston. Read you loud and clear.

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: Okay. That's pretty good. That's Upvoice Backup, and would you confirm that you're in Narrow Beam on High Gain?

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: Okay. Thank you. We're going to continue tracking and watching High Gain Antenna here for a couple of minutes, and I'll give you a call when we're ready to go back.

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We have completed this test. We'll be switching back to the full uplink. When you hear the noise associated with the loss of modulation, you can go back Uptelemetry Data switch to Data.

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: Real fine. We've just got one to go here if you'll put your Telemetry Input PCM switch to Low.

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: Okay. We'll be in that configuration for about 2 minutes, and then we'll be completed with the comm test.

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: I have some Service Module RCS quantities if you would like to take them sometime and check them against your onboard calculations.

a08_0124454.speaker: Anders
a08_0124454.text: Rog. Ready to copy. Could you give quad A, B, C, and D in that order?

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: Okay. Will do. And I'll give you weights in pounds and the percentages. Quad A, 231, for 76 percent.

a08_0124454.speaker: Anders
a08_0124454.text: Roger. Stand by. What time is that for?

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: Okay. Quad Bravo, 251, 82 percent. Quad Charlie, 240, 79 percent.

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0124454.text: Quad Delta, 245 [115 kg], 81 percent. GNC advises that these numbers are still good even though it is a 12:15 time. And we are completed with a comm test. You can take your High Gain Antenna and go back to Medium. [Pause.]

a08_0124454.speaker: Mattingly
