a08_0291800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 29 hours, 18 minutes into the flight. Our velocity; 4,797 feet per second [1,462 m/s]. Our distance; 116,658 nautical miles [216,050 km]. And in recent minutes, we have recorded this conversation, and we have every reason to believe it'll be a continuing conversation, because we've just heard additional calls. Let's have the tape.

a08_0291800-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0291800-pao.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0291800-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0291800-pao.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0291800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0291800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. We're looking presently at the biomed read-out on Bill Anders, and it looks like this: A mean heartrate of, around, between 68 and 69. And the highest the system has seen, in this sample period of roughly an hour, is about 88; the lowest it's seen is 51. His mean respiration rate is 10, and, let's see, that's all the data we have on that chart. No additional conversation since we gave you those readings. And at 29 hours, 21 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0293000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0293000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. Within the last half-hour, several members of the crew here have had another conversation with the Apollo 8, in private, regarding their medical situation and apparently it is much improved. We - we will have this tape for you shortly, but in general, Borman reports feeling much, much better. We'd estimate it'll be 15 minutes before we have the tape. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0293210.speaker: Borman
a08_0293210.text: Roger. We're dumping some water we collected here, and we're ready to dump the waste water down to 25 percent. Do you concur?

a08_0293210.speaker: Collins
a08_0293210.text: Roger. We concur. We're standing by for your dump.

a08_0293210.speaker: Borman
a08_0293210.text: Alright. We've already started the other.

a08_0293640.speaker: Collins
a08_0293640.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0293640.speaker: Collins
a08_0293640.text: Roger. We're getting geared up down here to do the first of the comm checks. We will be doing an Omni comm check, which is on your Flight Plan, listed mode 7.8, and we'll let you know when we are ready to proceed.

a08_0294001.speaker: Collins
a08_0294001.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0294001.speaker: Anders
a08_0294001.text: Roger, Houston. We're dumping waste water now. How do the nozzle temps look?

a08_0294001.speaker: Collins
a08_0294001.text: Stand by. Looks good, Bill; 64 degrees [18° Celsius]. Over.

a08_0294001.speaker: Anders
a08_0294001.text: Roger. We just got an O 2 flow high from purging to vent line on the cabin.

a08_0294001.speaker: Collins
a08_0294001.text: Roger. Understand. [Long pause.]

a08_0294001.speaker: Borman
a08_0294001.text: How is everything in Houston.

a08_0294001.speaker: Collins
a08_0294001.text: Oh, just fine, Frank. Everything down here is Go. How are you?

a08_0294001.speaker: Borman
a08_0294001.text: Fine. What's the news?

a08_0294001.speaker: Collins
a08_0294001.text: Well, did you get the intergalactic news summary we sent up to you a couple of hours ago? It might have been during your rest period. We gave you a couple of football scores. One of them in particular was - I don't know if you copied that - Army 21, Navy 14. Over.

a08_0294001.speaker: Borman
a08_0294001.text: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven; testing out.

a08_0294001.speaker: Lovell
a08_0294001.text: I got that one. [Pause.]

a08_0294001.speaker: Collins
a08_0294001.text: Rog. The Cowboys were destroyed by the Cleveland Browns yesterday. The Pueblo crew is expected to be released. And I now hear our air-to-ground has got a lot of background noise. Stand by; we are going to go through these comm test modes on page 2-23 of the Flight Plan. Over.

a08_0294001.speaker: Borman
a08_0294001.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0294001.speaker: Collins
a08_0294001.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Would you go S-band Aux switch to Down-Voice Backup. Over.

a08_0294001.speaker: Borman
a08_0294001.text: Down-Voice Backup. Roger and out.

a08_0294001.speaker: Collins
a08_0294001.text: Thank you.

a08_0294001.speaker: Borman
a08_0294001.text: Houston, be advised that it looks like your Quindars are clipping your voice during your transmission.

a08_0294001.speaker: Collins
a08_0294001.text: Roger, Understand. Are we still experiencing this intermittent condition that was there a few minutes ago?

a08_0294001.speaker: Borman
a08_0294001.text: Not always, but often in the beginning and in the end or your transmission.

a08_0294001.speaker: Collins
a08_0294001.text: Roger. Understand. I'll give it a little extra time.

a08_0294544.speaker: Collins
a08_0294544.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Could you try to find us a better Omni antenna? Over.

a08_0294544.speaker: Collins
a08_0294544.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're not able to read you on this Omni antenna. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0294544.speaker: Collins
a08_0294544.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0294544.speaker: Collins
a08_0294544.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We understand you're copying us. While we are trying to reestablish contact with you, would you put your optics switch to zero? We show you're drifting off in trunnion and request that you zero your optics. [Pause.]

a08_0294544.speaker: Collins
a08_0294544.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We copy your optics zeroed, and how are you reading us now? Over. [No answer.]

a08_0294544.speaker: Collins
a08_0294544.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're down to 25 percent on your waste water dump and ready to terminate. Over.

a08_0294544.speaker: Collins
a08_0294544.text: Roger, Our next comm test is a ranging only test. I have four switches I'd like you to throw, which will cause you to lose voice communications for approximately 3 minutes. Over.

a08_0294544.speaker: Collins
a08_0294544.text: Alright. The first one is S-band Normal, Mode, Voice, Off; the second, S-band Normal, Mode, PCM, Off; the third, S-band Normal, Mode, Ranging, switch to Ranging; and fourth, the S-band Aux tape switch, Off. Over.

a08_0294700-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0294700-pao.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0294700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0294700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 29 hours, 47 minutes. I'd like to amplify a bit more on this most recent taped conversation. Mike Collins opens it and this was a private conversation conducted from the communication room in this building, building 30. Collins asked the crew for additional detail on their condition and Frank Borman comes on the line and he describes his problems and he also says he's had several hours of rest this morning and is feeling much, much better. Jim Lovell, in the conversation, also reveals, for the first time, that he apparently wasn't feeling too well when they fir

a08_0294700-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0294700-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We understand you're copying us. While we are trying to reestablish contact with you, would you put your optics switch to zero? We show you're drifting off in trunnion and request that you zero your optics. [Pause.]

a08_0294700-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0294700-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We copy your optics zeroed, and how are you reading us now? Over. [No answer.]

a08_0295548.speaker: Collins
a08_0295548.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Request S-band Normal, Mode Ranging to Off, and S-band Normal, Mode, PCM, to PCM. I say again, S-band Normal, Mode, Ranging, Off; S-band Normal, Mode, PCM, to PCM.

a08_0295548.speaker: Collins
a08_0295548.text: Apollo 8. Houston. We'll stand by in this configuration for a moment.

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0295800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. That conversation concluded very briefly there with a great amount of static. But we now have the conversation which we've alluded to in two earlier announcements, a rather full development on an examination of the crew medical problems. You'll hear first Mike Collins, the Capsule Communicator. He's talking with Bill Anders. Then he talks to Frank Borman, and then Chuck Berry, who I believe identifies himself, comes on the line. Here's that tape now:

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0295800-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control, Houston. That concluded the private conversation to determine the medical status of the crew. And we learned - in the course of that conversation, obviously, we learned about some things that had gone on yesterday, much earlier in the flight, I think the report was 19 hours, which we had not learned until this point. We are satisfied though now that the crew, the situation is certainly improving and certainly settled down. At 29 hours, 57 minutes into the flight, we're 118,400 [nautical] miles [219,300 km] out, and we're moving at a velocity of 4,739 feet per second

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0295800-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Three communication switch positions. First, S-band, Aux, Tape, to Down-Voice Backup; S-band Normal, Mode, PCM, Off; Telemetry Inputs PCM, High. I say again, S-band, Aux, Tape, to Down-Voice Backup; S-band Normal, Mode, PCM to Off; Telemetry Inputs PCM to High.

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0295800-pao.text: Roger. Houston, this is Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0295800-pao.text: Reading you weak but clear now, Bill.

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0295800-pao.text: Roger. We still have a bad look angle on this antenna. [Pause.]

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Lovell
a08_0295800-pao.text: Please be informed that the [garble]. Over.

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0295800-pao.text: Apollo 8. Houston. Unable to copy. After about a minute of this configuration, we're going to return to normal voice, and at that time, we should be able to hear you better.

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0295800-pao.text: Roger. What [garble] are we going through right now? [Long pause.]

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0295800-pao.text: Roger. We are in Mode 7-10, and the comm test mode's on page 223. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0295800-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Three switch positions. Telemetry Inputs PCM switch to Low; S-band Normal, Mode, Voice, to Voice; S-band Normal, Mode, PCM, to PCM. I say again, Telemetry Inputs PCM switch, Low; S-band Normal, Mode, Voice, to Voice; S-band Normal, Mode, PCM, to PCM. Over.

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0295800-pao.text: Roger. We're switching over to backup now.

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0295800-pao.text: We're reading you loud and clear, Houston. [Long pause.]

a08_0295800-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0295800-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Requesting S-band Normal, Mode, Ranging, to Ranging. I say again, S-band Normal, Mode, Ranging to Range. Over.

a08_0295830.speaker: Collins
a08_0295830.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Three communication switch positions. First, S-band, Aux, Tape, to Down-Voice Backup; S-band Normal, Mode, PCM, Off; Telemetry Inputs PCM, High. I say again, S-band, Aux, Tape, to Down-Voice Backup; S-band Normal, Mode, PCM to Off; Telemetry Inputs PCM to High.

a08_0295830.speaker: Anders
a08_0295830.text: Roger. Houston, this is Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0295830.speaker: Collins
a08_0295830.text: Reading you weak but clear now, Bill.

a08_0295830.speaker: Anders
a08_0295830.text: Roger. We still have a bad look angle on this antenna. [Pause.]

a08_0295830.speaker: Lovell
a08_0295830.text: Please be informed that the [garble]. Over.

a08_0295830.speaker: Collins
a08_0295830.text: Apollo 8. Houston. Unable to copy. After about a minute of this configuration, we're going to return to normal voice, and at that time, we should be able to hear you better.

a08_0295830.speaker: Borman
a08_0295830.text: Roger. What [garble] are we going through right now? [Long pause.]

a08_0295830.speaker: Collins
a08_0295830.text: Roger. We are in Mode 7-10, and the comm test mode's on page 223. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0295830.speaker: Collins
a08_0295830.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Three switch positions. Telemetry Inputs PCM switch to Low; S-band Normal, Mode, Voice, to Voice; S-band Normal, Mode, PCM, to PCM. I say again, Telemetry Inputs PCM switch, Low; S-band Normal, Mode, Voice, to Voice; S-band Normal, Mode, PCM, to PCM. Over.

a08_0295830.speaker: Borman
a08_0295830.text: Roger. We're switching over to backup now.

a08_0295830.speaker: Anders
a08_0295830.text: We're reading you loud and clear, Houston. [Long pause.]

a08_0295830.speaker: Collins
a08_0295830.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Requesting S-band Normal, Mode, Ranging, to Ranging. I say again, S-band Normal, Mode, Ranging to Range. Over.

a08_0300450.speaker: Collins
a08_0300450.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Requesting S-band Normal, Mode, Ranging to Ranging. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0300450.speaker: Borman
a08_0300450.text: Houston, Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0300450.speaker: Collins
a08_0300450.text: Beautiful, Frank. I'm reading you loud and clear. How me? [Long pause.]

a08_0300450.speaker: Collins
a08_0300450.text: Apollo 8, Houston. How do you read? Over. [No answer.]

a08_0300450.speaker: Collins
a08_0300450.text: Apollo 8. this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0300450.speaker: Collins
a08_0300450.text: Roger. Reading you loud and clear. How me?

a08_0300450.speaker: Collins
a08_0300450.text: Okay. We're still looking for the S-band, Normal, Mode, Ranging to Ranging.

a08_0300450.speaker: Borman
a08_0300450.text: I guess we didn't hear that one. Going to Ranging.

a08_0300450.speaker: Borman
a08_0300450.text: And Houston, Apollo 8. What size antenna are you going through now?

a08_0300450.speaker: Collins
a08_0300450.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're working through Ascension, a 30-footer. Over.

a08_0300450.speaker: Borman
a08_0300450.text: Okay. 'Cause we - our signal strength is - or our AGC is pretty low up here.

a08_0300932.speaker: Collins
a08_0300932.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Requesting S-band Aux, Tape to Off. This should put us back in the normal configuration. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0300932.speaker: Collins
a08_0300932.text: Okay. S-band Aux, Tape to Off. That returns us to normal configuration, and we need a couple of items from you. First, the CMP and LMP status report, including PRD readings on all three crew members, and we'd like to know, did you chlorinate the water after your last meal? Over.

a08_0300932.speaker: Borman
a08_0300932.text: No, we haven't chlorinated the water, yet. We'll get the other for you.

a08_0300932.speaker: Anders
a08_0300932.text: Houston, do you show our FM - Houston, Apollo 8. Do you show the FM on now?

a08_0300932.speaker: Collins
a08_0300932.text: Stand by and we'll check it, Bill.

a08_0300932.speaker: Anders
a08_0300932.text: Because our S-band Aux, Tape has been Off. Possibly - we don't have control of it. [Long pause.]

a08_0301229.speaker: Collins
a08_0301229.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're showing all the communications switch functions operating normally, Bill.

a08_0301229.speaker: Borman
a08_0301229.text: Mike, the PRD readings for the CDR are 4 - 0.04, for the CMP is 0.64, and for the LMP is 0.25.

a08_0302229.speaker: Borman
a08_0302229.text: Oh, hi, Ken. How're you doing?

a08_0302229.speaker: Borman
a08_0302229.text: Hey, listen, we still have this TV coming up here - let's see - 31:20?

a08_0302229.speaker: Borman
a08_0302229.text: We're about in the right position for High Gain; we wondered if you wanted to take a trial run and see if it will work. Or do you just want to wait and try it when they're supposed to go on the air with it? [Pause.]

a08_0303025.speaker: Anders
a08_0303025.text: Roger. Could you ask the GNC to give us an update on our prop[ellant] quantity, please?

a08_0303025.speaker: Anders
a08_0303025.text: If you'll give it to me kinda slow, I'll plot it.

a08_0303513.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0303513.text: Okay. In reference [to] the early TV, we're losing the High Gain Antenna now, and it looks like the only way we would have gotten the early TV pass in anyhow was to send it to [a] remote site and look at it there. So we're going to scrub that idea and we'll just pick up with the scheduled TV. The comm checks that are remaining are the High Gain dependent type, and we'll put those off until the TV session is completed, and we're working on the fuel propellant curve for you now.

a08_0304150.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0304150.text: Okay, Apollo 8. What we're going to do on the TV is to go ahead and let you crank it up as soon as we get back on the High Gain Antenna, and it looks like - our guess is that this will be about 31:07, and we'll just use this to - as long as we have the coverage there. I have an update to your TLI plus 35 PAD. We have to correct a couple of times on there. So when you get that out, let me know and I'll read it to you. [Pause.]

a08_0304150.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0304150.text: Okay. On the TLI plus 35 PAD, the update I want to give you is the last three lines in the block: the EMS range to go, 1308.4, 35985, 098:42:17. Over.

a08_0304454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0304454.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're about to have a handover to Goldstone, and our downlink should improve then. I don't know if you'll notice any difference in the uplink or not. [Long pause.]

a08_0304454.speaker: Borman
a08_0304454.text: Go ahead, Houston. You are loud and clear.

a08_0304454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0304454.text: Okay. We've switched sites over to Goldstone now. I don't know if you can tell any difference in our uplink.

a08_0304454.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0304454.text: Okay. You have cleared up quite a bit. Sounds a lot better to us.

a08_0304935.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0304935.text: Okay. I've got some RCS quantity data for you. And we are all set up to receive the TV whenever you get the High Gain [Antenna] looking at us. [Expected to be in about 16 minutes.]

a08_0304935.speaker: Borman
a08_0304935.text: Okay. Let me get the [RCS Propellant usage] chart out here. [Long pause.]

a08_0304935.speaker: Borman
a08_0304935.text: Go ahead with the quad propellant quantities, please.

a08_0304935.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0304935.text: Okay, Apollo 8, Alpha, I have 225 pounds, 74 percent; Bravo, 240...

a08_0304935.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0304935.text: Rog. I'll repeat, Alpha, 225, 74 percent; Bravo, 240 pounds, 79 percent; Charlie 236, 78 percent; Delta, 238, 79 percent. Like to remind you on the TV that we need the narrow beamwidth when you get on the High Gain. Over.

a08_0310500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0310500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 31 hours, 5 minutes into the mission. We're standing by at this time to receive the first television transmission from the spacecraft. Now there is a certain element of uncertainty just as to when that signal will be received at the station at Goldstone and transmitted to Houston. Now the spacecraft at the present time is in a slow roll as part of the Passive Thermal Control program to maintain temperatures, and as soon as the High Gain Antenna is in the proper position, we expect to begin getting pictures. So we'll stand by and pick up the picture as soon as we have

a08_0310500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0310500-pao.text: At this time our estimate is that it will be about one minute before we pick up our TV transmission.

a08_0310500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0310500-pao.text: When we begin this television transmission, the spacecraft will be at a range from Earth of about 120,623 nautical miles [223,393 km], and will be traveling at a velocity of about 4,668 feet per second [1,423 m/s]. We're still standing by to receive the first indications that a picture is about to come through. We now estimate about 15 more seconds. As I've said before, there could be some variation in that depending on the position of the High Gain Antenna.

a08_0310500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0310500-pao.text: And we've gotten a call from the crew. We'll pick that up and then stand by for pictures.

a08_0310500-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0310500-pao.text: Houston, how do you read? Apollo 8.

a08_0310500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0310500-pao.text: That sounded like Bill Anders putting in a call to the Control Center here. We still do not have pictures. We'll continue to monitor.

a08_0310500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0310500-pao.text: We are getting a good signal through from Goldstone, but we still have not received any video from the spacecraft. We'll continue to monitor and also to monitor the audio loops for any conversations from the crew.

a08_0310718.speaker: Borman
a08_0310718.text: Houston, how do you read? Apollo 8.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Apollo 8. Loud and clear and standing by.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Say again.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: We read you loud and clear, and we're standing by.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Are you receiving television now? [Long pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We just got it.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: You are getting it? [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We have a good picture.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: We're rolling a...

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Okay. We're rolling around to a good view of the Earth, and as soon as we get to the good view of the Earth, we'll stop and let you look out the window at the scene we see. Jim Lovell's down in Lower Equipment Bay preparing lunch, and Bill is holding a camera here for us both. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Bill's going to take the camera down to the Lower Equipment deck with Jim:

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Rog.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay. We're getting a pretty good picture, but if you'd move it a little slower - every time you move it around, why, it breaks up on the scan.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: We gotcha.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: [Laughter.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Lovell
a08_0310957.text: This is known as preparing lunch and doing P23 at the same time. [Long pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: You've got everybody standing on their heads down here.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: How go - Has he got it turned upside down? You've got the wrong REFSMMAT.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Well, we all have our problems. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: How's the picture now, Houston?

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: That's really good. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Okay. Now we're coming up on the view that we really want you to see. That's the view of the Earth, and if you'll break for just a minute, Bill's going to put on the large lens. So we will be right back with you.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Houston, we're now showing you a view of the Earth through the telephoto lens.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay. We're not receiving a picture right now. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: How about now? [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay. We don't have a picture yet. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: You seeing anything at all, Houston? [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We don't have a picture yet.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Alright. We'll put the other lens back on, and we will show you that.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Apollo 8, how about standing by on that for just a minute. Let's check our ground link. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Apollo 8, we have a picture now.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Okay. Let's try that other lens again then, once again.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Do you have a picture now?

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: That's negative. [Long pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Apollo 8 - belay that.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Okay, now, do you have anything. Houston? We have it on the Earth.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: We're having no joy.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay. Stand by.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Okay. How about now, Houston?

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Still no joy. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: You don't have a lens cover on there, do you?

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: No, we checked that, as a matter of fact. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Anything?

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Still no joy. [Long pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: How about now?

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Still no joy.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: That's the Earth, but it is not the telephoto lens, unfortunately. It is just a regular inside lens.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay. It's coming in as a real blight - a real bright blob on the screen. It is hard to tell what we're looking at.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: You are looking through some haze on the window too, unfortunately.

a08_0310957.speaker: Lovell
a08_0310957.text: And the Earth is very bright, besides.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay. We've got the Earth in about the center of the screen and a little bit low, and it looked like there were some objects that moved across it - the screen at the same time. Do you have any comment on those?

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: That's some water - some water ice coming off the vent nozzle.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: How does it look now?

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Still the same thing; it is - the target is extremely bright, and it is very difficult to make out what we're looking at.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: It is unfortunate that we don't have - we can't make the other lens work here. I don't know what the problem is.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay. Apollo 8, would you verify that the ALC is on?

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: We've tried it both ways.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay; thank you. What we are getting now is a good picture.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Say again. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Okay. That's a - that's a real good picture. That's the best one that we've had. And how about just going and leaving your pictures inside until we can think some more of what we can do to adjust for that light?

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Roger. Jim, what are you doing here? Jim is fixing dessert. He's making up a bag of chocolate pudding. You can see it come floating by. Bill's coming up from the Lower Equipment Bay. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: This transmission is coming to you approximately halfway between the Moon and the Earth. We've been 31 hours and about 20 minutes into flight. We have about less than 40 hours left to go to the Moon. You can see Bill's got his toothbrush here. He's been brushing his teeth regularly. To demonstrate how things float around in zero g. It looks like he plays for the Astros, the way he tries to catch that thing. [Pause.] I certainly wish that we could show you the Earth. It's a beautiful, beautiful view, with predominantly blue background and just huge covers of white clouds, particularly one very

a08_0310957.speaker: Anders
a08_0310957.text: Houston, did you get any light at all coming through that telephoto lens?

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Apollo 8, we were getting what you're showing us on your normal lens, and I don't think we got anything on the telephoto. We're working on this now. One of the problems seems to be that it's a low light level lens; we're afraid that you may burn it out pointing it at something that's too bright.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Well, the Earth is very, very bright. There's nothing in the lens you can burn out. The camera still seems to be working. We can give you a lumens reading of the Earth right now if you'd like. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Hey, Frank, how about a couple of words on your health for the wide world.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Well, we are all in very good shape. Jim is busy working preparing lunch. Bill is playing cameraman right now, and I'm about to take a light reading on the Earth. We all feel fine. It was a very exciting ride on that big Saturn, but it worked perfectly, and we're looking forward now, of course, to the day after tomorrow when we will be just 60 miles away from the Moon.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Rog. You all look great on candid TV [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Okay. I just got a reading on the Earth, Houston. It's 320. The Earth is showing 320 lumens now. [Pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Lovell
a08_0310957.text: Happy birthday, Mother. [Long pause.]

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Okay. Jim's going to take a shot of us from the Lower Equipment Bay, and then we have to get back to our Passive Thermal Control in the barbecue mode so that we don't get one side of the spacecraft too hot for too long at a time. So we will be signing off here, and looking forward to seeing you all again shortly.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Roger.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Goodbye from Apollo 8.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Thank you. That's a good show.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: I hope we get that other lens fixed or some reading on it.

a08_0310957.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0310957.text: Rog. We're going to work on that one then. The one that is sensitive to light is the lens you are just using, so you want to be careful about pointing that at some bright object.

a08_0310957.speaker: Borman
a08_0310957.text: Rog. We're starting PTC again.

a08_0310957.speaker: Anders
a08_0310957.text: I believe that's only if it hasn't been used for quite a while, Ken.

a08_0311350-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0311350-pao.text: And we momentarily lose our picture while this lens change is in progress. We'll stand by for that shot of Earth.

a08_0311350-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0311350-pao.text: Houston, we're now showing you a view of the Earth through the telephoto lens.

a08_0311350-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0311350-pao.text: Okay. We're not receiving a picture right now. [Pause.]

a08_0312400-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0312400-pao.text: Thank you. That's a good show.

a08_0312400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0312400-pao.text: And we've had our picture cut off now after that television transmission. Total duration of some 20 minutes. And during that TV transmission, we got some very enthusiastic comments from the crew on the view from some 120,000 miles [220,000 km] from Earth. Borman described the Earth as very beautiful, looking blue, covered with white clouds, and he also reported that all three crewmen at this point are in very good shape and all feel fine. At 31 hours, 24 minutes into the mission; this is Apollo Control.

a08_0312400-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0312400-pao.text: I hope we get that other lens fixed or some reading on it.

a08_0312400-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0312400-pao.text: Rog. We're going to work on that one then. The one that is sensitive to light is the lens you are just using, so you want to be careful about pointing that at some bright object.

a08_0313900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0313900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 31 hours, 39 minutes into the mission. At the present time we've completed the shift change here in Mission Control. Flight Director Milton Windler has relieved Clifford Charlseworth and our Capsule Communicator is astronaut Ken Mattingly. This is a relatively quite period in the Flight Plan. It's a sleep period for Commander Frank Borman, and we do not have any significant activities listed for the other two crewmen until some 33 hours, 30 minutes into the mission. Just about two hours before any significant crew activies are scheduled in the Flight Plan. We

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: Go ahead Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: Okay, I've got a few items for you I'd like to clear up and then we'll let you alone for a while. The first thing is we'd like for you to confirm that your spotmeter had an ASA setting of 100.

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: That's confirmed.

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: Okay, thank you. That was one of the first questions that came to mind. We're ready for a cryo fan cycle at any time and use your normal procedures.

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: Okay.

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: Alright. You can anticipate a fuel cell purge at 35 hours, and we ought to be through with battery A charging somewhere after 34 hours; and looks like you'll have just about a full battery there. And we'll give you a call on the exact time to cut it off. We'd like to get some confirmation from you on the chlorine procedures. Did you get some in last night or not? And just a quick summary of how much sleep you got on Lovell and Anders?

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: Okay. We got the chlorine in and the water has been chlorinated and, just a minute I will check with them on their sleep. [Pause.]

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: I'm sorry, I didn't copy that sleep.

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: Say again, Ken.

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: I'm sorry I didn't copy your last, Frank.

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: I was asking you to say to say what you said. Jim had about 4 hours sleep, and Bill had about 3 hours sleep.

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: We feel pretty good today. We'd like to see, in looking over the Flight Plan, perhaps we ought to put the rest periods a little bit shorter and more frequent. It seems it might work out better. We got all out of kilter on it yesterday, and we're sort of trying to get back in a normal cycle.

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: Okay. We'll look into that. [Pause.]

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: Y'all are doing good work. Keep it up.

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: Okay. Thank you. Looks like the only other thing we've got left over is a comm check and if we can work that in without interrupting your present schedule, we'd like to.

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: Okay. Right now we're stopping for a break, but we'll go ahead and do that. What does it involve?

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: Okay. We'll need the High Gain Antenna, and there should be no comm loss during this mode. [Pause.]

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: Okay. Ken. I think we're going to lose the High Gain here shortly. Why don't we pick it up next time it comes around?

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: Real fine.

a08_0314004.speaker: Borman
a08_0314004.text: Remember, the most important part of the trip occurs in two days when we start back. So you all get better rested too.

a08_0314004.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0314004.text: We'll do that.

a08_0315241.speaker: Borman
a08_0315241.text: Houston, we're starting the H 2 fans now. [Pause.]

a08_0315448.speaker: Borman
a08_0315448.text: Houston, you just wanted 2 minutes cycling on those fans don't you? Two minutes each? [Pause.]

a08_0315700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0315700-pao.text: That brings up to date with the communications with the spacecraft at present. At this time, it is quiet. We've had no further communications with the crew. We expect that it will remain quiet probably for the next hour or two. At the present time, Apollo 8 is at an altitude of 123,768 nautical miles [229,218 km], and our current velocity reading here in Mission Control is 4,568 feet per second [1,392 m/s]. I believe this is in conflict with a figure given earlier on the velocity in our previous announcement. I recall the velocity as being reported at about 4,400 feet per second. I would like

a08_0321126.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0321126.text: Okay. Apollo 8. Looks like we're going to have to put this comm test off because of some tracking requirements. We can do it in about an hour if this will not interfere with your present operations too much. It'll take maybe 15 to 20 minutes, and it will involve some conversation on the part of the people on board the spacecraft. So if that's going to interfere with your sleeping and all, why go ahead and we'll defer to that and we'll pick these requirements up at another time. And, I've got a score here, looks like Baltimore 21 to nothing.

a08_0321126.speaker: Lovell
a08_0321126.text: How did last year's Army-Navy game come out?

a08_0321400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0321400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 32 hours, 14 minutes into the flight now. Apollo 8 is currently at an altitude of 124,506 nautical miles [230,585 km], traveling at a speed of 4,546 feet per second [1,386 m/s]. And we are in touch with the spacecraft at this time. We'll pick up communication and follow it along as it develops.

a08_0321400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0321400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, we don't appear to have any more conversations developing with the spacecraft. A check with the Flight Dynamics Officer here in Mission Control Center indicates that the spacecraft will continue to decelerate until about 55 hours, 38 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. At that point, our estimate is that it will come into the Moon's sphere of influence or perhaps more accurately the Moon's gravitational attraction will become the dominant force acting on the spacecraft, and the spacecraft will begin to accelerate again. At this point its altitude will be about 176,000 nautical

a08_0322247.speaker: Anders
a08_0322247.text: Roger. We've stirred up all the cryos. Could you give me your quantities, please?

a08_0322247.speaker: Anders
a08_0322247.text: Roger. Be advised the CMP just hit the hay for a while, and the LMP will go down in a little while.

a08_0322247.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0322247.text: Okay. And our guys down here are watching [the] High Gain Antenna pointing program, so anytime you're not using the DSKY for anything else, they'd like to watch it for a couple of cycles, so if you would leave that Noun 51 on the display, why, it'll help a lot down here.

a08_0322247.speaker: Anders
a08_0322247.text: Okay. Why don't you give us Reacq[uire] angles, and we'll try that for the next time. [Pause.]

a08_0322247.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0322247.text: Apollo 8, are you ready to copy some cryo quantities?

a08_0322247.speaker: Anders
a08_0322247.text: I'm ready. How about O 2 first.

a08_0322247.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0322247.text: Okay. O 2 tank 1, I show 88.1 percent.

a08_0322247.speaker: Anders
a08_0322247.text: Okay. Could you give it to me in pounds, please?

a08_0322247.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0322247.text: Okay. You'll have to stand by while we convert that.

a08_0322247.speaker: Anders
a08_0322247.text: That's okay, Ken. Go ahead, I'll take percent.

a08_0322247.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0322247.text: Okay. We'll try and get the pounds for you, too, Bill. Tank 1, oxygen 88.1.

a08_0322247.speaker: Anders
a08_0322247.text: Okay, thank you very much. It looks good.

a08_0322800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0322800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 32 hours, 28 minutes. We're in communication with the spacecraft at this time. We'll bring you up to date with a tape recording on the earlier portion of the conversation and then pick it up live.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0324003.speaker: Borman
a08_0324003.text: Go ahead, Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Okay. I've got a couple of things we need from you. I'd like to get a battery C voltage. I'd like to check a battery manifold pressure. Your High Gain...

a08_0324003.speaker: Borman
a08_0324003.text: Battery C is 37 volts.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Understand 37 volts on battery C. Is that affirm?

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Okay, thank you. And if you can get to the battery manifold pressure, like to read that one.

a08_0324003.speaker: Borman
a08_0324003.text: 0.6 volts

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Alright understand 0.6 volts. The angles you asked for on the High Gain Antenna are pitch, minus 45; and yaw, 90. [Long pause.]

a08_0324003.speaker: Borman
a08_0324003.text: Okay. Houston, this is Apollo 8. I'm going to just go into High Gain now. We're about ready to pick you up. We'll get this thing works on Reacq.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Okay, and I have a scanning telescope star visibility item for you to pick up, when you're ready to copy that.

a08_0324003.speaker: Borman
a08_0324003.text: Roger, we'll get that on High Gain when we get back to you.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Okay, thank you.

a08_0324003.speaker: Borman
a08_0324003.text: We'll come back on High Gain.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0324003.speaker: Borman
a08_0324003.text: That's not fair, we're there already.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: That's pretty good acquisition, huh?

a08_0324003.speaker: Borman
a08_0324003.text: You guys are reading the DSKY. Go ahead Houston.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Okay, Apollo 8. Maybe we ought to try that one again next time, and the scanning telescope star visibility is scheduled for 34:10 in the Flight Plan, and it'll be star number 31. The angles are roll, 184.7; pitch, 23.4; yaw, 14.3; shaft and trunnion zero. Over.

a08_0324003.speaker: Borman
a08_0324003.text: Understand; star 31; roll, 184.7; pitch, 23.4; yaw, 14.3; and star shaft and trunnion, zero.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: That's affirm, and that's copy star 31.

a08_0324003.speaker: Borman
a08_0324003.text: That's Roger, 31.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Okay, thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0324003.speaker: Anders
a08_0324003.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Go ahead.

a08_0324003.speaker: Anders
a08_0324003.text: The LMP would like to take a Seconal and hit the hay. [Pause.]

a08_0324003.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0324003.text: Okay. That's a Go.

a08_0324003.speaker: Anders
a08_0324003.text: Okay, thank you. [Pause.]

a08_0324500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0324500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 40 - rather 32 hours, 45 minutes. At the present time the spacecraft is at an altitude of 125,723 nautical miles [232,838 km], traveling at a speed now of 4,509 feet per second [1,374 m/s]. We've been in coversation with the crew for the last couple of minutes. At the present time Lunar Module Pilot Bill Anders and Command Module Pilot Jim Lovell are attempting to get a little bit of sleep. Anders requested a few moments ago that he be given a go ahead to take a Seconal tablet. This is one of the short acting sleeping pills carried aboard the spacecraft, And the medic

a08_0325006.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0325006.text: Okay. We'd like to go ahead and get in this comm check now here, on the last of this High Gain period. If you're ready to go on it, I'll read you some switches.

a08_0325006.speaker: Borman
a08_0325006.text: Stand by. We're ready. Go ahead.

a08_0325006.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0325006.text: Okay. Number 1. S-band Normal, Mode, Voice, to Voice.

a08_0325006.speaker: Borman
a08_0325006.text: Just read them - Just read them all up [garble]. [Pause.]

a08_0325006.speaker: Borman
a08_0325006.text: Normal, Mode, Voice, to Voice; and Uptelemetry Data, to Data.

a08_0325006.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0325006.text: High Gain Antenna, Beamwidth, to Narrow.

a08_0325006.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0325006.text: Okay, this will be our baseline data check. This will be a full uplink voice with ranging and full downlink.

a08_0325753.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0325753.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're going to have to belay the comm check again.

a08_0330109.speaker: Borman
a08_0330109.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0330109.speaker: Borman
a08_0330109.text: Roger. We lost you for a while there. Are you reading us now?

a08_0330109.speaker: Borman
a08_0330109.text: Okay. Thank you. So are we. [Pause.]

a08_0330109.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0330109.text: Okay, Apollo 8. Do you want to try that Auto, Reacq? 33 plus 24 looks like the good time and the angles are the same. And the late ball score is 24 to 14.

a08_0330109.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0330109.text: I say a late ball score there is...

a08_0330556.speaker: Borman
a08_0330556.text: We've reached the scan limit on the High Gain. What do you want us to do about it now? [Long pause.]

a08_0330556.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0330556.text: Apollo 8, what we'd like to do with these angles is to set it in Auto Reacq over on panel 2, and it's under the Tracking for the High Gain Antenna, and it'll - the lower position will say Reacq, and on the position dials, we'd like to set pitch to minus 45 and the yaw to 90.

a08_0330556.speaker: Borman
a08_0330556.text: Roger. If we could leave it in Reacq if you want to use the High Gain, it would keep from waking us up every rev.

a08_0331032.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0331032.text: Apollo 8, Houston. I think we may have gotten off on a tangent. These pitch and yaw angles that we called up to you for the High Gain Antenna were in response to Bill's request to know what positions we could put on there for a - for the Auto Reacq position. The constraint still remains if we don't want to be on an Omni antenna at the same time. We're in the Auto Reacq position; we should be in one or the other. So you can use that information if you want to try it out. Otherwise, the procedures you've been using all along will work just fine. Over.

a08_0331300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0331300-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 33 hours, 13 minutes. At the present time, we're involved in one of a series of communications checks with the spacecraft. We'll pick that up for you at the beginning and continue to monitor live.

a08_0331541.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0331541.text: Apollo 8, Houston. I'm transmitting in the blind right now. Our downlink isn't working so well; I'm just going ahead on an uplink.

a08_0331700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0331700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 33 hours, 17 minutes. At the present time, the spacecraft is at an altitude of 126,969 nautical miles from Earth, traveling at a speed of 4,471 feet per second. We have no further communication with the crew at this time - we'll take the circuit down and stand by to come up again when next we are in touch with the spacecraft. This is Apollo Control at 33 hours, 18 minutes.

a08_0332000.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0332000.text: Apollo 8, read you weak but clear now.

a08_0332000.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0332000.text: Okay. Looks like we had a ground problem there.

a08_0333331.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0333331.text: ...Looks like we're in a good attitude to try this High Gain Antenna on the comm check one more time. I believe you're still on an Omni. Is that correct?

a08_0333331.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0333331.text: Okay. If we could try the High Gain and maybe we can get started on this comm check. Also like to verify that you've got the LMP and the CMP trying to get some sleep here, and we could use an oral temp from you, too.

a08_0333331.speaker: Borman
a08_0333331.text: That's what it was this morning when I felt badly.

a08_0333331.speaker: Borman
a08_0333331.text: Do you want me to go to Omni now, Ken?

a08_0333331.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0333331.text: I'd like for you to go to High Gain.

a08_0333331.speaker: Borman
a08_0333331.text: This is Apollo 8 on the High Gain.

a08_0333331.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0333331.text: Rog. Reading you kind of weak now. We're taking a look at it. [Long pause.]

a08_0333331.speaker: Borman
a08_0333331.text: Houston, Apollo 8 on the High Gain.

a08_0333331.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0333331.text: Okay. I'm reading you loud with just a little background noise.

a08_0333800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0333800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 33 hours, 38 minutes. Spacecraft, at this time, is 128,179 nautical miles [237,387 km] from Earth and our velocity is 4,434 feet per second [1,351 m/s]. We're still involved from time to time with the communications checks with the spacecraft. One of those is in progress at this time and we'll pick up with the beginning and continue to follow it along.

a08_0333924.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0333924.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're not getting a good lock. I wonder if we could try making sure that we're in Auto on the track, and that we're in narrow beamwidth?

a08_0334207.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0334207.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. What we're doing right now is collecting baseline data, and we'll be in this mode for another couple of minutes and then we'll be moving on to the second sequence.

a08_0334355.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0334355.text: Apollo 8, Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a08_0334355.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0334355.text: Okay. We are [garble] we have some ground problems, and we're reading you weak but clear. We're ready to start into our test. We're going to be changing our modes so you'll probably hear a burst of noise as we make the change. This will be a noise that sounds like an S-band unlock. However, your AGC leader will not drop off. This is due to the loss of modulation on the uplink. There will be about 2 minutes, and during this time, you may hear one burst of noise. [Long pause.]

a08_0334355.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0334355.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Voice check. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0334355.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0334355.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Ready to check. [No answer.]

a08_0334355.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0334355.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Do you read?

a08_0334355.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0334355.text: Okay. Thank you. Were you reading all along? We just - This is the first time we've heard you call back.

a08_0334355.speaker: Anders
a08_0334355.text: We've been reading you; we're trying to hold the noise down so we can get some sleep.

a08_0334355.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0334355.text: Rog. We'll be through with this in just a minute, I think.

a08_0334355.speaker: Anders
a08_0334355.text: Roger. I'll answer you, but I'll try to do it quietly.

a08_0334355.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0334355.text: Okay, Apollo 8. The next portion of our test is like we did yesterday. We'll be changing the uplink modes to uplink command and ranging with no upvoice. We'll be in this mode for approximately 2½ minutes and send two test messages. During this time, we will not have uplink. We are going to this mode at time 33:48:30, and we'll be back in this configuration at 33:50. Over.

a08_0335059.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0335059.text: Okay, fine. How about telemetry inputs PCM [Pulse Code Modulation] switch to Low [bit rate], please? [Pause.]

a08_0335059.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0335059.text: Apollo 8, we've completed the third test; we're going into the final test now. PCM switch to High, please. [Long pause.]

a08_0335059.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0335059.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're going to switch uplink to the upvoice backup for about 2 minutes, and may take a few seconds to link the transition. And we'll be back up at 33:56 in our normal mode to place the Uptelemetry Data switch to Upvoice Backup at this time. Over.

a08_0335059.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0335059.text: Apollo 8, let's go back to Uptelemetry Data switch to Data. [Long pause.]

a08_0335059.speaker: MCC
a08_0335059.text: Stand by; guess we've got 85-foot site voice back now; the noise went away.

a08_0335059.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0335059.text: Okay, Apollo 8. That completes our comm test. Thanks for your cooperation. And I've got a change here to Nav sightings that come up at 34:20. And we want to change your star a little bit there. Are you ready to copy?

a08_0335059.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0335059.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We'd like to change the Nav sighting as follows: we'd like to use star 26, that's, two-six; we'd like to make it Earth-near horizon for two sets, two sets. Then we'd like to take star 16 Earth-far horizon, one set. If star 26 Earth-near horizon is not possible, star 16 Earth-far horizon, one set, and star 22 Earth-far horizon, one set. Over.

a08_0335059.speaker: Borman
a08_0335059.text: Roger, Houston. Be advised the CMP is asleep. Wonder if we could put those off for a while.

a08_0335059.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0335059.text: Apollo 8, okay; we can put this off. What we will probably need from you is some kind of an estimate of when you think somebody will be available to work on it, and we're working on how much lead time we need now. [Pause.]

a08_0335059.speaker: Borman
a08_0335059.text: Houston, why don't you figure the CMP will sleep another couple of hours, then the LMP, and then the CDR up to about 43 hours equally. Over.

a08_0335059.speaker: Borman
a08_0335059.text: Then we'll start off with the CMP again at about 44.

a08_0340658.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0340658.text: Okay. We can put off this Nav sighting. It was scheduled here at 34:20, and we can put it off, judging from your comments about sleeping, we would like to get it as soon as we can, and right now, our plans are to slide it 2 hours. We'll do the P52 by sliding it back to the same thing since it is associated with the P23. So if that's a convenient time for you, why, we will plan on that.

a08_0340658.speaker: Borman
a08_0340658.text: We're doing the P52 now. Do you want us to continue?

a08_0340658.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0340658.text: Well, as far as we are concerned, that isn't going to help us any. We will have to do it over again anyhow.

a08_0340658.speaker: Borman
a08_0340658.text: Okay. And what time do you want to do it?

a08_0340658.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0340658.text: Well, if you think Jim's going to be up in a couple of hours, why, that will slide us 2 hours to 36:20.

a08_0340658.speaker: Borman
a08_0340658.text: Okay. We'll go ahead and make another one there and pick it up then if that's okay.

a08_0340658.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0340658.text: Okay. That will be real fine. Thank you.

a08_0340658.speaker: Borman
a08_0340658.text: What we're going to try to do is get back on the sleep cycle to those sleep periods just prior to LOI [Lunar Orbit Insertion] by taking shorter cycles for each man.

a08_0341000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0341000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 34 hours, 10 minutes. As you heard in that conversation with Commander Frank Borman, we will be rescheduling part of the Flight Plan activity in order to allow Jim Lovell to continue sleeping. That is the mid-course navigation activity scheduled to occur between 34 and 35 hours in the Flight Plan. Current plans are to move that back about 2 hours, and do it after Lovell has had a chance to get some rest. Borman also advised that following Lovell's sleep period, Anders would attempt to get a few hours of rest and then he himself would try to get some rest. At 34 hours,

a08_0341352.speaker: Borman
a08_0341352.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Apollo 8, go ahead.

a08_0341352.speaker: Borman
a08_0341352.text: How about giving us some Reacq angles, and we'll stay in Reacq.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Say again, please.

a08_0341352.speaker: Borman
a08_0341352.text: Could you give us some Reacq angles?

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Wilco. [Pause.]

a08_0341352.speaker: Borman
a08_0341352.text: Say again. [Pause.]

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. I hadn't said anything at that time. We're digging some angles out for you now. In reference to your earlier question about the sleep cycle juggling and so forth: we agree with your comment. We would like to get back on the Flight Plan as far as the sleep cycles and so forth are concerned by the time we get into lunar orbit. So we'd like for you to use your own judgment about the most efficient way to accommodate the sleep cycles and proportion it up amonst yourselves. We would like to have you keep us informed of who's doing what and what your plans are. We have the

a08_0341352.speaker: Borman
a08_0341352.text: Okay, Houston. The CMP will be up at 36 hours. The LMP's going to sleep now, and he'll sleep through 'til 40 and then I'll stagger that in and try to go to sleep around 30 to 37 so that by the time we get to day 3 we'll all be back on the same direct sleep cycle.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Okay, real fine. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Reacq angles look like minus 45 in pitch, plus 90 in yaw, and 34:23 for the time.

a08_0341352.speaker: Borman
a08_0341352.text: Roger. Copy. This is - we'll use this Reacq because it keeps the Caution and Warning from going off again.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Roger. I understand that. Are you leaving the High Gain Antenna on after it swings over to the reset position?

a08_0341352.speaker: Borman
a08_0341352.text: Do you have any reason for us to use the High Gain Antenna?

a08_0341352.speaker: Flight
a08_0341352.text: EECOM, do we need that, really, very much.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Stand by.

a08_0341352.speaker: Flight
a08_0341352.text: Why, why can we just not use the High Gain Antenna for a while? [Pause.] Getting high bit rate on the Omnis. Okay, let's tell them that we'll just not worry about the Omni for a while. [Pause.] FIDO, you going to do... [Long pause.]

a08_0341352.speaker: Anders
a08_0341352.text: Houston, this is the LMP. Before I hit the sack, could you give me a rundown on our systems the way you see them?

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Okay, we'll put that together for you and we were just talking about the redundant ECS components check and we were going to put that off until everybody's had a chance to get some sleep. Trying to keep you from having to go under the left-hand couch.

a08_0341352.speaker: Anders
a08_0341352.text: Oh, that would be nice. I sent Lovell under the couch, though. [Long pause.] I've got one man sleeping under the left couch here - right couch and one man sleeping on our right couch.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Okay. I understand you've got one under and one on the right couch.

a08_0341352.speaker: Anders
a08_0341352.text: Roger. That's affirm.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Okay. And in reference to the Omni versus the High Gain, it looks like we can live with the Omni antennas here for several more hours, if you would like to delete the use of the High Gain. [Long pause.]

a08_0341352.speaker: Anders
a08_0341352.text: Okay. Goodnight, Houston.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Okay. Before you pitch your eyeballs there, we'd like to terminate the battery charge.

a08_0341352.speaker: Anders
a08_0341352.text: I knew you guys would get me.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Gotcha. [Pause.]

a08_0341352.speaker: Anders
a08_0341352.text: Okay. The battery A charge is terminated at 37.3 volts.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Okay. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0341352.speaker: Anders
a08_0341352.text: Standing by for your systems status.

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Okay. We're pulling that together now.

a08_0341352.speaker: Anders
a08_0341352.text: How are the PU (Propellant Utilization) valve and SPS (Service Propulsion System) line temps looking?

a08_0341352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0341352.text: Okay, I'll check that.

a08_0341352.speaker: Anders
a08_0341352.text: We just had [garble] I understand.

a08_0342300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0342300-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 34 hours, 23 minutes. In the past few minutes, we've been in conversation with the spacecraft, Frank Borman and Lunar Module Pilot Bill Anders. Bill advised that he was preparing to join Jim Lovell in getting a little bit of sleep, and Frank Borman advised that when one of the two wakes up a little later on, he'll try and get a few hours of rest, also. We'll play back the tape of that conversation and then continue to follow any conversation live.

a08_0342553.speaker: Anders
a08_0342553.text: Systems look okay to you, Houston? [Long pause.]

a08_0342553.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0342553.text: Okay, Apollo 8. All the systems - giving a quick look around the room - look real fine. You've gotten an RCS quad update on the quantity, so you have that information. The SPS oxidizer feed line temperature and the fuel temperature are both at 73 degrees. The cryo profile is running right on the line: Battery A - our calculations have 39.63 amp hours. Battery B, 37.94, and battery Charlie, 38.46. The comm continues to be running ahead of predictions in quality and circuit margins. Everything else looks like it's real fine.

a08_0342553.speaker: Anders
a08_0342553.text: Rog. Do you expect to have a low bit rate voice on the DSE off the Omnis at lunar distances? [Pause.]

a08_0342553.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0342553.text: That's negative on DSE of the Omnis. Not looking forward to that much improvement.

a08_0342553.speaker: Anders
a08_0342553.text: Roger. We need about a 30-foot dish, I figure, here for that [pause] on the spacecraft.

a08_0342553.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0342553.text: Rog. It runs up the fuel required for PTC, though, Bill.

a08_0343300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0343300-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. There are no further communications with the spacecraft at this point, so we'll take the circuit down and stand by. At the present time, Apollo 8 is at an altitude of 130,368 nautical miles [241,441 km], and our velocity is 4,370 feet per second [1,332 m/s]. This is Apollo Control at 34 hours, 33 minutes into the mission.

a08_0343936.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0343936.text: Okay. I know you're trying to be quiet, so I'll just read up some information to you. One of the things that we just turned up that might give you some confidence, is if you lose [one] oxygen cryo tank now: you have 80 pounds remaining now at CM/SM sep. The limiting factor on single tank operation right now is the hydrogen tank which has a positive margin at CM/SM sep, assuming our standard profile gives you about 143 hours. So it looks like you're over the hill on those.

a08_0343936.speaker: Borman
a08_0343936.text: Roger. We are flying PTC, and I was wondering why it was going out of the deadband; now I know. Thank you.

a08_0343936.speaker: Borman
a08_0343936.text: That's what happens when you let Anders fly. [Long pause.] He's asleep so he can't defend himself.

a08_0343936.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0343936.text: Rog. We've got it on tape though.

a08_0343936.speaker: Borman
a08_0343936.text: Good. [Pause.] They're both conked out; how about just filling me in on some news, and I'll keep quiet just to give me some words on what's going on in the world.

a08_0343936.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0343936.text: Okay. Give me a few minutes to collect some data, and we'll do that.

a08_0345655.speaker: Borman
a08_0345655.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?.

a08_0345655.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0345655.text: Loud and clear, Apollo 8. We haven't forgotten you, it's just, uh ...

a08_0345700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0345700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 34 hours, 57 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. Here in Mission Control Center, Flight Director Milton Windler has just held what he termed a midshift briefing, bringing all of the flight controllers here in the center up to date on the lastest developments as they stand with respect to the overall performance of the spacecraft and the status of the crew. In general, Flight Director Windler noted that the crew feels much better and they have been advised to set their own pace as you've probably heard in the air-to-ground commentary between the ground and th

a08_0345700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0345700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. We'll continue to stand by for any conversation with Frank Borman aboard the spacecraft. In the meantime, we'd also like to perhaps clarify some figures we gave earlier concerning the point at which the spacecraft comes under the dominant influence of the Moon's gravity and begins accelerating toward the Moon. That figure we gave you was a time of - a Ground Elapsed Time of 55 hours, 38 minutes. At that point, the spacecraft velocity, this is inertial velocity with respect to the Earth - is about 3,261 feet per second, and this occurs at an altitude from the Earth of 17

a08_0350920.speaker: Borman
a08_0350920.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0350920.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0350920.text: I'm going to have a maneuver PAD and...

a08_0350920.speaker: Borman
a08_0350920.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0350920.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0350920.text: I read you loud and clear, Apollo. 8. How me? [No answer.]

a08_0350920.speaker: Borman
a08_0350920.text: Hello, Houston. Apollo 8. Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0351220.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351220.text: Apollo 8, Houston. I believe we've lost our uplink. I'm transmitting in the blind. Read you loud and clear. [Long pause.]

a08_0351220.speaker: Borman
a08_0351220.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0351220.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351220.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Read you loud and clear. We may have some uplink problems; transmitting in the blind, at this time. Over.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [No answer.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [No answer.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [No answer.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Comm Tech
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii Network GOSS Conference. How do you read?

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Houston, How do you read? Apollo 8.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8, I read you loud and clear. How me? [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Go ahead, Hawaii M&O. This is the Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: [Unheard by spacecraft] Apollo 8, Houston. Read you loud and clear.

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Okay. Thank you, Hawaii. How do you read?

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Houston Network. Voice check on GOSS Conference.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Houston. GOSS Conference. How do you read? [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Comm Tech
a08_0351530.text: Network voice. Stand by. Okay.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Houston on GOSS Conference. [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Houston Network. GOSS Conference. [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Houston Network, Hawaii Net 2.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Houston on GOSS Conference. How do you read? [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Houston Network, Hawaii.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Houston, Hawaii, this is Houston. Am I on - Am I on your GOSS Conference now?

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: I'm reading you on our Net 2 line.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Okay. That's - that's good. At the present time, Net 2 is being utilized for GOSS Conference [garble].

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: [Garble.] [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Houston. GOSS - Net 2. [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Houston. Net 2.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Houston, Hawaii. Net 2.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, take your carrier down.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii unable to command carrier down. [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Network.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Network, Hawaii.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Roger. Leave your carrier up.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Roger. We'll have to bring it up again.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, do you have your Net 2 patched in to key the Quindars?

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, AOS.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, go for command, CSM. [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Roger.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Okay.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, LOS [Loss of Signal]. Unable to command. [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [No answer.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [No answer.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, this is Houston CapCom. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Houston CapCom, Hawaii.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Houston CapCom. I'd like to have a voice check.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Roger. I read you loud and clear.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Okay. I'm reading you loud and clear. Understand you have contact with the spacecraft. Is that affirm?

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Ah, I have uplink voice to the spacecraft; the downlink is too low in the mud.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Okay. Understand that you have good uplink, but your downlink is in the mud. You don't have any way of copying it either, is that correct?

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Houston, Apollo 8. [Garbled] again. How do you read?

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: That is affirmative.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Okay, Hawaii, we can hear Apollo 8, calling down. Would you answer and tell them that we did copy that?

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Roger.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8, Hawaii M&O. Houston reports they copied your last.

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Okay. Thank you.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Houston Network, GOSS Conference. [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Hawaii, Houston Network, GOSS Conference. You're Net 2.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Houston Network, Hawaii.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Roger. Do you copy the CapCom?

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Affirm. We copied the CapCom.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Is he - is he keying the transmitters out there? [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: He did key it one time, Network.

a08_0351530.speaker: Network
a08_0351530.text: Okay. I'm going to ask him to call the spacecraft again, and I would like for you to give me a report if he does not key the transmitters.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Roger. Network is our - Net 1 now conferenced up as our...

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Your Net - your Net 2 is conferenced to our GOSS Conference here.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Roger. How about our GOSS Conference loop? Is it the [garble].

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Your GOSS Conference loop - your GOSS Conference loop is dead.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: Roger. We are Go for command. We were unable to pass up before.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Understand.

a08_0351530.speaker: Hawaii
a08_0351530.text: We transmitted to the spacecraft as per CapCom and they acknowledged our transmission.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8. Houston.

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Okay. We got back together again. You're loud and clear. We've been reading you. We have a problem down here on the ground getting our signal from MCC out to the remote site. [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Roger. Understand. [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: I'm sorry that that TV - TV lens broke down.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Well, we - we're working on that some more. I'm not sure that the whole thing is lost yet. It appears that our problem is one where the light intensity that's sensed by our light meter in there is picking up an average field which is much larger than the Earth, and so it's sensing a great deal of the deep space environment, which is dark, and we're suspicious that this is probably opening up the lens aperture as wide as it'll go, and then when you point the camera at the Earth, why, the Earth is only filling about 3 degrees of cone angle, whereas lens takes in 9. So it looks like you're probab

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Apollo 8. Houston. I've got a ball score for you. It was Oakland 41, Kansas City 6 is the final score. That's 41 to 6, Oakland. We're trying to get some news releases over for you. I suspect we're going to find that the staged TV show was probably the biggest news of the day.

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: We just lost you again, Houston.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Say again.

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: I just lost your last transmission; you were clipped.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Okay. Did you get any of my comments about the TV tube?

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Roger. Got them.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Okay. What I - what we've got in mind here is that we're looking at some of the lenses you have on board for cameras, and we're going to see if one of them can possibly be used to attenuate some of this light so that you'll be able to take one of these pictures, and we are running some tests now, and we'll let you know about those. I also have a maneuver PAD that I need to read up to you whenever it's convenient.

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Let me get a pencil. Be fine right now.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Okay. The first one I'll give you is a TLI plus 44 maneuver PAD. [Pause.] I'll start reading down the left-hand column. TLI plus 44; SPS/G&N; 62970; minus 1.62, plus 1.29; 046:56:04.31; plus 0019.7, plus all zeros, plus 6070.1; 180, 133, 001; November Alpha, plus 0020.3; 6070.1, 7:04, 60451; 12, 137.5, 34.9. Boresight star is Earth, down 03.7, right 2.2; plus 10.68, minus 165.00; 1285.6, 36118, 098:27:17. The GDC alignment stars: the primary star is Sirius, secondary Rigel; 010, 294, 320; no ullage, fast return P37 Delta-V, 8750. This goes to the Indian Ocean and requires a high-speed procedur

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Okay, Houston. How do you read?

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Loud and clear.

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: TLI plus 44, SPS/G&N; 62970; minus 1.62, plus 1.29; 046:56:04.31; plus 0019.7, plus all zeros, plus 6070.1; 180, 133, 001; [H A omitted] plus 0020.3; plus 6070.1, 7:04, 60451; 12, 137.5, 34.9; Earth, down 03.7, right 2.2; plus 10.68, minus 165; 1285.6, 36118, 098:27:17; Sirius and Rigel. [Pause.] Hello, Houston. How do you read now?

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Loud and clear.

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Sirius and Rigel; 010, 294, 320; no ullage, fast return P37 Delta-V 8750, Indian Ocean minus MA, checklist NC 1.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: That's affirmative, Apollo 8. And I have a flyby PAD for you, also. [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Go ahead.

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Okay. This flyby PAD is an update to one that we gave you yesterday so you might want to note that this is the second one. And it'll be a flyby; SPS/G&N; 62970; minus 1.62, plus 1.29; 060:59:48.07; plus 0096.6, plus 0055.2, minus 0207.9; Roll, pitch, and yaw are all zeros; November Alpha, perigee height plus 0020.2; 0235.8, 0:22, 0228.1; 03, 040.7, 31.7; 013, up 04.7, right 3.9; plus 14.18, minus 165.05; 1290.4, 36160, 146:29:12. Primary star Sirius, secondary Rigel; 136, 310, 340; no ullage; requires realignment to preferred REFSMMAT. This burn will raise perilune to 550 miles. Over. [Long pa

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: Okay. Houston. The second flyby SPS/G&N. Are you with me?

a08_0351530.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0351530.text: Yes sir. [Pause.]

a08_0351530.speaker: Borman
a08_0351530.text: 62970; minus 1.62, plus 1.29; 060:59:48.07; plus 0096.6, plus 0055.2, minus 0207.9. Next three are all zeros; N/A, plus 0020.2; 0235.8, 0:22, 0228.1; 03, 040.70, 31.7; 013, up 04.7, right 3.9; plus 14.18, minus 165.05; plus 1290.4, plus 36160, 146:29:12. Sirius, Rigel; 136, 310, 340; none, requires realignment to preferred REFSMMAT. Pericynthion to 550 miles.

a08_0352200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0352200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 35 hours, 22 minutes into the flight. At the present time, Apollo 8 is 132,542 nautical miles [245,467 km] from Earth, and our velocity is 4,307 feet per second [1,313 m/s]. At this time here in Mission Control Center, we're working on a minor communications problem. We seem to have trouble getting the communications from the Control Center to Hawaii.
