a08_0573200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 57 hours, 32 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. We're in contact with the spacecraft at this time. Bill Anders reports that both Frank Borman and Jim Lovell are sleeping at the present time. And we've passed up some preliminary information to the crew on the midcourse correction that they'll be performing at 61 hours into the flight. We'll bring you up to date with the tape on the early part of that conversation, then stand by for any live communication with the spacecraft.

a08_0573200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0573200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. It appears that we have no more communication with Bill Anders during this period. We would also judge that the crew is following the advice of the ground given out yesterday that they set their own pace and sleep when they feel they need it. As you heard, Anders reports both Borman and Lovell are sleeping at the present time. Apollo 8 is continuing now to accelerate toward the Moon. Our current velocity reading is 4,018 feet per second [1,225 m/s]. That's up about 10 feet per second [3 m/s] in velocity in the past 30 minutes. And our current altitude now stands at 29,0

a08_0573200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0573200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 58 hours into the flight of Apollo 8. We've had no communications with the spacecraft since our last report, and here in Mission Control, this has also been rather quiet. At the present time, the spacecraft is at an altitude of 28,225 nautical miles from the Moon and the velocity reads 4,024 feet per second. Coming up in just a little under 3 hours, we have a midcourse correction maneuver scheduled. This is listed as midcourse correction number 4 in the Flight Plan and will actually be the second midcourse correction on route to the Moon. Midcourse corrections 2 and 3

a08_0580638.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0580638.text: Okay, Bill. I guess I want to belay my last about the - using the onboard state vector for MCC-4. After looking at it some more on the ground, they've got to get going on making their PADs and doing all their computations, and rather than put it off or do it twice, we're going to go ahead and go with the procedures we've been using all along.

a08_0580638.speaker: Anders
a08_0580638.text: Okay. With reference to the midcourse, I think that's generally agreed upon, that we do it like we've always been doing it. Now, with respect to the windows, center window's essentially usable. The two side windows are - may be alright for observation, and the problem with the rendezvous windows is they're pretty small. Kind of thought we'd just have to play the window game by ear almost. Not really sure what capability we're going to have but we'll give you some more thoughts on this later.

a08_0580638.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0580638.text: Okay. How about exercising the idea of rolling over and having Jim do his polarization through the telescope because if we have to change attitudes we'd like to go ahead and start thinking about what effects that'll have on such things as antenna orientation and all that.

a08_0580638.speaker: Anders
a08_0580638.text: Okay. We'll, I'll mention it to him when they wake up.

a08_0581200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0581200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 58 hours, 12 minutes. We've just been in touch with the spacecraft and received a status report from Bill Anders on the condition of the spacecraft windows at this time. We'll play back that conversation for you and then stand by briefly for any further communications with the spacecraft.

a08_0581200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0581200-pao.text: And it appears that we'll have no further communication at this time with Bill Anders aboard the spacecraft. We're continuing to monitor the velocity and altitude of Apollo 8 as it approaches the Moon. At the present time, our velocity reading is 4,030 feet per second [1,228 m/s] and we're at an altitude above the Moon of 27,575 nautical miles [51,069 km]. Our predictions in Mission Control Center are that the velocity will, of course, continue to accelerate as we approach the Moon rather slowly for the next 7 hours or so. We anticipate that by about 65 hours, the velocity will be somewhere ar

a08_0583034.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0583034.text: Okay. Apollo 8, we'd like to update your CMC clock. This is not to correct errors which we have now but just to make up for some effects that we're going to have in lunar orbit. And what we'd like to have you do is go to P00 and Accept and let us update the clock time.

a08_0583034.speaker: Anders
a08_0583034.text: Okay. You got P00 and Accept.

a08_0583700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0583700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 58 hours, 37 minutes. At the present time, our spacecraft velocity is 4,037 feet per second [1,230 m/s] and we are at an altitude now of 26,764 nautical miles [49,567 km] above the Moon. We had one rather brief conversation with Bill Anders in the past 15 minutes or so and have not heard from the spacecraft since. During that conversation, we passed up to the spacecraft an update to the computer driven clock aboard the spacecraft and that pretty much summarized the content of that communication. We'll play that back for you now, and then pick up live with conversation

a08_0583807.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0583807.text: Okay. We're completed with the clock update, and the computer's yours.

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Houston. Apollo 8. Go ahead.

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: Okay. We'd like to update CMC. The order that we'll update will be the LM state vector, the CSM state vector, and the external Delta-V and the REFSMMAT. So any time you're free with it, we can have P00 and Accept; we'll go ahead with it. [Pause.]

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Roger. Understand you're going to update LM state vector, CSM state vector, external Delta-V and the REFSMMAT.

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: That's affirmative. And I'll have one, two, three PAD's to read to you.

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Stand by. Okay. You've got P00 and Accept.

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: Okay, thank you. And just a minute, I'll be with you on the PAD's. They'll be three minute maneuver PAD's, one of them MCC-4.

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. We're ready to copy, if you read.

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: Okay. Stand by one, though.

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Okay. I thought maybe we'd lost comm here for a second.

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: No, I'm just behind. [Long pause.]

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: Okay. Apollo 8, let me read you midcourse correction number 4. [Pause.]

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Okay.

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: Alright. Midcourse correction number 4: the RCS/G&N; 62888; November Alpha, November Alpha; 060:59:54.30; minus 0001.2, minus 0001.1, plus 0001.2; 031, 008, 323; November Alpha, plus 0061.8; 0002.0, 0:11, 0002.0; 17, 296.5, 30.8; Alpha Centauri, up 07.3, left 3.4. [Pause.] For the stars, it will be the primary, Sirius; secondary, Rigel; 129, 155, 010. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Roger. MCC-4, RCS/G&N; 62888; N/A, N/A; 060:59:54.30; minus 0001.2, minus 0001.1, plus 0001.2; 031, 008, 323; N/A. Are you with me so far?

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: Keep going.

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Plus 0061.8; 0002.0, 0:11, 0002.0; 17, 296.5, 30.8; Alpha Centauri, up 07.3, left 3.4; primary, Sirius; secondary, Rigel; 129, 155, 010. Over.

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: That's correct, Apollo 8. [Long pause.]

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: And what else have you got?

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: Okay. I've got one for pericynthion plus 2, and it's a minimum Delta-V solution. [Pause.]

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Roger. Ready to copy.

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: Okay. This is pericynthion plus 2. RCS/G&N; 62871; November Alpha, and stand by one. Okay. We'll pick up with a pitch trim and yaw trim of Not Applicable; time, 071:07:22.16; minus 0046.8, plus 0025.4, plus 0018.1; 173, 101, 027; November Alpha, plus 0018.7; 0056.3, 5:15, 0056.3; 01, 316.9, 19.8; 044, down 04.4, left 4.5; plus 11.00, minus 025.00; 1296.7, 36198, 137:01:53; primary, Sirius; secondary, Rigel; 129, 155, 010; four jets plus-X. This assumes execution of midcourse correction number 4 and uses the same alignment as midcourse correction. Over.

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Roger. Pericynthion plus 2, minimum Delta-V; RCS/G&N; 62871; N/A, N/A; 071:07:22.16; minus 0046.8, plus 0025.4, plus 00181; 173, 101, 027; NA, plus 0018.7; 0056.3, 5:15, 0056.3; 01, 316.9, 19.8; 044, down 04.4, left 4.5; plus 11.00, minus 025.00; 1296.7, 36198, 137:01:53; primary, Sirius; secondary, Rigel; 129, 155, 010; four jets plus-X; assumes MCC-4 with same alignment. Over.

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: That's correct, Apollo 8. [Long pause.]

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Confirm that boresight star and SPA are exactly the same number and not typographical error. [Pause.]

a08_0594219.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0594219.text: Rog, Apollo 8. They're checking that. And Apollo 8, the computer is yours. You can take it back.

a08_0594219.speaker: Anders
a08_0594219.text: Roger. Going to Block.

a08_0594600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0594600-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 59 hours, 46 minutes. Capsule Communicator Ken Mattingly has just put in a call to the crew. We'll catch up with the tape and then follow the conversations live.

a08_0595906.speaker: Anders
a08_0595906.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. Do you copy?

a08_0595906.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0595906.text: I do now, loud and clear. I've got one more PAD for you, and the confirmation that those boresight star number and the pitch angle are correct at 44.

a08_0595906.speaker: Anders
a08_0595906.text: Roger. And we're ready to go do our P52 preferred alignment at this time. Are you ready?

a08_0595906.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0595906.text: Okay. This is a pericynthion plus 2 for a fast return. This will be SPS/G&N; 62871; minus 1.61, plus 1.29; 071:06:42.07; plus 4522.4, minus 0621.6, minus 1871.2; 001, 287, 351; November Alpha, plus 0018.7; 4933.6, 6:03, 4911.8; 11, 203.8, 29.6; Earth, up 01.0, right 3.7; plus 14.75, plus 065.00; 1323.9, 36913, 106:09:23; primary star, Sirius; secondary, Rigel; 129, 155, 010; no ullage, assumes execution of midcourse correction 4 and uses the same alignment. The time for MCC-5 for GERU determination, that's Golf Echo Romeo Uniform, this will be a GET of 83:02; use P37 NC-4, steps 1 through 10 a

a08_0601914.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0601914.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Appears that you have maneuvered around the gimbal lock [garble].

a08_0601914.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0601914.text: Okay. Sorry we were late on that answer.

a08_0602000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0602000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. During that series of conversations with the spacecraft, among the numbers passed up to the crew and then verified and read back down from the spacecraft, was the information that will be used for the midcourse correction coming up at 61 hours. That maneuver is scheduled to be an RCS maneuver using the four Reaction Control System jets on the Service Module, each of those having a thrust of about 100 pounds so we'd have a total of 400 pounds of thrust. The burn duration is scheduled for 11 seconds and with that much burn time and that much thrust acting on the weight of

a08_0602000-pao.speaker: Lovell
a08_0602000-pao.text: Well, we stopped and went through coarse align of P52 and then we got fine align, and pick-a-pair, pick Capella, but she drove and didn't get to any place. I didn't pick Capella, and I can't recognize any out there right now. Can I recycle here and go back and pick a pair? [Pause.]

a08_0602120.speaker: Lovell
a08_0602120.text: Well, we stopped and went through coarse align of P52 and then we got fine align, and pick-a-pair, pick Capella, but she drove and didn't get to any place. I didn't pick Capella, and I can't recognize any out there right now. Can I recycle here and go back and pick a pair? [Pause.]

a08_0602527.speaker: Lovell
a08_0602527.text: My plan is to go back into re-enter Program 52 - well, it did not drive to Capella, and I can't recognize it in the scanning telescope. My plan is to go back into recall P52.

a08_0602527.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0602527.text: Apollo 8, can you confirm that you zeroed the optics prior to starting?

a08_0602527.speaker: Lovell
a08_0602527.text: Roger. That's affirmative. We zeroed the optics. [Long pause.]

a08_0602527.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0602527.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You have a Go for a second try in P52 with an Option 3.

a08_0602527.speaker: Lovell
a08_0602527.text: Okay. I now have Aldebaran in the scanning telescope; I might want to call that one instead of Capella.

a08_0602527.speaker: Lovell
a08_0602527.text: I'll see what it comes up with first, though.

a08_0603000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0603000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. We've just now passed the 30-minute mark in the clock counting down to the midcourse correction maneuver, that clock currently reading 28 minutes, 35 seconds until the burn. And at the present time, Apollo 8 is at an altitude of 22,211 nautical miles [41,135 km] above the Moon, traveling at a speed of 4,085 feet per second [1,245 m/s]. We'll continue to stand by for any conversations from the spacecraft or from the ground to the spacecraft.

a08_0603223.speaker: Borman
a08_0603223.text: Houston, Apollo 8. We came up with an unacceptable difference in our stars; we're going to have to recycle.

a08_0603223.speaker: Borman
a08_0603223.text: If we don't get this midcourse in, what will that do to our pericynthion?

a08_0603223.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0603223.text: Apollo 8, Houston. In the event that we don't get this midcourse in, we're still go for an LOI, and it's been suggested you might try Mirfak which is octal 10.

a08_0603223.speaker: Borman
a08_0603223.text: That's the one we're trying now.

a08_0604000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0604000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 60 hours, 40 minutes into the flight; and we're continuing to countdown toward our midcourse correction; now 19 minutes, 57 seconds from that maneuver. And at the present time the crew is somewhat behind in the Flight Plan, and we suspect they are involved in aligning the Inertial Measurement Unit in the Guidance and Navigation equipment. We just heard from the Guidance Officer that it appeared that that operation was proceeding well at this time. We'll continue to follow activities and monitor for any conversation between the ground and the spacecraft.

a08_0604000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0604000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 60 hours, 46 minutes. We're continuing to monitor for conversations between the ground and spacecraft. It's been a very quiet period what with the crew busily involved in getting ready for the midcourse correction maneuver. That burn is scheduled to occur now in 14 minutes and to resummarize, that will be using the spacecraft Reaction Control System thrusters. It'll be an 11-second burn giving us a change in velocity of 2 feet per second. That velocity change will primarily be retrograde slowing the spacecraft down by about 2 feet per second in order to lower the peri

a08_0605150.speaker: Borman
a08_0605150.text: We're all set up and counting down at 8 minutes.

a08_0605150.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0605150.text: Apollo 8, our data is down right now; appreciate making sure you have the tape recorder on. [Pause.]

a08_0605150.speaker: Borman
a08_0605150.text: Roger. I'm going to go - I'll have to go Command Reset. You've got control [of the tape recorder].

a08_0605352.speaker: Borman
a08_0605352.text: Roger. You have some pitch and yaw angles for our PTC after the burn? [Pause.]

a08_0605352.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0605352.text: That's affirmative. And would you give us another hack on your countdown time? [Pause.]

a08_0605400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0605400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 60 hours, 54 minutes. We've just heard from the spacecraft. Jim Lovell [means Frank] advised that they are set and apparently ready to go at this time for their midcourse correction maneuver. We'll play back that conversation for you and then stand by for further communications with the spacecraft.

a08_0605400-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0605400-pao.text: Roger. You have some pitch and yaw angles for our PTC after the burn? [Pause.]

a08_0605551.speaker: Borman
a08_0605551.text: Houston, I'll give you a mark at 4 minutes.

a08_0605600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0605600-pao.text: And we're coming up now on 3 minutes until our midcourse correction maneuver. You will note a slight time delay from the time when the spacecraft is counting back and we're watching our clocks here. That's about one and one half second delay one way. Oh wait, here's another call to the crew.

a08_0605705.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0605705.text: Apollo 8, Houston. How about switching the Biomed switch over to the left.

a08_0605800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0605800-pao.text: Coming up on 2 minutes now, and still looking good for that maneuver. At the present time, the spacecraft is at an altitude of 21,144 nautical miles above the Moon and traveling at a speed of 4,100 feet per second. We're now coming up on 1 minute and 30 seconds until that midcourse correction maneuver.

a08_0605900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0605900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 60 hours, 59 minutes, 41 seconds; and we're counting down now the last 10 seconds to our maneuver. And we should have the beginning of that 11-second Reaction Control System maneuver at this time. We'll stand by for confirmation here on the ground. And we show the burn complete at this time. We should have some preliminary figures shortly."

a08_0605910-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0605910-onboard.text: Okay, at zero [i.e. ignition] [Verb] 16 [Noun] 85, null V GX , Y . and Z . Null component. Tell me when you're going to burn.

a08_0605910-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0605910-onboard.text: Okay, record Delta-V Counter, residuals; Tape Recorder is going to Stop

a08_0610102.speaker: Lovell
a08_0610102.text: Roger. Burn on time, angles nominal, burn time about 12 seconds, 0.2 feet per second after the Delta-V C , 0 in V GX . We have transferred the result of the burn over to the LM slot with Verb 66.

a08_0610102.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0610102.text: Roger. And got a couple of items to clean up. We'll get you an RCS budget. We've got one redline now; we're trying to get some firmer numbers for you, and we'll have those in a little bit. Right now your use - your PTC usage is right on the Flight Plan line, so everything looks pretty good there. We want to get a crew status report from you. We'd like to firm up the Rev 2 Flight Plan idea; and sometime at your convenience, we'd like to take a reading of the PRD [Personal Radiation Dosimeter] for the Commander and CMP and then have you swap them. We are trying to isolate the - what the possible

a08_0610102.speaker: Borman
a08_0610102.text: And we're maneuvering to the PTC attitude, Houston.

a08_0610517.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0610517.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Could you give us the sign of that Z residual? [Long pause.]

a08_0610517.speaker: Lovell
a08_0610517.text: Alright, Houston. Looks like we didn't record the Z. We recorded Delta-V C , which is minus two tenths.

a08_0610517.speaker: Lovell
a08_0610517.text: And Z was one tenth 0.1, but we didn't get the sign.

a08_0610517.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0610517.text: Roger. Understand that was Delta-V C was minus 0.2. I copied Delta-V Z ; Zulu is 0.2. Is that incorrect?

a08_0610517.speaker: Lovell
a08_0610517.text: Roger. It was 0.1, but we didn't get the sign.

a08_0610517.speaker: Anders
a08_0610517.text: We can get it. We have it on the tape, Houston, whenever you want to dump it.

a08_0610517.speaker: Anders
a08_0610517.text: It'll be about the last 5 minutes worth.

a08_0610759.speaker: Anders
a08_0610759.text: Okay, Houston, for the PRD's: CDR is 0.07, CMP is 0.64, LMP is 0.80. Note that the CMP's hasn't changed since we started and the Commander's hasn't changed much. We have swapped PRDs; Commander has LMP, CMP has Commander's, and LMP has CMP's PRD. Over.

a08_0610900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0610900-pao.text: Our Guidance and Control officer advises that they clocked the burn at about 12 seconds. We'd nominally planned it for about 11. That would be a 1-second differential."

a08_0610900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0610900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. Based on information passed back from the crew on that midcourse correction, and our figures here on the ground, it appears that the maneuver was within about 0.2 of a foot per second of being right on the nominal and that would put us very close to the preplanned pericynthion of 61½ nautical miles. We, of course, will be tracking the spacecraft following this maneuver to determine just exactly what effect it did have. But that was the preplanned (Delta-V). That maneuver would have had the effect then of lowering the pericynthion by about 6 or 7 nautical miles. A

a08_0610900-pao.speaker: Lovell
a08_0610900-pao.text: Roger. Crew status report as follows: water, the Commander has about 50 clicks so far today; CMP, 43; and the LMP is 44. We've eaten two meals so far today. Day 3, meal A and B; consumed most of it except for the - the hard, hard bites, which no one cares for. Pudding was outstanding. [Pause.] We're at a gain of pericynthion now of plus 63 [nautical] miles [117 km]. [Pause.] Commander and CMP have had a rest period just before the midcourse 4 of about 2 hours.

a08_0610953.speaker: Lovell
a08_0610953.text: Roger. Crew status report as follows: water, the Commander has about 50 clicks so far today; CMP, 43; and the LMP is 44. We've eaten two meals so far today. Day 3, meal A and B; consumed most of it except for the - the hard, hard bites, which no one cares for. Pudding was outstanding. [Pause.] We're at a gain of pericynthion now of plus 63 [nautical] miles [117 km]. [Pause.] Commander and CMP have had a rest period just before the midcourse 4 of about 2 hours.

a08_0611611.speaker: Lovell
a08_0611611.text: We're at a gain of about 20,500 miles from the Moon at 61:14. How does that agree with what you figure?

a08_0611918.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0611918.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Looks like you're on the secondary loop. We'd like to run that for about 5 minutes.

a08_0611918.speaker: Anders
a08_0611918.text: Roger. We're doing the ECS redundant component check.

a08_0611918.speaker: Anders
a08_0611918.text: Getting any data now Houston? Guess you are. Okay. See you stopped my tape then. I've been running for about 3 extra minutes here to record the check.

a08_0611918.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0611918.text: Rog. We have data now. There was a temporary loss. [Pause.]

a08_0611918.speaker: Anders
a08_0611918.text: What's the matter? Was it chow time down there?

a08_0611918.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0611918.text: Rog. [Pause.] Didn't know you could smell it that far away. [Pause.]

a08_0611918.speaker: Anders
a08_0611918.text: Give me a call when you're satisfied with the secondary loop; it's stabilized out here pretty well.

a08_0611918.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0611918.text: Wilco, and you might tell Jim that RTCC is about 4 miles off; we had 20,496 [nautical miles, 37,959 km]. [Pause.]

a08_0611918.speaker: Anders
a08_0611918.text: We just put compressor 2 on AC2.

a08_0612223.speaker: Anders
a08_0612223.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Do you show battery B voltage dropped some from the post-charge value? Over. [Pause.]

a08_0612223.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0612223.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Confirm that battery B is a little bit lower, and this is attributed to the parasitic loads that are on there. [Pause.]

a08_0612900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0612900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 61 hours, 29 minutes. A preliminary figure on the effects of that midcourse correction performed at 61 hours indicates that our height of perigee will be 62.3 nautical miles [115.4 km] as a result of that maneuver. Now we had been shooting for something on the order of 61.5 [113.9]. 62.3 is very good, and the flight controllers here in Mission Control Center are quite happy with that figure. The spacecraft also computed a height of pericynthion following the maneuver and we heard from Jim Lovell. Their onboard computation was that the maneuver would have placed their

a08_0613130.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0613130.text: Okay. Looking over the - our redundant component check here, it appears we have not yet checked the integrity of the secondary loop radiators; and if you haven't done that sometime, we'd like to open up the secondary radiators but not flow through them and just measure the accumulator pressure. [Pause.]

a08_0613130.speaker: Borman
a08_0613130.text: Houston, we don't show that in our pre-LOI check, but we're willing to go ahead and do it if you want to.

a08_0613130.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0613130.text: Rog. We just noticed that it isn't there, and, yes, we would like to. [Pause.] You understand that we are not proposing that you flow, but merely we check for any pressure decay.

a08_0613130.speaker: Borman
a08_0613130.text: Roger. Wait 'til I get my trusty assistant here to help me.

a08_0613130.speaker: Borman
a08_0613130.text: Okay, Houston. We're going to blow the secondary - or we're gonna open the secondary rads for 30 seconds now.

a08_0613500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0613500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. During that conversation with the crew, Jim Lovell gave us a status report on the eating and drinking and sleeping that they've done recently. And he said that they have logged 50 clicks of water for the Commander, and 33 clicks for the Command Module Pilot, and 44 clicks for the Lunar Module Pilot. That translates into one-half ounce per click which would be about 25 ounces for the Commander; about 21 or 22 ounces for the Command Module Pilot and about the same amount of water for the Lunar Module Pilot. Lovell noted that they have all had two meals today. And found th

a08_0613848.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0613848.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You take your tape recorder to stop, why, we'll reset it then and give it back to you.

a08_0614100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0614100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 61 hours, 41 minutes; and at the present time we show 7 hours, 17 minutes until our Lunar Orbit Insertion maneuver. We'll pass along to you information on that maneuver as soon as it is available. In the meantime we anticipate things will be quieting down somewhat both here in Mission Control Center and aboard the spacecraft. The Flight Plan is relatively quiet for the next several hours. It doesn't begin to pick up activity again until about 3 hours prior to the Lunar Orbit Insertion maneuver at which time the crew will begin checking out the guidance and navigation

a08_0615318.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0615318.text: Okay. We still need to talk about the Rev 2 attitudes we're going to use to work around the fact that you have a fogged center window. Whenever that's convenient, we'd like to go over what your thoughts are on the subject and make sure we can get our Flight Plan squared away.

a08_0615318.speaker: Borman
a08_0615318.text: My thoughts are to make to do with the best with what we have. We are not interested in changing a lot of things right now, Ken.

a08_0615318.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0615318.text: Okay. The one proposal that sounds like it has some advantage to it: if we let Jim do his evaluation through the telescope, you do everything exactly the same except you turn and roll over 180 degrees so that your head's up, and let Jim do his tracking through the telescope and you'll still be a yaw right when you go to pick up your TV and that type of thing. It looks like that probably will cover everything. We can do that or we can just go as is and just have to let some of that tracking evaluation go by. Another alternate would be to have Jim look out the right-hand rendevous window, and yo

a08_0615318.speaker: Borman
a08_0615318.text: I think we'll try to do that, but I don't - this is one of the things that we'll work out when we get there.

a08_0615318.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0615318.text: Okay. The reason we were looking into it in the Flight Plan is, if you do want to try rolling over and flying heads up or something of that nature, we can help Bill get a little more out of his photography by giving him some new film settings and that type of thing. We'll have something like that available; in case you do fly heads up, why, we'll have some numbers we can call up for film settings.

a08_0615715.speaker: Borman
a08_0615715.text: Roger. We are going to have to dump some urine here shortly. Will this bother your tracking? [Long pause.]

a08_0615715.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0615715.text: Apollo 8, we're checking on that with the tracking people now. [Long pause.]

a08_0615715.speaker: Borman
a08_0615715.text: Houston, just give us the time when we can start on it, and we'll hold off until you say so.

a08_0615715.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0615715.text: Okay. And you can anticipate a handover between stations here on the hour, and you might get a slight glitch as we go through. I'll give you a call when we get back.

a08_0615715.speaker: Borman
a08_0615715.text: Thank you, Ken. What station are we going to be going to, Ken? [Pause.]

a08_0615715.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0615715.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You're cleared for a dump at this time, and understand this is the last gas station for a long time.

a08_0615715.speaker: Borman
a08_0615715.text: You mean you don't want us to dump after this for a while?

a08_0615715.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0615715.text: That's affirm. Due to the tracking as you approach the LOI, they would like to minimize any of these type of perturbations.

a08_0615800-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0615800-pao.text: Houston, just give us the time when we can start on it, and we'll hold off until you say so.

a08_0615800-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0615800-pao.text: Okay. And you can anticipate a handover between stations here on the hour, and you might get a slight glitch as we go through. I'll give you a call when we get back.

a08_0615800-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0615800-pao.text: Thank you, Ken. What station are we going to be going to, Ken? [Pause.]

a08_0615800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0615800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 61 hours, 58 minutes; and at the present time Apollo 8 is at an altitude of 18,733 nautical miles [from the Moon, 34,693 km], traveling at a speed of 4,139 feet per second [1,262 m/s]. Since our last report we've had a couple of conversations with the crew in which we've discussed the - some of the methods for working around the fogged windows that the crew has on the spacecraft in order to carry out the planned tasks in lunar orbit. And we'll play those conversations back for you and then continue to stand by for live conversations from the spacecraft.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Apollo 8, Houston through Honeysuckle.

a08_0620406.speaker: Anders
a08_0620406.text: Roger. Houston through Honeysuckle. We read you loud and clear.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Okay. Good morning.

a08_0620406.speaker: Anders
a08_0620406.text: Good morning.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Thought you went to sleep.

a08_0620406.speaker: Anders
a08_0620406.text: You got off over to Australia - you got over to Australia pretty fast.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Rog. [Pause.] That gas station call wake you up?

a08_0620406.speaker: Anders
a08_0620406.text: Man, I've been all eyeballs and elbows here for the last several hours.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: I'll bet. If you've got nothing else to do, I do have two charts in your LOI table that I need to give you more update numbers on.

a08_0620406.speaker: Anders
a08_0620406.text: Standby. [Long pause.]

a08_0620406.speaker: Anders
a08_0620406.text: We'll get our LOI tables man [i.e. Jim] on the line here. Houston. Stand by.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Okay; Houston, CMP here. I understand you have some updates for me.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Yes, sir; I've got a couple of charts in your chart book under LOI, and I have some numbers to fill in, one of them being the chart of LOI Delta-V magnitude versus abort Delta-V.

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Okay. Stand by, and I'll get it out.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Okay, I have the chart out. Go ahead.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Alright. Mode 1, 5 hours; roll, 1.38; pitch, 7.89; yaw, 357.37. Mode 1, 15 minutes; roll, 180.73; pitch, 29.46; yaw, 1.65. Over.

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Roger. The new attitudes for the Mode 1, 5-hour, Mode 15 minute are as follows: roll; for the one - Mode 1, 5-hour; roll, 1.38; pitch, 7.89; yaw, 357.37. Mode 1, 15 minute; roll, 180.73; pitch, 29.46; yaw, 1.65.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Okay. That's correct. Now I also have to give you a couple of points to plot on that curve. The present curve you have drawn is based on a 60-mile perigee or perilune, and you right now have a 62-mile pericynthion; and the reason that your target is for 62 miles is to pass over the landing site, so I have five sets of coordinates for you to copy.

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Is this to go on the same chart to redraw the curve?

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: That's affirmative.

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Okay. We'll go in on the LOI Delta-V magnitude, 1600; abort Delta-V, 2450, two-four-five-zero. [Long pause.]

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Okay. LOI Delta-V magnitude, 1600; abort Delta-V, 2450. Stand by just one. [Pause.] I have it; continue.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Okay. The next one is the LOI Delta-V, 2000; abort Delta-V, 3130. [Long pause.]

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Roger. I've got that plotted.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: 2400, LOI Delta-V; abort Delta-V, 3880, three-eight-eight-zero. [Long pause.]

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: I've got it plotted.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: 2800, LOI; abort Delta-V, 4700. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Roger. I have that one plotted, too.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Alright. The last one is LOI Delta-V, 2990; abort Delta-V, 5114. That's almost directly into the end of the present curve; 5114. [Pause.]

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Say again the LOI Delta-V magnitude, please.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Alright. LOI Delta-V, 2990.

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Rog. 2990. [Long pause.] Okay. I have it plotted.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Alright. And on the next one, you should have a chart, number 10, and we have three numbers to go in there for a Mode 3 gimbal angle. [Long pause.]

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Roger. Go ahead with the Mode 3 gimbal angles.

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Mode 3 gimbal angles are as follows: roll, 180.87; pitch, 42.31; yaw, 1.65.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Roger. That's correct.

a08_0620406.speaker: Lovell
a08_0620406.text: Could you please send up a French curve for me?

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: Rog.

a08_0620406.speaker: Borman
a08_0620406.text: Send up a couple.

a08_0620406.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0620406.text: The only one I have is about 6 foot. [Pause.]

a08_0620406.speaker: Borman
a08_0620406.text: Houston, could you give us a - some gimbal angles to point at the Moon? I never have seen it the whole trip, and I'm wondering which way it is from us now.

a08_0621635.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0621635.text: And we're getting ready to give you a rundown on your systems. We're going over all the final steps, and we'll tell you what we see in the way of trajectory and systems information. And once again, Dr. Joe Kerwin has brought over all the latest news, and we can read that up to you a little bit at a time if you aren't going to sleep.

a08_0621635.speaker: Borman
a08_0621635.text: What's he going to do, read out of the AMA [American Medical Association] Journal?

a08_0621635.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0621635.text: Okay. Here's one: the previously scheduled 72-hour ceasefire by the Viet Cong went into effect today, 17 hours before the 24-hour allied truce was to begin. [Long pause.]

a08_0621635.speaker: Borman
a08_0621635.text: You lost us on the numbers there. What was that again?

a08_0621635.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0621635.text: The gist of it was that the VC went into a ceasefire earlier than the truce that we had planned on, as a Christmas holiday type. [Pause.]

a08_0622136.speaker: Borman
a08_0622136.text: Houston, how do you read Apollo 8.

a08_0622136.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0622136.text: Loud and clear. Sorry to have stepped on you there. We're going over the summary of the systems data.

a08_0622400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0622400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 62 hours, 24 minutes; and at the present time, Apollo 8 is traveling at a speed of 4,159 feet per second [1,268 m/s]. We're presently at an altitude of 17,657 nautical miles [32,701 km] above the Moon. We have some preliminary information on the Lunar Orbit Insertion maneuver. We anticipate that this information will be refined and updated as we get additional tracking information on the spacecraft. At the present time we anticipate that the maneuver will be performed at about 69 hours, 8 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The burn will be a total duration of about 4 minute

a08_0623119.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0623119.text: Okay. I have a rundown on your systems here, G&C status. Everything looks real...

a08_0623119.speaker: Borman
a08_0623119.text: I want to wait 'til the LMP gets on the head set, Houston.

a08_0623119.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0623119.text: Okay. We'll just start with the EECOM business, then. I'll give you a summary of your batteries; battery A, we calculate 38.3 amp-hours. battery B...

a08_0623119.speaker: Anders
a08_0623119.text: Let me get my chart out.

a08_0623119.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0623119.text: Okay. Battery A, 38.3; battery B, 36.9; battery C, 38.5. That's looking pretty good. Looks like we got all the things back in that we took out, and we're running right along prediction. We would like to get a battery C voltage from you if you can reach over there and switch it. [Pause.]

a08_0623119.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0623119.text: Rog. 37 volts. Okay. The predicted cryo quantities at [CM/SM] Sep: on oxygen tank 1, 170 [pounds, 77 kg]; oxygen tank 2, 170 [pounds, 77 kg]; hydrogen 1, 9.5 [pounds, 4.3 kg]; and hydrogen 2, 10.0 [pounds, 4.5 kg]. You essentially have single cryo tank capabilities all the way at full power now.

a08_0623119.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0623119.text: The secondary coolant loop really looked good. Looks like you had a nice tight radiator and everything else on there was working right along the performance curves. Your main oxygen regulators both filled at 104 psi during our check. Looking at the lunar orbit, expect to be doing a water boil of about 1 pound per hour, and this is just an approximation; there's quite a variety of estimates as to what the water boiling requirements may be. May go anywhere from boiling lots to not boiling at all.

a08_0623119.speaker: Anders
a08_0623119.text: [Garble] stay on normal voice, doesn't it? [Pause.]

a08_0623119.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0623119.text: Okay. Looks like may not be able to hack the normal voice. [Pause.] On the cryo tanks, we've had quite a bit of destratification, particularly in the oxygen, and you notice this during the fan cycles and Delta-V's, so we're going to be sure and we'll remind you again to stir up the oxygen prior to LOI.

a08_0623119.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0623119.text: On the SPS, the oxidizer and fuel feed line temperatures are 75 [degrees Fahrenheit, 24°C] and holding steady. The Service Module RCS quad package temps are cycling and holding between 120 and 140 [degrees Fahrenheit, 49°C and 60°C], and looks like we're getting good normal heater operation. [Pause.] We plan to have you in a 60-[nautical] mile [111 km] circular orbit after LOI-2. [Pause.] And we should have some PAD's for you on the LOI burn at about 67 hours. [Long pause.]

a08_0623119.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0623119.text: Okay. We're still going through the tracking, and as you know, we're going to hold down on water dumps and so forth during the last couple of hours in and out, sort of aid the tracking procedures. Everything's running along the line normally now. Do you have any other specific questions? We are looking for an angle on the Moon. I guess that about summarizes the system. Everything looks Go right now.

a08_0623119.speaker: Borman
a08_0623119.text: Okay, Ken. Thank you. We just completed day 3, meal C, and now we're going to break up and each take a rest period before LOI.

a08_0623119.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0623119.text: Okay, real fine. Everybody wanted to ask if you wouldn't try and get some sack time here before we go in. It's going to be a big day.

a08_0624600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0624600-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. At the present time, our spacecraft's traveling at a speed of 4,176 miles - rather, feet per second [1,273 m/s], and our altitude [above the Moon] is 16,814 nautical miles [31,139 km]. As you heard the crew advise, they do hope to get some rest now before activity picks up leading toward the Lunar Orbit Insertion maneuver. According to the Flight Plan, they'll have about 3 hours of relative quiet in which they will be able to get some rest prior to picking up activities leading toward that maneuver. Such things as preparing the guidance and navigation system, checking o

a08_0625821.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0625821.text: Finally found out where the Moon is, and your present PTC attitude, if you happen to look out the right window [window 5, beside Bill's couch] as you go by, roll attitude of 320, it should be there.

a08_0630400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0630400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 63 hours, 4 minutes. At the present time our spacecraft is at an altitude above the Moon of 100 - rather 16,035 nautical miles [29,697 km], and our velocity continuing to increase. Still increasing rather slowly but steadily. Our speed is now 4,194 feet per second [1,278 m/s]. We would expect this relatively slow velocity build up to continue until about 65 hours. At that point, the spacecraft will be some 11,000 nautical miles [20,400 km] from the Moon, and from that point on, the acceleration will begin to build up quite rapidly so that within about 4 hours from 65

a08_0630400-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0630400-pao.text: Roger. Bill would like to ask the doctor's permission to take a Seconal [sleeping pill].

a08_0630613.speaker: Borman
a08_0630613.text: Roger. Bill would like to ask the doctor's permission to take a Seconal [sleeping pill].

a08_0630806.speaker: Borman
a08_0630806.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. Did you call? We lost track for a minute.

a08_0630806.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0630806.text: Okay, Apollo 8. You're cleared to go ahead with that pill. Take - Surgeon recommends a small one.

a08_0631012.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0631012.text: Apollo 8, Houston. If you can, we'd like to have you stir up the oxygen cryo.

a08_0631012.speaker: Borman
a08_0631012.text: Okay, I'll do that right now. Two minutes each. Just the oxygen?

a08_0631012.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0631012.text: Okay. We want to get both the oxygen and hydrogen.

a08_0631012.speaker: Borman
a08_0631012.text: You say just the oxygen, Ken?

a08_0631012.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0631012.text: No, sir; both the oxygen and the hydrogen.

a08_0631012.speaker: Borman
a08_0631012.text: Okay. Start, starting with the hydrogen.

a08_0632001.speaker: Borman
a08_0632001.text: Okay. Houston, Apollo 8. We've cycled through all of the cryo fans.

a08_0635456.speaker: Borman
a08_0635456.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0635456.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0635456.text: Rog. We had a momentary loss there.

a08_0635456.speaker: Borman
a08_0635456.text: How's the tracking data look, Ken?

a08_0643809.speaker: Borman
a08_0643809.text: Houston. Apollo 8 with a radio check.

a08_0643809.speaker: Carr
a08_0643809.text: Howdy. [Pause.] The Black Watch is watching.

a08_0643809.speaker: Borman
a08_0643809.text: How do you read on this - how do you read on this antenna?

a08_0643809.speaker: Carr
a08_0643809.text: Loud and clear on that one, Bill.

a08_0645143.speaker: Borman
a08_0645143.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Do you read on Omni C?

a08_0645143.speaker: Carr
a08_0645143.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Reading you loud with some background noise.

a08_0645143.speaker: Borman
a08_0645143.text: Roger. You're loud and clear. Thank you.

a08_0652401.speaker: Lovell
a08_0652401.text: Roger, Houston. This is Apollo 8. Loud and clear. How me?

a08_0655549.speaker: Carr
a08_0655549.text: Apollo 8, Houston; with a preliminary LOI-1 PAD. Over.

a08_0655549.speaker: Carr
a08_0655549.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Roger. LOI-1; SPS/G&N; 62844; minus 1.61, plus 1.29; 069:08:18.41. Copy?

a08_0655549.speaker: Carr
a08_0655549.text: Roger, 8. 01, 068.9, 26.0, Persei Zeta, down 04.8, left 0.5. The remainder is Not Applicable. Sirius, Rigel, set of stars for GDG Align; 129, 155, 010; negative ullage. We'll pass the horizon window data later. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0655549.speaker: Lovell
a08_0655549.text: Roger. Preliminary LOI-1 PAD as follows: SPS/G&N; 62844; minus 1.61, plus 1.29. Are you copying?

a08_0655549.speaker: Lovell
a08_0655549.text: 069:08:18.41; minus 2983.7, plus 0239.0, plus 0099.4; 000, 200, 005; 0169.3, plus 0060.0; 2994.9, 4:02, 2978.2; 01, 068.9, 26.0; Persei Zeta, down 04.8, left 0.5. The remainder not applicable. Sirius, Rigel; 129, 155, 010. No ullage. We'll pass up the remainder up later.

a08_0655549.speaker: Carr
a08_0655549.text: Roger, Jim. One question - we talked about a P40 gimbal check. Would you like to do that during this maneuver to LOI-1 attitude, or would you rather hold that off until a little closer to LOI? Over. [Pause.]

a08_0655549.speaker: Lovell
a08_0655549.text: Let me check on that. Wait one, Houston.

a08_0660239.speaker: Lovell
a08_0660239.text: Roger. We could make this gimbal check as a [part of a] maneuver to the LOI attitude.

a08_0660239.speaker: Lovell
a08_0660239.text: Understand that you'll load us up with the LOI-1 PAD and we'll run through P40 as far as the gimbal check.

a08_0660239.speaker: Carr
a08_0660239.text: Roger. That's what we heard you were going to do on it. Are you going to run both the manual gimbals as well as the automatic? Over.

a08_0661842.speaker: Carr
a08_0661842.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Standing by to monitor P52. Over.

a08_0663900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0663900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 66 hours, 39 minutes, 52 seconds into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 drawing closer to the Moon. At this time we read a distance away of 6,848.8 nautical miles [12,684.0 km]. Our present velocity; 4,643.5 feet per second [1,415.3]. We have had only a brief conversation with the crew of Apollo 8 since our last transmission, and we'll pass that along now.

a08_0663900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0663900-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Although we expect an apolune of 169.3 nautical miles [313.5 km], and a perilune of 60 nautical miles [111 km] to result from the Lunar Orbit Insertion number 1 burn, we would anticipate ignition for the 2,994-feet-per-second [913-m/s] burn at an altitude of about 70 nautical miles [130 km]. Since on our trip out the Moon is below our trajectory plane or path and as Apollo 8 approaches the Moon, we'll see a velocity build up to around 8,400 feet per second [2,560 m/s] at the time of LOI ignition. Our approach for the spacecraft - on approach, the spacecraft sort of div

a08_0664201.speaker: Borman
a08_0664201.text: Houston, how do you read? Apollo 8.

a08_0664201.speaker: Carr
a08_0664201.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Loud and clear.

a08_0664201.speaker: Borman
a08_0664201.text: Okay, Jerry. At 67, we're going maneuver to the LOI-1 attitude, do a sextant star check, and then we'll have to go back to PTC. I want to know if you want us to go back to the same attitudes we are at now?

a08_0664201.speaker: Carr
a08_0664201.text: Apollo 8, Houston. That's affirmative. Break. We're getting ready to ask you to do an erasable dump, Verb 47. We're ginning up to get ready for it now, and we'll call you as soon as we're ready to copy.

a08_0664201.speaker: Carr
a08_0664201.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We're setting up for the dump now. It'll take about 3 minutes and 20 seconds once we start the dump. Over.

a08_0664709.speaker: Borman
a08_0664709.text: Roger. Can you point out the position of this Zeta Perseus to us a little better? We don't have it marked on our charts. We have got Mirfak, and we know Algol, but which one is Zeta Perseus?

a08_0664709.speaker: Carr
a08_0664709.text: Roger, Frank. Persei Zeta is just about exactly between Aldebaran and Mirfak. [Long pause.]

a08_0664709.speaker: Carr
a08_0664709.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We're ready for your CMC erasable dump. Key Verb 74 Enter. Over.

a08_0664709.speaker: Borman
a08_0664709.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Are you getting the dump?

a08_0664709.speaker: Carr
a08_0664709.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Indications are that we're getting it; we're checking. You'll have to leave the computer alone for 3 minutes and 20 seconds. Over.

a08_0664709.speaker: Carr
a08_0664709.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're getting your dump low bit rate through Honeysuckle.

a08_0664709.speaker: Carr
a08_0664709.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Persei Zeta is a third magnitude star same as Enif. Over.

a08_0664709.speaker: Borman
a08_0664709.text: Jerry, when are you going to send us the TEI-1 [Trans-Earth Injection] and the rest of that block data? [Long pause.]

a08_0664709.speaker: Carr
a08_0664709.text: Apollo 8, Houston. PC plus 2 does not need an update. We'll have your TEI-1 and 2 in about 10 minutes. Over.

a08_0665353.speaker: Carr
a08_0665353.text: Apollo 8, Houston. The dump is complete; you can have your computer back. The reason for the dump was to investigate further the P52 anomaly you had about 4 hours ago. We'll try to have some words for you in about 20 or 30 minutes. Over.

a08_0665353.speaker: Borman
a08_0665353.text: You mean when it wouldn't come up with the proper star?

a08_0665353.speaker: Borman
a08_0665353.text: We're going to go ahead and start our maneuver to LOI-1 attitude.

a08_0665353.speaker: Lovell
a08_0665353.text: Earlier in the flight, I noticed that the auto optics wouldn't drive to the star pick-a-pair selected. For example, we - it picked Alpheratz at one time, wouldn't drive there, and we drove to a spot that had no star; and I went back and reselected the program and came back, and it worked okay.

a08_0665353.speaker: Carr
a08_0665353.text: Jim; is this anomaly you're talking about - was that 4 hours ago when we did the REFSMMAT align?

a08_0665353.speaker: Lovell
a08_0665353.text: This happened, I think, yesterday. When we - we were doing a regular REFSMMAT alignment. Alpheratz was the first star selected, and it didn't drive to Alpheratz; and I went in and reselected the program again, and it worked okay.

a08_0665353.speaker: Borman
a08_0665353.text: Our PAD here hadn't been - Roger. Our PAD hasn't been correct. I understand the gimbal angles for LOI-1 are roll 0, pitch 200, and yaw 5. Is that correct?

a08_0665353.speaker: Carr
a08_0665353.text: Apollo 8, Houston with a map update. Over.

a08_0665353.speaker: Carr
a08_0665353.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Map update Rev 1, slash 2: 68:58:04, 69:05:05, 69:31:41, 70:14:48. Copy?

a08_0665353.speaker: Carr
a08_0665353.text: Roger. Remarks: Charlie Papa 1, 71:14:57; Charlie Papa 2, 71:28:32; Charlie Papa 3, 71:47:26; Bravo 1, 72:09:42. Over.

a08_0665353.speaker: Lovell
a08_0665353.text: Roger. Standby. I'll get the antenna. [Long pause.]

a08_0665353.speaker: Carr
a08_0665353.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Readback is correct.

a08_0665700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0665700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 66 hours, 57 minutes, 14 seconds now into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 now 6,077.3 nautical miles [11,255.1 km] away from the Moon. Its current velocity; 4,729.7 feet per second [1,441.6]. We've had considerable conversation over the past few moments or minutes with the crew and we'll pass that along now.

a08_0670426.speaker: Carr
a08_0670426.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Try to lock up an Omni for us? Over.

a08_0670426.speaker: Borman
a08_0670426.text: How do you read now, Houston?

a08_0670426.speaker: Carr
a08_0670426.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Reading you loud and clear. No TM [telemetry].

a08_0670426.speaker: Carr
a08_0670426.text: Roger, Frank. How far are you from your gimbal drive check? Over.

a08_0670426.speaker: Borman
a08_0670426.text: We're just maneuvering to the attitude now.

a08_0670426.speaker: Carr
a08_0670426.text: Roger, Frank. Can you lock up the High Gain at that attitude? We have a telemetry problem. Over.

a08_0670426.speaker: Borman
a08_0670426.text: We'll try to. I don't know if we can or not; have to wait 'til we get there.

a08_0670800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0670800-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. As you heard, Apollo 8 has begun its maneuver towards the LOI-1 burn attitude. Apollo 8 has started this maneuver. 'Map' by the way does not translate into 'Message Acceptance'. Paul (Haney) says it did in earlier manned flights. These numbers that were passed along are times in lunar orbit for acquisition and loss of signal for the Manned Space Flight Network. Lunar sunrise and sunset times in crossing of the Moon's prime meridian determined by the lunar sunset terminator longitude. It's almost, in fact it is 2 hours past midnight now. It's Christmas Eve and as we pro

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. We cannot get the High Gain at the burn attitude.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Roger, Frank. Thanks anyway. [Long pause.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We have a handover from Honeysuckle to Guam in about two minutes.

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Thank you.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [No answer.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [No answer.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [No answer.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Lovell
a08_0671125.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Loud and clear. How me? [Pause.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Lovell
a08_0671125.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Loud and clear. How me? Over. [No answer.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8 here.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. I have TEI-1 and TEI-2 PADs. We still have no telemetry; expect to get it soon. Over.

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Roger. You think it's a ground problem?

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Roger. It's a ground problem; we just got it back. [Long pause.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Go ahead with your data. [Pause.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston with an LOI-1 PAD. Over.

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Roger. Understand. LOI-1.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: That is affirmative, LOI-1; SPS/G&N: 62844; 1 - correction - minus 1.61, plus 1.29; 069:08:19.52; minus 2984.0, plus 0239.0, plus 0105.3. Copy? [No answer.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Roger. We broke lock; did not get the Delta-V X .

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. Beginning with Delta-V X : minus 2984.0, plus 0239.0, plus 0105.3; 000, 200, 005; 0169.3, plus 0060.0; 2995.4, 4:02, 2978.8. Copy?

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Roger.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Roger. 01, 068.8, 25.9; Persei Zeta, down 04.8, left 0.5. The remainder not applicable. Sirius, Rigel, 129, 155, 010; negative ullage. Horizon window, ignition minus 2 minutes, 40 degrees unlit, ignition 27 degrees unlit. Over.

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Roger. LOI-1, SPS/G&N: 62844; minus 1.61, plus 1.29; 069:08:19.52; minus 2984.0, plus 0239.0, plus 0105.3; [Pause.] 000, 200, 005; 0169.3, plus 0060.0; 2995.4, 4:02, 2978.8; 01, zero - 068.8, 25.9; Persei Zeta, down 04.8, left 0.5; Sirius, Rigel, 129, 155, 010; no ullage; horizon, 2 minutes, 40 degrees unlit; ignition, 27 degrees unlit.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Readback is correct. Ready to copy TEI-1. Over.

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Are you waiting for us to start - before you start your gimbal check? Over.

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: We can start the gimbals check right here.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Roger. You want to copy while you're doing it or stand by on TEI-1?

a08_0671125.speaker: Borman
a08_0671125.text: Stand by for a minute.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Roger. Standing by.

a08_0671125.speaker: Carr
a08_0671125.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Shifting command back to Honeysuckle [from Guam]. Over.

a08_0672700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0672700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 67 hours, 27 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 now 4,715 nautical miles [8,732 km] away from the Moon. Current velocity reading; 4,933 feet per second, 4,933 feet per second [1,504 m/s]. As we had indicated earlier, the Moon will have traveled about 130 [thousand] nautical miles from the time of lift-off to time of LOI-1. Apollo 8 has now achieved it's proper burn attitude, we've had considerable conversation with the Apollo 8 crew, which we'll pass along now.

a08_0672700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0672700-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. You heard an update to our LOI-1 maneuver PAD being passed along. This changed only one number and only by one second. The GET, Ground Elapsed Time, of ignition has changed to 69 hours, 19 minutes, 05 seconds - correction - that would be a change of one minute. So at 67 hours, 36 minutes, 05 seconds; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Apollo 8, Houston. How did that gimbal drive check go?

a08_0673446.speaker: Borman
a08_0673446.text: It went fine.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Roger, Frank. We're ready with the TEI-1 and 2 maneuver PADs. We've also got two state vectors and a target load to uplink and load if you'll configure for it. Over.

a08_0673446.speaker: Borman
a08_0673446.text: Roger. We're trying to get the High Gain [Antenna] now. We're maneuvering back to PTC attitude.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Go ahead with your TEI PADs.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. TEI-1, SPS/G&N; 462 - correction - 46728; minus 0.53, plus 1.21; 071:25:04.73; plus 3774.6, minus 0329.9, plus 0084.4. Copy?

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: We're copying.

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Copying.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Roger. N/A, N/A, N/A; plus 13.50, minus 165.00; 1305.0, 36389, 122:10:45; Sirius, Rigel, 129, 155, 010; ullage two-jets, 20 seconds, jet Bravo, Delta; horizon window, X-axis on horizon at ignition minus 3 minutes; assumes LOI-1. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Houston, Apollo 8. TEI-1 as follows: SPS/G&N; 46728; minus 0.53, plus 1.21; 071:25:04.73. Copy?

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Roger. Copy.

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Plus 3774.6, minus 0329.9, plus 0084.4; 179, 346, 357; not applicable, plus 0017.6; 3790.0, 3:36, 3770.5; 42, 127.9, 30.9; not applicable three times; plus 13.50, minus 165.00; 1305.0, 36389, 122:10:45; Sirius, Rigel, 129, 155, 010; ullage, two jets, 20 seconds, quads B and D; horizon window, X-axis on horizon at T IG minus 3, assumes LOI-1.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. Correct. [Long pause.]

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Standing by for TEI-2, if you have it. [Pause.]

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We'll be ready with a TEI-2 in about 1 minute.

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Apollo 8, Houston; with a TEI-2 maneuver PAD.

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Roger. Ready to copy.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Roger. TEI-2; SPS/G&N; 46728; minus 0.53, plus 1.21. Copy?

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Roger. Copy.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Roger. 073:21:30.24; plus 2846.6, minus 0035.0, plus 0240.6; 180, 022, 002; not applicable, plus 0018.8. Copy?

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Roger. Copy.

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Copy. Looks like you left out a digit in range to go and latitude.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Request you switch your Omni. It's getting pretty garbled now.

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Roger. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. I copied. I question the latitude and the range to go. It appears that you gave me one too few digits in both cases.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Roger. I repeat, latitude plus 09.20, minus 165.00; 1295.3, 36175, 146:32:16. Copy?

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: I copied.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Roger. Your GDC Align is no change; ullage, no change; horizon on the minus 2-degree line at ignition minus 3 minutes. Assumes LOI-1. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Roger. TEI-2 maneuver PAD; SPS/G&N; 46728; minus 0.53, plus 1.21; 073:21:30.24; plus 2846.6, minus 0035.0, I did not get the sign, 0240.6 for a Delta-V Z . 180, 022, 002; not applicable, plus 0018.8; 2857.0, 2:50, 2840.1; 42, 064.1, 29.6; not applicable three times; plus 09.20, minus 165.00; 1295.3, 36175, 146:32:16. No change in the GDC Align stars, no change in ullage, horizon on the minus 2-degree line at T IG minus 3, assumes LOI-1.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Roger. Correct. I repeat Delta-V Z plus 0240.6. Over.

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Roger. Plus 0240.6.

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0673446.speaker: Carr
a08_0673446.text: Apollo 8, Houston. If you can go [to program] 00 and Accept, we'll start the Nav loads.

a08_0673446.speaker: Lovell
a08_0673446.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0673800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0673800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 67 hours, 38 minutes. We've twisted our tongue on that last announcement. The Ground Elapsed Time of ignition should read 69 hours, 8 minutes, 19 seconds - we repeat, it should read 69 hours, 8 minutes, 19 seconds; a change of 1 second. So at 67 hours, 38 minutes, 40 seconds; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0675000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0675000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We're going to cut short here for a moment because very shortly we will have our Go/No-Go decision. Incidentally, this block data that's being passed along is contingency information only - making ground information available to the crew for a Trans-Earth Injection burn at the end of the first or second lunar orbits plus PC plus 2 which translates into pericynthion plus 2 hours; the time of closest approach to the Moon plus 2 hours. This information is entered into the onboard equipment, but is used only if an alternate mission becomes necessary. So, at this ti

a08_0675120.speaker: Carr
a08_0675120.text: Apollo 8, Houston. The CM [state] vector is in; working on the [vector for the] LM [slot] now. Over.

a08_0675120.speaker: Carr
a08_0675120.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We'd like a cryo fan cycle when you can. Over.

a08_0675120.speaker: Carr
a08_0675120.text: Apollo 8, Houston. The LM vector is loaded. Target load going in now.

a08_0675520.speaker: Carr
a08_0675520.text: Apollo 8, Houston. The update is complete. You can have the computer, TLM [Telemetry] to Block. Be advised, the erasable dump checks out okay.

a08_0675520.speaker: Lovell
a08_0675520.text: Roger. Thank you. We have the computer; we're in Block.

a08_0675520.speaker: Carr
a08_0675520.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We'd like to make, at this time, a down-voice backup comm check. Set the S-band Aux, Tape to Down-Voice Backup, TLM inputs PCM, Low. Over.

a08_0675520.speaker: Anders
a08_0675520.text: Roger, Houston. And we'd like to have a check of our DSE on low bit rate for voice.

a08_0675520.speaker: Carr
a08_0675520.text: Roger. Understand you want the DSE check on low bit rate for voice. [Pause.]

a08_0675520.speaker: Anders
a08_0675520.text: That's affirmative, and we'll give it - we'll give it about 10 minutes now or about 5 minutes, then you can check it out.

a08_0675755.speaker: Lovell
a08_0675755.text: As a matter of interest, we have yet to see the Moon. [Pause.]

a08_0675755.speaker: Carr
a08_0675755.text: Apollo 8, Houston. What else are you seeing? [Pause.]

a08_0675755.speaker: Anders
a08_0675755.text: Nothing. It's like being on the inside of a submarine.

a08_0675755.speaker: Borman
a08_0675755.text: Houston, we just ran a Program 21. We show a pericynthion of plus 74.9 (nautical) miles with the state vector you just uploaded.

a08_0675755.speaker: Carr
a08_0675755.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Reading your down-voice backup loud and clear. Request you keep those switches where they are for the remainder of the pass. Over.

a08_0675755.speaker: Anders
a08_0675755.text: Roger. And I'm rewinding the tape recorder for a dump - for a DSE voice check.

a08_0675755.speaker: Anders
a08_0675755.text: It's rewound; are you ready to dump? [Pause.]

a08_0675755.speaker: Anders
a08_0675755.text: We'd like to go to S-band Aux, Tape, briefly so you can dump the tape while we're on the High Gain. We've only got about 30 seconds worth. [Long pause.]

a08_0675755.speaker: Carr
a08_0675755.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. We'll do that from the ground. Over.

a08_0675755.speaker: Anders
a08_0675755.text: Roger. And our switch configuration is Down-voice Backup and Stop. And you've got it?

a08_0675755.speaker: Anders
a08_0675755.text: You won't need to dump more than about a minute's worth.

a08_0675755.speaker: Carr
a08_0675755.text: Roger. That pericynthion you read out is for ignition. We read that as 75 (nautical) miles; your true pericynthion is 64 miles at 69:10:35. Over.

a08_0675755.speaker: Carr
a08_0675755.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston with an addition to your TEI-1 maneuver PAD. Over.

a08_0675755.speaker: Carr
a08_0675755.text: Roger. Under remarks, add the following: "requires minus MA procedure". Over. [Pause.]

a08_0675755.speaker: Carr
a08_0675755.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. At 68:04, you're Go for LOI.

a08_0675755.speaker: Carr
a08_0675755.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You're riding the best one we can find around. [Pause.]

a08_0675755.speaker: Carr
a08_0675755.text: You're riding the best bird we can find. Over.

a08_0680000-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0680000-pao.text: Roger. And I'm rewinding the tape recorder for a dump - for a DSE voice check.

a08_0680000-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0680000-pao.text: It's rewound; are you ready to dump? [Pause.]

a08_0680000-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0680000-pao.text: We'd like to go to S-band Aux, Tape, briefly so you can dump the tape while we're on the High Gain. We've only got about 30 seconds worth. [Long pause.]

a08_0680000-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0680000-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. We'll do that from the ground. Over.

a08_0680400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0680400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 68 hours, 32 seconds. We have conversation going back and forth with the crew now. The Apollo 8 spacecraft at this time 3,125.7 nautical miles [5,788.8 km] away from the Moon. And our velocity; 5,319.6 feet per second [1,621.4 m/s]; and we're standing by at this point for our decision which appears very likely to be a Go for lunar orbit. Standing by.

a08_0680400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0680400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; continuing to stand by for that decision point at 68 hours, 1 minutes, 49 seconds.

a08_0680400-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0680400-pao.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. At 68:04, you're Go for LOI.

a08_0680400-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0680400-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You're riding the best one we can find around. [Pause.]

a08_0680400-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0680400-pao.text: You're riding the best bird we can find. Over.

a08_0680400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0680400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 68 hours, 4 minutes, 40 seconds. As you've just heard, we've passed along a Go for the Lunar Orbit Insertion burn with the Service Propulsion System engine. Our flight control team here in Mission Control has examined the data and it looks good. So we have a combined crew/ground decision. We are Go. Repeat - Go for Lunar Orbit Insertion One. At 68 hours, 5 minutes, 10 seconds into the flight, Apollo 8; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0681145.speaker: Anders
a08_0681145.text: The cryo's have been stirred, Houston.

a08_0681145.speaker: Carr
a08_0681145.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We just saw an MC&W light.

a08_0681145.speaker: Anders
a08_0681145.text: We just tested the caution and warning.

a08_0681145.speaker: Carr
a08_0681145.text: Roger. Clint there is getting white.

a08_0681200-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0681200-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We just saw an MC&W light.

a08_0681200-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0681200-pao.text: We just tested the caution and warning.

a08_0681200-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0681200-pao.text: Roger. Clint there is getting white.

a08_0681200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0681200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 68 hours, 12 minutes, 12 seconds now into the flight. Apollo 8 draws closer to the Moon. Our current distance away; 2,555.9 nautical miles [4,733.5]. Our velocity building up, now reading 5,527.5 feet per second [1,684.7 m/s]. We've stored some tape so we could pass along that Go-No Go decision to you live, so we'll turn and play back that tape now.

a08_0681559.speaker: Carr
a08_0681559.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're 42 minutes from LOS, and we caught another caution and warning light.

a08_0681559.speaker: Borman
a08_0681559.text: That was the High Gain Antenna going out of limits.

a08_0681600-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0681600-pao.text: That was the High Gain Antenna going out of limits.

a08_0682100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0682100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 68 hours, 16 minutes, 42 seconds. We're continuing to monitor.

a08_0682100-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0682100-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. The voice quality on the DSE dump is very good. The DSE is yours. Over.

a08_0682100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0682100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 68 hours, 21 minutes, 22 seconds now into the flight of Apollo 8. Our spacecraft at this time; 2,100 nautical miles [3,900 km] away from the Moon. Velocity continuing to rise; our current reading of 5,743.8 feet per second [1,750.7 m/s]. We had a brief conversation with the Apollo 8 crew moments or minutes back. And we're going to pass that conversation along now.

a08_0682100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0682100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. You heard the indication from our Capsule Communicator as to time of Loss of Signal over the backside of the Moon. During this pass over the backside, Apollo 8 will perform its Lunar Orbit Insertion burn number 1 with the Service Propulsion System engine. Following this burn, the spacecraft weight should be some 16,000 pounds [7,300 kg] lighter with the expenditure of propellants. A slight plane change of about 2 degrees is combined into this engine firing. The intent of the plane change is to make Apollo 8 pass over a given heading over the primary Apollo zone

a08_0682104.speaker: Carr
a08_0682104.text: Apollo 8, Houston. The voice quality on the DSE dump is very good. The DSE is yours. Over.

a08_0682625.speaker: Lovell
a08_0682625.text: Read you loud and clear, Houston.

a08_0682800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0682800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 68 hours, 28 minutes into the flight now of Apollo 8. We're drawing closer to the Moon with the Apollo 8 spacecraft. Our current reading; 1,773.1 nautical miles [3,283.8 km] away. Velocity going up the steep curve now. Our current reading; 5,945 feet per second [1,812 m/s]. We had a very brief communications check with the Apollo 8 spacecraft. They acknowledged that communications looked fine. We're some 30 minutes now away from our time of Loss of Signal and the time that the Apollo 8 spacecraft goes over the backside of the Moon, out of sight from the groun

a08_0683037.speaker: Anders
a08_0683037.text: Roger. We're ready to activate the primary water boiler.

a08_0683037.speaker: Anders
a08_0683037.text: We got a Go [for the boiler]?

a08_0683037.speaker: Anders
a08_0683037.text: Okay. Steam pressure going to Auto; H 2 flow going to Auto. [Long pause.]

a08_0683037.speaker: Carr
a08_0683037.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're on low bit rate. We won't see your steam pressure; your Rad Out is 33. Over.

a08_0683037.speaker: Anders
a08_0683037.text: Roger. We're below the boiling limit, and steam pressure is steady at 0.15.

a08_0683037.speaker: Carr
a08_0683037.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We've got our lunar map up and ready to go.

a08_0683300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0683300-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 68 hours, 33 minutes, 8 seconds now into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 now 1,517 nautical miles [2,809 km] away from the Moon. Current velocity reading 6,120.2 feet per second [1,865.4 m/s] and accelerating. The Apollo 8 is currently going through a series of systems checks. We've had some conversations, Jerry Carr Capsule Communicator with Bill Anders aboard the spacecraft, and we'll pick those up for you now.

a08_0683300-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0683300-pao.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We've got our lunar map up and ready to go.

a08_0683300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0683300-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. You heard that last report. Our lunar map - lunar display is up here in Mission Control Center and we are ready to go at 68 hours, 34 minutes, 48 seconds into the flight of Apollo 8; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0683738.speaker: Anders
a08_0683738.text: Roger. We're showing a fuel pressure of 167, an Ox(idizer pressure) of 163. Wondering, do you think there's a possibility of us having a transient Caution/Warning trip on fuel/Ox pressure at the beginning of the burn that would correct itself nominally as we had a chance to pressurize? Over.

a08_0683738.speaker: Carr
a08_0683738.text: Roger. Understand; will check. Stand by.

a08_0683738.speaker: Carr
a08_0683738.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We've been reading fuel 173, Ox 167; holding steady for a long period of time. We expect no Caution and Warning trip. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0684000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0684000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 68 hours, 40 minutes, 54 seconds now into the flight. Apollo 8 now 1,128 nautical miles [2,089] away from the Moon. Our current velocity reading; 6,467 feet per second [1,971 m/s]. We've had a brief conversation. Jerry Carr has talked to Bill Anders aboard the Apollo 8 spacecraft regarding Service Propulsion System tank pressures, and we're going to play that conversation now.

a08_0684000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0684000-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Meanwhile here in Mission Control Center, our LOS clock, Loss of Signal clock, continues to count down. We now read, Mark, 15 minutes, 26 seconds until that time that the Apollo 8 spacecraft will pass out of communications range over the backside of the Moon. And at 68 hours, 42 minutes, 50 seconds into the flight; this is Apollo Control, Houston,

a08_0684000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0684000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 68 hours, 47 minutes, 12 seconds now into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 now 825 nautical miles [1,528 km] away from the Moon. Our velocity continuing its rise at an increasing pace now. We read 6,836 feet per second [2,084 m/s]. And at this time we're 10 minutes, 29 seconds away from time of Loss of Signal. We've had no further communications with the crew who are no doubt quite busy as of this moment in preparation for their first Lunar Orbit Insertion burn. And at 68 hours, 48 minutes, continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0684830.speaker: Carr
a08_0684830.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Nine minutes, 30 seconds from LOS.

a08_0684830.speaker: Carr
a08_0684830.text: Roger. In about 10 seconds, we'll have you 19 minutes from ignition. Five, four, three, two, one...

a08_0684900-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0684900-pao.text: Roger. In about 10 seconds, we'll have you 19 minutes from ignition. Five, four, three, two, one...

a08_0684900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0684900-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 68 hours, 49 minutes. Apollo 8 now 730.7 nautical miles away. Velocity; 6,957 feet per second. We've had conversation with the Apollo 8 crew and we're going to pick that up now.

a08_0684900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
