a08_0684900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. As you heard on that mark, they were counting down for time of ignition. Meanwhile at Mission Control Center, our time away from LOS now reading 7 minutes, 50 seconds. And at 68 hours, 50 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0684900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0684900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 68 hours, 52 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 now 582 nautical miles [1,078 km] away. Velocity reading; 7,191 feet per second [2,192 m/s]. We're some 5 minutes, 30 seconds away from LOS at this time. At this time Glynn Lunney has gone around the room taking a status check with his flight control team. We look Go. We continue to stand by, and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0685306.speaker: Carr
a08_0685306.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Five minutes LOS, all systems Go. Over.

a08_0685306.speaker: Carr
a08_0685306.text: Roger, Frank. The custard's in the oven at 350. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0685400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0685400-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 68 hours, 54 minutes now into the flight. Our Apollo 8 spacecraft now 529 nautical miles [980 km] away. Velocity reading 7,286 feet per second [2,221 m/s]. Jerry Carr has spoken with the crew and we're going to pick up that conversation now.

a08_0685400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0685400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We're now some 3 minutes, 35 seconds away from LOS and standing by.

a08_0685400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0685400-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 2 minutes, 50 seconds away from time of LOS now. Our distance away from the Moon; 460 nautical miles [852 km]. Velocity, 7,417 feet per second [2,261 m/s]. Here in Mission Control, we're standing by. There's certainly a great deal of anxiety at this moment as in the next 2½ minutes we will not talk with the crew for some period of time. We acquire at 36 minutes. So at 68 hours, 55 minutes continuing to monitor this is Apollo Control.

a08_0685606.speaker: Carr
a08_0685606.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Two minutes until LOS.

a08_0685606.speaker: Carr
a08_0685606.text: Apollo 8, Houston. One minute to LOS. All systems Go.

a08_0685606.speaker: Anders
a08_0685606.text: Roger. Going to Command Reset, tape recorder Forward, low bit rate.

a08_0685606.speaker: Lovell
a08_0685606.text: We'll see you on the other side. [Long pause.]

a08_0685606.speaker: Carr
a08_0685606.text: Apollo 8, 10 seconds to go [to LOS]. You're Go all the way.

a08_0685700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0685700-pao.text: Two minutes away now from LOS. 418 nautical miles [774 km] now away from the Moon. Our velocity continuing to build up; 7,518 feet per second [2,291 m/s]; continuing to climb. One minute, 30 seconds away now from Loss of Signal. Our distance away from the Moon now 401 nautical miles [743 km]. Velocity reading 7,535 [fps, 2,297 m/s] as we continue with this flight of Apollo 8.

a08_0685700-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0685700-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. One minute to LOS. All systems Go.

a08_0685700-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0685700-pao.text: Roger. Going to Command Reset, tape recorder Forward, low bit rate.

a08_0685700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0685700-pao.text: Current altitude away from the Moon; 377 nautical miles [698 km].

a08_0685700-pao.speaker: Lovell
a08_0685700-pao.text: We'll see you on the other side. [Long pause.]

a08_0685700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0685700-pao.text: You heard the remark of Jim Lovell. 'Thanks a lot troops. We'll see you on the other side.'

a08_0685700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0685700-pao.text: We have a correction to that voice from the spacecraft. That was Bill Anders.

a08_0685751-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0685751-pao.text: Apollo 8, 10 seconds to go [to LOS]. You're Go all the way.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Well, the main thing to be is be cool.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0685800-onboard.text: It's up to 80 [Fahrenheit, 27°C] in the cockpit.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: No, I think - just when my clothes touch me, it gets cold, huh?

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Well, I'll tell you, gentlemen; that Moon is pretty close.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Pressure should go down to about 1,500 [psi, 10.3 MPa].

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Helium pressure will be going down to about 1,500.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Okay. Main Bus Ties, going On.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: A is On; B is On.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: TVC [SPS Thrust Vector Control] Servo Power, one, AC 1, Main A.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Okay. Stand by for the primary TVC check.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Okay. Go ahead and start Pitch 1.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Verify no MTVC [SPS Manual Thrust Vector Control].

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Okay, SCS sec - TV - secondary TVC check.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Okay. You want to trim it one more time.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Proceed. We're right there [at the correct attitude].

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Oh, you Entered instead of - you Entered, Jim. All right, you would bypass [garble]

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Okay, Rotational Control Power, Direct, both, Main A, Main B.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Okay, at 2 minutes to go, we'll hit the Delta-V Thrust A, Normal.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: I'm going to give you a Go...

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Hey, you know the one thing. The problem is we didn't go to trim.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Yeah, I said trim - it goes to trim...

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0685800-onboard.text: On that horizon, boy, I can't see squat out there.

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0685800-onboard.text: You want to turn off your lights to check it?

a08_0685800-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0685800-onboard.text: Well, come on - Let's - What's, what's the....

a08_0690100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0690100-pao.text: Bill Anders again with that remark, 'Roger', when advised 10 seconds LOS, you're on your way.

a08_0690100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0690100-pao.text: We've had loss of a signal with Apollo 8 at 68 hours, 58 minutes, 45 seconds. We will watch with continuing interest the AOS clock here in Mission Control.

a08_0690100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0690100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 69 hours now into the flight of Apollo 8. We're going to pick up that transmission when Jerry Carr advised that we were LOS.

a08_0690300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0690300-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 69 hours, 3 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 now traveling over the back side of the Moon. Time of ignition for our Service Propulsion System engine burn; 69 hours, 8 minutes, 52 seconds [sic - planned time of ignition is 069:08:19.52]. Some - a little over four minutes away from this time, Apollo 8 will perform its burn in the guidance and navigation mode, using the onboard computer and the DSKY - the Display Keyboard. To do this, the crew will key into one of their guidance programs on the DSKY. The Service Propulsion System gimbal is trimmed before

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Well, I see two - Look at that - fantastic!

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: See it? Fan - fantastic, but you know, I still have trouble telling, the holes from the bumps.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0690645-onboard.text: All right, all right, come on. You're going to look at that for a long time.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0690645-onboard.text: 1 minute. Come on, Jim, let's watch it real good.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Okay. Okay, average g, On; Flight Recorder's going to Record; EMS Mode, Auto.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: No ullage required. Standing by for Engine On Enable. [Press] Proceed when you get it [that being Verb 99 on the DSKY].

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Start your watch when you get ignition.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Stand by for Delta-V, Normal, B.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: We got them. Pressure's holding good.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Alright. Everything's good over here, so far.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: That's four ball valves; everything is great.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Drifting a little bit in roll.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Great shape. Pressures are holding. Helium's coming down nicely. All the systems are Go.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: We're past 2 minutes; we're in mode 30. Free area for flange Temp. Thing is looking good.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: You know, it seems like about 3-g's.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Okay, you're running a little bit longer on the time on the computer. I got 58, 6, 5, Stand by.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0690645-onboard.text: It went a little bit over, I think.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Okay, Delta-V Thrust, A and B, Off.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Verify thrust is Off; it is Off; helium valves are okay; pressure is static; Flight Recorder okay.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Got it. TVC Servo Power, 1 and 2. Off.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Flight Recorder's Off; Main Bus tie's going Off; A is Off; B is Off.

a08_0690645-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0690645-onboard.text: Hold it a second or we're not going to null any.

a08_0690800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0690800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 69 hours, 8 minutes. Apollo 8 is now less than 30 seconds away from the planned time of Lunar - the Lunar Orbit Insertion burn. The crew should be now looking at the countdown to ignition on the face of their Display and Keyboard. Heads down, they should be seeing the features, the rugged features over the back side of the Moon moving below them at a high rate of speed. Standing by, this is Apollo Control.

a08_0691000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0691000-pao.text: Although we will not know until we reacquire, their retrograde burn with the Service Propulsion System engine should be progressing now, assuming no last minute complications. We won't know, however, until we acquire.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Hold it a second or we're not going to null any.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: SPS Pitch 1 and 2, Yaw 1 and 2 circuit breakers, Open.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Verb 82, Enter. Check it at zero [Program 00, where the computer is not running a major program]; I'd better go to zero, now.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: You want to put that in the other state vector, too, don't you?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Well, now is no time for congratulations yet.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: No, we get stuck with that on the carrier. Okay, Verb 82, Enter.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: We go to [Verb] 37 and then P00, though.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: That's it. Dig out the Flight Plan.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Whew! Well, we answered it. They're meteorites, aren't they? (Laughter.)

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Hey, I don't see a thing. Where are we?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: It looks like a big - looks like a big beach down there.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Let me have the Flight Plan.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Holy cow, it's completely blank here.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Have we got all the gimbal motors off and all that sort of thing?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: You want to take some pictures, Bill?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Let's just go by the - whatever the Flight Plan says there.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Let's see what it says to do. SPS monitor, you're all through with that? Camera Prep.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Okay, Jim has got to get them out or I'll have to - one of us - both of us probably had best get them out.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Yeah, I'll just take a look here a minute.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Don't we - we have a lot of time for looking; let's get those cameras out. Here, do you want to stick those in, Jim? Please, when you go by?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Can I call a Verb 83 here, Jim?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Yeah, you can do that. You're below 482 miles or whatever it is.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: What do you need? Who are you talking to, me?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Yes, I thought you said something about Verb 97?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: You get the camera equipment, and I'll get this stuff out.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Okay, what's our camera configuration, Frank?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Okay, stand by a minute while I get...

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Call them out real loud, because I'm going off the air.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Alright, I'm supposed to - Let's see; 16, 18, new C, exposure, 1/250th; 1 foot per second, one Mag[azine].

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Hey, you know something; it's gray, huh?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Okay, I've got to roll right, so watch out.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: You got that thing running, Bill?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: 2; 150; new; black and white; mag D.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Okay. Okay, mag D. I got it off the camera. 70 millimeter?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Doesn't say anything about filters. Oh, yes, red and black filter, U-4.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Something went flying down when we started burning, didn't it?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Did I write on there that - the orbit we are in?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: It was just what they told me, yes - 169.1 by 60.5 [nautical miles, 313.2 by 112 km].]

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Okay. Okay, when I give the burn status report there, will you...

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Hey, look at - Can you put these cameras someplace? Stash them against the back of your bulkhead. Stash this back there, too.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Are these cameras all set up right?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: That's what I thought: it doesn't work.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Well, that - the camera doesn't work.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: You want me to try it out?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: We're not that hard up; don't worry about it.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: I just want to take a picture.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Hey, look; just slow down and take your time. Okay.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Okay. Bill, get me MSFN, will you?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Oh, is it that late? Okay, I thought it was...

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: It says I'm supposed to run one mag here of 16-millimeter; new color exposure [means exterior film], 1/250th, spot, 1 foot [means frame] per second.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Did you take your bracket up?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Boy, there're no shadows in those craters down there. Are we near the subsolar point?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Well, we're pitch down. We're going around it.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Jim, have you unstowed the orbital charts?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Yeah, I'm in the process right now. I've got part of them unstowed.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Why don't we put it - why don't we temporarily stow it someplace? You're never going to use this thing at all? I think you're making a big mistake using that 250-millimeter [lens].

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Where do we start doing the fan work, Frank?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Well, first of all, we've got to got these cameras set up.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Bill, that's not in the Flight Plan.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: You want me to take pictures with that 16-millimeter?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: New color exposure [means exterior film], 1/250th, spot[meter], 1 foot [means frame] per second; one whole magazine they want.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Trying to figure out where we are, Frank.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: We're passing over Brand right now.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Holy cow, there's no resolution whatso - there's no shadows on the craters.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Hey, there we go. There we are.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Well, listen, Bill, if this is the way it goes, the way you say, look at that.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: You have it all the way in, Frank?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Yeah. There's a stop on that thing; it won't go any higher than that.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Gee, you ought to get a picture of Tsiolkovsky.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Hey, how am I going to get any fan, with this window the way it is?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: I'm going to have to use another window.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: What do you want this on, Bill?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Oh, where's the other Flight Plan?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Okay, be about - Going to f/8, Frank.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0691315-onboard.text: And we just passed the subsolar point.

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: You through with the Flight Plan?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Can I have that other Flight Plan when you get a chance?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Are you hooked on to them, Bill?

a08_0691315-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0691315-onboard.text: Houston, Houston, this is Apollo 8. Over.

a08_0691500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0691500-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Now we are in our period of the longest wait thus far in the mission. We're 19 minutes, 50 seconds awayfrom acquisition at this time. During Mission Control simulations, this was a good time for coffee breaks for the flight controllers, but that is not true today. Continuing to monitor, this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0691500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0691500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 69 hours, 15 minutes now into the flight. Our display readings now show an altitude of 86 nautical miles [159 km], a velocity reading of 8,355 [feet per second, 2,547 m/s]: this last reading assuming that we did not have a burn. Our AOS [Acquisition Of Signal] at this time; 16 minutes, 40 seconds. If, for any reason, the Service Propulsion System engine did not burn, we would see the spacecraft perhaps 10 minutes before a normal acquisition time. So here in Mission Control, continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0692300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0692300-pao.text: Houston here. In Mission Control Center, Cliff Charlesworth getting our - correction there - Glynn Lunney we should say, getting ready to talk to his flight control team. Our time-of-acquisition clock now reading 9 minutes, 45 seconds and we're continuing to watch it. Meanwhile our top clock is counting forward, now reading 25 seconds. The top clock was used to denote an acquisition time if we had a no-burn situation. We will continue to monitor here in Mission Control Center.

a08_0692800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0692800-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Just under four minutes away now from our time of acquisition with Apollo 8. Apollo 8 still out of range, should be rolling 180 degrees shortly, if not already, to establish S-band High Gain Antenna communications with the ground. We're standing by in Mission Control. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0692900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0692900-pao.text: Mark. Three minutes from predicted time of acquisition. Standing by.

a08_0693000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0693000-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Mark, two minutes from predicted time of acquisition.

a08_0693200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0693200-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Mark one minute from predicted time of acquisition.

a08_0693200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0693200-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Jerry Carr has placed a call. We're standing by. We've heard nothing yet, but we're standing by.

a08_0693202.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693202.text: Go ahead, Houston, (This is) Apollo 8. Burn complete. Our orbit (is) 160.9 [sic] by 60.5; 169.1 by 60.5.

a08_0693202.speaker: Carr
a08_0693202.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Roger, 169.1 by 60.5. Good to hear your voice. [Long pause.]

a08_0693300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0693300-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. We've acquired signal but no voice contact yet. We're standing by.

a08_0693300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0693300-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. We're looking at engine data, and it looks good, tank pressures look good. We have not talked yet with the crew, but we're standing by.

a08_0693300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0693300-pao.text: We've got it! We've got it! Apollo 8 now in lunar orbit! There's a cheer in this room! This is Apollo Control, Houston, switching now to the voice of Jim Lovell.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Are we on the High Gain, Jim? Bill?

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: What are you doing here? Let's get rid of that.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Roger. You're coming in very weak. Our orbit is 169 by 60.5.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Give them the whole [burn] report there, Jim.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693414-onboard.text: I think I'm talking to myself.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Why don't you get a Roger for the [DSE] dump we sent then?

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Okay, that's - Let me go into High Gain.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read? How do you read Apollo 8, Houston?

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693414-onboard.text: You taking that at one frame per second?

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Yes, that's what it says to.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: I hear - They're reading us now.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693414-onboard.text: There we go. Houston, Apollo 8. Over.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Are we hooked on with the High Gain?

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693414-onboard.text: They came through at one time, didn't they?

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Well, look here - this DSKY is way up.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Bill, how come this is so high here now?

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Now, Jim, let's get this problem squared away here, or we won't be going anywhere.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Well, you might reverify it again. It's the one next to the secondary one that you had turned on.

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693414-onboard.text: Can you get water to it?

a08_0693414-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0693414-onboard.text: How's the secondary one - primary one doing - secondary one doing, Bill?

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Verify your evaporator water control [is] in Automatic. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8. Apollo 8. This is Houston, Houston. Over.

a08_0693524.speaker: Borman
a08_0693524.text: Roger, Houston. We read you loud and clear. How do you read us?

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, This is Houston. Reading you loud and clear now. And verify your evaporator water control panel switch to the Auto position. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: Burn status report as follows: Burn on time. Burn time 4 minutes, 6½ seconds; V GX , minus 1.4; attitudes nominal, no trim, V GY was zero, V GZ was plus 0.2, Delta-V C was minus 20.2. Orbit, 169.1 by 60.5.

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. The burn on time. Burn time of 4:06.5. V GX is minus 1.4. [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8. Houston. Verify your Evap. water control on panel 382 is Auto. Your Evap. Out temperature is high. Over.

a08_0693524.speaker: Anders
a08_0693524.text: Houston. Apollo 8. Roger. Primary Evap. is Auto. H 2 flow Auto. Do you recommend activating the secondary water boiler?

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Re-verify manual valve on panel 382, Evaporator water control, Automatic. Over.

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Recommend you activate your secondary water evaporator. [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Anders
a08_0693524.text: Secondary Evap. coming on the line.

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Turn off your DSE and we'll go to high bit rate. Over.

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8. This is Houston. I'll continue my readback of the burn status report. Copied V GX , zero; V GY , zero; V GZ , 1.2; Delta-V Charlie, minus 20.2. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Anders
a08_0693524.text: Stand by; he's getting the chart out again.

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Roger. Understand; 0.2 on V GZ . [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Anders
a08_0693524.text: Houston. This is Apollo 8. We're on malfunction 1 of 6, going through step 1 to step 2. Over.

a08_0693524.speaker: Anders
a08_0693524.text: Looks like the boiler dried out somewhere along the line.

a08_0693524.speaker: Borman
a08_0693524.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. I'd like to confirm that burn status report. V GX was minus 1.4. V GY , zero. V GZ , 0.2, minus .2 that is. Delta-V C was minus 20.2.

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8. This is Houston. Roger. I'll read back again. The burn was on time, 4 minutes and 6½ seconds; V GX , minus 1.4; trim nominal; V GY , 0; V GZ , minus 0.2; Delta-V Charlie, minus 20.2. Over.

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Roger. We copy your apogee and perigee. [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. We concur. [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Anders
a08_0693524.text: Okay. Houston, keep a good eye on it.

a08_0693524.speaker: Anders
a08_0693524.text: Tell Ken, nice job on the malfunction procedures.

a08_0693524.speaker: Anders
a08_0693524.text: Give us a call when you think we ought to stop the secondary boiler, Houston.

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: Roger. For information, we're passing over just to the side of the crater Langrenus at this time, going into the Sea of Fertility.

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, Houston. What does the ole Moon look like from 60 miles? Over. [Pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: Okay, Houston. The Moon is essentially gray, no color; looks like plaster of Paris or sort of a grayish beach sand. We can see quite a bit of detail. The Sea of Fertility doesn't stand out as well here as it does back on Earth. There's not as much contrast between that and the surrounding craters. [Pause.] The craters are all rounded off. There's quite a few of them, some of them are newer. [Pause.] Many of them look like - especially the round ones - look like hit by meteorites or projectiles of some sort. [Pause.] Langrenus is quite a huge crater; it's got a central cone to it. [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: And coming up now in the Sea of Fertility are the old friends Messier and Pickering that I looked about so much on Earth.

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: And I can see the rays coming out of blaze [?] Pickering. We're coming up now near our P-1 initial site which I'm going to try and see. Be advised the round window, the hatch window, is completely iced over; we cannot use it. Bill and I are sharing the rendezvous window.

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. Got any more information on those rays? Over.

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: Roger. The rays out of Pickering are quite faint from here; there are two different groups coming - going to the left, they don't appear to be - have any depth to them at all, just rays coming out.

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: They look like just changes in the color of the mare. [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Bill, if you can tear yourself away from that window, we'd like you to turn off the secondary evaporator. Over.

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. You can leave that secondary pump on for just a few minutes. Over.

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: Okay. Over to my right are the Pyrenee Mountains coming up and we're just about over Messier and Pickering [Messier A] right now. Our first initial point is easily seen from our altitude. We're getting quite a bit of contrast as we appear - as we approach the terminator. [Pause.] The view appears to be good, no reflection of the Sun back to our eyes; it appears that visibility at this particular spot is excellent. It's very easy to pick out our first initial point; and over this mountain chain we can see the second initial point, the Triangular Mountain. [Pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Anders
a08_0693524.text: Now we're coming upon the craters Colombo and Gutenberg. Very good detail visible. We can see the long parallel faults or grabens. [Pause.] And they run through the mare material right into the highland material. [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: We're directly over our first initial point now for B-1. It's almost impossible to miss, very easy to pick out and we can look right over into the second initial point.

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: I can see very clearly the five crater star formation which we had on our lunar charts.

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: And right now, I'm trying to pick out visually B-1. [Pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Roger Jim. Bill, you can turn off the secondary Evap. pump now. [Pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Borman
a08_0693524.text: Roger. How about giving us a system status, please?

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: Okay. I've got B-1 in sight now, Houston. [Pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: It's very easy to spot. You can see the entire rims of the craters from here with, of course, the white crescent on the far side were the Sun is shining on it. The shadows are quite lengthy now. Maskelyne B has quite a few shadows off of it, but could be recognized. Just to the west of Maskelyne B, we start going to the terminator. The terminator is actually quite sharp over the Pyrenees, and it's - I can't see anything in Earthshine at this present time. Bill says that he can see things out the side window since he's not looking down on sunshine on the Moon. [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. All systems are Go. We're evaluating the strip charts on your SPS burn and we'll give you a read-out on that shortly. Over.

a08_0693524.speaker: Borman
a08_0693524.text: Roger. Thank you. It's seemed smooth. Do you need high bit rate anymore? [Pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Roger. We'd like high bit rate. We have dumped your DSE, and we'd like to stick with high bit rate for a while.

a08_0693524.speaker: Lovell
a08_0693524.text: Well, we're just about over Maskelyne B now, and our target is just directly below us. [Long pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. If you want the recorder now, it's yours. [Pause.]

a08_0693524.speaker: Carr
a08_0693524.text: Apollo 8, Houston. MSFN [Manned Spaceflight Tracking Network] tracking is comparing very well with your onboard nav.

a08_0693524.speaker: Borman
a08_0693524.text: ...we lost radio contact at the exact second you predicted.

a08_0693524.speaker: Borman
a08_0693524.text: Are you sure you didn't turn off the transmitters at that time?

a08_0693900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0693900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control Houston. The conversation taking place is with Bill Anders aboard the spacecraft.

a08_0694000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0694000-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Our ground data closely coincides with that aboard the spacecraft.

a08_0694300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0694300-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. What you're hearing here is checkout procedure of the Environmental Control System. The voice principally from the spacecraft, that of Bill Anders, the systems engineer member of the team aboard.

a08_0694400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0694400-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Our ground readings on this orbit; 168 nautical miles in apolune, perilune of 60.4 nautical miles [311.1 by 111.9 km].

a08_0694400-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0694400-pao.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. I'd like to confirm that burn status report. V GX was minus 1.4. V GY , zero. V GZ , 0.2, minus .2 that is. Delta-V C was minus 20.2.

a08_0694500-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0694500-pao.text: Roger. We copy your apogee and perigee. [Long pause.]

a08_0695000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0695000-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. So you've had the first status report from an Apollo crew in lunar orbit. The unmanned Lunar Orbiter spacecraft traversed the Moon, perhaps over 10,000 times, but this is the first that man aboard, in this case Frank Borman, reported to his compatriots here on Earth.

a08_0695000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0695000-pao.text: As you heard, Apollo 8 approaching the Sea of Fertility.

a08_0695000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0695000-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Our first batch of ground tracking data shows agreement in velocity within one foot per second with that of the spacecraft.

a08_0695900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0695900-pao.text: The principal speaker that you've heard during most of this discourse has been Jim Lovell but that last voice was that of Bill Anders.

a08_0700000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0700000-pao.text: The reference to B-1 is a landmark, a landmark which relates to a projected landing site.

a08_0700000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0700000-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. As a matter of interest, spacecraft Commander Frank Borman's heart rate has been ranging between 78 and 80 since we acquired.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: We completed target 72 strip and target 90 strip and the terminator photography to the south.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, we're going to get updates. And a P52.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Can I have the other lunar flight plan there, Jim?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Are we on high gain, Bill?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Well, this is [garble] see if I can [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Here's the - I'll bet you that's what we're supposed to do.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Have you got the Delta counter over there, please?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Those two strips and the terminator photography on camera I were taken on magazine E which is now reading 29 exposures.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: I don't think so. Okay, I'm going out [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: What did you take a picture of, Frank? Do you remember?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: And Frank took a took a picture on camera 2, magazine A, which is now reading 40.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Now we're going to change - take off magazine A.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Jim, didn't I hand you 4 magazine over there?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, what I meant for you to do [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Well, it looks - sure looks that way.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Have you charged these batteries, Bill?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, I'll [garble] lights out [garble] I could just mark them without even...

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, the next thing we put up is my [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, Jim, go ahead and eat.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, let me see whether I have this [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: This thing must be [garble]. Oh no, don't tell me the thing dried out.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: No, the boiler isn't acting up; it just dried out.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Did you verify all the systems?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Now don't - Let's not even screw with the telephoto, okay, Frank?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Well, ought to use that wide angle. Then you could really...

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Jim? Have you got time to get that red filter out of there or not?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Out of that other - I'll get it; I'll get it.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Did you see that other map around here someplace?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: No, I've got the flat one; the other - folded one.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Well, I'm not worried about these [garble], but I am about the other two.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Frank, what else have you got, [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Well, I know we may need it. I got some more for you. [Garble] remember...

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Did you bring the temporary stowage bag?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: What other crises by the board?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: I don't need any if you want to know. After what I've got in my pocket, I (laughter) can go anyplace for a while.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: How about just holding that [garble] tape [garble]. The thing is, the damn thing has 16 moving parts.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Well, I got it, but [garble] I'll bet - You can just put a piece of tape on it so it stays [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, what's this coming up [garble]? [Garble] coming up here.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: At 71 hours - exactly - it's 70:21 right now. The realignment has been completed already. It's an eat period for Bill, eat period for myself; prepare to do GDC align to the IMU [Inertial Measurement Unit]. Okay, at 70:55...

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, yes, let me [garble]. At 70:55, you're going to pitch up. Your ORDEAL, 180, 250, and 00.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay. And we're going to have to share a window here, Bill at 71...

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Yes, because - I've got to get out the [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Well, I was real worried about the evaporator.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Frank, that's the best I can do for you. If you can just hold it and - like that and take the picture.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, now look, can you - could you stick that [garble] stick it in the holder behind your head. I'll take that film out of your way - ...get a chance, stow it, that'll be the best thing to do.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Jim, did you get that Flight Plan?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Yes, I got it right down here [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Why don't we keep it right in here, I guess and...

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Well, listen, how about - now [garble]. Okay, [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: We could use Frank on the keypunch for the control point.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Yes, either way, it makes no difference because you have that...

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0700258-onboard.text: I've got a keypunch here. I [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Yes, I think, Frank, [garble] the attitude.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, Frank, you want to configure your 16-millimeter camera as follows: you've got two thirds of a magazine in there.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, we're sticking - magazine J onto the 16-millimeter camera, and removing magazine H. We had magazine H running at one frame per second, and what was the f-stop - you remember? F/8 all the way through the pass; we didn't get around to changing the f-stop.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, now it starts at f/2.8, 1/250th of a second. Sorry, but I got the wrong [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: One - f/2.8, one frame per second.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Well, Frank, I'm going to have to give you - Would you remind me to give you new exposures every now and then as on this map? I'll have - I'll have the map right in front of me so I can ... without any trouble. The only thing is you have to remind me.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay. Tell them I've got the earth in the sextant.

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: Okay, Frank? Would you start the 16-millimeter camera when you're coming across the terminator with the pass. Okay?

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: I'll take the spotmeter readings and be able to tell you what the [garble] when we're all set for TV, and then [garble].

a08_0700258-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0700258-onboard.text: I'm ready for a map update.

a08_0700300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0700300-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Our tracking data from the ground still compares very well with the guidance and navigation computer on the spacecraft.

a08_0700722.speaker: Carr
a08_0700722.text: Apollo 8. This is Houston. Are you eating?

a08_0700722.speaker: Carr
a08_0700722.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Are you eating dinner?

a08_0700722.speaker: Borman
a08_0700722.text: Negative. We'll have breakfast in a little while here.

a08_0700722.speaker: Carr
a08_0700722.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. When you go into the dark in about 7 or 8 minutes, I have some words for you on the filters for the wide-angle lens, for your TV camera. Over.

a08_0700722.speaker: Carr
a08_0700722.text: Roger. Let me know when you're ready to copy. [Long pause.]

a08_0700722.speaker: Carr
a08_0700722.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Any words on Earthshine? Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0700722.speaker: Anders
a08_0700722.text: Earth - Earthshine is about as expected, Houston. Not as much detail, of course, as in the sunlight, but you can see the large craters quite distinctly, and you can see the albedo contacts quite distinctly. And, also, the - there's a good three-dimensional view of the rims of the larger craters.

a08_0700722.speaker: Anders
a08_0700722.text: I think our high-speed film will be able to pick some of this stuff up quite well.

a08_0701200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0701200-pao.text: The reference there was to Loss of Signal as they went over the back side of the Moon.

a08_0701200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0701200-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. As Apollo 8 passes over the night portion of the Moon, the guidance and navigation - the platform is to be aligned. This during periods of darkness, since the spacecraft remains in an inertially fixed attitude for this procedure. This leaves lunar daylight periods for maneuverability needed for photography and visual observations. At 70 hours, 12 minutes, continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0701244.speaker: Borman
a08_0701244.text: Go ahead with your information on the filter, Houston.

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. We recommend you use a wide-angle lens on this particular TV run. You can use the telephoto lens with the same setup as yesterday's TV show. However, we recommend a wide-angle lens. Step number 1, tape the single red filter to the red filter on the red/blue filter holder; do it so that the filter slide still functions. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0701244.speaker: Anders
a08_0701244.text: Go ahead.

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Roger. Step number 2, attach the filter holder to the lens with tape on the top and bottom. Do this with the slide forward. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0701244.speaker: Borman
a08_0701244.text: Go ahead.

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Roger. Then at the end of your second rev TV pass, or on request from here, we'd like you to remove that red filter from the holder and transmit briefly with it that way, then slide it over the blue side for your final transmission. Over.

a08_0701244.speaker: Borman
a08_0701244.text: We got you.

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Okay, Frank.

a08_0701244.speaker: Borman
a08_0701244.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Standing by to record TEI-1 and TEI-2.

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Your TEI-1 and -2 PADs you received last pass are still good. Using these PADs, your next midcourse would be less than 20 feet per second. Over.

a08_0701244.speaker: Borman
a08_0701244.text: Roger. Understand. [Long pause.]

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We have all of the SPS experts looking at your data now. The preliminary look is very good, and we'll give you some final words later.

a08_0701244.speaker: Borman
a08_0701244.text: Roger. We could feel the chug when we threw in bank B - not a chug, but we could feel the additional thrust.

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Roger. Copy. [Pause.]

a08_0701244.speaker: Anders
a08_0701244.text: Houston, be advised on this red/blue filter technique on the TV. You cannot slide the two filters out of the way with them taped onto the TV camera. So I suggest we do red, blue, and then take them off. [Pause.]

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Roger. We concur, but make sure that the little red filter is taped over the big one. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0701244.speaker: Anders
a08_0701244.text: Rog. You don't want the red fil - you want the blue by itself. Is that correct?

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: That's affirmative, Bill. [Pause.]

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Bill, we'd like you to use the double red filter for the first transmission. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0701244.speaker: Anders
a08_0701244.text: Roger. In work. [Long pause.]

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0701244.speaker: Anders
a08_0701244.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. If you should decide that you want to roll heads up on rev 2, one thing to remember, be sure you yaw 45 degrees right in order to maintain your High Gain Antenna comm. Over.

a08_0701244.speaker: Borman
a08_0701244.text: We will not do that; we're going to stick with the Flight Plan and make the best we can here.

a08_0701244.speaker: Carr
a08_0701244.text: Roger, Frank. [Pause.]

a08_0701244.speaker: Borman
a08_0701244.text: As usual, in the real world, the Flight Plan looks a lot fuller than it did in Florida.

a08_0701900-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0701900-pao.text: We will not do that; we're going to stick with the Flight Plan and make the best we can here.

a08_0702701-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0702701-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. A period of relative quiet; perhaps the crew has decided to start their first meal in lunar orbit.

a08_0702719.speaker: Carr
a08_0702719.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We need an O 2 purge now. [Pause.]

a08_0702719.speaker: Anders
a08_0702719.text: Roger. And we're standing by for a map update.

a08_0702719.speaker: Lovell
a08_0702719.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Just for information, after we completed P52, I've acquired the Earth in the sextant. It's quite a sight from here.

a08_0702719.speaker: Borman
a08_0702719.text: How are the systems experts on the SPS coming, Jerry?

a08_0702719.speaker: Carr
a08_0702719.text: They're still working, Frank; another five or ten minutes.

a08_0702719.speaker: Carr
a08_0702719.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Your SPS data; looking real good. It is just a matter of getting it all in from the site and getting it looked at.

a08_0702900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0702900-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. We're now less than 30 minutes away from our LOS time on this, the first revolution in lunar orbit. Continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0703042.speaker: Carr
a08_0703042.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We'd like to take about five minutes of high bit rate. Over.

a08_0703042.speaker: Borman
a08_0703042.text: Roger. Five minutes of high bit rate coming on.

a08_0703042.speaker: Carr
a08_0703042.text: Apollo 8, Houston, with a map update.

a08_0703042.speaker: Borman
a08_0703042.text: Go ahead with the map update.

a08_0703042.speaker: Carr
a08_0703042.text: Roger, Frank. Map update. Rev 1/2, no change; rev 2/3 follows: 73:04:57, 73:09:37, 73:19:01, 73:48:53, 74:24:23. Remarks: Bravo one, 74:16:24. Over.

a08_0703042.speaker: Carr
a08_0703042.text: Roger. We show you 23 minutes to LOS.

a08_0703042.speaker: Anders
a08_0703042.text: Roger. And are you going to dump the tape? [Long pause.]

a08_0703042.speaker: Carr
a08_0703042.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. You're Go for Rev 2. All systems are Go. SPS evaluation is still underway and looking good. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0703042.speaker: Borman
a08_0703042.text: Understand; Go for Rev 2. Thank you.

a08_0703042.speaker: Carr
a08_0703042.text: Roger, Apollo 8. We're still using the tape recorder. We'll dump it in a little bit. [Long pause.]

a08_0703042.speaker: Carr
a08_0703042.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. The recorder is yours. You can go to low bit rate.

a08_0703500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0703500-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. We've just received data from our Flight Surgeon that Frank Borman's peak heart rate at LOI-1 read 130. The same reading that he had, as a matter of fact, at lift off. Thought we would pass that along. Continuing to monitor, this is Apollo Control.

a08_0703500-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0703500-pao.text: Roger, Apollo 8. We're still using the tape recorder. We'll dump it in a little bit. [Long pause.]

a08_0703500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0703500-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. You just heard that Go for Rev 2. Flight Director Glynn Lunney...

a08_0703755.speaker: Carr
a08_0703755.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Request Biomed switch, Center. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0704350.speaker: Carr
a08_0704350.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Put your Telemetry Input switch to Low. Over.

a08_0704350.speaker: Borman
a08_0704350.text: Houston, Apollo 8. We're in the process of preparing meal 4, day - correction - day 4, meal A.

a08_0704529-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0704529-onboard.text: A little bit of - a little bit of - Left yaw - a little bit.

a08_0704529-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0704529-onboard.text: [Garble] we'll just have to get one. But you can't for 30 minutes [garble]. Well, you can [garble].

a08_0704529-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0704529-onboard.text: This is a report of the photography accomplished on Rev 1. We got target 68 [Langrenus], target 72 [craters near Colombo], target 90 [Capella], and the terminator photography - near-side terminator, Rev 1, south. I had cameras 1 and 2 configured properly. Camera - camera 2 now reads - simply one exposure on Mag G. That's the high speed; we've had zero exposures on Mag G.

a08_0704529-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0704529-onboard-nr.text: A little bit of - a little bit of - Left yaw - a little bit.

a08_0704529-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0704529-onboard-nr.text: [Garble] we'll just have to get one. But you can't for 30 minutes [garble]. Well, you can [garble].

a08_0704529-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0704529-onboard-nr.text: This is a report of the photography accomplished on Rev 1. We got target 68 [Langrenus], target 72 [craters near Colombo], target 90 [Capella], and the terminator photography - near-side terminator, Rev 1, south. I had cameras 1 and 2 configured properly. Camera - camera 2 now reads - simply one exposure on Mag G. That's the high speed; we've had zero exposures on Mag G.

a08_0704813.speaker: Anders
a08_0704813.text: Are you going to be able to dump that tape prior to LOS? [Pause.]

a08_0704813.speaker: Carr
a08_0704813.text: Roger. Bill, they say they've already dumped the tape, and it's almost totally clean. [Pause.]

a08_0704813.speaker: Carr
a08_0704813.text: That means you have got about 2 minutes of low bit rate on there, but the rest is clean. Over.

a08_0704813.speaker: Anders
a08_0704813.text: The high bit rate of the burn wasn't on there?

a08_0704813.speaker: Carr
a08_0704813.text: Negative. We've already dumped and got that. [Long pause.]

a08_0704813.speaker: Anders
a08_0704813.text: Okay. Let me know when you're going to dump it next time, Jerry. I understand we're Go now on the DSE. Have you got any voice off of it?

a08_0704813.speaker: Carr
a08_0704813.text: Apollo 8, Houston. The voice quality on your tape was just fair to middling. We were able to monitor your burn and hear most of that pretty well. [Pause.]

a08_0704813.speaker: Anders
a08_0704813.text: Roger. Did you get a report of the photography accomplished, or is that on the tape at present?

a08_0704813.speaker: Anders
a08_0704813.text: Okay. We'll put it on the tape now.

a08_0705100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0705100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. Now less than 5 minutes away from Loss of Signal on our first revolution.

a08_0705153.speaker: Carr
a08_0705153.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You're 4 minutes and 40 seconds from LOS. I would like a reconfirmation on your S-band Aux switch in the Downvoice Backup position. Over.

a08_0705153.speaker: Borman
a08_0705153.text: Negative; it's in Normal voice. We will go Downvoice Backup.

a08_0705153.speaker: Carr
a08_0705153.text: Roger. Request you leave it there forever. Over.

a08_0705153.speaker: Borman
a08_0705153.text: Roger. In Downvoice Backup now. [Long pause.]

a08_0705153.speaker: Carr
a08_0705153.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. All systems are Go. You're still Go for rev 2. Over.

a08_0705532.speaker: Carr
a08_0705532.text: Apollo 8, Houston. 10 seconds to LOS. All systems Go.

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard.text: Mag H - When you're through taking Mag H, I'll [garble].

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard.text: Mag H was on the 16-millimeter cam...

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard.text: [Garble].

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard.text: ...16-millimeter camera, run at one frame per second, at - Look at that f-stop.

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard.text: On f/8 through the entire Rev.

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard.text: We now have Mag - What was that again, J? - Mag J installed for the second pass.

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0705640-onboard.text: Are you all set with the TV, Bill?

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard.text: Oh, we've got a long time.

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard.text: The TV doesn't come until at 30 minutes [garble].

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard.text: Next - next AOS?

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard.text: [Garble] the Flight Plan.

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0705640-onboard.text: Next AOS is 30.

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0705640-onboard.text: Yes.

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard.text: 71:30 would be [garble].

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0705640-onboard.text: [Garble] half an hour.

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard.text: Is that right?

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard.text: Yes.

a08_0705640-onboard.speaker: Lovell
