a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: [Garble] take a look at [garble] the Flight Plan.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Give me that Flight Plan there real quick, will you, Frank?

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Okay, let's track along the ground and run the camera [garble] time.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Here - It'll - At the terminator, it will be - 2.8, and it'll stay that way for a good while.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: [Garbled.]

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: [Garble], we're looking good.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Okay, starting on the right now, [garble].

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: No, no, no, don't - don't write it down.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Well, you're going to get...

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: No, it - it - Wait, wait'll it comes up...

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Well, why not? Why don't you get it tracking? That thing's just going into the terminator.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Well, I'd wait, or you're never going to make it through the pass. It's the other terminator that's more important. Just take a couple here, Frank.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: All right. We should be over America right now.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Now, we're passing over America.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: There she is.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: And we're coming up on von Braun.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Okay, we're to the north of our track...

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Yes.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: ...aren't we? No, we're not! My gosh, we're just about on it!

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Now, can you turn up the lights a little bit because we need this thing because we're going to - turn the light [garble].

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: We're coming [garble] right now [garble].

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: You want this thing going now, Bill?

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Yes, good.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: 3.5 still [the required F-stop on the lens]?

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Huh?

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Yes.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: I don't think the angle is the best, though.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: [Garbled.)

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Oh, you can see out of this one. Bill, this is good lighting for one of those.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Take those pictures [garble.]

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Okay, we got the six pictures of the terminator, south.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: That's the north, Jim. Isn't this America sitting right out here - this big one? Or did you...

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: No, no, we're over - still over America right now. See look at this big picture. I've got the - I've got the photograph on...

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Is this von Braun right here, this big...

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: No, we're right in the middle of America, right now.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: You've got two other craters sticking up [garble].

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Right in the middle of it? Are they those...

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: You still want it 3.5, Bill? I think I...

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: I want you to keep it 2.8 until we've gone 7 minutes. [Garbled.)

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Yes, I know. It doesn't work; it goes out.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: There is the big [garble] down below us.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Is that it?

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Yes. [Garble] down south right now.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Why, the rim of America is very hard to see, isn't it?

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Yes.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Yes.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Okay, you're right, here's von Braun. This must be von Braun, here.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Yes, okay.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Boy, it sure feels like you're running [garble]. Very pretty.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Okay, getting target 10.

a08_0705640-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0705640-onboard-nr.text: Target 10 is mag D, frame...

a08_0710200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0710200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. As Apollo 8 passed over the lunar hill, out of communication, we read an apolune of 168.2 nautical miles [311.5 km], a perilune of 60.3 nautical miles [111.7 km]. Velocity of the spacecraft at that time descending downward from its apogee was 5,224 feet per second [1,592 m/s]. Our current digital indications say that the present velocity is 5,297 feet per second [1,615 m/s]. So at 71 hours, 02 minutes, 35 seconds into this most historic flight; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0712200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0712200-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. 71 hours, 22 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 continuing on its pass over the back side of the Moon. We're some 17 minutes away from time of reacquisition. At this time, Command Module Pilot Jim Lovell should be taking a look at three control points, evenly distributed across the back side of the Moon. These, repeated on later orbits with the optics, are designed primarily as a mapping tool, and increasing data in establishing a point in space. Each control point has two IPs, initial points associated with it. These serve the same homing end purpose to

a08_0712200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0712200-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 71 hours, 32 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 8. We're within 8 minutes of acquiring the Apollo 8 spacecraft now in its second revolution around the Moon which - the first revolution began at a midpoint on the back side. Apollo 8 should be yawing about 45 degrees just about now to establish a proper attitude for TV sighting. We'll continue to monitor as we draw nearer to that point when we reacquire the spacecraft. So at 71 hours, 32 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0712200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0712200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 71 hours, 38 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 8. We're now within 2 minutes of our predicted time of acquisition on this second pass across the front side of the Moon. During this pass, we expect to acquire via television. Our prime tracking site for the TV is the Madrid site. Meanwhile, Glynn Lunney here in Mission Control, has gone around the room, updated all his flight controllers on requirements - Flight Plan requirements for this revolution. And we'll stand by and continue to monitor. At 71 hours, 38 minutes.

a08_0712200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0712200-pao.text: Mark. 1 minute to predicted time of acquisition. Standing by.

a08_0713800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0713800-pao.text: That's Jerry Carr making a call. No reply yet. Standing by. We're receiving telemetry data now. Standing by.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8 with the TV going. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Reading you loud and clear. We see your TV. It's a little bit - little bit clearer.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger. The Moon is very bright and not too distinct in this area. I'll give you a shot of the horizon.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: How's that look? Is it on the top of your picture?

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. It's a good picture - the horizon - we can't see many terrain features as yet. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're beginning to pick up a few craters very dimly. The whole thing is pretty bright.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger. There's not much definition up here either out on the horizon. We're now approaching the craters See [Alden] and Bassett [Scaliger].

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: I'll shift to the rendezvous window.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger, Bill.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We want to take the DSE.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger. You've got it.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. Looks like we've got a real good picture now.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Okay, that's the crater Brand [Danjon].

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Sorry, we missed Carr [Perepelkin].

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Me too. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We're going to need a cryo fan cycle sometime during this pass.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger. Can we wait 'til sunset?

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. We can wait.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Okay. I think we are coming up on Mueller [Meitner] right now. [Long pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: There's a very new bright impact crater. Should be in the field of view now.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger, Bill.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: You see it in the upper part of your screen.

a08_0713946.speaker: Lovell
a08_0713946.text: Say, Bill. How would you describe the color of the Moon from here?

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: The color of the Moon looks, ah, a very whitish gray, like dirty beach sand, and with lots of footprints in it.

a08_0713946.speaker: Lovell
a08_0713946.text: Don't these new craters look like pick-axes striking concrete creating a lot of fine haze dust? [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: There's some interesting features out on the other window. Let me switch windows on you now.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger, Bill. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: You should see the horizon now in the top of your picture.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. We have the horizon, Bill. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: I believe these are the craters now Bassett [Scaliger] and See [Alden].

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger, Bill. If you have the polarizing filter handy, try flipping it in front, would you?

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger.

a08_0713946.speaker: Lovell
a08_0713946.text: Jerry, as a matter of interest, there's a lot of what appears to be very small new craters that have these little white rays radiating from them.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger, Jim. [Long pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. We see the filter going over. [Pause.] Apollo 8, this is Houston. Looks like we have too much light. The polarizing filter doesn't help much. Go ahead and remove it again. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger. It's removed. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Looks like we just got...

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger. We're just passing over the crater Borman [Pasteur], and there's Anders [Backlund] out there, Lovell [Hilbert] is right south of it.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. TV is breaking up now. Okay. We are back with a good picture. Looks like we just have too much light. Our definition is rather weak.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Also, I'm fogging up the window here, Houston, among other problems.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger, Bill. The other window is better than this one.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Yeah, much better picture, Bill. Much better.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: All right. The right side of the camera is pointing retrograde. [Pause.] We are now passing abeam of the crater Houston [Sklodowska]. And I'll shine the camera over there once for the folks in Texas.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: It's a big and sprawly one; It's got those two impact craters, one to the right and one to the left.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger, Bill. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: How's your picture?

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Still about the same, Bill. It's - The terrain's pretty bright. We're not getting much definition at all. [Pause.] Definition on this side is much, much better.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Okay, I think - Okay. We are leaving the window. That gives you an idea how bad our window is.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. This picture now is much better. I guess the light levels are decreasing now.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Okay, we are coming up on the crater Collins [Brunner].

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. What crater is that that's just going off (out of the frame).

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: That's some small impact crater.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: We'll call it John Aaron's.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Okay.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: If he'll keep looking at the systems anyway.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: He just quit looking. [Long pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Lovell
a08_0713946.text: Jerry, another of ID feature: these small impact craters have dark spots in the center, where it appears that they buried in it and hit some new material down below and scattered a lot of fine white dust around them. [Long pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: , Roger. Understand, Jim. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: This - ah, Houston - Apollo 8, This is Houston. Looks like we can see Collins [Brunner] now.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger, there is Collins [Brunner] for you.

a08_0713946.speaker: Lovell
a08_0713946.text: And Collins [Brunner] is right on the edge of Smythe's Sea which we're about to pass over.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8. This is...

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: We are now going across the Smythe Sea. Go ahead.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. We just saw a Stellenword [?] go by.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Rog. He was really in a hurry.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. Picture is much improved now. Getting better all the time.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Roger. The terrain here is, as you can see, not well defined. [Pause.] We're going to start a roll to the left, in order to come across the target area, with the television...

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: ...landing site area.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger, Bill. [Long pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: How is that crater in - right in the middle look now?

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. That's a very good one; that must be O'Neill.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger, Bill. We see O'Neill real well. Also the smaller crater off to the side of it.

a08_0713946.speaker: Anders
a08_0713946.text: That's Dennis.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Borman
a08_0713946.text: Houston. This is Apollo 8. We're going to terminate our program for this pass and get on with preparations for LOI-2, if you say we're Go.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8. This is Houston. Roger.

a08_0713946.speaker: Borman
a08_0713946.text: Okay. Signing off until the ninth rev. Apollo 8.

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0713946.speaker: Carr
a08_0713946.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. Thank you for the look.

a08_0713946.speaker: Borman
a08_0713946.text: Roger.

a08_0714000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0714000-pao.text: The picture is coming in now.

a08_0714000-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0714000-pao.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8 with the TV going. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0714000-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0714000-pao.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Reading you loud and clear. We see your TV. It's a little bit - little bit clearer.

a08_0715400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0715400-pao.text: Apollo - Apollo Control, Houston. Most of those craters identified in the conversation, largely over the east part of this front-side pass are actually unnamed. They have been coded for purposes of this flight. Perhaps you recognized some of the names, names like Bassett, See, and by the way, John Aaron, John is EECOM on the Green Shift. So at 71 hours, 54 minutes; we continue to monitor.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. You have the DSE.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Thank you, Houston.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. Apollo 8, on your backside data, it's pretty much unintelligible. We suggest, Bill, that you recheck the position of your mike for your backside pass and try to speak a little bit louder and more distinctly. The last one we listened to was pretty much unintelligible. Over.

a08_0715502.speaker: Anders
a08_0715502.text: Roger. As soon as we get squared away, we'll give you a real quick real-time summary.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Anders
a08_0715502.text: And, Houston, you might let us know, can we do the red/blue filter exercise with both of these filters - red filters on. Over.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Stand by. [Pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Apollo 8, Houston. Negative. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston with an LOI-2 maneuver PAD. Ready to copy?

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Stand by.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. Standing by. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Okay, Houston. Go ahead.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. LOI-2, SPS/G&N; 46427; minus 0.53, plus 1.41; 073:35:05.70; minus 0135.0; plus all zeros, plus all zeros. Copy?

a08_0715502.speaker: Anders
a08_0715502.text: Roger.

a08_0715502.speaker: Anders
a08_0715502.text: Roger.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. Taurus, Aida. I repeat; Taurus, Aida, Up 16.2, left 0.1; the remainder not applicable. GDC Align, Sirius, Rigel; 129, 155, 010; negative ullage. Horizon window, ignition minus 3, 27 degrees, horizon left. At ignition 18 degrees, horizon left. Before readback, configure for receiving an update. Over.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Roger. Understand. Configure for receiving an update.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Okay. We're in P00 and Accept. Go ahead.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. I'm ready for your readback.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: LOI-2; SPS/G&N; 46427; minus 0.53, plus 1.41; 073:35:05.70; minus 0135.0, plus 0000, plus 0000; 000, 175, 358; 0060.7, plus 0060.6; 0135.0, 0:09, 0126.5; 02, 311.2, 19.7; Taurus, Aida, up 16.2, left 0.1; the remainder not applicable. Sirius, Rigel, 129, 155, 010; no ullage. Ignition minus 3, 27 degrees, ignition, 18 degrees.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. Readback is correct. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Your map update for rev 2/3, no change. Over.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Understand. No change, revs 2/3.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger, Frank. You can expect Go/No Go for the next rev at 20 minutes before LOS Over.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We'll try to make that call 20 minutes before every LOS Over.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Fine. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We have the CSM vector in, starting on the LM. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Lovell
a08_0715502.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Go.

a08_0715502.speaker: Lovell
a08_0715502.text: Roger. Just an interesting feature: on my center window, which has ice on it, it is now beginning to melt. I'm beginning to see through it.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. That's good news.

a08_0715502.speaker: Lovell
a08_0715502.text: And again we're directly over our favorites, Messier and Pickering (Messier A). [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Lovell
a08_0715502.text: The view at this altitude, Houston, is tremendous. There's no trouble picking out features that we learned on the map.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger, Jim, that's good news. What do you think of the lighting situation as far as the range of lighting for good visibility?

a08_0715502.speaker: Lovell
a08_0715502.text: The range from here is outstanding. I wish we had the TV still going because the brown area now is darker. We're just past over the Sea of Fertility, and the mare is darker. The mountain range has got more contrast, has more contrast because of the Sun angle. Bill's got the 16-mm going for us.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger.

a08_0715502.speaker: Lovell
a08_0715502.text: There is a crater, Taruntius, I believe, over there. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Lovell
a08_0715502.text: We'll try to get TV on this at a later time, when we are not getting ready for a burn.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger, Jim. [Pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Lovell
a08_0715502.text: I can see the old second initial point here very well, Mount Marilyn.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Lovell
a08_0715502.text: Houston, at these Sun angles, everything is quite distinct; shadows are good; the ground doesn't have any Sun that returned. It appears very good visibility from these Sun angles.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Lovell
a08_0715502.text: As a matter of fact, Bill just mentioned that the visibility seems to be excellent just about up to the terminator. It's something which I didn't expect. I thought there'd be a little bit more gradual shift to darkness, but it's very sharp and distinct.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger, Jim.

a08_0715502.speaker: Anders
a08_0715502.text: Of course, we're in a very high phase angle now.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, Houston. All of your updates are in; the computer is yours. Over.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: The update block.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. Break. Apollo 8, Houston. Your TEI-2 PAD is good; stand by to copy your TEI-3. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: We're ready for TEI-3.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger, TEI-3; SPS/G&N; 46427; minus 0.53, plus 1.41; 075:31:29.95; plus 2896.0, minus 0045.6, plus 0072.0. Copy?

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Roger.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Roger.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. 033, 000.0, left 1.7; plus 08.83, minus 165.00; 1295.5, 36185, 146:35:07; Sirius, Rigel, 129, 155, 010; ullage, 2 jets, 20 seconds, quads Bravo and Delta. Horizon on the two degree line at ignition minus three minutes. Assume there's no LOI-2. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Roger. SPS G&N; this is for TEI-3; 46427; minus 0.53, plus 1.41; 075:31:29.95; plus 2896.0, minus 0045.6, plus 0072.0; 180, 021, 002; N/A, plus 0018.8; 2897.2, 2:51, 2879.3; 40, 276.9, 39.6; 033, 000.0, left 1.7; plus 008.83, minus 165.00; 1295.5, 36185, 146:35:07. Sirius, Rigel, 129, 155, 010; two jet, 20 seconds, B and D; horizon, two degrees at ignition minus three minutes, assumes no LOI-2.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Readback is correct. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston with a TEI-3, with an (assumption of) LOI-2 (having occurred). Over. [Pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Go ahead.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Roger.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. Plus 08.88, minus 165.00; 1295.5, 36185, 146:34:50; GDC Align, no change; ullage, no change; horizon, one degree at ignition minus three. Assumes LOI-2. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Go ahead - or Houston, this is Apollo 8. TEI-3 with LOI-2; SPS G&N; 45810; minus 0.53, plus 1.41; 075:21:28.46; plus 3012.8, minus 0054.0, plus 0191.1; 180, 019, 001; N/A, plus 0018.8; 3019.3, 2:55, 3000.8; 40, 274.2, 39.6; 033, down 02.1, left 1.8; plus 08.88, minus 165.00; 1295.5, 36185, 146:34:50. No change, no change, one degree in the rise of ignition minus three. Assumes LOI-2. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. I made one mistake; horizon window is minus one degree. Over.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Minus one degree.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. Readback is correct. [Long pause.]

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. You're Go across the board for LOI-2. We'd like to take the DSE for a dump. Over.

a08_0715502.speaker: Borman
a08_0715502.text: Roger. You got it. I understand we are Go for LOI-2.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: That's affirmative.

a08_0715502.speaker: Anders
a08_0715502.text: Before you take the DSE for a dump, let me give you a quick - let me give you a quick rundown on the DSE before you dump it, if you will.

a08_0715502.speaker: Carr
a08_0715502.text: Roger. Standing by.

a08_0715502.speaker: Anders
a08_0715502.text: Roger.

a08_0722000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0722000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. Our GET for ignition of LOI-2 is 73 hours, 35 minutes, 5 seconds. Apolune resulting from this burn, 60.7 nautical miles [112.4 km]; perilune, 60.6 nautical miles [112.2 km] - just about as close to circular as you can get. The burn duration expected, 9 seconds; Delta-V for this burn, 135 feet per second [41 m/s]. On this pass over the front side of the Moon, our spacecraft was at 115 nautical miles [213 km] in altitude at time of acquisition, 115 nautical miles in altitude. Our apolune, which also occurs on this - over this side of the Moon, 168.5 nautical mile

a08_0722000-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0722000-pao.text: Okay, Houston. You've got the tape.

a08_0722102.speaker: Anders
a08_0722102.text: Okay, Houston. You've got the tape.

a08_0722102.speaker: Carr
a08_0722102.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Would you believe that Taurus, Aida is the Pleiades? Over.

a08_0722400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0722400-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control, Houston; 72 hours, 24 minutes into this mission. In this lull, perhaps we can clarify some of the names you heard being given to craters during that recent television pass. Our geology group here had to apply some names to certain key landmarks instead of using just numbers and code, they decided to give them real life names. These are in no way officially named craters. In some cases, I think in most cases, the names aren't even - have not even been submitted to the international body which must pass on those kinds of official names. But to clarify this, we thought

a08_0722400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0722400-pao.text: We had some pictures to work from, and you distinctly heard Lovell - Anders and Lovell talk about craters named for themselves. Incidentally, this is perhaps a pardonable bit of geologist personality creeping into it. Historically they have been named for discovering geologists or observers. One was got a real time name of John Aaron because he is the electrical, environmental and communications console operator who spotted the need for cutting in the secondary water boiler as we started to circle the Moon, that is that he noticed the water level was down. He suggested we go to the secondary l

a08_0722400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0722400-pao.text: Moving along the line we see craters named for Grissom, Gus Grissom, Ed White, Roger Chaffee, clustered three craters fairly close together and just to the south of the ground track we just heard about. Coming along that same track we see one bearing the name of Chris Kraft, Don Slayton, Jerry Carr, and on along. I'm sure we'll here more of these. You did hear today about the crater Bassett, so named for Charlie Bassett, the late Charlie N. Bassett, and Elliot See, a crater right beside it; two men killed in an airplane crash in St. Louis, in February of 1966. At 72 hours, 27 minutes into the

a08_0722400-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0722400-pao.text: Have you got the tape dumped, Houston? We're about to lose the High Gainer. [Long pause.]

a08_0722400-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0722400-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're dumping now - looks like we'll be five or ten more minutes. [Pause.]

a08_0722715.speaker: Anders
a08_0722715.text: Have you got the tape dumped, Houston? We're about to lose the High Gainer. [Long pause.]

a08_0722715.speaker: Carr
a08_0722715.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're dumping now - looks like we'll be five or ten more minutes. [Pause.]

a08_0722715.speaker: Anders
a08_0722715.text: Okay. Try to get it dumped, and I'll play it, rewind it if necessary.

a08_0722855.speaker: Anders
a08_0722855.text: We are about to lose it [the HGA], Houston. How far are you on the tape dump? [Long pause.]

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Looks like we've lost it, they weren't quite done. We're standing by for a countdown to Biomed switch left. Over.

a08_0722855.speaker: Anders
a08_0722855.text: Roger. Look, we would like to get it dumped if we could. Stand by a second.

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Okay.

a08_0722855.speaker: Anders
a08_0722855.text: Did you get it stopped? [Pause.]

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Bill, you can go ahead and turn it off. [Long pause.]

a08_0722855.speaker: Anders
a08_0722855.text: Okay. We're not going to have High Gain now until the next time around. Can you give me an idea of how much of that pass you got.

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We - negative. We can't tell. You can go ahead and turn it off.

a08_0722855.speaker: Anders
a08_0722855.text: Well, how long did you - did you dump it?

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Roger. Stand by; they're checking. [Long pause.]

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Apollo 8, Houston. [Pause.]

a08_0722855.speaker: Anders
a08_0722855.text: Go ahead Houston.

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston reading you with a great deal of noise in the background. Go ahead and rewind your tape and start it in low bit rate, and we'll try and catch that dump at the end of the next rev. [Long pause.]

a08_0722855.speaker: Anders
a08_0722855.text: Roger, I would like to have an idea on how much you dumped. So I know whether [garbled) all these things or whether we have better setting in.

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Roger. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're working on that time. We should be able to tell you before LOS. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0722855.speaker: Anders
a08_0722855.text: Go ahead.

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Roger. Did you read my last?

a08_0722855.speaker: Anders
a08_0722855.text: That's affirmative, Jerry. You'll give us a rundown when you figure out how much tape you dumped.

a08_0722855.speaker: Carr
a08_0722855.text: Roger. They feel reasonably sure, however, that if you rewind and start low bit rate, we'll be able to get all of the burn and still not run into what needs to be downlinked yet.

a08_0723532.speaker: Borman
a08_0723532.text: Roger. What REFSMMAT are we using for this LOI-2 burn? [Long pause.]

a08_0723532.speaker: Borman
a08_0723532.text: Okay, I notice it's an LOI-2 REFSMMAT. If it is, I don't understand why the pitch is 175.

a08_0723812.speaker: Carr
a08_0723812.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. You're right; the REFSMMAT is LOI-2. The REFSMMAT was determined out there before the last midcourse correction, and since that time, there's been a slight change in your trajectory, and the point at which you're burning LOI-2 now is just a shade different than where it was originally planned. Over.

a08_0724526.speaker: Carr
a08_0724526.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. DSE is rewound, and it's yours - available for use is about one hour of low bit rate and two minutes of high bit rate for your burn without running over your good data. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0724526.speaker: Borman
a08_0724526.text: Roger. Do you read us now, Houston.

a08_0724526.speaker: Carr
a08_0724526.text: Roger. Reading you loud and clear now.

a08_0724526.speaker: Carr
a08_0724526.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. You're Go for LOI-2 on the next rev. Over.

a08_0724526.speaker: Borman
a08_0724526.text: Roger. Understand Go for LOI-2 on the next rev.

a08_0724526.speaker: Carr
a08_0724526.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Reading you loud and clear. How me?

a08_0724526.speaker: Carr
a08_0724526.text: Roger. Frank, did you get my message on the DSE?

a08_0725015.speaker: Carr
a08_0725015.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Verify the Telemetry Input switch, Low. Over.

a08_0725015.speaker: Borman
a08_0725015.text: Going to Low; it was in High.

a08_0725937.speaker: Carr
a08_0725937.text: Apollo 8, Houston. 5 minutes to LOS. Over.

a08_0730330.speaker: Carr
a08_0730330.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. One minute to LOS; all systems Go. Over.

a08_0730400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0730400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 73 hours, 04 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 8. We're at 8 seconds away from time of Loss of Signal. Okay, they said goodbye to the ground as they passed over at - on their next pass over the back side of the Moon. This is the pass over the back side where we will have our Lunar Orbit Insertion burn number 2. To quickly go over those numbers again; we have a Ground Elapsed Time of ignition at 73 hours, 35 minutes, 05 seconds. Apolune, 60.7 nautical miles [112.4 km]; perilune, 60.6 nautical miles [112.2 km] are expected to result from the burn. The burn, o

a08_0734900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0734900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We expect to acquire just momentarily. The first call has gone out. We have acquired; we're reading good tank pressures, and here goes the first call.

a08_0734925.speaker: Carr
a08_0734925.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Loud and clear. How me? [Pause.]

a08_0734925.speaker: Carr
a08_0734925.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Loud and clear. How me?

a08_0734925.speaker: Anders
a08_0734925.text: Roger. Reading you loud and clear, and ready for the burn status report.

a08_0734925.speaker: Borman
a08_0734925.text: Houston. Roger. The burn was on time, 11 seconds, 0.2 with a V GX . [Long pause.], 1.8; V GY - that's minus 1.8; minus 0.2, V GZ ; Delta V C was minus 9.4. Verb 82 gives us an apogee [means apolune] of 62 and a perigee [means perilune] of 60.8. [Pause.]

a08_0734925.speaker: Carr
a08_0734925.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Roger. Your burn was on time, 11 seconds; V GX was plus 0.2, V GY was minus 1.8, V GZ minus 0.2, Delta-V C minus 9.4, apogee 62, perigee, 60.8. Over.

a08_0735500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0735500-pao.text: Apollo Control here. That circuit's noisier than we can recall on the last two passes, but we have heard the crewmember, I think Borman, confirm an apogee of 62 miles, a perigee of 60.8, a virtually perfect second burn, giving us a circular orbit. We'll continue to leave the line open.

a08_0735500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0735500-pao.text: Apollo Control again. Apogee on this, the third rev around the Moon will occur at 80 degrees west longitude, 9 degrees, 30 minutes north latitude. Those are lunar coordinates of course. The perigee on this rev will occur at 9 degrees, 29 minutes south latitude and 99 degrees, 28 minutes east longitude. That'll be on the back side of the Moon. And our numbers now show an apogee of 60.9 [nautical miles, 112.8 km] versus of perigee of 60.5 [nautical miles, 112.0 km], compared to 62-[nautical] mile apogee and a 60.8-[nautical] mile apogee [means perilune] from the crew. Excellent agreement.

a08_0735500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0735500-pao.text: The press corps should be advised that we're planning a press conference to begin in about 45 minutes in the MSC Auditorium, 9:30 Houston time [that is, 9:30am on December 24].

a08_0735906.speaker: Anders
a08_0735906.text: Houston, how do you read? This is Apollo 8.

a08_0740049.speaker: Borman
a08_0740049.text: Houston, Apollo 8. We're on High Gain now if you want to get the high-speed data to look at that burn.

a08_0740049.speaker: Borman (onboard, may be Anders)
a08_0740049.text: Okay, I think I've made a mistake, on the last DSE [garble] I've gotten confused here.

a08_0740049.speaker: Carr
a08_0740049.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We are taking the DSE.

a08_0740049.speaker: Borman
a08_0740049.text: Thank you. Can you hold it for about 5 seconds - or about one minute?

a08_0740049.speaker: Borman
a08_0740049.text: Okay. You can dump the data now.

a08_0740049.speaker: Carr
a08_0740049.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. We're taking the DSE for dump.

a08_0740600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0740600-pao.text: We got an exceptionally quiet pass across here. We're reading a pitch attitude of 192 degrees; it's down, and yaw, 356 degrees; a 177-degree roll attitude - a very steady attitude and I believe they are in orbital rate; that is a rate calculated to hold their windows in a specific position and move them in - as they move across the face of the Moon. Lovell should be in a rest period, 2 hours duration now. Perhaps that's why they are keeping quiet. Bill Anders is extremely busy taking pictures. 70-millimeter and 16-millimeters - 70-millimeter stills - 16-millimeter movies.

a08_0740600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0740600-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We are 52 minutes from Loss of Signal on this pass and let's look over our ECS, Environmental Control Systems summary table. The cabin pressure, 4.9 [psi, 33.8 kPa] and holding very nicely. The cabin temperature, 77 degrees [Fahrenheit, 25°C]. I think that's up a few degrees from yesterday. I don't recall exactly. In general we can expect to see, we should be seeing a slight rise in temperature. This was predicted by the thermal people, a rise particularly, in the outside temperature, the outside skin temperature of the spacecraft, a rise of something like 10 t

a08_0740600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0740600-pao.text: Apollo Control Houston here, 74 hours, 12 minutes. After a long quiet period there, Mike Collins put in a call and he is getting some conversation from Frank Borman, be it ever so brief. Let's hear it now, and we'll catch up and go into the live situation.

a08_0741138.speaker: Collins
a08_0741138.text: Hey, good morning, Frank. We've been tracking you for about 18 minutes now, and we show your orbit 61 by 60½. Over.

a08_0741138.speaker: Collins
a08_0741138.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Your SPS engine looked good on LOI number 2 burn.

a08_0741624.speaker: Collins
a08_0741624.text: Bill has got the tape recorder now; we're evaluating the dump. The data is good, and we're evaluating the voice quality here shortly.

a08_0741906.speaker: Collins
a08_0741906.text: I've got a few jolly updates for you when you're ready to copy.

a08_0742100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0742100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston, over all this noise. We will take the line down at this point; try to figure out where the source of all of our noise is. Fortunately it's an extremely quiet pass; but if there is any further conversation, we'll come back up and play it for you. It's 74 hours, 21 minutes into the flight. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0742133.speaker: Borman
a08_0742133.text: Go ahead, Houston, with your updates.

a08_0742133.speaker: Collins
a08_0742133.text: Roger. Apollo 8, Houston. I have a TEI-3, TEI-4 and map update for revs 3 and 4 to read to you. Actually, the TEI-3 update which you have onboard is still valid, so we will not update that one. Which do you want first, the TEI-4 or the map update?

a08_0742133.speaker: Collins
a08_0742133.text: All right. This is the TEI-4 update: SPS/G&N; 45695; minus 0.53, plus 1.41. Are you with me so far? Over.

a08_0742133.speaker: Collins
a08_0742133.text: Very good. 077:21:27.58; plus 3062.7, minus 0062.5, plus 0057.7; 180, 018, 001; not applicable, plus 0018.8; 3063.9, 2:56, 3045.2. Are you with me so far? Over.

a08_0742133.speaker: Borman
a08_0742133.text: So far seems [garble]. Hold it a minute though, will you? [Long pause.]

a08_0742133.speaker: Collins
a08_0742133.text: Okay, the last number I gave was Delta-V C , picking up at the sextant star; 40, 273.0, 39.6; 033, down 03.0, left 1.9. Are you with me? Over.

a08_0742133.speaker: Collins
a08_0742133.text: Okay. Plus 08.58, minus 165.00; 1296.0, 36195, 146:37:21. Comment: north set of stars Sirius and Rigel; roll, 129; pitch, 155; yaw, 010; ullage, 2 quads, 20 seconds, 2 0 seconds from quads Bravo and Delta. Horizon on 2-degree line at time of ignition minus 3 minutes. Over.

a08_0742133.speaker: Borman
a08_0742133.text: Roger, Houston. We got a TEI-4; SPS/G&N; 45695; minus 0.53, plus 1.41; 077:21:27.58; plus 3062.7, minus 0062.5, plus 0057.7; 180, 018, 001; N/A, plus 0018.8; 3063.9, 2:56, 3045.2; 40, 273.0, 39.6; 033, down 03.0, left 1.9; plus 08.58, minus 165.00; plus 1296.0, plus 36195, 146:37:21. Sirius, Rigel, 129, 155, 010; 2 quads, 20 seconds, B and D. Horizon 2 degrees at T IG minus 3 (minutes).

a08_0742133.speaker: Collins
a08_0742133.text: That's about the size of it, Frank, and a map update for revs 3/4 when you're ready. [Pause.]

a08_0742133.speaker: Collins
a08_0742133.text: Revs 3/4, LOS, 75:01:23; Sunrise, 75:10:16; Prime meridian, 75:17:16; AOS, 75:47:18; Sunset, 76:23:11; Remarks: Subsolar point, 75:46:55; IP-1 acquisition, 76:11:17; IP-2 acquisition, 76:12:30. For IP-1 and 2 those ACQ(uisition) times are for shaft and trunnion angles equals zero. Over.

a08_0742400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0742400-pao.text: Apollo Control here, we'll break it off at this point so the news conference can be picked up. One other pertinent comment that did not play out on that tape exchange. Frank Borman said we're getting - we had noted, that his - the voice quality of Bill Anders was not quite what it should be on the data record system and which is being dumped here each on each rev back to Houston. This was noted and Bill said they were all so busy right now he would do what he could, make notes on the Flight Plan and that sort of thing, but he - we just have to understand. So at this time let's break over to th

a08_0742400-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0742400-pao.text: Okay, the last number I gave was Delta-V C , picking up at the sextant star; 40, 273.0, 39.6; 033, down 03.0, left 1.9. Are you with me? Over.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. When Bill gets a minute, we'd like to get battery B started charging. Over.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. Thank you. He'll take a minute right now.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 74 hours, 35 minutes into the flight. And in the last 10 or 15 minutes we've had a couple of brief exchanges with the crew, who still seem to be in a rather resting mode, but here are those exchanges, primarily numbers updates. We have the tapes.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Go.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. For Bill - the voice quality on the backside DSE is extremely poor. We consider it unusable, and we recommend that all pertinent comments be hand recorded so we don't lose them. We should not count on using the tape at low bit rate for voice.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Okay, Houston. We're getting so busy that we are having a hard time trying to do a neat job of logging. I'll try to do it on the Flight Plan; and if I make any visual observations, we'll put them on the DSE and I'll try to scribble some notes here and there.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. Understand. Now high bit-rate is working great.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Hey, Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: How about giving us the TV times for the ninth rev, will you please?

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Oh, we sure will, Frank. Stand by.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Go ahead.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. We're checking into precise start and stop time for the TV, and you are Go for the next rev. Over.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Understand; Go for the next rev. Mike, we'd like to, if we could, time the TV to a passing over the terminator. We would like to track the terminator with the TV; think that's the most impressive thing we've seen, and that might be the best thing rather than trying to acquire the Earth.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Okay, Frank. That's one of the things we're looking at. Right now, we have you ending at about 86 hours and we're looking at extending that few minutes to include that terminator view. Over.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Okay, I don't want us to run into rev 10 very much at all, though.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. Understand.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Go ahead, Apollo 8.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: ...since the DSE qual's not so good. How do you read, Mike?

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: I read you loud and clear. You were cut out about the DSE. Say again.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. Since the qual[ity] is...n't so good, let me give you a quick rundown of the status of photo targets. You ready to copy?

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Ready to copy.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Okay. At rev 1, we got photo target 90 and terminator photography south for near-side terminator. Starting on rev 2, we've got target 12 and target 10, 14, 16, 19, 20, 21 and 23. Unfortunately, we got into a high - I got into the high-speed film there somewhere, and I think those 250-mm targets were on high speed. We did change film, and starting out in Tex - Crater Texas, with target 28, 31, 40, 36, plus several targets of opportunity that were recorded on the DSE, but apparently lost. Have you been able to copy?

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Yeah, I'm with you, Bill. Keep going.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Okay. I might be calling up too fast. Okay. On the third rev, we got target 58 and 63 and 65. The training photography was accomplished, and it was done on magazine D, which now has [pause] correction, that's magazine E which now shows 95 exposures. Magazine D is fresh. Magazine K was also used for training photography, and it's showing 0.51. [Long pause.]

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Rog, we copy all that, Bill. [Long pause.]

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: ...Mike, this is Frank again.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Go ahead, Frank.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Go ahead.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Rog for Bill.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: ...around.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston standing by.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: I say is Rod Rose around?

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Stand by one, Frank; we'll look for him, and while we're doing that, for Bill the DSE voice quality on high bit rate is very good, so if he wants to use the DSE in high bit rate for a limited amount of time to record important things, we suggest that he do that. We'd like him to wait 20 seconds after turning it on prior to talking. Over.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. Copy.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Thank you, Bill. [Pause.]

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Go ahead.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Rod Rose is sitting up in the viewing room; he can hear what you say.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: I wonder if he is ready for experiment P-1?

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: He says thumbs up on P-1. [Pause.]

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Houston, with reference to the DSE on high bit rate, what I'd like to do then is, if you got the last pass, I'd like to play it - run it back and start at AOS on low bit rate and then go to high when we need it. How would that be? [Pause.]

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: John Aaron buys it.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Okay, Mike. This is Frank again.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Go.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. Rod and I got together, and I was going to record a little - saying a little prayer for the church service tonight. And I wonder - I guess that's what we are ready on?

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Stand by one, Frank.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: All right.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Are you still there?

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: You're still loud and clear, Frank. [Long pause.]

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Go ahead, Frank, with your message.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Okay. This is to Rod Rose and the people at St. Christopher's, actually to people everywhere. Give us, O God, the vision which can see thy love in the world in spite of human failure. Give us the faith to trust the goodness in spite of our ignorance and weakness. Give us the knowledge that we may continue to pray with understanding hearts, and show us what each one of us can do to set forth the coming of the day of universal peace. Amen.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Amen.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: I was supposed to lay-read tonight, and I couldn't quite make it.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Rog. I think they understand.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Houston, how do you read? Apollo 8.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. Frank, we'd like to know about the water chlorination. Have you - when was the last time you chlorinated the water? Over.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: About an hour and a half ago; we've already done it.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. We copy an hour and a half ago. Affirmative?

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. You know we wouldn't forget that.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Jim spilled a little, and it smelled like a bucket of Clorox about an hour ago.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Say again.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: I said Jim inadvertently spilled some of that chlorine, and it smelled like a bucket of Clorox in here a little while.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. Understand.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. We have two and a half minutes to LOS, and all systems are looking good. Everything's looking just fine down here, Frank.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Thank you.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: We'll have some more information on the TV on the next rev. We don't - we're not planning any big change in the time, just to extend them a little bit, I think, closer to the terminator.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Just give us the time, will you, because we just want to know when it is. I'd like to get the terminator if we could, and we've got a little message, and that's it.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Roger. We'll do that the next time you come around.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Borman
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Thank you. Okay. And have the EECOM guys keep a sharp watch on our systems. Old Anders is so busy fooling around with these pictures that - not much else is getting done.

a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.speaker: Collins
a08_0743000-pao-press-conference.text: Rog. The EECOM is doing that.

a08_0743253.speaker: Collins
a08_0743253.text: Roger. When Bill gets a minute, we'd like to get battery B started charging. Over.

a08_0743253.speaker: Borman
a08_0743253.text: Roger. Thank you. He'll take a minute right now.

a08_0754700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0754700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 75 hours, 37 minutes into the flight. Before we lost signal with the spacecraft, some half hour ago, I suppose, 20 minutes ago, Frank Borman came up on the line and said he would like to dedicate a prayer to the people of St. John's [means St. Christopher's] church, his church here in Seabrook and he added to all the people of the world. Here is that prayer.

a08_0754700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0754700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. That was Frank Borman reading a prayer, he mentioned the name to Rod Rose and the people of St. John's [means St. Christopher's, see below]. Rod Rose is an assistant to Chris Kraft, the Flight Operations Director. He is a member of the same church. And we'll see to it that St. John's receives a high fidelity quality copy of that tape for an evening service tonight which Frank Borman regrets that he could not make. There is - there was other conversation, primarily updates on contingency type events. Those events and that tape will be passed directly to the transcription

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Hey, don't take that, it's not scheduled. (Chuckle.)

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0754737-onboard.text: [Laughter.] You got a color film, Jim?

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Hand me that roll of color quick, will you...

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Just grab me a color. That color exterior.

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Well, I think we missed it.

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Hey, I got it right here! [In the hatch window.]

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Let - let me get it out this window. It's a lot clearer.

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Bill, I got it framed; it's very clear right here.

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Take several of them! Here, give it to me.

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Wait a minute, let's get the right setting, here now; just calm down. Calm down, Lovell.

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Well, I got it ri - Oh, that's a beautiful shot.

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Now vary the - vary the exposure a little bit.

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0754737-onboard.text: I did. I took two of them.

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0754737-onboard.text: You sure we got it now?

a08_0754737-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0754737-onboard.text: Yeah, we'll get - we'll - It'll come up again, I think.

a08_0754930.speaker: Collins
a08_0754930.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0754930.speaker: Collins
a08_0754930.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0754930.speaker: Collins
a08_0754930.text: Roger. We've been having a little antenna problem on the ground here. We're reading you now with a lot of noise in the background. How me?

a08_0754930.speaker: Collins
a08_0754930.text: Roger, Frank. We're still trying to get a bit better comm here. Stand by; you're unreadable.

a08_0755000-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0755000-pao.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0755000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0755000-pao.text: And we're advised we're having antenna problems at our prime site. We have handed it to another site, Goldstone, I believe. You will notice, on some of these transmissions, a lot of background noise. That's being done on the smaller-powered antennas from the spacecraft. Around the High Gain Antenna - the one which transmits the television pictures and other data, the reception's much clearer. Another call has gone out, here's the conversation.

a08_0755226.speaker: Collins
a08_0755226.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over.

a08_0755226.speaker: Borman
a08_0755226.text: You're loud and clear, Houston. Apollo 8

a08_0755226.speaker: Collins
a08_0755226.text: Rog. Understand you're reading us loud and clear; we're barely reading you. Would you go to P00 and Accept, please? We're going to send you a P27 update.

a08_0755226.speaker: Borman
a08_0755226.text: Roger. Going to P00 and to Accept. [Long pause.]

a08_0755226.speaker: Borman
a08_0755226.text: We're in P00 and Accept, Houston.

a08_0755226.speaker: Collins
a08_0755226.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You're unreadable. We're going to delay that P27 until we get a little bit better lock on you. [Long pause.]

a08_0755226.speaker: Collins
a08_0755226.text: As long as you're reading me okay, Frank, I'll bring you up to date on a couple of things. The P27 which we will be sending you is a state vector update going to the LM slot, and we'd like you, as per plan, to transfer that to the CSM slot by a Verb 47 Enter, and we'd like to just remind you that prior to doing your Verb 47 Enter, manually select P00 and wait for the computer activity light to go out. Did you copy? Over.

a08_0755226.speaker: Borman
a08_0755226.text: Roger. Roger. We copy. [Pause.]

a08_0755226.speaker: Collins
a08_0755226.text: Okay, Frank. Are you still reading me loud and clear? Over.

a08_0755226.speaker: Borman
a08_0755226.text: Roger. Loud and clear.

a08_0755226.speaker: Collins
a08_0755226.text: All right. I'll go ahead with a map update when you're ready to copy. [Pause.]

a08_0755226.speaker: Borman
a08_0755226.text: Okay. Can you hold off a minute? [Long pause.]

a08_0755226.speaker: Collins
a08_0755226.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. How are you reading now? [Long pause.]

a08_0755226.speaker: Borman
a08_0755226.text: Go ahead, Houston. This is Apollo 8. [Long pause.]

a08_0755226.speaker: Collins
a08_0755226.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston with a map update. Are you ready to copy?

a08_0755226.speaker: Borman
a08_0755226.text: Just a minute, Mike.

a08_0755226.speaker: Collins
a08_0755226.text: Roger. Apollo 8, Houston. Your map update for rev 4/5: LOS, 76:59:59; sunrise, 77:09:06; prime meridian, 77:15:47; AOS, 77:45:50; sunset, 78:22:03; IP-1 position time for control point 2, 77:29:42; IP-1 time closest approach for target B-1, 78:10:25. Over.

a08_0755226.speaker: Borman
a08_0755226.text: We'll have to get that data later on. [Pause.]

a08_0755226.speaker: Collins
a08_0755226.text: We'll try it again later, Frank.

a08_0755226.speaker: Borman
a08_0755226.text: Thank you.

a08_0755400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0755400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We are having antenna difficulties. We'll take the line... Oh, we are going to try some more. Stand by. Let's continue to monitor.

a08_0755400-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0755400-pao.text: As long as you're reading me okay, Frank, I'll bring you up to date on a couple of things. The P27 which we will be sending you is a state vector update going to the LM slot, and we'd like you, as per plan, to transfer that to the CSM slot by a Verb 47 Enter, and we'd like to just remind you that prior to doing your Verb 47 Enter, manually select P00 and wait for the computer activity light to go out. Did you copy? Over.

a08_0760000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0760000-pao.text: Apollo Control here. I want to correct something I apparently said; Frank Borman dedicated that prayer to St. John's Episcopal church. He is a member of St. Christopher's. The confusion is due to the fact, I believe that Jim Lovell is a member of St. John's Episcopal church, so we have two Episcopalians going to two different churches. I apologize. The correct name of the church is St. Christopher's. We have the correct town. Now let's get back and monitor.

a08_0760000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0760000-pao.text: We'll take the line down in view of the noise and record and come back up to you with anything significant. At 76 hours into the flight, this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0760314.speaker: Anders
a08_0760314.text: Do you want to take this nav sighting?

a08_0760612.speaker: Anders
a08_0760612.text: Roger, Houston. How do you read?

a08_0760612.speaker: Collins
a08_0760612.text: Reading you a lot better now, Bill. How are you reading me?

a08_0760612.speaker: Anders
a08_0760612.text: I'm reading you five - loud and clear, and are you copying our low bit data to record this - these tracking passes? Over.

a08_0760612.speaker: Collins
a08_0760612.text: That's affirmative. We are getting low bit data now.

a08_0760612.speaker: Anders
a08_0760612.text: Okay. I've played the - run the tape recorder back to the beginning. We have quite a bit of high bit, so all you'll have to do is start recording when you're ready. [Pause.]

a08_0760612.speaker: Collins
a08_0760612.text: Roger. Stand by one, Bill. [Long pause.]

a08_0760612.speaker: Collins
a08_0760612.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Stand by one on the tape recorder dump. We'd like you to look at your steam pressure. We think that the primary evaporator may have dried out, and if the steam pressure shows off-scale low, would you please close the back pressure valve and reservice the evaporator? Over.

a08_0760612.speaker: Collins
a08_0760612.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're ready to send you the P27 LM state vector update when you are ready. Over.

a08_0760612.speaker: Borman
a08_0760612.text: You'll have to wait until this tracking exercise is over with, Mike.

a08_0760900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0760900-pao.text: Apollo Control here. 76 hours, 09 minutes into the flight. In the past few minutes, we've established a much cleaner communication with Apollo 8. Here's a sample.

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Apollo 8.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Were you calling? Over.

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Roger. You can go ahead now and give you the computer, get the updates, and let's get going on the PAD messages.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: It's in P00 and Accept. [Pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Okay, Houston. You ready to talk about the water boiler problem?

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Rog. We copy you in P00 and Accept, and we're sending you a P27 LM state vector. On the water boiler, it looks to us like the evaporator has been reserviced. How does it look to you? Over.

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Roger. I reserviced it, put it to Auto, H 2 O flow to Auto; and the steam pressure went to zero again. So I tried reservicing it a second time for 1 minute, and again no results. I'm in the present process of closing the back-pressure valve manually. Over.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Roger. Understand you've tried to reservice it twice, both times steam pressure has gone to zero, and now you're closing the back-pressure valve manually.

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Roger. Each time I've reserviced it, the steam pressure came up to about 0.07 to 0.1; but as soon as the steam and water were put to Auto, the steam pressure went right back down again.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Roger. We copy, and we're reading you loud and clear now, Bill. On your map update, did you copy that that I gave you previously? [Pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Lovell
a08_0761809.text: Negative. We have not copied it yet.

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Negative.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Okay. I have it for you again when you're ready to copy.

a08_0761809.speaker: Lovell
a08_0761809.text: Ready to copy.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: This is a map update for revs 4/5: LOS, 76:59:59; sunrise, 77:09:06; prime meridian, 77:15:47; AOS, 77:45:50; sunset, 78:22:03. Remarks: IP-1, acquisition time for CP2 is 77:29:42; IP-1 time closest approach for target B-1, 78:10:25. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: That's right, and the prime meridian time is 77:15:47, and you got your computer back. We've got a good P27 update.

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Okay. We will go to P00 and Transfer.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Houston, do you have a TEI-5 for us?

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: We're working on it now, Frank. Have it for you momentarily.

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Go.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Roger. On your back-pressure valve, we'd like to know how long after you closed the back-pressure valve the first time - how long it was from the time you closed it until you started the reservicing. We'd like you to wait about 15 minutes to prevent any ice from forming due to flash freezing. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Okay. I start immediately to reservice it. [Long pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We showed that you closed it this last time about 4 minutes ago, so we'd like to wait another 15 minutes and then try to reservice it again at that time and then go to Auto. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Roger.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Roger. Thank you. The TEI-4 PAD which you have is still valid. We'll have a TEI-5 PAD for you shortly.

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Roger. And be advised we're presently in steam pressure, Manual, and we're in H 2 O flow, Auto; and are now in H 2 O flow, Off, as of about 5 seconds ago.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Roger. We copy that, Bill. [Pause.] And we confirm that's a good configuration.

a08_0761809.speaker: Anders
a08_0761809.text: Right now, I've got the H 2 O flow, Off. Do we stay that way?

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Affirmative. [Long pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Apollo 8, Houston. On your television update, we propose that you start the TV at the Flight Plan time of 85 hours, 37 minutes and simply extend the stop time a few minutes. You're currently scheduled to stop at 86 hours, and we'd like to keep it going until the terminator, which should be approximately 86:14. Over.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Frank, I know you're busy up there. We've got the daily news for you whenever and if ever you'd like to hear it.

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: I'll give you a call.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston.

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Go ahead.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: I have the TEI-5 PAD for you whenever you're ready to copy.

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Okay. TEI-5; SPS/G&N; 47 - correction - 45701; minus 0.43, plus 1.16; 079:21:26.03. Are you with me so far?

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Roger.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Plus 3117.1, minus 0076.7, minus 0021.4; 180, 017, 001; not applicable, plus 0018.8; 3118.1, 2:59, 3100.3. Are you with me? Over.

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Roger.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Roger. 40, 271.1 39.8; 033, down 04.3, left 2.3; plus 08.32, minus 165.00; 1295.6, 36208, 146:39:44; north set of stars remain Sirius and Rigel; roll, pitch, and yaw remain same angles, 129, 155, 010; ullage remains 2 quads for 20 seconds, quads B and D. Horizon on 4 degree line at T IG minus 3 minutes. Over.

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Roger. Here we go. TEI-5; SPS/G&N; 45701; minus 0.43, plus 1.16; 079:21:26.03; plus 3117.1, minus 0076.7, minus 00214; 180, 017, 001; N/A, plus 0018.8; 3118.1, 2:59, 3100.3; 40, 271.1, 39.8; 033, down 04.3, left 2.3; plus 08.32, minus 165.00; plus 1295.6, 36208, 146:39:44. Set stars are the same; ullage - we'd like - do you have any objection to using four quads for 15 seconds? [Pause.]

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: No objection to four-quad ullage, Apollo 8.

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Okay. We'd like to just go ahead and use four quads at all times, unless we get a lot shorter on fuel than we are now.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Understand.

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: And is that 15 seconds?

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Affirmative: 15 seconds, four quads.

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: Apollo 8...

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Thank you, and horizon is 4 degrees at minus...

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: That readback is correct, Frank, and we'd like to advise that the voice quality on the high bit rate is excellent. Over.

a08_0761809.speaker: Borman
a08_0761809.text: Thank you. Mike, it's 4 quads for 15 seconds. Is that right?

a08_0761809.speaker: Collins
a08_0761809.text: That is affirmative, Apollo 8: 4 quads for 15 seconds.

a08_0762400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0762400-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston here. 76 hours, 24 minutes. Communication much improved now as we move out on the front side of the Moon. Here's how it is going."

a08_0763400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0763400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston, here with 24 minutes left to run in this period of acquisition. We might make note of our velocity in this revolution; it's approximately 3,560 statute miles per hour. And here goes another call from Mike Collins."

a08_0763545.speaker: Collins
a08_0763545.text: Roger. For Bill, he can go ahead and do his standard reservice on the - on the water now. It's looking good.

a08_0763545.speaker: Borman
a08_0763545.text: Okay. You want us to reservice it now?

a08_0763545.speaker: Collins
