a08_0774900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 77 hours, 49 minutes into the flight and just three minutes ago we acquired Apollo 8 as it came around the corner on this fifth revolution around the Moon. Here's the conversation as it progresses.

a08_0775700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0775700-pao.text: And that brings us up to this point. We've had no additional comments now, for perhaps a minute or so. That's excellent data though. The kind of - precisely the kind of data that we had hoped to get. The navigational side of lunar orbit which will be flown by both the command - future command module and LM flights around the Moon. Lovell will continue to his navigational work; and dear old Bill Anders, sitting off in one corner there, squeezing off pictures at a rate that most professional photographers wouldn't believe. Frank Borman is entering a rest period here, which is to extend for three

a08_0780415.speaker: Collins
a08_0780415.text: Rog. I am about 15 minutes early with the TEI-6 update and the map update. I'll have them here whenever it's convenient for you to copy.

a08_0780415.speaker: Anders
a08_0780415.text: Okay. Just a little bit, Mike.

a08_0781328.speaker: Collins
a08_0781328.text: Roger. We'd like to ask you to stop using auto optics on the pseudo-landing site. It's necessary that we send you up a P27 to update the RLS values stored in the computer. Over.

a08_0781328.speaker: Lovell
a08_0781328.text: Roger. I found out it didn't work [garble] I went to manual optics on B-1.

a08_0781644.speaker: Collins
a08_0781644.text: Roger. If you'd go to P00 and Accept, please, we're going to send you a P27 load which will update an RLS value which will be followed by a procedural change, Jim, we'll give you later; and auto optics should be working shortly.

a08_0781644.speaker: Lovell
a08_0781644.text: Roger. Or I could use no-landmark Auto Optics instead of the code. [Long pause.]

a08_0781644.speaker: Collins
a08_0781644.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're also sending you up a state vector update at the same time.

a08_0781644.speaker: Lovell
a08_0781644.text: Okay. We'll be expecting that. [Long pause.]

a08_0781644.speaker: Collins
a08_0781644.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We taking the DSE for a dump. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0781644.speaker: Collins
a08_0781644.text: Roger. We would like to take Bill's DSE for a dump. Over.

a08_0781900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0781900-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston here; 78 hours, 19 minutes into the flight. We've had a few sporadic conversations with two very hard working pilots, actually I guess all the conversation has been with one, Jim Lovell, in the last few minutes. Here's a collection of those conversations.

a08_0781900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0781900-pao.text: And that brings up to snuff with all the tape of this pass. I think we're going to go back to live action, let's cut up there.

a08_0781900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0781900-pao.text: Our orbit this rev, sixty - shows a 62-[nautical] mile apogee [means apolune] and a 60.1-[nautical] mile perigee [means perilune], perigee occurring at 10 degrees south by 101 degrees east and apogee occurring at 10 degrees north by 78 west. Here goes a call.

a08_0782433.speaker: Anders
a08_0782433.text: Houston, Apollo 8. We're ready for the - your updates, your PADs.

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. I have updates, a map update for rev 5/6, and TEI-6 update. Which would you like first?

a08_0782433.speaker: Anders
a08_0782433.text: Okay. I've got the map update page now. Why don't you give me that one?

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Okay. Map update for rev 5/6. LOS, 78:58:49; sunrise, 79:08:07; prime meridian, 79:14:30; AOS, 79:44:36; sunset, 80:21:05; IP-1, time of closest approach to target B-1, 80:09:08. Now your two new control points that Jim gave us: control point number 1, acquisition, 79:10:32; control point number 2, acquisition, 79:23:14. Over.

a08_0782433.speaker: Anders
a08_0782433.text: Roger. Copy. Ready for the TEI. [Pause.]

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Okay, Bill. Before we read the big TEI update here, I'd like to give Jim, briefly, a procedure for P22. When he comes to Noun 89, we request that he do a Verb 34, Enter. Do not Proceed, and by so doing then, he will not incorporate the lat. and longitude from his mark, and he will not change the reference value of the landing site, and we will solve this auto optics problem. Over.

a08_0782433.speaker: Lovell
a08_0782433.text: Let me see if I have this correct, Mike. When flashing [Verb] 06 [Noun] 89 comes up with the latitude and longitude information, I will not Proceed but will go to Verb 34 and terminate. Is that correct?

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Yes, that is affirmative. Do a Verb 34, Enter, instead of a Proceed. And that will...

a08_0782433.speaker: Lovell
a08_0782433.text: All right. Is this technique true? [Pause.]

a08_0782433.speaker: Lovell
a08_0782433.text: Houston, is this technique true for both the node control point auto optics on G-25 ?

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Stand by one, Jim.

a08_0782433.speaker: Lovell
a08_0782433.text: And the len... [Long pause.]

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: That's affirmative, Apollo 8. That is always true.

a08_0782433.speaker: Lovell
a08_0782433.text: Okay. Roger. True for the code auto optics and the no landmark. I'll Proceed instead of going on - or I'll use 34 instead Proceeding on 89.

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Roger. Thank you, Jim, and I have the TEI-6 hour, when you're ready - or TEI number 6. [Long pause.]

a08_0782433.speaker: Borman
a08_0782433.text: Go ahead. [Pause.]

a08_0782433.speaker: Anders
a08_0782433.text: Ready to copy.

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Rog. I'm glad you're ready to copy TEI number 6. I've got one last comment for Jim before you do so. The Verb 89 - or correction - the Noun 89 we're talking about is the one that he gets after marking. There are two Noun 89s, one prior to marking and one after, and our procedure references the Noun 89 after marking. Over.

a08_0782433.speaker: Lovell
a08_0782433.text: Roger. Understand.

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Thank you, and, Bill, you still ready to copy?

a08_0782433.speaker: Anders
a08_0782433.text: Ready to copy, Mike.

a08_0782433.text: TEI-6, SPS/G&N; 45701; minus 0.40, plus 1.57. Are you with me so far?

a08_0782433.text: 081:21:24.43; plus 3177.6, minus 0082.3, minus 0136.5; 180, 016, 001; not applicable, plus 0018.8. Are you still with me? Over.

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Yeah, I'm with you, Bill.

a08_0782433.text: 39.6; 033, down 05.4, left 2.1; plus 08.10, minus 165.00; 1296.8, 36222, 146:42:04; same GDC Align, Sirius and Rigel, 129, 155, 010; 4 jet, 15 seconds; horizon, 6 degrees, T IG minus 3. Over.

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Roger, Bill. On your ignition time, GET I is 81 hours, 081. Over.

a08_0782433.speaker: Anders
a08_0782433.text: Roger. Got it, 081.

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Thank you, sir.

a08_0782433.speaker: Anders
a08_0782433.text: Thank you, Michael. As a matter of interest, these side windows are so hazy, that when the Sun shines on them, they just about - they're real poor for any visual observation or photography - heads up.

a08_0782433.speaker: Collins
a08_0782433.text: Roger. Understand.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay. Okay, IMU align, REFSMMAT - We've done that.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay. Did you finish that camera, or do you want me to do it?

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay, I'm going to go to Block, right?

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Yes. You did the IMU alignment? Think the GDC will last for another REV or not?

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: That's okay.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Roll 180 degrees at 2 degrees per second.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: You ready to roll, Jim?

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Yes, you're going back to what now?

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay. Here's a piece of camera equipment. Where does this go?

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay, man.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Here's your map, and here's your book, Jim.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay. Okay, let me make sure I'm [garble].

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay, now here's what we have to do this time, Bill. I've got two AUTO OPTICS positions in, and - and - I've got to get a third landmark. Okay, let me see. The time would be...

a08_0783605-onboard.text: No, they just said don't worry about the sixt - No, it's working, but they said if it does act up, don't worry about the...

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Frank, here's a map floating or - Jim, here's a map floating around.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: 0h, it's right there.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: You know, that was one of the easiest points I've ever found.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Good.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: You didn't need maps or anything to make that [garble]. You saw it, too, didn't you? You didn't have to look at the map but one time?

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Yes, out the side window there when we had the TV pass.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: I hope you got some good 70-millimeter shots of the area, Bill, because that's - that's it...

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Of our prime landing area, because right now we'll be passing over lighting conditions of our P-2...

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: No, I'm still taking pictures. I'm still landmark tracking.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Yes, I can't take - I can't take pictures when you're tracking, because these side windows are shot. They look out the side anyway.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Well, that's why I wanted to get some before when we were doing that tracking, because then - Did you do them when we got that other track?

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: I tried to.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: I think - Probably be our primary landing site.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Why don't you just make it a project just to make sure you get some, because you can recognize it better than I can.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Oh, yes, but you...

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: You got...

a08_0783605-onboard.text: No, the 16's no good. You've got to - you've got a 70-millimeter lens? If you have image - if you - if you - if you track your target, then you've got better resolution than the other one.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Well, the thing is, it doesn't show enough of what you want to look for; that's the big thing, too. Yet, in spite of the place to land, you...

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Huh? Okay, let me show you how much you get, though.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: What - what I'm trying to show the people is the big - big areas around there, what they can see in the way of craters and mountains and things. You see, if I just show them a real fine resolution of a bunch of craters, they don't know what they are.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: That's the big point.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: That's why that Earth-Moon shot with a whole big expanse of - What have we got?

a08_0783605-onboard.text: High gain. Okay. It's behind us and up. Let's try omni B. Okay.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay. [Garble] pitch down at 0000.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: It'll get worse before it gets better.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay. Let's see, out first control point is at...

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay, let's see how much time we got.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: ...78:46. We got all sorts of time. We got 25 minutes.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: 0.2 of a degree per second.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: You get - give me the word on the ORDEAL, here, Jim, and - let me know how we're doing. 62 60?

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Yes.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay, that sounds good. How about giving me a...

a08_0783605-onboard.text: The other one's 1/250?

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Take a look, take a look.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: [Garble] left and then 150th.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay, 1/500th of a second.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay.

a08_0783605-onboard.text: It seems like I've been here forever.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: The things that I saw that were interesting were the new craters.
