a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: You got it, looking at you.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Okay, that's...

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: That's your pitch.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: What? Zero? Or 34?

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0783605-onboard.text: 34 degrees.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: That's good. Good.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Coming up on rev 6.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0783605-onboard.text: [Garble].

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: Yes, you just went down about 5 minutes ago.

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0783605-onboard.text: [Garble].

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: No. [Laughter.]

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0783605-onboard.text: [Garble].

a08_0783605-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0783605-onboard.text: That's right. [Laughter.]

a08_0783630.speaker: Collins
a08_0783630.text: Roger. The last state vector updates we sent you, Jim, was to the LM slots and you'll have to transfer that over to the CSM slots using Verb 47 Enter. Over.

a08_0783816.speaker: Collins
a08_0783816.text: Roger. Bill has got his tape recorder back, and we noticed during that last dump, it was all in low bit rate. We wonder whether that was intentional or not? Over. [Pause.]

a08_0783816.speaker: Anders
a08_0783816.text: Roger. We didn't have much to say; we couldn't see out of the windows very well, Mike.

a08_0783900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0783900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston here; and that's a pretty tired Jim Lovell we're hearing today. Take it from somebody who's listened to him now for some 18 - 14 and 4 and 3 - 21 days [he is adding up the days Jim has spent in space on Gemini 7, Gemini 12 and Apollo 8 so far]. Here's some more conversation, I think he's just about to get a Go for Rev 6.

a08_0784031.speaker: Collins
a08_0784031.text: Roger, Bill. This next time around into the sunlight, we do not expect any problem with the primary evaporator. If it does start drying out, we think it's best just to close the back-pressure valve, and there's no need to activate the secondary boiler. Over.

a08_0784031.speaker: Anders
a08_0784031.text: Okay. I guess the 60-degree limit will still hold then. [Pause.]

a08_0784031.speaker: Collins
a08_0784031.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're suggesting you disregard the 60-degree limit; let it go ahead and rise up above 60. There's no need to activate the secondary. Over.

a08_0784031.speaker: Anders
a08_0784031.text: Okay. We just don't want to boil our IMU.

a08_0784031.speaker: Collins
a08_0784031.text: Apollo 8, you're Go for the next lunar orbit rev.

a08_0784031.speaker: Lovell
a08_0784031.text: Roger, Houston. I'll read the book this time.

a08_0784300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0784300-pao.text: Apollo Control here. We're 15 minutes to Loss of Signal. We'll take the line down and bring you any additional comments that may occur between now and Loss of Signal. This is Apollo Control, Houston at 78 hours, 43 minutes.

a08_0785408.speaker: Collins
a08_0785408.text: Rog. We have about 4½ minutes to LOS; and before we have LOS, we'd like your last PRD readout. Over.

a08_0785408.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785408.text: Stand by. The Commander's asleep; we'll get his when he wakes up.

a08_0785408.speaker: Anders
a08_0785408.text: The LMP is still 6, point - correction, 0.64. [Pause.]

a08_0785804.speaker: Collins
a08_0785804.text: Apollo 8, Houston. About 40 seconds to LOS, and everything's looking good down here.

a08_0785804.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785804.text: Roger. Houston. We'll give it another try here.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: What time is it there? About 2 o'clock?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Are you finished with the computer?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Well, the last time I looked at them, they were pretty good, chief.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: All the gauges are looking at each other.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: If you want to say anything about your tracking pass this time, I - Just let me know and we can go into high bit rate.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Okay, how about keeping your eye on these camera settings, too, on the next couple of passes?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: You wanted to be 10 degrees, didn't you?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Okay, the first one is 1/500th of a second.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: All those scientists are saying now, "Ohhh, if we only had a geologist onboard.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Okay, he couldn't see anything. I took that monocular and tried to eyeball it out the window last time.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Nothing but a big blur out there. He'd see enough to make it interesting, but not enough to do anything.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Okay, I'm going to go out of here.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Okay. when's your first PCA - TCA?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Oh. boy. I may see the Sun; I'd better be careful too. Hey, there is - there's a - Here's a glow, you can see the Sun come around a little bit.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Yes, I can see the Sun come up before it comes up.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Like zodiacal light, a little bit, maybe.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Rim brightening, they call it? (Probably means Limb brightening)

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Yes, it's a real bright glow right in one spot, and it fans out all over the horizon. And I'm just trying to move my eye away, because the Sun's going to peek over here any second now, and it's getting brighter and brighter, and it's get - It's an even light.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Bright spot fans out over horizon?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Yes, yes, then it fans up into the air; it's an even light; then all of sudden, it - The Sun is peeking out right now.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Geez, I got a start there. I saw that - some stuff come out of the optics or something; I thought it was a star whirling by.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: All right, now you want to roll to keep that trunnion...

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: We wouldn't want - I didn't realize you were that quick. Okay, which way?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Watch her - watch her as she comes down.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Yes, right now. You got enough roll? What happened?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: I went to Manual. I'll get it for you.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: You all right? You got your camera on?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: I'll put it on, just as soon as we get rid of the Sun.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Wait a minute, you - you want me to - you want me to try to avoid it?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Yes, you can pitch down a little bit.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Hey, wait a minute, are you - I'm roll - I may roll over 10 degrees.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: No, I'm not driving it now. Well, I'm driving it now, yes. That's enough. That's enough.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Let me go back there and try this CMC again.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Okay, let's try that one again.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: You can pitch down a little more, if you want to.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Okay, Auto Optics is doing the whole thing for me. Now - get this camera going.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: My Auto Optics has put it right on.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: We going to make that angle, or not?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: I'm just letting it run here for a little bit before I try to brake it.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: That's - that's okay. Don't bother using up gas. Okay.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: All right. I already bothered, I'm sorry.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Yes. Sorry, Frank, I didn't mean to disturb you. Thought I pushed the wrong button.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Okay, just hold it right there.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Okay, we've got another one coming up. Same procedure.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: This is - Now, where's that book?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Should be coming up on Low right now.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Okay, we're tracking the new one.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Do we have the recorder on?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: On LOW bit rate. Do you want to say something?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: You're quite welcome. Okay, why don't you stop it, and put it to high bit rate, and put it forward again?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Tape recorder is where - Record, Forward...

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Just put it - put it to Stop

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Which one is it, the center?

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: No, no, no, no. Push this forward.

a08_0785832-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0785832-onboard.text: Put it this way in the middle.

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Tape recorder is where - Record, Forward...

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Just put it - put it to Stop

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Which one is it, the center?

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0792400-onboard.text: No, no, no, no. Push this forward.

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Put it this way in the middle.

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Good and loud; they'll never be able to hear you there.

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Several comments on landmark tracking. The last time I used Auto Optics, putting in the coordinates, I found the first time in Manual Optics for CP-1, the G&N system did quite well. It tracked almost as good as I could track manually right on the target, and I tipped it over just at the last moment to take my five marks. There - appears to be very smooth tracking; no problem - with this particular system. I'm now in CP-2; I have it just below the horizon now, and it's tracking down from the horizon automatically.

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Okay. Now, what do you want me to do?

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Look at that! It is right on!

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Are you using this map for anything, Jim?

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: No, this is pretty good, though, I didn't - Maybe that could be the problem. Maybe I could [garble].

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Oh, it's scheduled a little later in the day [garble].

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: You hear that noise over there?

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0792400-onboard.text: How long does this hand controller stay armed?

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Did you see our landing site, Frank?

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: I'll do one thing until I get up there, but [garble].

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: You want to take a look at this? [Garble] it's something - I don't know what.

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: Frank, we're just finishing up the [garble] here. [Garble].

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0792400-onboard.text: We've got to copy this [garble], too.

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0792400-onboard.text: [Garble] Frank, the SPS is about [garble] hours [garble].

a08_0792400-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0792400-onboard.text: We got about 4 hours [garble]. It's about 4½ hours.

a08_0794536.speaker: Collins
a08_0794536.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0794536.speaker: Collins
a08_0794536.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0794536.speaker: Collins
a08_0794536.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.

a08_0794536.speaker: Collins
a08_0794536.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0794600-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0794600-pao.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0794600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0794600-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 79 hours, 46 minutes into the flight. Mike Collins has sent up two calls and we've got no response - we think we've got some keying action, but that's all. To date, we've - on the basis of earlier revs, we've gotten used to now, to turning to our EECOM and asking the first question as we come around the corner, 'how's the evaporator' and the answer is this time it's working great. They apparently have the right handle on it. As I mentioned earlier, it's seeing large temperature excursions, apparently no larger than people within the project office and at North

a08_0795100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0795100-pao.text: Still no - no answer, no additional calls as a matter of fact. Mike Collins tries again. And we might have a ground antenna problem. Checking our ground stations now. In this temperature area, the evaporator, of course, isn't the only area seeing the same order of temperature excursions. I'm looking at a Command Service Module RCS summary here, which shows - presents temperature readings at four or five points, on various tanks surfaces in the Service Module and, see one valve inlet temperature here which is a specific six digit identified point which varies the low and the high are listed ove

a08_0795100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0795100-pao.text: It's been nearly six minutes now since we acquired and just getting a general background noise. We've had no additional - no additional attempts to raise the spacecraft. So based on what EECOM says, we may wait a few minutes before trying additional calls. We'll be back up then. It's 79 hours, 51 minutes into the flight; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0795100-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0795100-pao.text: Roger. Reading you very weak but a lot of background noise. Welcome back around. How are you reading us?

a08_0795156.speaker: Collins
a08_0795156.text: Roger. Reading you very weak but a lot of background noise. Welcome back around. How are you reading us?

a08_0795543.speaker: Lovell
a08_0795543.text: Roger, Houston. A few words on our optics tracking system. I used auto optics for control points 1 and 2 on the backside, and they worked beautifully, tracked both targets for me. And I went to the control point 3, as designated in our orbital control book, to see the latitude and longitude that was given to me and used auto optics to track that particular coordinate with it, and it was very close to the actual tracking plot. I picked the mark there where I did a final marking and recorded latitude and longitude. I'm now about to come up on the landing site and using auto optics, using the cod

a08_0795700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0795700-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston here. We are locked up and Jim Lovell is giving us an interesting description of his use of the auto optics in his tracking tasks on the back side of the Moon. Here it is.

a08_0795700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0795700-pao.text: Apollo Control here. In this lull, we perhaps should take advantage at least to point out to the people in the newsrooms, who, may not - not have not noticed it yet. Our latest data display on our - one of our walls, there's the words Merry Christmas, Apollo 8. The Merry is in red letters, the Christmas is in white letters, and the Apollo 8 is in blue letters. That display went up about an hour ago. I guess it technically should be called data. The consensus here is of course, that the crew is and remains quite busy and we're going to have some updates in the course of this pass, the sixth rev

a08_0795900-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0795900-pao.text: Roger. We know you're busy so we're not going to bother you. We're watching your progress on the DSKY. You're looking good; all your systems are looking good and we have maneuver PADs for you any time at your convenience.

a08_0795900-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0795900-pao.text: Roger. We'll take them when we're doing the P52, if that's okay.

a08_0795900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0795900-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control, Houston; at 80 hours, 1 minute into the flight. We apparently are not going to have very much communication at this point. We'll come back up when we do. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0795928.speaker: Collins
a08_0795928.text: Roger. We know you're busy so we're not going to bother you. We're watching your progress on the DSKY. You're looking good; all your systems are looking good and we have maneuver PADs for you any time at your convenience.

a08_0795928.speaker: Anders
a08_0795928.text: Roger. We'll take them when we're doing the P52, if that's okay.

a08_0800756.speaker: Lovell
a08_0800756.text: Roger. I drew up in Auto Optics now on the landing site. It would just warm up old Jack Schmitt's heart. The auto optics is tracking perfectly on the - on the target, and the two IPs turned out beautifully. I have a beautiful view of it. The first IP's just barely beneath the vertical now, and the second one's coming up. It's just a grand view.

a08_0800756.speaker: Collins
a08_0800756.text: Glad to hear it, Jim. Jack's listening. [Long pause.]

a08_0800756.speaker: Lovell
a08_0800756.text: For Jack's information, the Sun angles that we see now from the first IP, second IP, and the B-1 are just right, I think, for landing conditions. The shadows aren't too deep for you to get confused, but the land is - has texture to it, and there are enough shadows to make everything stand out. [Pause.]

a08_0800756.speaker: Anders
a08_0800756.text: If Jack's listening, tell him that the optics may be doing all right, but the eyeballs are having a little trouble looking through all this smear on the windows.

a08_0800756.speaker: Collins
a08_0800756.text: Roger. Understand the optics are doing better than the eyeballs. How about the cameras?

a08_0800756.speaker: Anders
a08_0800756.text: The cameras have the same smear to look through. The rendezvous windows are okay, but they're so small and looking in the wrong directions here so far.

a08_0800756.speaker: Anders
a08_0800756.text: I think the vertical stereo will be okay.

a08_0800756.speaker: Anders
a08_0800756.text: It certainly looks like we're picking the more interesting parts of the Moon to land in. The back side looks like a sand pile my kids have been playing in for a long time. It's all beat up, no definition. Just a lot of bumps and holes. [Pause.]

a08_0800756.speaker: Lovell
a08_0800756.text: I'm looking 2P-2 right now, Houston, and it's a great spot.

a08_0800756.speaker: Anders
a08_0800756.text: The area that we're over right now gives some hint of possible volcanics, though I really can't eyeball it at the moment to pin that down. There are some craters and build-ups that just definitely suggest volcanic activity.

a08_0800756.speaker: Collins
a08_0800756.text: Rog. Understand, Bill, and understand Jim thinks the ole 2P-2 is a winner. [Pause.]

a08_0800756.speaker: Anders
a08_0800756.text: Yeah, that backside doesn't look too interesting.

a08_0801500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0801500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 80 hours, 15 minutes into the flight. In the last few minutes we've recorded some most enthusiastic comments from Jim Lovell on his assignment. Comments from Lovell and from Anders on their tracking assignment during this - these inner - these middle revs around the Moon. Lovell pays astronaut Jack Schmitt, Harrison Schmitt actually, a PhD in Geology, a great compliment with the work that he and other members of the Lunar Mapping Science Laboratory here in MSC have done in picking various Moonmarks or landmarks leading to the sites we've picked out as probable

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Roger, Jim.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: We have you on the High Gain Antenna. We'd like you to take the DSE and dump it. Over.

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: Houston. Are you going to use our computer to update our state vector?

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: That's affirmative, Jim. We'd - we'd like to - stand by one, and I'll tell you when to go to P00 and Accept.

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: Roger. Then I'll work my 52 around your [garble]. [Long pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Jim, would you please go to P00 and Accept, and we'll send you a P27, LM state vector update.

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: Roger. You have P00...

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Thank you.

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: ...and Accept.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. We have a little piece of useful information if you're interested in deliberating over it.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Go ahead. Say again?

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: Roger. Our first control point is very near the terminator, and as the optics were tracking it, I had occasion to watch the Sun come up. And at about 2 minutes before sunrise, you get - the limb begins to brighten up into sort of a fine white haze, a faint glow completely over the space just behind the limb. [Pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Rog. Understand. About 2 minutes before the Sun comes up, you get a fine white haze radiating out from behind the limb. How far out does it extend?

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: It goes up quite a ways. It takes a fan shape, unlike the sunrise on Earth where the atmosphere affects it. This just sort of is a complete haze all over the local area. It's concentrated at the exact spot the sun comes up at ignition and then goes away from the sun spots. Very interesting.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Roger, Jim. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're standing by with your map and TEI-7 updates. [Pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: Stand by. [Pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You can go back to Block at your computer.

a08_0801852.speaker: Lovell
a08_0801852.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Okay, Mike. We're ready for the map update and - and then the TEI.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Okay. When you got your - before you get your map book out, the Houston Comm Techs have got a little word for an old ex-CapCom. They say they consider you go on Remote. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Not permanently, I hope.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Okay. Your map update for rev 6/7: LOS, 80:57:24; sunrise, 81:06:57; prime meridian, 81:13:02. Are you with me?

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: You cut out after the prime meridian. I got it, but not AOS

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: AOS, 81:43:05; sunset, 82:19:54; remarks: IP-1, TCA for B-1, 82:07:39; and now I've got four more times for you which are acquisition times for when various things come over the horizon. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Okay. Control point 1, acquisition time, 81:09:05; control point 2, acquisition time, 81:21:48; control point 3, acquisition time, 81:43:17; B-1 acquisition time, 82:03:54. And I say again, all those ACQ times are when they first come over the horizon. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Roger. Copy, Houston. And in about 2 seconds, I'll be ready for the TEI.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: All right. [Long pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: I am ready.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: TEI-7; SPS/G&N - stand by one, Bill. [Long pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Just a matter of general interest, Houston: everybody is feeling good, and the CDR is taking a snooze.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Roger. Glad to hear it. We're just talking about a water dump down here. We've got one coming up, and it looks like on this rev prior to the time around LOS or just prior to LOS, would be a convenient time to do it. Do you concur?

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Okay. We will. Down to 25 percent again?

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: That's affirmative, and we'd also be interested in any comments about what these various dumps have done to your optics, if anything, and how long the effects last after a dump.

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Don't seem to have done anything to the optics, but they've definitely got in some of the windows. There are a few little chunks of ice on window number 1, which is nearest the vent, and also on window number 5 a little bit; windows 2 and 4 remain amazingly clear. [Pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Roger. Thank you, Bill, and I'm ready to resume the PAD when you are.

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Okay. Press on with the weight.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: All right. Weight, 45701; minus 0.40, plus 1.57; 083:18:20.80; plus 3234.6, minus 0116.8, plus 0573.0. Are you with me so far? Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Go ahead, Mike.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Rog. I got down through Delta-V, X, Y, and Z. Did you copy these? Over.

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: No I didn't read a word. I'm still waiting for the weight.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Roger. Let's go back to the weight: 45701; minus 0.40, plus 1.57. Are you with me? Over.

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Sounds good.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Okay. GETI, 083:18:20.80; plus 3234.6, minus 0116.8, plus 4 - correction - plus 0573.0. Are you with me? Over.

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Roger.

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Thank you. 179, 009, 001; not applicable, plus 0018.7; 3287.0, 3:07, 3267.6; 42, 088.0, 25.3; 033, down 12.1, left 2.7; plus 07.90, minus 165.00; 1297.3, 36238, 146:44:14; same north set, Sirius and Rigel, roll 129, pitch 155, yaw 010; 4 quads for 15 seconds; horizon on the 2-degree mark at T ignition . Over. [Pause.]

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Roger. TEI-7; SPS/G&N; 45701; minus 0.40, plus 1.57; 083:18:20.80; plus 3234.6, minus 0116.8, plus 0573.0; 179, 9 - correction - 009, 001; N/A. Are you with me?

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: Yeah, I'm with you, Bill.

a08_0801852.speaker: Anders
a08_0801852.text: Plus 0018.7; 3287.0, 3:07, 3267.6; 32 - correction - 42, 088.0, 25.3; 033, down 12.1, left 2.7; plus 07.90, minus 165.00; 1297.3, 36238, 146:44:14; same north set, Sirius, Rigel, 129, 155, 010; 4 jet, 15 seconds, 2 degrees on the horizon at T IG .

a08_0801852.speaker: Collins
a08_0801852.text: That's all correct.

a08_0803600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0803600-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston here; 80 hours, 36 minutes into the flight and I think we're going to have a little pause here perhaps for another 10 to 15 minutes before we come upon our final conversation and the spacecraft goes over the hill on this sixth rev around the Moon. Present orbit; apogee, 62.3; perigee, 59.8; velocity, 5,338 feet per second. At 80 hours, 36 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0803912.speaker: Collins
a08_0803912.text: Roger. You got your DSE back, and you are Go for the next lunar orbit. Over.

a08_0803912.speaker: Anders
a08_0803912.text: Roger. How far did you want us to dump that water?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: We ought to get that thing set up right now.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Because I can be - we can be tracking while we're dumping, too.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Are you getting out, Frank? You getting out?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Wait a minute; pitch up. You [garble] you pitch down [garble].

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Well, let me see now. That's the right connection; I think so. We got - Where is the filter, Bill?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: I think they made a mistake here in the Flight Plan.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Oh, you have it on here, huh?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Do you have the water - This - Urine Heater's been On, right?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: If you pitch down, yes...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, we have the hose connected, so we want to go through the procedure.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, Waste Stowage Vent, Vent for 5 seconds.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: You want to be...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: (Garbled.)

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: I'll show you; just a minute.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes, they're Opened and Closed [garble] here. I'm in 4-A? Okay, if it's reading 1, I could put Waste - Waste Tank's Vent for 5 seconds, huh?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Right, Waste Stowage, Vent, yes, for 5 seconds.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Done.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Battery, Vent.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes. Take her down?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Take the Battery, Vent, down. It's not down; let it come down.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Well, it's getting real close to it.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Oh, there it goes. Okay, it's down.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: It's down?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, close them both.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Make sure your Urine Heater's On.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Urine Heat's on A.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay. And - go ahead and dump the waste.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, we take that over and put it an - where it says, "Open/Close, Waste Tank Servicing.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Put that to Open. Leave it go in there.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, now we got to watch the waste tank.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes, I'm watching it.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: You're watching it? Okay. You got Waste Tank, On, then?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: I don't know, Frank.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: It's still pretty good. Let's see here [garble].

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: You want to get up here now?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, just about even.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: You want to get up on one of these seats? You want to get up here?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: This is okay over here. Clear.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: It'd be a good time to do it, because there's more - Jim's really the only one that's busy, and I can fix his.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes, it - it'll take a good while.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: It's up at 85 percent. Right now, it's 47.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Now much film do we have left over, Bill?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Well, I'll tell you, Jim, these windows are so bad, you can just take pictures - say one - We need - we need - Don't get into that interior - interior's for inside stuff; and we need one - 16 millimeter for the convergent stereo, and - oh, about a half of one for that image-motion compensation which - kind of a low-priority thing.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Do you do you want Verb 83? Did you look for...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes, it's the [garble] isn't all that bad, but we could try - we are allowed to yaw. We could try Verb 83 for drill.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, I'd better get out the books and...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: This one says 92; I'll crank it around a little bit.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, how's our RCS doing?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Good.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Let's see if...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Well, it hasn't changed since we started. See, it's still about - 67 percent.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: SPS is holding steady.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Did you cycle through the EPS, Jim? [Garble]...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: No, I haven't done that, yet. Okay, and don't forget...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: (Garbled.)

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes, well...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, EPS. You're on BAT B charge, you know?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes, just leave that there, don't change that.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, it's 39 [garble] now.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, I can cycle this one okay, right?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Slip those around those cameras, Jim, and I'll fix them while you're shooting that landing site.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay, we got - let's see, we got 23 minutes until sunrise, so we've got a lot of time.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: I haven't seen that water going down any at all.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: (Garbled.)

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Well, [garble] steam pressure's...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: It's not going down any.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Bill.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Not going down.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: What?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Not going down.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Okay. you want to - Let's see here. Put the purge line - Take that wat - Shut the wa - Well, that off - put the water on, and - put that purge fitting on it.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Ask Houston if it's...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: (Garbled.)

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Oh!

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: (Garbled.)

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: That's one thing you forgot to tell us!

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: (Laughter.)

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Here it goes.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes, I can see it; it's dumping.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: And we solved another mystery!

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: We have three problems and one's F. Borman.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: (Garbled.)

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes, it's going down.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: (Laughter)

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes, it is. Yes.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: [Garble.]

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Huh?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: [Garble] water?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: 60 - 70 - 75 percent, 75 percent.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: (Singing.)

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Well, did you guys ever think that one Christmas you'd be orbiting the Moon?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: I say, one Christmas Eve you'd be orbiting the Moon?

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Just hope we're not doing it on New Year's.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Hey, hey, don't talk like that, Bill; think positive.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0803943-onboard.text: [Garble.]

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: I said, just hope we don't do it on New Year's.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: That was pretty spectacular: never to see the Moon until just before braking into - into LOI.

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: That's kind of a nonchalant approach, you know that (laughter)? Remember Warren North's procedure of eyeball the Moon, and whatever we had to do to...

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0803943-onboard.text: Yes, [garble].

a08_0803943-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0803943-onboard.text: The other way [laughter].

a08_0804052.speaker: Lovell
a08_0804052.text: Are you receiving our - our tracking data? [Pause.]

a08_0804052.speaker: Collins
a08_0804052.text: That's affirmative, Jim. We are receiving.

a08_0804052.speaker: Collins
a08_0804052.text: And also, Jim, we - That last P27 we sent you was for the LM state vector only, and it will require a Verb 47 Enter to transfer to the CSM slot. Over.

a08_0804539.speaker: Anders
a08_0804539.text: Okay. We're dumping the waste tank now, Houston.

a08_0805257.speaker: Collins
a08_0805257.text: Roger. We've got four minutes 'til LOS, and everything's looking good down here.

a08_0805257.speaker: Anders
a08_0805257.text: How much longer do you think we have to go into battery charge there, Mike?

a08_0805257.speaker: Anders
a08_0805257.text: If you can wake up the EECOM, why don't you have him ask the back room?

a08_0805257.speaker: Collins
a08_0805257.text: Oh, you really know how to hurt a guy. [Pause.]

a08_0805257.speaker: Collins
a08_0805257.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We estimate charge will be complete in another 45 minutes. Over.

a08_0805559.speaker: Collins
a08_0805559.text: Apollo 8, Houston. One minute to LOS, and standing by.

a08_0805559.speaker: Anders
a08_0805559.text: Okay. See you on the other side, Mike.

a08_0805650-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0805650-onboard.text: Would you turn my S-band volume down to about 2, Mike - Jim?

a08_0805700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0805700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 80 hours, 57 minutes. We're - we've just lost signal with the spacecraft, we have several minutes of conversation to play out for you, but before we get to that I want to mention one or two things. I don't think we've made mention of the fact today that we have finally, after six revolutions, gotten used to watching the spacecraft go from the right side of our front wall map to the left, just as it is proceeding around the Moon in a retrograde orbit. This, after all these years of watching the spacecraft move from the left side of the wall map to the right, i

a08_0805700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0805700-pao.text: One other announcement, we presently plan no press conference this afternoon, I repeat no press conference at our change of shift because we really see no new information to offer. You've heard the bulk of the conversation today and I think it's all been very straightforward. And in view of the extraordinarily long hours that many of us have been in the control center, we would like to bypass the afternoon press conference which would have occurred about 6 o'clock, and continue to observe the activities through the evening hours, and top off the evening with a Trans-Earth Injection some time a

a08_0813309-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0813309-onboard.text: The last two control points I've been tracking with the sextant which gives us - gives me much finer control to track the landmark with. I've been using the same landmarks as before. And the sextant magnifies the landmark, and it's very easy to maintain the sextant on the landmark.

a08_0813309-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0813309-onboard.text: Resolved to Medium were the control modes.

a08_0813309-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0813309-onboard.text: On the second control point, the crater which I take, which is in the middle of Gemini, is very easy to see one side has collapsed, the side to the west. And you can see rocks and debris tumbling down. On many of the craters that go by, especially near the one on control point 1, I can see where hard rock had stayed in place around the rim of the crater as the rest of the debris had folded over into a mound down into that crater floor.

a08_0813309-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0813309-onboard.text: I'm coming up on the crater - as a matter of fact, the Crater Slayton right now. We're going directly over it.

a08_0813309-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0813309-onboard.text: And just beyond that one is the Crater Carr.

a08_0813309-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0813309-onboard.text: The newer craters that surround the older ones have sharper ridges - and the - They're more roundly formed - like - like cones, funnels, and along the insides are a brighter material than the other craters. And they also don't have the step functions that the ligger - bigger craters have. There's one - there's two bright craters just to the west of Slayton that have this particular characteristic.

a08_0813309-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0813309-onboard.text: In the vicinity of the Crater Carr, it's very difficult to see the ground now; it's very bright, a uniform brightness, and the craters seem to dim out somewhat.

a08_0813309-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0813309-onboard.text: You can still make some of the rilles and hills of the smaller craters and the white material of the newly formed ones, but - it's much more a hazy appearance than craters on either side. That must be near the sub-solar point.

a08_0813309-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0813309-onboard.text: Okay. You can stop it now, if you want to.

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814035-onboard.text: You got a program alarm, Bill.

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814035-onboard.text: Well, you got a Restart that time.

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814035-onboard.text: Verb 34, huh? Well, you gave me bum dope. Well, I'll be dog-gonned!

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814035-onboard.text: No, it's the Earth coming up.

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814035-onboard.text: What did you get, another program alarm?

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0814035-onboard.text: Fine. Okay, Jim, well, it's your time to take a rest.

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814035-onboard.text: [Garble] reach those two program alarms and the Restart. And it is your time to take a rest.

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814035-onboard.text: Okay, just a minute. Let me - Verb 37 - Verb 37, Enter, 00. Okay, we got one more coming up here.

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814035-onboard.text: Minus 89, then plus 48631, Enter; minus 00253, Enter, Proceed.

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0814035-onboard.text: What do you want, the gun? I'll hand it to you.

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814035-onboard.text: Where's the update book? Does anybody know?

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814035-onboard.text: Yes, I got it here in my hand.

a08_0814035-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814035-onboard.text: If I got a program alarm, disregard it - it's because I took too many marks.

a08_0814300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0814300-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston here; 81 hours, 43 minutes. We have not yet acquired nor have we put in a call, but since it's about that time, we thought we had better come up and let everybody know we're here. We have acquisition now and we're getting telemetry data. And apparently Mike Collins is going to wait a few minutes before he initiates the conversation. Here we go with the call. Let's bring it up.

a08_0814300-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0814300-pao.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0814358.speaker: Collins
a08_0814358.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0814358.speaker: Collins
a08_0814358.text: Roger, Frank. Good morning. You're loud and clear, how me?

a08_0814651.speaker: Collins
a08_0814651.text: Roger. We have a request that Jim space his marks, his five marks out a bit more slowly. If possible, we'd like to get a couple of them past the zenith. We're getting five of them with rather rapid spacing, and from a geometry viewpoint, it would be better if you'd slow them down a little bit and lengthened them out so as to include a couple of them past the zenith. Over.

a08_0814651.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814651.text: Houston, Apollo 8. That last set of marks are invalid. Disregard what Jim [?] drew the last time.

a08_0814651.speaker: Collins
a08_0814651.text: Roger. Understand the last set of marks are invalid. Over

a08_0814651.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814651.text: Roger. If you'd correlate with - The set I'm about to take is the last set.

a08_0814651.speaker: Collins
a08_0814651.text: We've got an awful lot of background noise, Jim. Could you say again please?

a08_0814651.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814651.text: Rog. I'm coming up on control point 3. I tried to stick another control point in between 2 and 3, but didn't do it, so I just - to get out of the program, I just marked and got out of the program.

a08_0814651.speaker: Collins
a08_0814651.text: Rog. Understand you are coming up on 3. Thank you.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: If I got a program alarm, disregard it - it's because I took too many marks.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: This time, it did though, huh?

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: I'll stretch her out all the way.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: You got the hot water on? I can pour some hot water while I'm waiting.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0814949-onboard.text: Let me know if anybody else wants some.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: Had his leg against the hose.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: I just gave it to you.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: That's okay. It's below the Earth.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: It won't drive now until it - If it's below 50.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: You can't keep up with the landing site, I should say.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: There goes the trunnion now, see, Bill - Frank?

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: It's tracking us beneath the Earth.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: Oh, I'm a little tired. I guess we all are.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: You're going to be busy right afterwards. Those last two rev's.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: I've got a sleep period coming up here, though, I think. Don't I?

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: What do we have on our TV debut?

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: You mean on the left there?

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: Well, it's always here; I haven't started tracking, yet.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: Do you see it coming up already?

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: On the left; I'm not sure if that's it or not, though, but it's a triangular - shaped mound.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: Oh, here we go, right now.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: This isn't computing the right thing, here.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: I'm down some. You want me to pitch up?

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: I could easily see a LM on here.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: I'm through with the landing site right now. Don't touch the computer, though.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: Let me see - Have you got the update book, Bill?

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: No, I gave it back to you if I recall. Did you look down in here?

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: I did, I gave it back, because I don't think that...

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: Get rolled over here, Jim. Then, you can do a P52.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: You might as well start shooting some of this film, Bill, because we're not going to do this convergent stereo because we've got that high TV. And then we're going to get ready for TEI and knock everything else off.

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0814949-onboard.text: Bill, you want to take care of this 16-millimeter camera?

a08_0814949-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0814949-onboard.text: We should be able to get them on - on High Gain here in a minute, Bill.

a08_0815100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0815100-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control. Let's see our cabin temperature. Cabin pressure is 4.9 [psi]. Cabin temperature, 77 degrees [F] and we apparently have the biomed switch on none of the pilots at this point. We're getting no data there. Here goes our call.

a08_0815100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0815100-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control, Houston. It sounds like another long, quiet - very much of a working pass. The 81 hours, 51 minutes, the - with Frank Borman up as you heard. He'll be very busy flying the spacecraft. Lovell continues doing Program 22 auto optic exercises. Got just a solid block, one after another to do through this entire rev. Bill Anders is sandwiching - literally sandwiching in an eat period here between additional landmarks, more photography. Here's more conversation.

a08_0815203.speaker: Collins
a08_0815203.text: Roger. On Jim's marks, we'd like to get spacing of approximately 30, 30 seconds between each mark. The last ones, we're copying roughly 15 seconds between marks and we'd like to stretch it out even further if that's okay with you.

a08_0820220.speaker: Lovell
a08_0820220.text: Roger, Mike. I find that tracking is much easier using the sextant than the scanning telescope. You have finer control, and at these orbital speeds, Resolved and Medium seems to be the best combination.

a08_0820220.speaker: Collins
a08_0820220.text: Roger, Jim. I copy that it's easier for you to use the sextant than the scanning telescope. It gives you finer control, and say again after that. [Pause.]

a08_0820220.speaker: Collins
a08_0820220.text: Roger. I copy that it's - tracking is easier using the sextant than the scanning telescope; it gives you finer control, and say again after that? Over.

a08_0820220.speaker: Lovell
a08_0820220.text: And the combination of Resolved and Medium is perhaps the best combination - the combination of - Speed, Low is too low; we can't catch up with the target.

a08_0820220.speaker: Collins
a08_0820220.text: Roger. Understand that the best combination is Resolved and Medium. Low is just too low.

a08_0821300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0821300-pao.text: Ground Elapsed Time, 82 hours to 83 hours, 10 minutes - an hour and 10 minutes - Bill Anders will get a rest, a well deserved one with all his lunch. At 81 hours, 53 minutes this is Apollo Control, Houston. We'll be back up with more action when it occurs.

a08_0821333.speaker: Lovell
a08_0821333.text: Roger. I'm not to too sure what happened that time, Mike. I was marking on the landing sites, using the code, and I kept getting a large trunnion for auto optics. And I could see the target, or landing site was coming up, so I just went manually and marked, and yet the - the latitude and longitude was - were quite different from the nominal.

a08_0821700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0821700-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 82 hours, 13 minutes into the flight, and we are in the midst of one of our quieter passes today. We've had very little conversation. Here's what we've had in the last 10 or 15 minutes.

a08_0821700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0821700-pao.text: Apollo Control here, that brings us up to the live action. I can't really tell if this conversation will be extended or not. Mike Collins is doing a lot of note taking. Let's hold on for a minute or two and see. Each revolution around the Moon today, the crew has been given a Go approximately about 20 minutes before Loss of Signal. Right now we stand 38 minutes from Loss of Signal on this particular rev. About to pass the navigational updates to the crew. Here it goes.

a08_0821700-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0821700-pao.text: Roger. We're checking into Jim's remarks on his P22; and in the meantime, I have your maneuver PADs and map updates, at your convenience. Over.

a08_0821720.speaker: Collins
a08_0821720.text: Roger. We're checking into Jim's remarks on his P22; and in the meantime, I have your maneuver PADs and map updates, at your convenience. Over.

a08_0821720.speaker: Borman
a08_0821720.text: Go ahead with your data, Mike.

a08_0821720.speaker: Collins
a08_0821720.text: Okay. Before that, we'd like to take the DSE away from you, please, for a while. [Pause.]

a08_0821720.speaker: Collins
a08_0821720.text: Thank you, and we'd like you to go to P00 and Accept. We have a P27 state vector update for you. [Pause.]

a08_0821720.speaker: Borman
a08_0821720.text: There's P00, and I'm going to Accept.

a08_0821720.speaker: Collins
a08_0821720.text: Which would you like first, the map update or the TEI-8?

a08_0821720.speaker: Collins
a08_0821720.text: Okay. Map update. LOS, 82:55:54; sunrise, 83:05:49; prime meridian, 83:11:38; AOS, 83:41:43; sunset, 84:18:45; remarks: control point 1 acquisition, 83:07:39; control point 2 acquisition, 83:20:21; control point 3 acq., 83:41:51; B-1 acquisition, 84:02:28. Over.

a08_0821720.speaker: Collins
a08_0821720.text: Roger. The TEI-8 PAD; SPS/G&N; 45701; minus 0.40, plus 1.57; 085:18:19.04. Are you with me so far? Over.

a08_0821720.speaker: Collins
a08_0821720.text: Okay. Plus 3319.5, minus 0126.7, plus 0471.6; 179, 008, 001; not applicable, plus 0018.7; 3355.2, 3:11, 3335.5; 42, 090.9, 25.2. Are you still with me? Over.

a08_0821720.speaker: Collins
a08_0821720.text: Okay, Picking up with the boresight star, it's old Dschubba, who is the center star in the head of Scorpion; he's down 06.0, left 4.2; plus 07.73, minus 165.00; 1298.2, 36256, 146:46:18; north set stars remain Sirius, Rigel; roll, 129; pitch, 155; yaw, 010; four quad ullage for 15 seconds, horizon on a 4-degree line at T IG . And requesting that you zero the optics. Over.

a08_0821720.speaker: Borman
a08_0821720.text: Are you through with the computer now, Mike?

a08_0821720.speaker: Collins
a08_0821720.text: It's your computer. P27 LM state vector in and verified.

a08_0821720.speaker: Lovell
a08_0821720.text: Roger. We're going to put it in the CSM slot.

a08_0821720.speaker: Collins
a08_0821720.text: You keep good books; that's all correct.

a08_0822000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0822000-pao.text: Apollo Control here. While Mike is passing this update up, we're looking at biomedical data on Jim Lovell. And his mean heart rate is registering 66; his high heart rate over the recent sample period has been 76; his low is - well, we have a new data point here so his low is now 70; his mean rate is 74. He must be moving around a little bit. His respiration rate is up somewhat, 20 to 21, and shows an activity mode as normal. Could be that he just went from the couch down to his G&N station or moved in the opposite direction. Cabin pressure, 4.9; cabin temp, 77 degrees (Fahrenheit, 25°C), where

a08_0822000-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0822000-pao.text: Roger. The TEI-8 PAD; SPS/G&N; 45701; minus 0.40, plus 1.57; 085:18:19.04. Are you with me so far? Over.

a08_0822200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0822200-pao.text: Apollo Control here. The crew now is directly opposite the Earth. They're just west the Sea of Tranquillity, just south of the Imbrium Sea, southeast of the big crater Aristarchus, and directly east of the enormous Ocean Procellarum. They're only just a few miles north of a cluster of landing sites which are right along the lunar equator. They're about 8 degrees, 8 lunar degrees north of these sites, four of them that we consider prime sites in that central Apollo zone which is boxed in by an area of about 45 degrees west by 45 degrees east and running 5 degrees north and south of the lunar eq

a08_0822200-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_0822200-pao.text: Okay, Picking up with the boresight star, it's old Dschubba, who is the center star in the head of Scorpion; he's down 06.0, left 4.2; plus 07.73, minus 165.00; 1298.2, 36256, 146:46:18; north set stars remain Sirius, Rigel; roll, 129; pitch, 155; yaw, 010; four quad ullage for 15 seconds, horizon on a 4-degree line at T IG . And requesting that you zero the optics. Over.

a08_0822644.speaker: Collins
a08_0822644.text: Roger. Some time back, we noted evidence of a restart in the computer and wondered if you had any remarks about it. Over.

a08_0822644.speaker: Borman
a08_0822644.text: I know that Jim got screwed up on one of those programs. He's getting kind of tired here, and we got a restart and a couple of program alarms. I don't know what he did.

a08_0822644.speaker: Collins
a08_0822644.text: Roger, Frank. Main point is the computer is looking fine to us now.

a08_0822644.speaker: Lovell
a08_0822644.text: Houston, don't believe all you hear up here.

a08_0822644.speaker: Collins
a08_0822644.text: We have a filter, Jim, for that.

a08_0822832.speaker: Collins
a08_0822832.text: Roger. Some of Jim's previous comments about the limb brightness as the Sun was about to come up has sparked a lot of interest down here. And we'd like to ask him, if he gets a chance to notice again or perhaps he can recall, whether there were any changes in the appearances of the stars. Such as, did he notice any twinkling while this was taking place, and did he notice any narrow limb brightening within 10 to 20 seconds prior to the Sun's rising. Over.

a08_0822832.speaker: Anders
a08_0822832.text: He'll be with you - he's doing a P52 now.

a08_0822832.speaker: Lovell
a08_0822832.text: Houston, my comments concerning the sunrise was the comments above the terrain. There appeared to what might be called the diagonal light or light due to haze or something like that. As the Sun came above the - or before the Sun came above the limb, definite rays could be seen coming from the other side. It was a uniform haze emanating from the center spot where the Sun was going to rise, and this was something which I didn't expect.

a08_0822832.speaker: Collins
a08_0822832.text: Roger, Jim. Understand. We copied that and just were curious, if you see it again whether you notice any stars twinkling or any additional information.

a08_0822832.speaker: Lovell
a08_0822832.text: Will do. Might have a chance at control point 1. [Pause.]

a08_0822832.speaker: Anders
a08_0822832.text: Actually, he doesn't want to pass out too much of that information. He wants to save it, write a paper when he gets back, Mike.

a08_0823557.speaker: Borman
a08_0823557.text: Okay. What time is that TV, Mike, 85:37?

a08_0823557.speaker: Collins
a08_0823557.text: 85:37 to terminator, which is probably like 86:14.

a08_0823557.speaker: Borman
a08_0823557.text: Okay. Well, I don't know if we can go that long with it, and I'm going to scrub all the other experiments, the convergent stereo or the other photography, and we are a little bit tired; I want to use that last bit to really make sure we're right for TEI.

a08_0823557.speaker: Collins
a08_0823557.text: A couple of miscellaneous items for you. We'd like you to discontinue charging battery B at this time. We'd also like to get a cryo stir, 2 minutes on all four (tanks), and your Up Telemetry IU switch, put to Block, please, and you are Go for the next lunar orbit.

a08_0824010.speaker: Borman
a08_0824010.text: Rog. I want to scrub these control point sightings on this next rev, too, and let Jim take a rest.

a08_0824010.speaker: Collins
a08_0824010.text: Understand you want to scrub control points 1, 2 and 3 on the next rev and the convergent stereo on the following rev.

a08_0824010.speaker: Borman
a08_0824010.text: That's right. We're getting too tired.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: I mean, do you want to sleep?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: No, no. They've - they've got - Jesus Christ, they've got plenty of data. You can tell them almost anything [garble] everybody...

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Oh, I did, you're too tired; you need some sleep, and I want everybody sharp for TEI; that's just like a retro.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Why don't - Hey, Frank, how about on this next pass you just point it down to the ground and turn the goddamn cameras on; let them run automatically.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Shit, I just burned this film up.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Unbelievable - the detail these guys study up. A very good try, but just completely unrealistic, stuff like that. I should have...

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: I should have warned you. No. You try it, and then we'll make another mistake, like entering instead of proceeding or screwing up somewhere like I did.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: I want you to get your ass in bed! Right now! No, get to bed! Go to bed! Hurry up! I'm not kidding you, get to bed!

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: No, they said they don't want to.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: What - what would you like me to do?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Go to bed! When we come over it, we'll get that thing going when we get to daylight, and then you guys go sack out for 2 hours.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Shall we - shall we do that detailed thing there, that really...

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Say, give me that lens back there, will you?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Down below. Why don't you - why don't you - go local horizontal, sometime before you turn - We haven't shot a single high-speed picture yet, that's any good; just let me just turn the goddamn thing on prior to...

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: You haven't been in there since we've been in lunar orbit yet, have you?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: This is the tail end [garble] this time.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: No, I don't want to go to local horizontal yet.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Oh, no, just go to sleep, Jim.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: I know how I felt, and I know how you guys do.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Hey, I can see the Moon out here [garble].

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Is that Earth's turn on here, or what?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: I - I - Yes, that's why I want to get the pictures over here.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: You want to put it on Omni?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Okay, give me the roll left - Which way are you going to go?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Well, let's see. I can roll to the right, and that'll keep us good, won't it?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: The only window that's any good - are these rendezvous - You kind of pitch it down, and you get some...

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Okay, which way are you headed? Oh, you're going to roll, going to roll...

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: We're going to roll to the right, so we can get that High Gain up. Right window...

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: All right, I keep expecting to be seeing the Moon.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Well, you're going to have to just yaw towards me a little bit.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Would you hit those lights down there with your foot, Frank.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Hell, we're going away from it, huh?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: We're going away from it, huh?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: I'm pitching down, but we're going that way.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Are we? We're going this way?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: You know, it kind of gets you down.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: I thought we were going - we're going towards the Earth.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Why don't you snap a few? Can you see it still in your rendezvous window?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Snap that thing on or we end up doing another automatic one.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: You going to point at the horizon, Frank?

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: I pointed it straight down, I thought.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Like when we get ready to go inertial, we get a shot of the horizon as it comes up.

a08_0824054-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard.text: Well, I'm already straight down pointing [garble]. Thought you might [garble] one of these [garble].

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: I mean, do you want to sleep?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: No, no. They've - they've got - Jesus Christ, they've got plenty of data. You can tell them almost anything [garble] everybody...

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Oh, I did, you're too tired; you need some sleep, and I want everybody sharp for TEI; that's just like a retro.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Why don't - Hey, Frank, how about on this next pass you just point it down to the ground and turn the goddamn cameras on; let them run automatically.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Shit, I just burned this film up.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Unbelievable - the detail these guys study up. A very good try, but just completely unrealistic, stuff like that. I should have...

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: I should have warned you. No. You try it, and then we'll make another mistake, like entering instead of proceeding or screwing up somewhere like I did.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: I want you to get your ass in bed! Right now! No, get to bed! Go to bed! Hurry up! I'm not kidding you, get to bed!

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: No, they said they don't want to.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: What - what would you like me to do?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Go to bed! When we come over it, we'll get that thing going when we get to daylight, and then you guys go sack out for 2 hours.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Shall we - shall we do that detailed thing there, that really...

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Say, give me that lens back there, will you?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Down below. Why don't you - why don't you - go local horizontal, sometime before you turn - We haven't shot a single high-speed picture yet, that's any good; just let me just turn the goddamn thing on prior to...

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: You haven't been in there since we've been in lunar orbit yet, have you?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: This is the tail end [garble] this time.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: No, I don't want to go to local horizontal yet.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Oh, no, just go to sleep, Jim.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: I know how I felt, and I know how you guys do.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Hey, I can see the Moon out here [garble].

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Is that Earth's turn on here, or what?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: I - I - Yes, that's why I want to get the pictures over here.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: You want to put it on Omni?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Okay, give me the roll left - Which way are you going to go?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Well, let's see. I can roll to the right, and that'll keep us good, won't it?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: The only window that's any good - are these rendezvous - You kind of pitch it down, and you get some...

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Okay, which way are you headed? Oh, you're going to roll, going to roll...

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: We're going to roll to the right, so we can get that High Gain up. Right window...

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: All right, I keep expecting to be seeing the Moon.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Well, you're going to have to just yaw towards me a little bit.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Would you hit those lights down there with your foot, Frank.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Hell, we're going away from it, huh?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: We're going away from it, huh?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: I'm pitching down, but we're going that way.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Are we? We're going this way?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: You know, it kind of gets you down.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: I thought we were going - we're going towards the Earth.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Why don't you snap a few? Can you see it still in your rendezvous window?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Snap that thing on or we end up doing another automatic one.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: You going to point at the horizon, Frank?

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: I pointed it straight down, I thought.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Anders
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Like when we get ready to go inertial, we get a shot of the horizon as it comes up.

a08_0824054-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0824054-onboard-nr.text: Well, I'm already straight down pointing [garble]. Thought you might [garble] one of these [garble].

a08_0824139.speaker: Collins
a08_0824139.text: Rog. This rev coming up, we'd like to clarify whether you intend to scrub Control Point 1, 2, and 3, only, and do the pseudo landing site; or whether you also intend to scrub the pseudo landing site marks. Over.

a08_0824139.speaker: Borman
a08_0824139.text: We're scrubbing everything. We'll - I'll stay up and point - keep the spacecraft vertical and take some automatic pictures, but I want Jim and Bill to get some rest.

a08_0824600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0824600-pao.text: This is Apollo Control here. You heard the last transmission from Frank Borman wherein he indicated that he planned a drastic reduction of activities in the next several revs. We've been noting that we - and suggested earlier we had a tired crew. Certainly indicated in Lovell's voice. We've heard very little from Frank, from Bill Anders who is presently in a sleep period. It just could be that it'll wind up our activities in lunar orbit. There's a conference going on, now, around the Flight Director's console, and it will be from that, the ground will make up its mind on what - what, if anythi

a08_0825142.speaker: Collins
a08_0825142.text: Apollo 8, Houston. 4 minutes to LOS. You have control of the DSE now, and all your systems are looking good.

a08_0825142.speaker: Collins
a08_0825142.text: Yeah, we can hear him down here.

a08_0825435.speaker: Collins
a08_0825435.text: Roger. We have 1 minute to LOS, Frank. You can terminate stirring up your cryos any time, and we agree with all your Flight Plan changes, and have a beautiful backside and we will see you next time round.
