a08_0825500-onboard.text: Huh?

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Is that thing running now?

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Is that thing running already?

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Huh? Did you put it on Off?

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Here you go.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: We're doing fine; why don't you go to bed? I'll [garble]. Just tell me what the click - just turn that thing? Look! This thing here? Right over your head?

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: No, I want you to get to bed. Come on now. You've been up all the time; it's in the Flight Plan. God damn it, go to bed! To hell with the other stuff! We'll bust our ass for it.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Do I just turn that when the time comes? What do I have to do to start it?

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0825500-onboard.text: [Garble] eighth; it's going to start with me.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0825500-onboard.text: [Garble] stay 1 more minute.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: I know it. Get going! I think this is a closed issue. Get to bed!

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: I don't care; get to bed!

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: No, you get to bed; get your ass to bed. You quit wasting one - one - I - I - I - I don't want to talk about it.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Shut up; go to sleep, both you guys.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: I'll just click it on when the time comes.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: You should see your eyes; get to bed!

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Don't worry about the exposure business, Goddamn it, Anders; get to bed! Right now! Come on!

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: I don't want [garble] All right. You want me to take some pictures? Get some sleep now. You've only got a couple hours, Bill, before we're going to have to be fresh again.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Yeah. Okay. I'll take care of it all. All right. I just got up, remember? I slept for 4 hours.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: No, I didn't.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0825500-onboard.text: [Garble].

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Yeah. Go to sleep.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Houston already came back and said, "Fine."

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: Yeah.

a08_0825500-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0825500-onboard.text: A quick snooze, and you guys will feel a hell of a lot better tomorrow.

a08_0825600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0825600-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston here; 82 hours, 56 minutes into the flight. We have just lost signal with the spacecraft and I believe you heard earlier Frank Borman declare that he had a tired crew. Jim Lovell, very tired; you could tell it from his voice as the afternoon wore on, and he said he was relieving him of all further Flight Plan responsibilities. Five minutes after he said that - he came back up on the line and said Lovell is snoring already. Here is the last few conversational items with the crew before they went over the hill. Let's have the tape.

a08_0825900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0825900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston here. You heard Borman and since that conversation, the project manager George Low has come over to our console and he said that he urged me to make it very clear that the Apollo Spacecraft Program Office is altogether happy with the data they've gotten today and they feel like they have gotten as nearly 100 percent of the data as they could possibly get. He's quite pleased with it and he's ready to give the crew a very well earned little extra bonus rest. We - According to the best information we have from the Flight Director Cliff Charlesworth, and from the in

a08_0831100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0831100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 83 hours, 11 minutes. At the present time, Apollo 8 is nearing the end of its seventh revolution. We've had Loss of Signal now for about 16 minutes. Our displays here in Mission Control Center show that we should reacquire the spacecraft again in about 30 minutes. At the present time here in the Mission Control Center, Flight Director Milton Windler is in the process of relieving Clifford Charlesworth, and our Capsule Communicator will be Ken Mattingly replacing Mike Collins in that position. Windler at present is going over the status of the spacecraft and the missio

a08_0831100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0831100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 83 hours, 41 minutes into the mission. We're standing by at this time to reacquire the spacecraft as it comes over the lunar horizon on it's eighth revolution. Here in Mission Control Center, Flight Director Milton Windler and his team of flight controllers are becoming busily involved in getting prepared for the Trans-Earth Injection burn, scheduled to occur at 89 hours, 15 minutes. Particularly, the flight dynamics people down in the front of the Control Center. They are, of course, the gentlemen who will be coming up with the information needed by the crew

a08_0834500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0834500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. During this pass on the eighth revolution across the front side of the Moon, we expect to begin passing up some information to the crew relevant to that Trans-Earth Injection maneuver. We do anticipate that both Lovell and Anders will be resting at this time. Shortly before we lost the spacecraft - lost signal from the spacecraft on the previous revolution, Borman advised us that Lovell was sleeping, and he said that he had removed a number of items from the Flight Plan in order that both Jim Lovell and Bill Anders would be able to get some rest before this Trans-Earth

a08_0834500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0834500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 83 hours, 54 minutes. We've just put in a call to the spacecraft. We're in communication with them at this time. We'll pick that up for you now.

a08_0835344.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0835344.text: Rog, Apollo 8. Couple of notes for you: on the P52 you're coming up to on this rev, we've looked at your state vectors and all your information. The platform looks good, and it appears that's your option if you'd like to bypass this P52; your platform will still be good at the following TEI pass. And we would like to have your PRD reading and I guess we're behind the sleep summary. Over.

a08_0835344.speaker: Borman
a08_0835344.text: Okay. Well, Jim and Bill are both resting now. I had just about 3 hours or 4 hours during the period earlier today.

a08_0835344.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0835344.text: Copy, 144. And we have an update ready to go into your computer for the state vector if you want to go to P00 and Accept. [Pause.]

a08_0835600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0835600-pao.text: This is Houston. We're continuing to stand by here for further conversation. At the present time, the spacecraft is transmitting back to us with their omni antennas and there will be about 12 or 13 minutes before we bring on the High Gain Antenna. At that point, we would expect that the noise level would drop off somewhat. We are also here in Mission Control going ahead with the TV circuits - calling up those circuits and maintaining them on the assumption that we will have the TV transmission at the scheduled time, and that is 85 hours, 40 minutes Ground Elapsed Time at the beginning. We have

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: [Garble] am standing by to copy the TEI-9 PAD. [Long pause.]

a08_0835952.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0835952.text: Okay, Apollo 8, we've completed with the computer, and you can use the Verb 47 to transfer and I have the TEI-9 PAD.

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: That's Ken, isn't it? Just a minute and I'll take care of it.

a08_0835952.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0835952.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: Okay, I went to P00 and then Verb 47, and I'm ready to copy.

a08_0835952.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0835952.text: Okay. Do you have it in Block?

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: Say again.

a08_0835952.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0835952.text: I say, do you have the Up Telemetry in Block?

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman (under Mattingly)
a08_0835952.text: It's in Block.

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: Roger.

a08_0835952.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0835952.text: Okay. This PAD is a TEI-9; SPS/G&N; 45597; minus 0.40, plus 1.57, 087:19:18.20; plus 3418.8, minus 0135.3, plus 0078.0; 180, 008, 001; November Alpha, plus 0018.7; 3422.3, 3:13, 34021; 42, 089.8, 25.3; 033, down 13.1, left 2.8; plus 07.58, minus 165.00; 1298.7, 36277, 146:48:16; primary star, Sirius; secondary, Rigel; 129, 155, 010; 4 quads, 15-second ullage; horizon's on 1.2-degree window line at T minus 3; use the high speed procedure with minus Mike Alpha. After looking at the burn information from your previous SPS burns, it appears that our engine performance should give us a 3-second bur

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: Roger. Thank you. [Pause.]

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: TEI-9; SPS/G&N; 45597; minus 0.40, plus 1.57; 087:19:18.20; plus 3418.8, minus 0135.3, plus 0078.0; 180, 008, 001; N/A, plus 0018.7; 3422.3, 3:13, 3402.1; 42, 089.8, 25.3; 033, down 13.1, left 2.8; plus 07.58, minus 165.00; 1298.7, plus - or 36277, 146:48:16; and that's Sirius and Rigel; 129, 155, 010; 4 jet, 15 seconds; 1.2-degrees on the window at T minus 3, high speed minus MA, engine 3.7 seconds longer than given.

a08_0835952.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0835952.text: That's affirmative, Apollo 8. And when you get around to it, if you'd like for us to dump your tape, we can do that when you get on the High Gain. [Pause.]

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: Okay. Should have it on the High Gain now, Houston.

a08_0835952.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0835952.text: Roger. And we're going to go ahead and dump the tape.

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0835952.speaker: Borman
a08_0835952.text: Ken, will we get the real TEI PAD the next time around now? [Long pause.]

a08_0835952.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0835952.text: Apollo 8, we'll have one for you the next time around, and we'll update it if necessary on the following rev.

a08_0841100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0841100-pao.text: At the present time the spacecraft is crossing over the Sea of Tranquility, and it's approaching the terminator, the point at which it will go into darkness - actually not total darkness - that would be the area of the Moon that would be lighted by Earthshine, and from previous reports - Stand by. We have a call from the crew.

a08_0841134.speaker: Borman
a08_0841134.text: Do you have any idea why quad B seems so much lower in quantity than the other three quads?

a08_0841548.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0841548.text: Okay. a08_0841800-pao.speaker: Mission Control

At this point, we have passed up all of the information that Flight Director Milton Windler wanted to get to the crew on this pass, on the 8th revolution, and we anticipate that any further conversation with the spacecraft before we lose signal in about 36 minutes, will be initiated by the crew. We'll continue to monitor and pick up the conversation as it develops. At the present time, it appears that Frank Borman is the active crewman. Lovell and Anders, we expect, are getting some rest at this time in preparation for the busy schedule they're g

a08_0841800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0841800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We've had one very brief conversation with the crew since our previous report. We'll pick that up and then come up live with conversation that is developing at this time.

a08_0842435-onboard.text: Hey, this little radiometer that I got is up to 124 now. What's yours reading?

a08_0842435-onboard.text: How do you read me on Omni A, Ken?

a08_0842435-onboard.text: We didn't have to do one, Jim. No, they said that they'd checked it, and it looked real good, and they'd let you sleep.

a08_0842654.text: Okay, we've just finished looking at all your systems and all the trajectory information, and you have the Go for another rev.

a08_0842901.text: How's the weather down there, Ken?

a08_0842901.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0842901.text: It's really beautiful; loud and clear, and just right in temperature.

a08_0842901.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0842901.text: Yeah. They tell us that there's a beautiful Moon out there.

a08_0842901.text: Now, I was just saying that there's a beautiful Earth out there.

a08_0842901.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0842901.text: It depends on your point of view.

a08_0842901.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0842901.text: If you're looking for things to do up there, Frank, you might hit that biomed switch over to the left position.

a08_0843400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0843400-pao.text: Based on that count from Frank Borman aboard the spacecraft, we've concluded here in Mission Control, that we have about a 3-second delay from the time the signal is sent until the time we receive it here.

a08_0843400-pao.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0844424.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0844424.text: Okay. We're about - inside 10 minutes to LOS. We'll be picking you up again at 85:40, and we'll have all of the TV types information standing by. a08_0844424.speaker: Borman
a08_0844424.text: Roger. We're not going to use that telephoto lens. I don't believe we'll be able to get a picture of the Earth. It's going to have to be the terminator, the lunar surface. I'm looking at the Earth right now; and we won't see it again during that period.

a08_0844424.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0844424.text: Okay. Real fine then. And next time around, why, we'll take an extra special look at all of the parameters; we'll have a TEI PAD for you. a08_0853154-onboard.text: We're pointed straight up in the air, now.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: No, we're not. We're just about horizontal.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Probably be best out that rendezvous window there.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yes. If you'd yaw about 30 degrees this way, you could probably pick the Earth coming up over the hill.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Here, we'll take it out that window over there...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: We'll have to yaw to the left, wouldn't I?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: No, you'll have to yaw to the right, and - to get the rendezvous; maybe pitch up just a little bit.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Well, it's just - The trouble is, I don't think would normally get it out the rendezvous window and have the High Gain, too, Frank.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: The thing to do would be, - if you want to get the Earth, to get the yaw - to yaw up and pitch up.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Try to get comm, will you, Bill?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Okay, well, gee - I don't see it out there anywhere. Do you? The Earth? I don't think we've had AOS yet.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: You're going down, it says right here.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I'll know when to get them as soon as we get on an Omni.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: You'll have to pitch up, Frank; I can't get them now, on - on the...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: You'll have to pitch up; I can't get them on the High Gain there. Pitch or - or yaw - pitch up or yaw and/or yaw right.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Where's the PAD book? Doesn't it have the...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Get a good shot of her?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Well, keep the camera there. Keep the camera.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Here it comes. Here it comes. But you're not on yet.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Oh, I get it off this camera - window over here.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Roll her a little bit. Roll her a little bit to the - to the right.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Here, you want me to fly it just to come a...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: That one's got it, the roll. Yes, yes. It's the roll that's got it. Roll right, if you can.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: We're going to radial out. Are we - You got her coming up? You see her, Frank?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: We're over 45 degrees in yaw right now.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: We're still yawing, and we're still rolling.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Where is it, Frank? Point to it.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I'm pointing right at it with the camera.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Then why in the hell we're not getting it? Okay.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: There, you got it; you're on.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: There you got it. It was in some kind of a gimbal lock up there.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Roll left a little, can you?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Did he say it was a good picture?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Okay, why don't you describe what - where abouts are we here anyway?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Tell them - this camera's just the thing. Tell them what we're going to do.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: You got the - got the thingamajig? Want me to roll a little bit?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: You're going to have to show it out that picture now; I've lost it.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Can you pitch down now and...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: ...and let me get out the rendezvous window and yaw, maybe?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Which way do you want to yaw?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yaw toward me and away from - away from the Earth.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Can't you get it down? I can't see it, Jim.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: ...and it certainly would not appear to be a very...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: You got it - you got to do something.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I'm changing to the other window now.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: What sea are we coming up to? Smyth's Sea?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Pyrenees. Okay, hold it right there. Hold it.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: No, I take that back; it's [garble].

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Tell them there's a very bright impact crater now.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yes, the more right roll, the better.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I can't even see it is the trouble.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: After the Sea of Fertility; first, we're going over the Sea of Crises.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Are we coming up near our - near our target area?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: No, I don't think - we've got quite a ways to go.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Do you need this anymore? I'll find out where we are here in a hurry.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yes, you better leave it on there.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Okay, there's two big craters coming up on the right. I don't know which ones they are.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Where? What does it look like here?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Don't tell me we've broken lock.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: That might be Kastner and Gilbert, although I'm no too sure. I can't see out.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: It's hard to get me and the camera in the window at the same time [laughter].

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Could I look out here just a second just to find out where we are? Well, we're still over the - Okay, we're still over the east side. Here comes Smyth's Sea now.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Hey, Bill, you're not talking to geologists.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: What do you want me to say?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yes, watch out for gimbal lock, please.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: How are you doing, Bill? Can you see it?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yes, that's good. I can't see much out here with this camera in the way.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Boy, that baby really took some [garble], didn't it?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Don't stop, Bill, [laughter] I didn't mean to cut you off.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: We'll have another thought soon - there are a lot of holes down there.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Is that crater on the backside called Tchaikovsky Kil - Kil - Kilkowsky [Tsiolkovsky] or something like that?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: It's an old Russian name, isn't it? That's the Goddard of...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I'm checking that. No, we - think maybe - No, there's a bright crater right there.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Unless we could have rotated off here.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I don't know where we are now because we yawed off so much.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: We're going sideways. Frank's window would be the best one to look - Do you see the terminator coming yet, Frank?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I don't know which way it is. I - I didn't look to see which way we were going.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: What is that mare up there now, that big one?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: North? Okay, let me check it here. Well, there's the Sea of Crises coming up - Oh, that big one is the Sea of Crises over there.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I made a mistake with the...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: What's the name of that crater right between us and it?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Okay, I'll get it for you right now. That's - Condorcet Crater.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Let me see just to make sure. Are we under a sea right now, Smyth's Sea? That's the Condorcet Crater. Condorcet.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: You want me to try it out this window?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I'll have to watch out for gimbal lock this way

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yes. Be careful when you grab that handle, because apparently you can turn it Off.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Okay, you'll have to - [garble] I can't see where you are, Frank.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Okay, what is the problem here? Okay.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I can't pitch up too much.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Can you roll? Don't pitch up, just roll You can roll...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Roll right, and you can yaw - yaw left, - Get your right gimbal off a little bit. Roll right and yaw left.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: All right, you better - We're going to lose it if you don't move over.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: What's the name of the crater out in the Sea of Crises? That's probably the one they're talking about.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Picard is right out there on the right-hand - left-hand side of it.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: How are we going to keep lock now, Bill?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Okay, keep - the thing to do is to - is to roll right - is the best thing to do.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Okay, I'm rolling right. I've got - I'm in there right now...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Well, we're not able - That's their problem.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: What's this - what sea are we over now, Jim?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: This is part of the Sea of...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Don't - don't - You better - you better yaw a little bit to the left. You're going to get the Sun on Frank's window now.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Do you want me to still roll?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: The Sea of Fertility we're on.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: We're over the Sea of Fertility.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: How many miles across is that crater?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Is that - You're looking at Taruntius?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yes, how many - Just give me a guess. 20 miles? 30miles?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Ro - You better - You better roll left.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yaw left, too. I see the - Here's Earth in our background.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Now, you better stop the roll.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yawing a little bit too far left.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yes, why don't you yaw right a little bit?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Or else, you may just - If you went to keep going, I'll put it out this window now.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: That's fine on there - that's fine. Who do you want to give it to?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Now, that crater right out there is - that nice round one is...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Well, they can - Frank is at the other one.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Is this our landing site we're going over now?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Yes, this is our landing site right down here.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Hey, why don't we start reading that thing, and that would be a good place to end it.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: No, we've got to go into it very nicely. Why don't we - as we go into sunset...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: ...or is it sunrise? This is sunrise, yes. We're approaching lunar sunrise.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: You want to pass it over here, Jim?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: No, it's perfect right where it is.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: I just turned it Off. You want it On again?

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: No. leave it Off. Great! Great!

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Hey, how can you beat that? Geeze, we just went into the terminator right in time.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Okay, let's get the spacecraft back in even keel again. Here, here's this, Frank.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: All right, let's get the Flight Plan out here.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Don't tell me they didn't hear us.

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0853154-onboard.text: Why don't you just roll-over to the right, Frank, and then you can ...

a08_0853154-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0853154-onboard.text: You want me to get that, or...

a08_0853900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0853900-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston here; 85 hours, 39 minutes and we're very nearly at the acquisition point. Only 10 seconds away. And we should, if we're on plan, move right into a television transmission. The time of 85 hours, 40 minutes has been passed to the crew. The prime site for this picture will be the Goldstone Station from California.

a08_0853900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0853900-pao.text: We're getting telemetry now via Honeysuckle Creek the dish in Australia. And no word yet on Goldstone.

a08_0853900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0853900-pao.text: Getting a carrier noise now. It's probably indicative of transmission coming.

a08_0854200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0854200-pao.text: There's still no calls, although we're a minute and a half - we're a minute and a half into acquisition. The capsule communicator has been advised to pass to the crew, when we acquire, that all of the systems look good.

a08_0854200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0854200-pao.text: Two minutes now since we did acquire the spacecraft. Rather noisy data. The data on the 9th revolution around the Moon, with an apogee of 63 [nautical] miles [116.7 km] of a perigee of 58.9 [nautical] miles [109.1 km]. Velocity, 5,352 feet per second. We've got a picture here, and we've got a voice to go with it. Bill Anders.

a08_0854200-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854200-pao.text: Loud and clear and initial look at your systems are good.

a08_0854200-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0854200-pao.text: Roger. We've got the T - Roger. We've got the TV [garble]. [Pause.]

a08_0854200-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0854200-pao.text: How does the picture look, Houston?

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Houston.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Loud and clear and initial look at your systems are good.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Over.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: We've got a picture, Apollo 8.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Roger. We've got the T - Roger. We've got the TV [garble]. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: How does the picture look, Houston?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Loud and clear. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: The TV look okay?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: That's very good. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: Welcome from the Moon, Houston.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Houston, you're seeing a view of the Earth taken below the lunar horizon. We're going to follow the track until the terminator, where we will turn the spacecraft and give you a view of the long shadowed terrain at the terminator, which should come in quite well in the TV.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Roger.

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: We don't know whether you can see it from the TV screen, but the Moon is nothing but a milky white. Completely void.

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: We're changing the cameras to the other window now. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: This is Apollo 8, coming to you live from the Moon. We've had to switch the TV camera now. We showed you first a view of Earth as we've been watching it for the past 16 hours. Now we're switching so that we can show you the Moon that we've been flying over at 60 miles altitude for the last 16 hours. Bill Anders, Jim Lovell, and myself have spent the - the day before Christmas up here doing experiments, taking pictures, and firing our spacecraft engines to maneuver around. What we'll do now is follow the trail that we've been following all day and take you on through to a lunar sunset. The Moon

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: ...inviting place to live or work. Jim, what have you thought most about?

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: Well, Frank, my thoughts are very similar. The vast loneliness up here of the Moon is awe inspiring, and it makes you realize just what you have back there on Earth. The Earth from here is a grand oasis in the big vastness of space.

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Bill, what do you think?

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: I think the thing that impressed me the most were the lunar sunrises and sunsets. These in particular bring out the stark nature of the terrain, and the long shadows really bring out the relief that is here and hard to see in this very bright surface that we're going over right now.

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: You're describe - that's not color, Bill. Describe some of the physical features of what you're showing the people. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're not receiving a picture now. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: We are now coming on to Smyth's Sea, a small mare region covered with a dark, level material. There is a fresh, bright, impact crater on the edge towards us and a mountain range on the other side.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: These mountains are the Pyrenees. [onboard] Is that right?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Apollo 8, we are not receiving modulation on the signal; we have - do have sync.

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Are you reading us? Apollo 8, Houston. [onboard] Maybe it's turned off, Bill.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Apollo 8, we're reading you loud and clear, but no picture. We have no modulation.

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: Roger. We understand. Take a look now.

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: How about now? Apollo.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Loud and clear. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Good picture. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: What you're seeing as we cross Smyth's Sea are the craters Castner and Gilbert...

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: ...and what we've noticed especially, that you cannot see from the Earth, are these small bright impact craters that dominate the lunar surface. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: The horizon here is very, very stark.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: The sky is pitch black, and the Earth - or the Moon, rather, excuse me, is quite light. And the contrast between the sky and the Moon is a vivid dark line. Coming into view of the camera now are some interesting old double ring craters, some interesting features that are quite common in the mare region and have been filled by some material - the same consistency of the maria and the same color. Here are three or four of these interesting features. Further on the horizon you see the Pyr - [Pause]. [onboard] These are the Pyrenees, aren't they?...

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Okay. The mountains coming up now are heavily impacted with numerous craters whose central peaks you can see in many of the larger ones.

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: Actually, I think the best way to describe this area is a vastness of black and white, absolutely no color. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: The sky up here is also rather forbidding, foreboding expanse of blackness, with no stars visible when we're flying over the Ear - over the Moon in daylight. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: You can see by the numerous craters...

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: ...that this planet has been bombarded through the eons with numerous small asteroids and meteoroids, pock marking the surface every square inch.

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: And one of the amazing features of the surface is the roundness that most of the craters - seems that most of them have a round mound type of appearance instead of sharp, jagged rocks.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Only the very newest features have any sharp definition to them, and eventually they get eroded down by the constant bombardment of small meteorites. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: How's the picture now, Houston? [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Houston, are you reading us?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Our picture is - Loud and clear, and the picture looks real fine.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Thank you.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Can you see the two large craters to the - just to the right of our track, Houston? [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: That's affirmative. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: The very bright features you see are the new impact craters, and the longer a crater has been on the surface of the Moon, why, the more mottled and subdued it becomes. Some of the... [Stops himself. Long pause].

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Apollo 8, we've apparently lost your voice; the picture is still good.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: . Houston, we're passing over an area that's just to the east of Smyth's Sea now, in checking our charts. Smyth's Sea is coming up in a few minutes.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Apollo 8, if you go to P00 and Accept, why, we'll uplink some information. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: We are now coming up towards the terminator, and I hope that soon we'll be able to show you the varying contrast of white as we go into the darkness. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Houston, we're in P00, and you have the computer.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: We're now approaching a series of small impact craters. There is a dark area between us and them which could possibily be an old lava flow. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: You can see the large mountains on the horizon now ahead of the spacecraft, to the north of our track. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: The intensity of the Sun's reflection in this area...

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: ...makes it difficult for us to distinguish the features we see on the surface, and I suppose it's even harder on the television, but as we approach the terminator and the shadows become longer, you'll see a marked change. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: There's a very dark crater in the filling material in this valley in front of us now. It's rather unusual in that it's sharply defined, yet it's dark all over its interior walls, whereas most new-looking craters are very bright interior. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Small impact crater in front of us now in the little mare. Well defined, quite new, and another one approaching. The spacecraft is facing north. From our track, we are going sideways to our left. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: You're now seeing the Sea of Crises coming over the horizon.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: We believe the crater, the large dark crater between the spacecraft and the Sea of Crises is Condorcet crater. The Sea of Crises is amazingly smooth as far as the horizon, past this rather rough, mountainous region in front of the spacecraft. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Apollo 8, we're through with the computer, if you go back to Block, and it looks like we are getting a lot of reflection off your window now. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Roger. We'll switch windows. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: How's that look now, Ken?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: That's real fine. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Apollo 8, can you tell us which window you're looking out? And there's a large crater, looks like it's sticking up in the upper right hand corner of our picture. Can you identify that one? [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Roger. We're just about to lose our lock here. That's why we're slowing up a little bit. [onboard] You're alright.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: We see the Sea of Crises in front of us now. We are looking out the left hand rendezvous window. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: We... [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Houston, how you reading us now?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Loud and clear.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: The crater you see on the horizon is the Sea of Crises. [Pause through static.] How are you reading us, Houston?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Loud and clear, Apollo 8, and we have a picture that's good.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Roger. We're getting a lot of static. The Sea of Crises is in front of us on the horizon, and the dark crater Picard can be seen in the middle. We're now breaking the Moon's sunrise or the spacecraft's sunset. This is an area that the Sun has just recently come up on the Moon. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: See the mare we're over now has a mottled look about it,...

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: ...but not very heavily cratered, so it must be relatively new.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: This is the Sea of Fertility, and we're coming up on a large crater, the delta rim variety. [Pause.] Has a strange circular cracks pattern around the middle of it. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: The crater that you're seeing now is about 30 or 40 miles across. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: How's your picture quality, Houston?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: This is phenomenal!

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: There's an interesting rille directly in front of the spacecraft now, running along the edge of a small mountain. Rather sinuous shape with right angle turns. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: This area just to the west of the Sea of Crises is called the Marsh of Sleep, and to the west of that is the Sea of Tranquillity.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Can you see the fracture patterns going across the mare in front of us now, Houston?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: That doesn't quite stand out.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: Roger. The series of cracks or faults across the middle of the mare; they drop down in about three steps to the south. The parallel fault pattern to the north has a drop-down in the center. [Long pause.] [onboard] I think you may be going too far now, Jim.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: I hope that all of you back on Earth can see what we mean when we say that it's a rather foreboding horizon, a very - rather...

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: ...stark and unappetizing looking place.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: We're now going over our...

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: ...approaching one of our future landing sites...

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: ...selected in this smooth region to...

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: We are now approaching lunar sunrise, and for all the people back on Earth, the crew of Apollo 8 has a message that we would like to send to you.

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: In the beginning, God created the Heaven and the Earth. And the Earth was without form and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters, and God said, "Let there be light." And there was light. And God saw the light, that it was good, and God divided the light from the darkness. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: ...called the Sea of Tranquility - smooth in order to make it easy for the initial landing attempts in order to preclude having to dodge mountains. Now you can see the long shadows of the lunar sunrise. [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day. And God said, "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters. And let it divide the waters from the waters." And God made the firmament and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament. And it was so. And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: And God said, "Let the waters under the Heavens be gathered together into one place. And let the dry land appear." And it was so. And God called the dry land Earth. And the gathering together of the waters called he seas. And God saw that it was good. And from the crew of Apollo 8, we close with good night, good luck, a Merry Christmas and God bless all of you - all of you on the good Earth.

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Houston, how do you read? Apollo 8.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Loud and clear, Apollo 8. And thank you for a very good show. We have a maneuver PAD for you when you're ready to copy.

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Apollo 8, read you loud and clear.

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Roger. Are we off the air now? [Long pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: That's affirmative, Apollo 8. You are.

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Did you read everything that we had to say there?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Loud and clear. Thank you for a real good show.

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Okay. Now, Ken, we'd like to get all squared away for TEI here. Can you give us some good words like you promised?

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Yes, sir. I have a maneuver PAD. I think we'd like to start by dumping the tape. If we can have that, I have your...

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: ...TEI-10 maneuver PAD, and then we will run through a systems brief. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: I understand this is the maneuver PAD that we will use for TEI. Is that correct? [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Anders
a08_0854256.text: And you got the tape, Houston.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: Ready to copy, Ken.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Roger. TEI-10; SPS/G&N; 45597; minus 0.40, plus 1.57; 089:19:15.64; plus 3518.9, minus 0151.3, minus 0034.6; 180, 007, 000; November Alpha, plus 0018.6; 3522.3, 3:18, 3501.9; 42, 092.8, 25.3; boresight star, Scorpi Delta - another name for it is Dschubba - down 07.1, left 4.5; plus 07.48, minus 165.00; 1299.5, 36300, 146:50:05; primary star, Sirius; secondary, Rigel; 129, 155, 010; four quads, 15 second ullage; horizon on the 2.9 window line at T minus 3; use high-speed procedure with minus Mike Alpha. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Lovell
a08_0854256.text: Okay. TEI PAD as follows: SPS/G&N; 45597; minus 0.40, plus 1.57; 089:19:15.64; plus 3518.9, minus 0151.3, minus 0034.6; 180, 007, 000; not applicable, plus 0018.6; 3522.3, 3:18, 3501.9; 42, 092.8, 25.3; Scorpi Delta, Dschubba, down 07.1, left 4.5; plus 07.48, minus 165.00; 1299.5, 36300, 146:50:05; Sirius, Rigel, 129, 155, 010; four quads, 15 seconds; 2.9-degree window line at T IG minus 3; high-speed procedure, minus MA.

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: That's correct, Apollo 8. [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Ken, this is Frank. I want to - I want to make one thing certain. This the load that we're to use to burn with, right? This is not just a PAD data for a [TEI-]10 abort? [Pause.]

a08_0854256.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0854256.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We will update this PAD prior to the burn.

a08_0854256.speaker: Borman
a08_0854256.text: Oh, you will? Okay.

a08_0854400-pao.speaker: Anders
a08_0854400-pao.text: Houston, you're seeing a view of the Earth taken below the lunar horizon. We're going to follow the track until the terminator, where we will turn the spacecraft and give you a view of the long shadowed terrain at the terminator, which should come in quite well in the TV.

a08_0855600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0855600-pao.text: We're theorizing here that that bright spot in the top left center of your picture is the Earth. It's not very clear.

a08_0860900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0860900-pao.text: We estimate it's about 325 miles to the horizon just to help your reference.

a08_0861800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0861800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. The speakers in the order that they read from what we believe to be chapters from Genesis were Bill Anders and Jim Lovell, and close out with Frank Borman. That's both a biblical and a geological lesson that none of us will forget. At 86 hours, 9 minutes into the flight; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0861800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0861800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 86 hours, 18 minutes into the flight. Just a word or two on where the crew is looking. They're particularly - they identified the track extremely well as they moved along. But some of the areas were not so well identified because of the reading which concluded their pass. The reading came while they were moving across [the Sea of] Tranquility in a generally westerly direction. The look angle is to the northwest and to a series of mountains, rimming the northwest edge of the Sea of Tranquility. Earlier we, you recall, they pointed out the Sea of Crises, conclu

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Apollo 8. Houston.

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Roger. I'm reading you with a lot of background noise. Can you read me clearly?

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: Roger.

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Okay. I'm going to give you a quick summary of the systems. Basically, all systems are good. In respect to your return trajectory, we can still get to the mid-Pacific line at 146 hours by waiting as late as the 13th rev. After 138 seconds of the burn, you're on your way home. The weather in the recovery area looks good. Apollo 8, did you call?

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: Continue, Houston. [Long pause.]

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Apollo 8. Houston. Could we have the High Gain for a little bit longer?

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: We broke scan on it, Ken.

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Oh Roger. You're coming in loud and clear now. Did you copy my trajectory information?

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: We're on omni B though.

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Rog. That's fine.

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: Say again, please. Go ahead. We are 130 - Will you say it again, please?

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Wilco. [Pause.] Apollo 8. First, if you can spare, we'd like to have the High Gain to complete the dump. [Long pause.]

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: Stand by. We'll try to get it for you.

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: In a couple of minutes there, Houston.

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Roger. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Okay, Apollo 8. While we're... [Pause.]

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Apollo 8 - while we are waiting for the High Gain, I will continue the trajectory summary. We can still get back to the mid-Pacific line in 146 hours from the thirteenth rev, and you're on your way after 138 seconds of the burn. That's 138 seconds, gets you clear of the butterfly region. We recommend not trying reignitions or restart after 20 seconds. If you go beyond 20 seconds, this may get the trajectory beyond the correction - RCS correction capability to a free return. The weather in recovery area is good. We have an AOS following TEI of 89 plus 28 plus 39, and an AOS without TEI of 89 pl

a08_0861939.speaker: Lovell
a08_0861939.text: Roger. Thank you, Houston. We appreciate the summary. We're trying to get High Gain.

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Rog.

a08_0861939.speaker: Lovell
a08_0861939.text: I think we have it.

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: You do have the High Gain (antenna). Now, Ken, as I understand it, if it shuts down after 20 seconds of burn, you don't want us to try to relight it. Is that what you said?

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Stand by. [Pause.]

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Apollo 8, the intent was; do not delay ignitions beyond 20 seconds. Over.

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: Oh, do not delay ignition beyond 20 seconds. Roger.

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: That's affirm.

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: Okay. You want me to start it on bank A and then switch to B again, like we did on LOI, right? [Pause.]

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: That's affirmative.

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: Okay.

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: Did you put in this PAD for us? Should P30 and 40 be in our computer now? [Long pause.]

a08_0861939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0861939.text: Apollo 8, that's negative. We had not uplinked this PAD. We'll put this one in on the next pass.

a08_0861939.speaker: Borman
a08_0861939.text: Okay. Roger.

a08_0863300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0863300-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 86 hours, 33 minutes. A part of the information passed up to the crew during that last series of conversations was the information they will use for their Trans-Earth Injection maneuver. This is preliminary information. We do anticipate that it will be updated, probably on the next revolution. These figures, as they were read up to the crew, are as follows: the time of ignition is 89 hours, 19 minutes and 16 seconds; the burn duration will be 3 minutes, 17.8 seconds; and that will give us a nominal change in velocity of 3,522.3 feet per second, and the maneuver will o

a08_0863300-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0863300-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You have a Go for this rev.

a08_0863328.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0863328.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You have a Go for this rev.

a08_0863829.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0863829.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We've completed the tape dump, and the recorder is yours.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0863845-onboard.text: [Singing.]

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0863845-onboard.text: Do you still have the [garble]?

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: I'll get it afterwards, Bill.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0863845-onboard.text: That temporary storage bag, Bill, is located - Yeah, it's up here.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0863845-onboard.text: I got trash in that temporary storage bag I'm leaving there.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0863845-onboard.text: Okay.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0863845-onboard.text: It stinks to high heaven.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: All that urine always stinks real bad, too.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: What was the time for the rev before?

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: No, I don't know what day it is. This is day 4. No, hell; eat it - it doesn't matter. Eat any one you want.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: What?

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: Yeah. What were the gimbal angles there? 180, 8 - See, it's about the same. And the horizon was what? 1.2?

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0863845-onboard.text: Degrees.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: Okay. minus 3, right? So, we'll get the...

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0863845-onboard.text: [Garble].

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: This is the picture it's going to be right now.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: Huh?

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: Yeah. That's ours - The other one was 1.8.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0863845-onboard.text: I've got to update this one.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: Yeah, but we'll see - see, what I'm saying is we'll see just as we come around into the - into the Sun now, we should see just the way it's going to be. See what I mean?

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0863845-onboard.text: Checking that boresight star is going to be kind of difficult.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: Yes, you're looking right into the Earth's - the Earth. And it looks like the Sun's going to be right in our face, too.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0863845-onboard.text: You can probably check your star through the sextant while we're on the other side. Maybe.

a08_0863845-onboard.speaker: Lovell

a08_0864800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0864800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 86 hours, 48 minutes into the flight. At the present time, we have just about 5 minutes before Loss of Signal, and we've had about a minute and a half of conversation with the crew since our last report. We'll play that back for you and then stand by for any parting conversations from the crew before they go over the lunar horizon on this revolution.

a08_0865000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0865000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. I'd like to clarify one aspect of the figures we gave you concerning that Trans-Earth Injection maneuver. The return time that was listed; Ground Elapsed Time of 146 hours, 49 minutes, 37 seconds; was the time at which the spacecraft could nominally reach 400,000 feet altitude. The splash time would be about 14 minutes, 10 seconds beyond that, and these numbers of course will be updated both prior to the Trans-Earth Injection maneuver, and also en route back to Earth, so we would expect some change in those, some update. a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: Okay, I see the horizon. Yes.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: Right on the edge here - here - We're swinging in like this to it.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: It's like doing a loop.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: Look at down there, Bill: all those lines in a straight row like sand dunes.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: Okay, 2 minutes - minute and a half. about.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: I think you're about right.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: Now. Let's see. No, wait a second- In 18 seconds. Okay, how's it now?

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: [Garble].

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: We're going the right way now.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: Yes, we're upside down going that way. And we re going with the orbit.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: [Singing.] Well, you still might be pitched down. It might be that you burn like this. You might be burning before you get to the top.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: I don't know, but I'll find out.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: I don't think this is a good place for this, Bill. I'm going to put this - in here or some place. Huh? No, this - Did you find it?

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: Is that yours?

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: That's Jim's there.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: Now is burn time We got - little bit about 10 - 15 seconds after burn time.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: Where's your checklist?

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: I don't know.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: You didn't put it in my seat, did you?

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell
a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: I'm going to put this volume 2away, too.

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: Why don't you keep up this...

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Borman

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.speaker: Lovell

a08_0865251-onboard-nr.text: We can stop it

a08_0865400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0865400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 86 hours, 54 minutes. As the spacecraft went over the horizon and we lost signal, Capsule Communicator Ken Mattingly passed up to the crew an all systems Go report. We'll play that back for you now.

a08_0871800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0871800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 87 hours, 18 minutes into the flight. Our spacecraft is currently nearing the end of its ninth revolution and the beginning of the tenth. We still have about 21 minutes before we reacquire. I'd like to pass along some preliminary figures on the Acquisition of Signal and Loss of Signal times that we'll have on either side of that Trans-Earth Injection maneuver. These were passed up to the crew previously. The Loss of Signal time on the tenth revolution will be about 88 hours, 51 minutes, and this would be about 28 minutes, 5 seconds prior to the Trans-Earth Injection m

a08_0873800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0873800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 87 hours, 38 minutes into the flight. At the present time our spacecraft is in its tenth revolution and we're standing by for Acquisition of Signal as Apollo 8 comes over the horizon. That should be in about 15 seconds. The current velocity is 5,352 feet per second. And at this point we are at the time when we should be acquiring the spacecraft. We will stand by for a call to the crew or from - for a message from the spacecraft.

a08_0875410.text: Houston, this is 8. I take it you've loaded both state vectors, is that correct?

a08_0875410.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0875410.text: We loaded your CSM and LM nav and external Delta-V, in that order.

a08_0875900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0875900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. Currently our spacecraft velocity is 5,354 feet per second, and our orbit measures 58.8 nautical miles [108.9 km] at its low point. We've got a high point of 63.2 nautical miles [117.0 km] above the Moon's surface. At 87 hours, 59 minutes; this is Apollo Control.

a08_0880328.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0880328.text: Okay, Apollo 8. We've reviewed all your systems. You have a Go for TEI. One of the things we'd like to do as soon as you come out on the other side is a P23. We are checking into your helium pressures now. We're going to correlate, not only the last rev, but the previous rev for the same location, and we will have that number for you in a little bit.

a08_0880500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0880500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 88 hours, 5 minutes. The crew has just been given a Go for Trans-Earth Injection on this revolution. Here's how that sounded.

a08_0880947.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0880947.text: Apollo 8, Houston. The tape recorder is yours. And I have your PTC attitude.

a08_0880947.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0880947.text: Okay. PTC attitude will be pitch, 10; yaw, 45. This begins at 92 hours. Over.

a08_0880947.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0880947.text: That's affirmative. And looks like that'll go with the entry REFSMMAT. Begins at 92 hours.

a08_0880947.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0880947.text: Apollo 8, would you put your Up Telemetry to Block, please?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: We've got a lot of good things going here. Every time I start to do that, somebody interrupts. You know, we've got to get a new REFSMMAT and the whole bloody works right after we [garble].

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, Auto. Time me 10 seconds, somebody -

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: What's the Delta-V? Is it in there now? Let's double check each other.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You want to put down pitch and yaw attitude, gimbal lock (laughter) for, you know, PTC: 10 and 45. Yaw is 45, Jim.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, you've got your burn time there now , Bill?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: No, I didn't get it. Oh, I got the - I haven't got the updated one yet; what have you got?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: We got to add 3.7 seconds to what they gave us because this motor hasn't been performing like it should.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: So we got a burn time of 3:22 now?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: So, we're going to - You still going to ignite on 19:15?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: That's what you gave me, wasn't it?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, shutdown will be at 40 then, right?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I mean emergency shutdown will be at 40.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Starting at 89:19:16, burning 3:22, shutting down at...

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Shit, we got a lot to do.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: That's the worst one we've had here.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You know the colder, the better.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Are you going to pull out Pitch 2 and Yaw 2 circuit breakers?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Trying to get in place so you can get some sighting going.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Oh, P52 - Yeah, we're going into it. North is down.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Are we? Man, look at that. There you go.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Get a P52, will you? Let me have a Flight Plan.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Which way is my optics pointing?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Pointed at the - pretty - should be...

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yeah, Enter that. You didn't get it?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Based on helium pressure, I get 46, 50.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, you got two good ones, huh?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: We'd have enough there to blow it down, wouldn't we?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Just a minute, let me add it.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: All balls; want to record that?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Proceed. Gimbal angles: minus three zeros 40, plus four zeros 2, plus three zeros 48.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I'm not sure we can blow it quite all the way. We can blow it for the time to get to get to that short - I think we can blow it for over - for about 190 seconds down to 70 psi; if you want to go a little lower, you might as well go to chug; why, you can probably do it all the way.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: If we do have - If we do get one tank stuck, I'm going to shut the other one off, and blow them both down together.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: If we get - one tank's not getting pressurized, I'll shut off the other one, so you don't get a big Delta-P between them.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: What do you mean by that, Bill?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, let's go, start through the checklist. Shall we?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, first of all, the external Delta-V, right?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I'm getting my little library squared away here.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Want me to go through P30?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Because you can start right then with P40. There's the - there's the burn stuff.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, 61, this is not applicable, okay?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: If you set it at three counting up. I think you'd have it, wouldn't you?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I've got to get some of that Murine out; My eyes are... (Murine is a popular eye drop of the time)

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yeah, my eyes are bothering me, too.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You want to take a look at this, too?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: No, I don't think so; it just keeps you guys from seeing it, doesn't it?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yeah, a little. Let's just - do you ever want it?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I don't ever seem to have ever...

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: It's in my stowage bag if you think you - if you ever want to get it.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Oh, is that in the checklist?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Alright, then let's go with Bill.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, let's go to P40: P30,complete; CMC, On.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Test the Caution/Warning lamp; EMS Mode, Standby.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, EMS Mode, Standby; Delta-V set; set Delta-V C .

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: EMS Function, Delta-V; NonEssential Bus, Main B; cycling cryo fans. Good a time to do it as any.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Auto RCS select, 16, as required for ullage.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, we only need 12, I think. Right?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: We don't need the Y thrusters.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You've got all... We got all we need.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Load the DAP. Okay, four jets: one, two, three, four jets. Okay?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Minus three balls 40, plus two balls 157, right?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I don't know - Is that right?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay. Rotational Control Power, Normal, both, AC/DC.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: 6 22, load desired maneuver PAD gimbal angle.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You know, it might be worth putting out Flight Plans up.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I've got to get down there and take boresight, star, though.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I thought someone told me we weren't going to have any when we - hardly any of the Earth when we came back.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Probably won't, I don't think, because we're going to be way out...

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: We'll run over that entry tomorrow once and Thursday once. Okay?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You know, this kitchen down here's a pretty good deal.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Brings sort of homey atmosphere here.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yeah. How do you like your cryo, medium or well? Let me know when you get there.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: It takes a long time to get there.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I'll tell you what; I'll hurry it up so Jim can check the boresight star while we're in the dark.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, don't forget I got the Earth - or the Moon. If you're going back again, will you make a meal?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: That's a pretty good checklist now, isn't it?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Can you still see the Earth over there?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yeah, very distinct - half the Earth.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Does that mean they need the High Gain?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, I'll stop right here then.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Oh, I got it. I got it.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: It was in the Flight Plan. I read it.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Think so? I feel like I'm sitting straight up.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yeah, they might as well not build simulators any other way than they've been doing it. You're laying on your back in this thing no matter what you do.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I feel like I've been in the whole time like I've been here in the simulator.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: The only difference is that this is...

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I feel like I'm In the DCPS.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I'm giving these an extra little whack here just so there won't be any surprises.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: 42's a pretty small star, too; Peacock.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Why don't you let the old DAP take it from here?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I'm going to. As soon as we get in close, I'm going to give it to the DAP. It's going faster than the DAP can take [garble] roll [garble] It's going the way we want it to go.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You going to align the GDC here?(Yawn)

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yeah. I left it this way so we can tell where we're pointing.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I left her in Orb Rate.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Where's the Earth; can you see it?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Gentlemen, Peacock should be rising above the Moon right now.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: No. Oh, it's out here, Bill - up this way.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, so what we are going to do is pitch down this way, huh?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: We've got an Earthset picture for Life magazine!

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You're kind of in deep trouble for doing that. It's impossible.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You guys could go ahead with the checklist without me in case I don't pick it up right away.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You're looking right at the Moon.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yeah, you have to wait a while.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Gee, that's a pretty interesting view, Isn't it? That Earthshine is bright.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: When the Earth sets, then we'll have enough - -
