a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Oh, yeah, I see it quite well.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Oh, I might be able to get a star up there, though. What was the - what was my star?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Your star was Scorpii Delti - Delta.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, how in the hell would you ever get it?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, there are some stars up here, see, that just...

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You're not going to be able to get it until damn near just prior to ignition.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I won't be able to get a boresight star because we'll be in the daylight.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yeah, but you've got an inertial Moon in your way.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, if it - if the COAS - If you set the COAS and it doesn't hit the moon, then it's okay.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: That's right. It's kind of hard not to hit it though (laughter), looking down at it like this.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I think you're looking at Saturn.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, I can't even see... I'm not getting in your way, am I?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Alright, I'm going to put this thing Inertial - Inertial Power, Off; lighting, Off; select one - IMU.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I could - I guess I could get out the optics and set the thing all the way up. All I'd have to do is wait until we get there.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Look at that red star going down there.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I was trying to figure wit what that was, too, Bill.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Boy, they set in a hurry, don't they?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, it's Scorpius, maybe it was - Yeah?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: That wouldn't be setting now, would it?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yes, it would be. If it's going to be part of the boresight star, it's got to be near the horizon - near the plus-X axis.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, Bill, that should complete it.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, I don't know; I hope he can.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Are you going to do that before we press on, Jim?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: When we get - when we get...

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: ...your double umbra, why, you can do it then.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Double shadow. When the Earth sets, then you'll be able to - you'll be looking at 90 degrees back and you can look right down on it.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yeah, the umbra is the shadow.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: So we're in the shadow of the Sun; that the umbra of the Moon, and when we're in the shadow of the Earth, that's the umbra. You should be able to get a boresight star pretty soon, because we're going, to come to the end of the...

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Are we? Okay, I'll go down there and set it up.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Wait a minute. Where in the hell are we?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: We're not doing anything - are we? Are we maneuvering?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: No, we're not. We're holding steady, but...

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yes, that's right; we're not 90degrees from our burn from our burn place yet. If we're 90 degrees from our burn place, we'll be looking straight at the Moon.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yes, I know. And we're not upside down like that. We're - well - you have your optics are up.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Optics are posigrade. They'll go to up.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, Bill, when do you start reading the 6-minute checklist?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, let's see here. 89:19 we'll call it; let's make it 89:13, okay? And the 5 one will be at 89:14, and the 2 will be at 89:17 - 35

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I'm just looking where the Pitch 2 and Yaw 2 circuit breakers are. I want to make sure you pull the right one.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I'm really screwed up. It looks to me we ought to be going the other way.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Huh? Yes, well, look. Well, here we are right here.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I should have got down here a long time ago.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Here's where we're going to be when we burn, right?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Yes, and we're right here now. See? And we're looking straight down at the Moon, and the Earth is over here.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Okay, you're not going to be able to do it until we get past this...

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Now, if I can't do it until real late, go - Start without me.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You'll be able to do it here. You're 15 minutes - 20 minutes out of the burn.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I wonder if the Moon is made out of basically the same material as the Earth is.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Anders is going to tell you when he alights from the first LM - Pick up all the gold.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I think he doesn't have to; he knows it all right now. Didn't you hear him? Ye geologists of the world: I see a few grabens, a few slipped discs.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: There's a strange light down there.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I think you're going to be able to see it pretty soon.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Well, I'll put it in and wait for it.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Are you going to read this off to me?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Oh boy, we're going to hit that damned thing to 10 again.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: No, he needs it read off to him.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Verb 41, Noun 91, Enter. Okay, we'll lose them here pretty soon.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You want me to write - you want me to log this?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: 09240. Okay. Enter. And the trunnion is plus 25300. Plus 25300. Enter.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: There's no trouble reading by Earthshine.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Oh, I don't have anything yet.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You got the Earth - the Moon, I mean?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I think I'm still on - still on the Earth - or the Moon.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: What did your - what's your shaft and trunnion? Jim?

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: Oh, well, you're looking down at its eye. You've got to wait until you get down past the 90-degree point.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I think I see it coming up.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0880955-onboard.text: I see the limb, and I see the stars coming up.

a08_0880955-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0880955-onboard.text: You got optics power, zero, and - Oh, you haven't done that yet, huh?

a08_0881449.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0881449.text: Okay. On the helium tank temps: that's not recorded on low bit rate, and looking over our tape dumps, most of this stuff we have on the back side there is low bit rate. So we won't be able to get you an exact number, but looking at what we have every time we go out of sight and come back over the hill, it looks like you can expect about 82 to 84 degrees as a nominal temperature.

a08_0882000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0882000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 88 hours, 20 minutes. At the present time, we are about 31 minutes, 15 seconds from Loss of Signal. And the crew, at this time, is involved in aligning the platform on their guidance and navigation system. Here in Mission Control Center, Flight Director Milton Windler has just gone around the room again, pulsing all of the flight controllers and in every case the word was Go. We have gotten all of the necessary information up to the crew at this point that they will need for the maneuver. And at the present time, the mood here in Mission Control Center could best be d

a08_0882828.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0882828.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We'd like to have the tape recorder for about 5 minutes for one last look.

a08_0882828.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0882828.text: Thank you. And I guess we still have a cryo stir ahead of us, and we've checked your PIPA bias, and there's no change.

a08_0882828.speaker: Anders
a08_0882828.text: Roger. And we're stirring the cryos right now.

a08_0883157.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0883157.text: Apollo 8, the tape recorder is yours. We have your Double Umbra update, 89:07...

a08_0883157.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0883157.text: Rog. And no change on your AOS time.

a08_0883157.speaker: Borman
a08_0883157.text: Say that again, will you, Ken?

a08_0883157.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0883157.text: There's no change on your AOS time.

a08_0883700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0883700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 88 hours, 37 minutes. We're now some 13 minutes, 55 seconds from Loss of Signal. The Guidance Officer has confirmed that the spacecraft at this time is in the proper orientation for the Trans-Earth Injection maneuver. That maneuver scheduled to occur at 89 hours, 19 minutes, 16 seconds into the flight. There have been a very few brief comments passed back and forth from the ground to the spacecraft since our last report and we'll play those back for you now and then stand by for any live conversation with the crew.

a08_0884200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0884200-pao.text: At this point, Flight Director Milton Windler has just advised his flight controllers that we are just about 10 minutes now from Loss of Signal. And recommend they take a last look at all their displays before we lose communication with the crew. We're coming upon that Trans-Earth Injection maneuver. Currently, the spacecraft is traveling at a speed of 5,331 feet per second. Our current altitude is 63 nautical miles [116.7 km] and the orbital parameters are 63.2 nautical miles [117.0 km] for apocynthion, 58.6 nautical miles [108.5 km] for pericynthion. At 88 hours, 42 minutes into the flight o

a08_0884600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0884600-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 88 hours, 46 minutes. We are now just under 5 minutes from Loss of Signal. We'll stand by for any communications with the crew, as we - as the spacecraft goes over the lunar horizon and we lose touch with them. At the present time, Jim Lovell should be finishing a sextant star check. This will be a verification of the spacecraft attitude for the maneuver. He will then be transferring to his couch, joining Commander Frank Borman and the Lunar Module Pilot Bill Anders, who are in their couches at the present time. We'll stand by now for any parting communications with t

a08_0884737.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0884737.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We have 3 minutes to LOS; all systems are Go. [Long pause.]

a08_0884737.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0884737.text: Apollo 8, Apollo 8. This is Houston. Three minutes LOS; all systems are Go. Over.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I should see Peacock rise over that - I'm just amazed the way this thing operates.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: A pretty fantastic week, isn't it?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: This is utterly fantastic, though. This pawl line is lined up exactly with Gruis.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: You know what I think made me sick that night?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Seconal - one of the big ones

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I didn't know you had small ones. I'd have taken one of those.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Maybe I did, I don't know, but it seems like you guys would have gotten it.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Well. I think that basically your stomach was just upset because you can get it very easily. There's nothing wrong, you know.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Yeah, I know, but I never had it before, not even in zero-g airplane, which is a - a real...

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I hope this baby holds out for another 2½ days. It sure has performed admirably, hasn't it?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: And there it is. Just a minute, And I'll verify it.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: You can leave that off - Looks like we're going to be burning in the daylight anyway.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay. Drive trunnion [to] less than 5 degrees.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Optics, zero. Don't hit the IMU switch; Optics, Off.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, why don't you - Frank, you can have your lights ups I guess - Unless you wanted to check your star.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Frank, let me come down the other side.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I doubt if I'll be able to.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: No, I mean around the other side.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I guess you probably won't; you'll be pitched into the Moon, won't you?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Yeah, that's the trouble, I - I just barely get - then when I do see it, I see a lit horizon.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, align spacecraft roll to GDC. You got...

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: 16 minutes. Do you went to wait awhile to do this?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Well, It's already aligned. I'll do it now, Bill - I don't think I'll have to do much - Put in a little bit of yaw that way.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, align spacecraft roll and GDC aligned. We'll trim it again here - before the burn.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Stability Control System's circuit breakers, panel 8. Closed.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Alright. Now, let's watch this, Jim.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Don't want to leave that, out.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I'm going to check mine over here, too.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, SPS circuit breakers, Closed, except for gauging.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Gauging Open, okay; Pitch 1, Yaw 2, Pitch - Yaw 1, Yaw 2. They're in.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I'm just checking all mine here.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Don't push on them when you've got [garble].

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Rotational Control Power Direct, both, Off.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: TVC Gimbal Drive: Pitch and Yaw, Auto.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Boy, it's blacker than pitch out here.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, (yawn) you're going to burn with the lights on anyway, aren't you, because you've got to get sunlight.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Yeah, I watched the Sun - I watched that star rise, and I could just see the black horizon of the Moon fade away and the star come up and - right on it.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, if we get a Main A or an AC1 failure, you change gimbal drives, right?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: You got a Main B or an AC 2 failure, don't change gimbal drives or do anything, except put your gimbals to - from Auto to 1.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Do you see anything hanging around that could come down?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Tell you one thing these flights are good for: an old fatty like me, I bet I lost a lot of weight. I didn't eat much those first two days. and I didn't - didn't even get much to eat today.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I'm doing a P23 right after we leave this place, huh?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: No, I hope not. It looks low. It's just cold in there.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: It does look a little low. When did I say I had the star?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Because we still have 60 degrees to go there, if we want to be parallel - perpendicular - horizontal to the horizon.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: The horizontal, because I was 60 degrees down and I - I just saw the...

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: We're still looking at the Moon - flat at the Moon.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Oh, no, not flat at it, but boy, it's black out there.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: If you don't got G&N ignition, what are you going to do?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Wouldn't it be smart to take it around again?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Why? If we didn't got it this time, why would we get it better the next time?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: There's a 10-degree excursion on this thing.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Make sure you hit the corridor.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: You're right. It would be smart to take it around again.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Get set up to do an SPS burn, huh?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I haven't looked at your G - you might still be able to get...

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Wait a second; let me check it.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Now, you should see something. Yeah, there it comes.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I see it off the side of the terminator from sunrise.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I wonder if that - that sort of a zodiacal light was a glare off the optics, or something.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: You ought to draw a little picture of it, and people could tell you what it was.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: You got the gimbal thing handy right off the bat?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Yeah, why don't we write that down?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I bet we had the - The weight hadn't - the trim hadn't - changed any since the last time. (Laughter). Getting worried there for a minute.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: We've been eating a lot of food.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Let's see now, that's 2 - 2 minutes and 13 seconds. Is that what we said? 2:18.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: 2:18 must give you a slow return home.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Probably, one of the things we've been hearing is these oxygen masks snapping up and down.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Boy, it took three acts of Congress to get those little strings.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Oh. That - that's peculiar, isn't it?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Yeah, looks to me like we're going right at it. Doesn't it look like that to you?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Why is it we do all these burns upside down?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: (Laughter) You want to look at that?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: If it makes you feel bad, look out the side windows.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Yeah, that makes it look better.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: I've got - coming up on 10 minutes.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Yeah, Geeze, don't let me forget that.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, we better write that down.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Yes. You're going to call it off, right?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Yes. Ullage as required down there, I guess. You'll see 15 seconds right on here.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: All it does is let you see whether it's there or not; then if it is, it doesn't do anything.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Yeah, I know, but it drifts off a little. The deadband affects it, I guess.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Boy, you think you're going to burn right into the - water - I mean, right into the sand.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Did you have trouble scooping up those type of rocks? You said you went up to West Texas for that.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, Main Bus ties are coming On.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay. SPS, TVC, two, Rate Command; And TVC Gimbal Drive, Pitch and Yaw in Auto. Recheck them.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, TVC Servo Power 1, AC 1, Main A.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Well, I'll try to remember - Got it in there.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Stand by to start the Gimbal Motors.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Should I pull the circuit breakers?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, let's start Pitch 1 and Yaw 1.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Boy. You sure can't tell when you're...

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: S - Spacecraft Control, CMC and Auto.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay. Gimbal test option, Accept, Spacecraft Control, CMC; verify.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Hey, listen. It looks to me like I'm going to burn right into the ground. Oh! There's the horizon. Hurry! We're going the right way.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0885205-onboard.text: 3.2 degrees at T IG minus 3 - right about now.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, I can - It looks good.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: We've got to arm this Translational Hand Controller. Did you tell me to do that?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, 5 seconds after you start, get Delta-V Thrust B, On. Okay?

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Okay, yeah. Then I'm all set.

a08_0885205-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0885205-onboard.text: Don't forget to start your watch, Jim. Reset it now.

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0891739-onboard.text: [Garble] a hell of a kick in the pants now, I'll tell you that.

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0891739-onboard.text: Right. Comes back on at 30; 15 seconds later you give it the ullage.

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0891739-onboard.text: You got one Delta-V Thrust, On?

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0891739-onboard.text: I'll give you a mark for ullage.

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0891739-onboard.text: How many seconds do you need?

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0891739-onboard.text: [Garble] g's are building up. [Garble] get lighter.

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0891739-onboard.text: Okay. We're coming down the pike.

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0891739-onboard.text: Okay. Four valves closed. [Garble] closed. Delta-V Thrust A and B...

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0891739-onboard.text: Delta-V Thrust A and B, Off.

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0891739-onboard.text: Okay. Pitch 2, Yaw 2, circuit breakers, In. Turn them off slowly.

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0891739-onboard.text: Flight Recorder's Off; Main Bus ties, going Off; A is Off...

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0891739-onboard.text: Wait a minute. Did you get all this, Jim?

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0891739-onboard.text: You don't have to do a thing to that.

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0891739-onboard.text: I got 26.4, and the burn time was...

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Lovell
a08_0891739-onboard.text: I have it. Burn time was 2 minutes (cough) and 23 seconds.

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Borman
a08_0891739-onboard.text: Okay, can we proceed out of here, then? You got all this?

a08_0891739-onboard.speaker: Anders
a08_0891739-onboard.text: EMS - just a minute, EMS Function, Off.

a08_0891900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0891900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 89 hours, 19 minutes into the flight. We're now less than 30 seconds to the scheduled time of ignition for the maneuver to start Apollo 8 on its course back to Earth. In the last 15 seconds, prior to ignition, the crew will be burning their Service Propulsion System - rather the Reaction Control System engines to settle propellants. And here in Mission Control Center, we have just counted down to the burn. We should have ignition at this time. That will be a 3-minute and 18-second burn nominally. It will increase the spacecraft velocity by about 3,522 feet pe

a08_0892200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0892200-pao.text: Coming up in just a few seconds now, we should have shutdown of the Service Propulsion System engine on the spacecraft. That should have occurred at 89 hours - or rather will be occurring at 89 hours, 22 minutes, 34 seconds. Actually, we are just a little less than a minute from that event. And the clock here in Mission Control Center that is counting down to the time when we will reacquire the spacecraft shows that we have 6 minutes, 30 seconds until reacquisition.

a08_0892200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0892200-pao.text: At this point, the SPS engine should be shut down and we will now be waiting for the spacecraft to come over the lunar horizon and give us a report on their status. We now show 5 minutes, 45 seconds until reacquistion.

a08_0892600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0892600-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 89 hours, 26 minutes. Flight Director Milton Windler has just advised flight - his flight control team here in Mission Control Center that we have less than 3 minutes now until reacquisition of the spacecraft and he requested that they monitor their consoles, get prepared to reacquire and to get a status from the crew. [Pause.]

a08_0892600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0892600-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We now show less than 30 seconds until reacquistion. We'll stand by for the first words from the Apollo 8 crew as they come over the lunar horizon, and into acquisition.

a08_0892600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0892600-pao.text: We have RF signal, and there's a little bit of a cheer going up from the flight controllers here. We should be hearing from the crew shortly.

a08_0892600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0892600-pao.text: Our station at Honeysuckle, Australia, reports that we do have a radio signal from the spacecraft. They're having a bit of trouble locking up at this point, to the point where we can get voice communication from the crew.

a08_0893416.speaker: Lovell
a08_0893416.text: Roger. Please be informed there is a Santa Claus.

a08_0893416.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0893416.text: You're the best ones to know.

a08_0893416.speaker: Lovell
a08_0893416.text: And burn status report: it burned on time; Burn time, 2 minutes, 23 seconds; seven-tenths plus V GX . Attitude nominal, residuals; minus five-tenths V GX , plus four-tenths V GY , minus 0 V GZ ; Delta-V C , minus 26.4.

a08_0893416.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0893416.text: Apollo 8, could you comfirm your burn time, please? [Pause.]

a08_0893416.speaker: Lovell
a08_0893416.text: Roger. We had 2 minutes, 23 seconds. Our - wait one. [Pause.] Stand corrected to that; 3 minutes, 23 seconds.

a08_0893600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0893600-pao.text: This is Mission Control, Houston. Our Flight Dynamics Officer says that burn is good.

a08_0893633.speaker: Borman
a08_0893633.text: You get the sensation that you're climbing, Ken.

a08_0893633.speaker: Borman
a08_0893633.text: I say, this gives you the sensation that you're climbing.

a08_0893633.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0893633.text: Apollo 8, at the first convenient moment, we'd like to have the High Gain Antenna.

a08_0893633.speaker: Borman
a08_0893633.text: You've got it; you're on the High Gain.

a08_0893900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0893900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. We continue to get a great deal of noise coming from our site at Honeysuckle, Australia. However, the pertinent information has been received, and that is that the maneuver, the Trans-Earth Injection maneuver, was very close to nominal. Flight Dynamics Officer expressed his pleasure with it and - stand by, here's a call to the crew.

a08_0893950.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0893950.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We do not have any data on the ground yet; the voice looks very good.

a08_0894144.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0894144.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We'd like to try to have you manually acquire on the High Gain.

a08_0894144.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0894144.text: And this will take a wide beamwidth.

a08_0894306.speaker: Borman
a08_0894306.text: Houston. Apollo 8. We've manually acquired in wide beam.

a08_0894306.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0894306.text: Roger. Reading you loud and clear. Initial tracking indicates a 4 foot per second at 8 hours [probably after TEI] will put you on target.

a08_0894306.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0894306.text: Apollo 8, we have data; we'd like to have the tape recorder.

a08_0894511.speaker: Lovell
a08_0894511.text: Roger. Do you wish me to reinitialize the W-matrix at this time? [Pause.]

a08_0894511.speaker: Borman
a08_0894511.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Which battery do you want us to start charging? [Pause.]

a08_0894511.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0894511.text: Okay. We'd like to start on battery Alpha.

a08_0894511.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0894511.text: Apollo 8, would you go to narrow beam on High Gain? [Long pause.]

a08_0895100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0895100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 89 hours, 51 minutes. And in here Mission Control Center, we're continuing to assess the effects of that maneuver, and we're just in the process now of playing back the tape data of the burn. Of course, that maneuver occurring on the back side of the Moon, we were unable to monitor as it occurred. We're now looking at the results that we would have seen had we been able to receive communications from the spacecraft as the burn occurred. We just put in a call to the crew. Here is that conversation.

a08_0895133.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0895133.text: Okay. If you'll go to P00 and Accept, we'll update the REFSMMAT, and I have some backup GDC angles for the new entry REFSMMAT.

a08_0895133.speaker: Borman
a08_0895133.text: Roger. Understand; P00 and Accept, and you'll give us a new REFSMMAT.

a08_0895254.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0895254.text: Roger. Your backup GDC alignment; roll, 308; pitch, 209; yaw, 357. Over.

a08_0895406.speaker: Slayton
a08_0895406.text: Morning, Apollo 8. Deke here. I'd just would like to wish you all a very Merry Christmas on behalf of everyone in the Control Center, and I'm sure everyone around the world. None of us ever expect to have a better Christmas present than this one. Hope you get a good night's sleep from here on and enjoy your Christmas dinner tomorrow; and look forward to seeing you in Hawaii on the twenty-eighth.

a08_0895406.speaker: Borman
a08_0895406.text: Okay, leader. We'll see you there. That was a very, very nice ride, that last one; this engine is as smooth as glass.

a08_0895406.speaker: Slayton
a08_0895406.text: Yeah, we gathered that. Outstanding job all the way around.

a08_0895406.speaker: Borman
a08_0895406.text: Thank everybody on the ground for us. It's pretty clear we wouldn't be anywhere if we didn't have them doing it or helping us out here.

a08_0895406.speaker: Anders
a08_0895406.text: Even Mr. Kraft does something right once in a while. [Pause.]

a08_0895406.speaker: Slayton
a08_0895406.text: He got tired of waiting for you to talk and went home.

a08_0895600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0895600-pao.text: This is Houston. Our capsule communicator in that last exchange was astronaut Donald K. Slayton, Chief of Flight Crew Operations here at the Manned Spacecraft Center.

a08_0895600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0895600-pao.text: Shortly after we acquired the spacecraft and established communications with the crew, here in the Control Center, our big display up in the front changed from a lunar map to an Earth map and the colors on it are red and green. We also had a Christmas tree brought in and it's now standing down in the front of the Control Center. It looks like it stands about 6 feet tall and it's decorated with lights and tinsel and with a big blue ornament up on top.

a08_0895600-pao.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0895600-pao.text: Okay. The computer is yours, and I guess we have an IMU alignment and a P23 on the schedule.

a08_0895600-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_0895600-pao.text: Okay. Thank you. Do an IMU alignment coming up. CM in Block.

a08_0895706.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0895706.text: Okay. The computer is yours, and I guess we have an IMU alignment and a P23 on the schedule.

a08_0895706.speaker: Borman
a08_0895706.text: Okay. Thank you. Do an IMU alignment coming up. CM in Block.

a08_0895901.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0895901.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We'd like to have you cycle your zero optics switch prior to beginning P52.

a08_0895901.speaker: Borman
a08_0895901.text: Roger. We're gonna see if we can find some stars here before we do this P52.

a08_0895901.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0895901.text: Rog. And, I got a couple of words for you. Jack (Schmitt)'s been watching you since LOI, and he has a few words he wanted to give you.

a08_0895901.speaker: Schmitt
a08_0895901.text: Typhoid Jack here, and we've got some good words here that originated at the Cape with a bunch of friends of yours. And it's sort of in a paraphrase of a poem that you're probably familiar with. Do you read me, Apollo 8?

a08_0895901.speaker: Schmitt
a08_0895901.text: Okay. "Twas the night before Christmas and way out in space, the Apollo 8 crew had just won the Moon race. The head sets were hung by the consoles with care, in hopes that Chris Kraft soon would be there. Frank Borman was nestled all snug in his bed, while visions of REFSMMATs danced in his head; and Jim Lovell, in his couch, and Anders, in the bay, were racking their brains over a computer display. When out of the DSKY, there arose such a clatter, Frank sprang from his bed to see what was the matter. Away to the sextant he flew like a flash, to make sure they weren't going to crash. The light

a08_0895901.speaker: Borman
a08_0895901.text: Thank you very much. That was a very good poem; but in order to win the race, you have got to end up on the carriers.

a08_0895901.speaker: Lovell
a08_0895901.text: Hey, Jack. You really got Bill trained. [Laughter.]

a08_0895901.speaker: Schmitt
a08_0895901.text: You did pretty well, Jim. You must have talked on the way out there. [Laughter.]

a08_0900300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0900300-pao.text: That rendition of The Night Before Christmas was read up to the crew by astronaut Harrison Schmitt - Jack Schmitt - who worked with Lovell quite extensively prior to the mission in going over the lunar sightings and the photography that he would do in lunar orbit. At 90 hours, 3 minutes into the flight; this is Apollo Control.

a08_0900721.speaker: Borman
a08_0900721.text: Roger. We got an alignment with your new REFSMMAT now. What's on the program here? You want us in P23 and then what?

a08_0900721.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0900721.text: Looks like some sleep's coming up.

a08_0900721.speaker: Borman
a08_0900721.text: That's what I wanted you to say. We used up the gimbal angles of 10 and 45 with the - this REFSMMAT, right?

a08_0901356.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0901356.text: Rog. Notice that you're starting on your P23 which is the last scheduled activity. Initial tracking looks like the initial midcourse may be less than the 4-foot-per-second on the first guess. And we've looked at your burn data, and it's all just as smooth as you said; everything on there looked real nominal. Systems now look good; looks like in PTC attitude, we should be able to switch omni's for you, if you would like to do that. We were having good success with predicting, on the way out, where to switch the antennas; and if it'll help you, why, we can do that on the way back in.

a08_0901356.speaker: Borman
a08_0901356.text: That'd be nice if you could do it, but we will keep one man at the shop to watch the gimbal angles; but if you could switch the ang - the omnis, it would sure save us a lot of problems.

a08_0901356.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0901356.text: Okay. We'll do that. When you get in that PTC attitude, why, we'll - we'll let you know when we're taking command on the omni antenna switching.

a08_0901356.speaker: Borman
a08_0901356.text: Okay. [Pause.] Just be careful what you do with the tape recorder. Bill's a little sensitive about that.

a08_0901356.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0901356.text: Rog. We were listening to the tape dumps, and it looks like Bill gets a happy new year after all. [Pause.]

a08_0901356.speaker: Borman
a08_0901356.text: A happy new year? How come, again. Is that an in joke?

a08_0901356.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0901356.text: No, we got that off of his tape dump; he and Jim were discussing that one.

a08_0901800-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0901800-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 90 hours, 18 minutes. Our displays here in Mission Control are now beginning to show the effects of that Trans-Earth Injection maneuver. We show an altitude above the Moon at this time of 2,802 nautical miles [5,189 km]. Our spacecraft velocity is 6,050 feet per second [1,844 m/s], and slowing. And our weight following that maneuver is now 32,180 pounds [14,597 kg]. On board the spacecraft at the present time, the crew is finishing up some last minute activities connected with onboard navigation and then they plan to get a little bit of rest, Frank Borman is

a08_0903516.speaker: Borman
a08_0903516.text: Houston, are you getting all this data from P23? [No answer.]

a08_0903516.speaker: Borman
a08_0903516.text: I wanted to know if you're getting the data from P23?

a08_0905000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0905000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 90 hours, 50 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. At the present time our spacecraft is at an altitude above the Moon of 4,504 nautical miles [8,341 km] and traveling at a speed of 5,645 feet per second [1,721 m/s]. We've heard very little from the crew since our last report. We do have a couple of brief exchanges on tape, and we'll play those back for you and then stand by for any conversation.

a08_0905000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0905000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control. We're expecting Capsule Communicator Ken Mattingly to put in a call to the crew shortly. While we wait for that, we'll pass along some information that we've been requested to gather, and also some additional information on the results of that Trans-Earth Injection maneuver. The Trans-Earth Injection burn occurred on time. It lasted for 3 minutes and 23 seconds. We had originally estimated that it would last about 3 minutes, 18 seconds. We obtained almost precisely the amount of velocity change from that burn that had been planned. The figure that we have at this point

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: Go ahead, Apollo 8. [Long pause.]

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: Go ahead, Apollo 8.

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Hey - hey Ken, we've about run out of gas here on this next set of stars. Would you ask your people to be especially alert there watching the systems tonight?

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: Sure will, Frank.

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Okay. It's maneuver to pitch 10 and yaw 45.

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: Roger. I have - let's see, we've got a hydrogen purge line here that ought to come on about 91:40 and an oxygen-hydrogen fuel cell purge for 92 hours. [Pause.]

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Okay. Will you call us about those, please?

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: I sure will. And, let's see, we just wanted to let you know we've got a real good battery charge going here this time. Looks like - it looks just like the ones in the book, and I'd like to get a battery C voltage before you shut down and a sleep report on what you did in...

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Okay.

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: ...lunar orbit and your plans for the next couple of hours.

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: 37 volts on battery C.

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: Roger. 37 volts. [Pause.]

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: We only got about 2 hours sleep today, max. Ken. We're going to now - Bill's going to stay up awhile, and Jim and I are going to sack out, then we're going to try to rotate to short sleep cycles till we can get back to the normal ones.

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: Roger, sounds like a good idea. And EECOM on the ground tells us that the flying EECOM (is) to go ahead and put his hydrogen purge line heater on, and we'll get ready for a fuel cell.

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Thank you. He can't turn on his radio. There he goes. [Pause.]

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: I hope it won't disappoint anybody too much if we knock off those last two stars, but Jim is just in a daze, and so am I.

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: Rog. No sweat.

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: Apollo 8. One of the things we'd like to have before you shut down also is a Verb 64 so we can watch these pointing angles.

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Roger.

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: Hey, Frank, you might be interested; they are having some trouble with the medics' pee tube.

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: What?

a08_0910955.speaker: Anders
a08_0910955.text: The medics can't clean out their pee tube. [Pause.]

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Oh, is that right? It's been so busy.

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: Oh, yeah. It's worn the thing out at the bearings. [Laughter, Long pause.]

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: Hey, Ken, tell the people if you see anything getting close to the gimbal lock to be sure and whistle, too, will you?

a08_0910955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0910955.text: We sure will, Frank. You will want to make sure one of you keeps your comm carrier on.

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: We'll keep one man with a headset on.

a08_0910955.speaker: Borman
a08_0910955.text: That's right. We'll keep one man with a comm carrier on.

a08_0911939.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0911939.text: Apollo 8. You have got some big yaw angle there. [Long pause.]

a08_0912200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0912200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control at 91 hours, 22 minutes. Since our last report, we've had a couple of brief conversations with the crew. They indicated that they were very tired and had perhaps gotten about 2 hours of sleep prior to the Trans-Earth Injections maneuver. Frank Borman advised that he and Jim Lovell were going to attempt to get some sleep shortly and that Bill Anders would stand watch while they were getting some sleep and then when one of them awoke, Bill would get some sleep. We'll play back that tape for you and then stand by as our Capsule Communicator puts in a call to the crew.

a08_0912816.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0912816.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Copy that you are now in the PTC attitude, and we're watching your gimbal angle. We apparently do not have a downlink voice, but the data is good. [Long pause.]

a08_0912816.speaker: Anders
a08_0912816.text: Okay. We're establishing PTC. We took one last look at the Moon and are on our way back.

a08_0913100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0913100-pao.text: This is Mission Control, Houston at 91 hours, 31 minutes. Our spacecraft is at an altitude of 6,673 nautical miles [12,358 km] above the Moon and we're traveling at a speed of 5,375 feet per second [1,639 m/s]. Appears that we're going to have no further communication with the spacecraft at this time and we'll take the circuit down and come back up when next we reestablish contact or with a periodic status report.

a08_0913217.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0913217.text: Okay. In order for us to handle the antenna switching, I guess we'd like to have the Aux Tape switched to Off, and the Tape Forward switch, Off; and we'll be switching between omnis Bravo and Delta. [Long pause.]

a08_0913217.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0913217.text: Okay. We're going to be switching between omnis Bravo and Delta.

a08_0913217.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0913217.text: All right. And I'm gonna - you bug me when you get over 50 degrees of yaw, so I'll probably be watching that number pretty closely. We'd like to have the Biomed switched to the right position. [Long pause.] Okay. And for your own information: the fuel we show in the different quads I have here if you'd like to copy it.

a08_0913550.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0913550.text: Okay. I'll give you the percentage. On Alpha, 60; Bravo, 57; Charlie...

a08_0913550.speaker: Anders
a08_0913550.text: Wait a minute. It asks for present time, and I can't plot that fast, Ken.

a08_0913550.speaker: Anders
a08_0913550.text: That's a coincidence. That's just what I worked out on Lovell's slide rule. [Pause.]

a08_0913550.speaker: Anders
a08_0913550.text: How are we doing on the cryos?

a08_0913550.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0913550.text: Oh, you've got some pretty good numbers on that today. Sent up yesterday, and you had about 160 hours. Well, I'll check that out, but you were fat on cryo. I've got some SPS Delta-V. You've got 3,320. You fly the Service Module RCS through the DAP, you have 142; and through SCS, it's 121. [Long pause.]

a08_0913955.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0913955.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We can't monitor on low bit rate whether you started your fuel cell purge. If you haven't, we can go ahead and start now; and if you keep us posted as you go through it.

a08_0913955.speaker: Anders
a08_0913955.text: Roger. You want an O 2 and an H 2 purge, Ken?

a08_0915159.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0915159.text: Looks like you may be in omni Alpha. Can you confirm that we're set up to switch between Bravo and Delta? [Long pause.]

a08_0915159.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0915159.text: Okay. Thanks very much. And you are in the fuel cell purge?

a08_0915159.speaker: Mattingly
a08_0915159.text: Okay. Understand the purge is complete. Thank you. And in reference to your cryo, looks like we'll have 180 pounds in each oxygen tank at Sep and 11 pounds in each hydrogen tank. And you're well above the single tank capability. [Long pause.]

a08_0922222.speaker: Carr
a08_0922222.text: Apollo 8, Houston in the blind. Select Omni Charlie. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0922222.speaker: Carr
a08_0922222.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Apollo 8, Houston in the blind. We've lost all data on you and request you select us a good Omni antenna; try Charlie. Over. [No answer.]

a08_0925728.speaker: Carr
a08_0925728.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. How do you read?

a08_0925728.speaker: Anders
a08_0925728.text: I read you loud and clear; my comm here must have come unconnected.

a08_0925728.speaker: Carr
a08_0925728.text: Roger, Bill. We lost data on you for about 15 minutes and voice comm for about 45 and were beginning to get a little itchy. Is your PTC set up for Rate Command attitude hold? [Pause.]

a08_0925728.speaker: Anders
a08_0925728.text: Roger. Pitch and roll is in PTC

a08_0925728.speaker: Carr
a08_0925728.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Set up Omni Charlie. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0925901.speaker: Carr
a08_0925901.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're showing yaw 54.5. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0925901.speaker: Anders
a08_0925901.text: Roger. It's been deadband right around there the whole time. [Long pause.]

a08_0925901.speaker: Anders
a08_0925901.text: You can take command P00, also, if you want to. You might have to use it again.

a08_0925901.speaker: Anders
a08_0925901.text: You can take over command P00; you might have to use it again.

a08_0925901.speaker: Anders
a08_0925901.text: I'm trying to be quiet so the other guys can sleep, Jerry.

a08_0930200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0930200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 93 hours, 2 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 now 11,290 nautical miles [20,909 km] away from the Moon, Current velocity, 5,110 feet per second [1,558 m/s]. We placed several calls in the blind to Apollo 8 and it took a while before we got a response from Bill Anders, and we're going to play that sequence for you now.

a08_0930200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0930200-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. This sequence, somewhat dramatic sounding, was more a matter of curiosity than concern here in Mission Control since we were and are getting in good to the spacecraft with commands, and receiving solid telemetry. The curiosity, quite frankly, we didn't know for sure if Bill Anders had dozed briefly or if he had gone to the Lower Equipment Bay, or just what. The solution, as Bill himself explained, he had a loose connector. So, at 93 hours, 6 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8, continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0930624.speaker: Carr
a08_0930624.text: Switch to Omni Bravo, and we'll try the Bravo-Delta switching again. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0930900-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0930900-pao-press-conference.text: We're on Omni B now, Houston.

a08_0930900-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0930900-pao-press-conference.text: Looks like B couldn't quite hack it; I'll put it back there in a minute.

a08_0930900-pao-press-conference.speaker: Anders
a08_0930900-pao-press-conference.text: Houston, if EECOMs need any more help, just tell them to give me a call.

a08_0932200.speaker: Anders
a08_0932200.text: We're on Omni B now, Houston.

a08_0932200.speaker: Anders
a08_0932200.text: Looks like B couldn't quite hack it; I'll put it back there in a minute.

a08_0932200.speaker: Anders
a08_0932200.text: Houston, if EECOMs need any more help, just tell them to give me a call.

a08_0933057.speaker: Anders
a08_0933057.text: We're going on Omni Bravo now, Houston.

a08_0933258.speaker: Carr
a08_0933258.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Looks like we're getting pretty far off in both pitch and yaw. Showing about 50 degrees in pitch and about 25 in yaw.

a08_0941308.speaker: Carr
a08_0941308.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. All systems looking good. Over.

a08_0945320.speaker: Carr
a08_0945320.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Your systems are all looking good. Got a Flight Plan update for you: at time 96, you can delete P52. Your drift rates are real small. [Pause.]

a08_0945320.speaker: Anders
a08_0945320.text: Roger. And I'd like to do the chlorination at about 95:30 if I could.

a08_0945320.speaker: Anders
a08_0945320.text: And Houston, we're on Omni C and going to Bravo now - correction, Dog.

a08_0945320.speaker: Anders
a08_0945320.text: We're on - we're on Charlie now.

a08_0945320.speaker: Carr
a08_0945320.text: Roger. Understand you're on Charlie. Break. Verify your Up TLM switch is - Command Reset is at Normal. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0945320.speaker: Anders
a08_0945320.text: Roger. It's in Normal. I've had it Command Reset since we broke lock there, and I had to get back and control the omnis, so why don't you go command it over to Dog. Then give it back, and I'll set the other one on Bravo.

a08_0945320.speaker: Carr
a08_0945320.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We have you on Delta; you can go to Bravo. Break. Give us a call when you've finished your chlorination. Over.

a08_0945320.speaker: Anders
a08_0945320.text: Okay. Everybody seems to be stirring around now, so we'll probably just do it on time.

a08_0945926.speaker: Anders
a08_0945926.text: Houston, and the other two space aces are up now, and LMP's going to hit the pad and like to take a Seconal prior.

a08_0945926.speaker: Carr
a08_0945926.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. Permission granted, Bill. Have a good sleep.

a08_0945926.speaker: Carr
a08_0945926.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Looks like you'll need about 3 more hours on that battery A charging. Over.

a08_0945926.speaker: Anders
a08_0945926.text: Okay. Well, my cohorts can handle it.

a08_0945926.speaker: Carr
a08_0945926.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Can we get a crew status report on Bill before he goes to sleep?

a08_0945926.speaker: Anders
a08_0945926.text: He's feeling fine. [Pause.] A little sleepy.

a08_0945926.speaker: Anders
a08_0945926.text: And had a meal about - had a meal about 2 hours ago; drinking lots of water.

a08_0945926.speaker: Anders
a08_0945926.text: Good night. Wish everybody a Merry Christmas for me.

a08_0945926.speaker: Carr
a08_0945926.text: Sure will, Bill. Same to you. [Long pause.]

a08_0945926.speaker: Carr
a08_0945926.text: Make sure Bill hangs up his stocking before he goes to bed. [Pause.]

a08_0945926.speaker: Anders
a08_0945926.text: I've got it right next to my teddy bear.

a08_0950534.speaker: Borman
a08_0950534.text: Roger. We're - we're up and on the job; Bill's going to sleep; just thought I'd let you know.

a08_0950700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0950700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 95 hours, 7 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. Although the Apollo 8 spacecraft won't enter the Earth's sphere of influence until it's at an altitude of 175,528 nautical miles [325,078 km] above the Earth, our displays here in Mission Control have now switched to an Earth-reference system. At the present time, relative to the Earth, we read an altitude of 189,133 nautical miles. Our velocity reading, relative to the Earth, currently reads 4,055.9 feet per second [1,236.2 m/s]. As we pick up conversation with the crew, we find that spacecraft Commander Frank

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. I have a little feature news and sports news for you if you'd like to hear it. [Long pause.]

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Roger, Frank. I have some feature page and sports page news if you'd like it.

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: Roger.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Roger. First of all, Frank, the guys down here on the consoles want to spread their appreciation for a beautiful television job done. [Pause.]

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: Thank you.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Roger. We'll start out with the sports news. Los Angeles Dodger pitcher, Sandy Koufax, and Ann Widmark, 23-year-old daughter of actor Richard Widmark, plan to marry sometime in the near future. Koufax said Tuesday that no date for the wedding was set, but he and Miss Widmark have been dating for some time. At Springfield...

a08_0950956.speaker: Lovell
a08_0950956.text: [Garble] again.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Say again. [Pause.]

a08_0950956.speaker: Lovell
a08_0950956.text: Morning. How do you read?

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Morning, Jim. [Pause.]

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Let's see. In Springfield, Missouri, Mickey Owen, the old-time catcher for the Brooklyn Dodgers who made the record books by dropping a third strike that led the New York Yankees to a victory over the Dodgers in the '41 World Series, decided that he would be remembered by more than just his sports record. Forty-five boys and girls have been the recipients of ponies that he offered. These youngsters were requested to send letters in telling him how they would care of a pony. When the letters poured in, he added five ponies to the 20 he already offered; and other donors pitched in 20 more. And s

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We read your antenna change. You still reading us?

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: Roger. This is Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Roger.

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: We just now changed antennas, or you must have.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Okay.

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: You lost...

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: In Reno, Nevada... [Pause.] Oh, that's affirmative, Frank. We changed the antenna from here.

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: Thank you.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: In Reno, Nevada, because there's no fireplace in his home, [garble] a little boy wrote Santa Claus in care of the local newspaper and suggested, "Would you please use the front door. You'll have to kick the bottom a little bit because it sticks." In Little Rock, Arkansas, babies born at St. Vincent Infirmary during the week before Christmas and through Christmas Day are being released to their mothers at discharge time in huge red Christmas stockings. [Pause.] Here's one in ecumenical cooperation. In Indio, California, the Chief of Police was armed, Christmas Day, with a prayer book. Rabbi Phi

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: From the Associated Press, Americans watch Pope Paul celebrate Christmas Mass in Italy, and Europeans viewed a Christmas greeting from Apollo 8 via the most powerful communications satellite yet sent aloft. The views of Pope Paul and the Apollo 8 crew Tuesday night were the first to be relayed across the Atlantic commercially by Intelsat III, which was launched from Cape Kennedy last Wednesday. That's the one we saw go.

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: Roger. I remember that.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Intelsat is a 63-nation international communications consortium; provides a start on the first global communications network. The new satellite is scheduled to begin full commercial service on January 2nd, initially serving North and South America and Europe. Further coverage of the Apollo 8 mission is to be relayed to Europe this week. [Pause.]

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: From Washington: "This Christmas, the world is brightened with the hope of peace. When it comes, when hope turns to substance and the guns are quiet once again, it will come because you have pursued it with courage and skill." This was a message from President Johnson to the Armed Forces on Christmas [Pause.]

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Here's a feature by Harry Rosenthal of Associated Press. It says: from Houston. Two Santas brighten the Christmas Eve for 2-year-old Jeffrey Lovell. The first one knocked on his front door and brought presents. The second started his daddy home from the Moon. The first wore a red suit and a white beard and ho, ho'd, loud enough to be heard down the block. The second was a huge engine spitting flame behind the Moon, and thousands of people are awaiting - were awaiting word that it had fired. "Please be informed that there is a Santa Claus." were the first words from Apollo 8 as it emerged from

a08_0950956.speaker: Lovell
a08_0950956.text: Thank you, Jerry.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Roger. We have a newspaper coming in after a while; and we'll give you a little more news later.

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: Thank you, Jerry; that's nice. [Long pause.]

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: Jerry, we have chlorinated the water. We're changing the canister now.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Roger, Frank. Copy.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Would you put the Biomed switch to the left, and we'd like a crew...

a08_0950956.speaker: Borman
a08_0950956.text: Roger.

a08_0950956.speaker: Carr
a08_0950956.text: ...status report on Jim and Frank when you get a chance. [Long pause.]

a08_0952700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0952700-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. As you heard, Bill Anders, just before retiring, had requested and received permission to take a short-acting sleeping pill. Borman and Lovell now up, listened to their early morning deep space newscast. After Jerry Carr completed his newscast to the crew, Flight Director Glynn Lunney grinned and said, quote, there's a new item on the wire, Jerry, they want you to take a job in New York as a newscaster. And so at 95 hours, 27 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0952901.speaker: Borman
a08_0952901.text: Jerry, this is Frank. Do you have any later word on our trajectory and how the charging looks?

a08_0952901.speaker: Carr
a08_0952901.text: Roger. Stand by, Frank. We'll give you an update. [Long pause.]

a08_0952901.speaker: Carr
a08_0952901.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're looking at a midcourse correction at 104 hours of about 5 feet per second. Your tracking is real good. We got you in the center of the corridor and on target.

a08_0952901.speaker: Borman
a08_0952901.text: Understand; 5 feet per second at 104 hours.

a08_0952901.speaker: Carr
a08_0952901.text: Frank, did you get the word that we deleted the P52 at 96 (hours)?

a08_0952901.speaker: Borman
a08_0952901.text: Roger. Do you mind if we go ahead and do it now?

a08_0952901.speaker: Carr
a08_0952901.text: Negative; we've deleted it. Your drift rates are so small that you don't even need to unless you want to do it.

a08_0953719.speaker: Carr
a08_0953719.text: Roger, Frank. In 3 minutes, we're handing the control from Honeysuckle over to Madrid. Over.

a08_0954146.speaker: Carr
a08_0954146.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Buenos dias from Madrid.

a08_0954146.speaker: Carr
a08_0954146.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Reading you loud and very noisy.

a08_0954347.speaker: Borman
a08_0954347.text: Houston, Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_0954347.speaker: Carr
a08_0954347.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Loud and clear. How me?

a08_0954505.speaker: Borman
a08_0954505.text: Hi, Jerry, this is Frank. Do you read me?

a08_0954505.speaker: Borman
a08_0954505.text: Okay. I wasn't sure we were lined up. Thank you. Enough [garble].

a08_0955137.speaker: Carr
a08_0955137.text: Apollo 8, Houston. If you don't need the computer, we'd like to have you call up Verb 64 Enter so that we can do the B-D antenna switching from the ground. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0955137.speaker: Carr
a08_0955137.text: Jim, if you don't need the computer, would you call up Verb 64 Enter, and we'll take care of the antenna B-D switching down here. Over.

a08_0955137.speaker: Borman
a08_0955137.text: We just did an automatic maneuver and then get on back to PTC attitude.

a08_0960000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0960000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 96 hours into the flight of Apollo 8. The Apollo 8 spacecraft at this time is 187,043 nautical miles [346,404 km] away from Earth. Its velocity, relative to Earth, now reads 4,063 feet per second [1,238 m/s]. During the past 20-some odd minutes, we've had a couple of conversations with the Apollo 8 crew and we're going to pass those on to you now.

a08_0960000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0960000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. This 5-feet-per-second midcourse correction at 104 hours is performed perpendicular to the radius vector or roughly this would be perpendicular to the flight path. So at 96 hours, 4 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8, this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. All your systems looking good. Over.

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: Thank you, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Roger, Frank. I got some more newspaper you if would like to hear it.

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: We would enjoy it.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Roger. We'll start out with the world news. On page 1 of the Houston Post: praise for America's Apollo 8 astronauts and hopes for international cooperation in space exploration with the worldwide Christmas Eve messages as the tiny spaceship orbited the Moon. Even in the Communist world, there was enthusiasm for man's first voyage to the Moon. In Moscow, Soviet scientist Anatoly Besaranov recalled his country and the United States had shared space knowledge before and predicted the Apollo 8 flight would lead to more cooperation. In Cuba, Radio Havana rebroadcast the Voice of America program to

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: It doesn't look too flat from here, but I don't know; maybe something is wrong with our vision.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Roger. Elsewhere in the world news, the Pueblo crew landed at NAS Miramar yesterday afternoon at 14:00, and they'll spend a few days there in Balboa Hospital with their families celebrating Christmas. On the local scene here, the - on the local scene, the Retail Merchants' Association has announced that its Christmas gift exchange policy was going to be the same this year as it was last year; that is, very liberal. Fellows, we'll be glad to replace any broken items that you might bring back, too; but, sorry, there won't be any cash refunds.

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: Okay.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Another little bit of local news: the County Court House at Huntsville burned down before dawn yesterday, so, looks like they're going to go into the construction business there again. On the feature page: got a little bit about the waiting families. This one is by Ann James, Post reporter. "We rest on the backside of the Moon," said Valerie Anders on Christmas Eve, as she and her family waited for Apollo 8 to get out of the Moon orbit and head back toward home. Mrs. Anders had been up since 2:00 am Tuesday, and neighbors had just collected all the youngsters so the family could get some rest

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: Neil will be crying.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: (Laughter) You bet. On the sports page, not too much activity. UCLA is tops in both basketball polls. If you got any - any particular one you want to ask about, let me know, and I'll tell you if it's in the top ten on either poll. As far as the North - the college All Star game that's going to be played tomorrow is concerned, the North is a slight favorite over the South. Ara Parsegian is the coach of the North team, and he's got six of the Notre Dame troops working for him, so they ought to be pretty tough. The coach of the South team is Frank Howard of Clemson. He says it ain't easy, he quip

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: No. Thank you very much, Jerry.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Okay, Frank.

a08_0962615.speaker: Lovell
a08_0962615.text: Jerry, you can do this every Sunday.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Do you want me to read you the funnies?

a08_0962615.speaker: Lovell
a08_0962615.text: No, thanks. [Long pause.]

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Hey, Frank, did you get the word that - that Fred made all-district football team?

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: Yes, thank you. I heard about that before - before the lift-off.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Yeah. I thought you'd heard about that. Now, back to the workaday; we need a cryo fan cycle from you. [Pause.]

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: We're starting it right now.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_0962615.speaker: Lovell
a08_0962615.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Go.

a08_0962615.speaker: Lovell
a08_0962615.text: Jerry, in a little while, I'd like to try out a little P37 exercise based on the minus MA. I'll just run one through, and maybe we can get a solution from the ground and see how they compare.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Okay, Jim. [Long pause.]

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Retro says they are ready to copy.

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: That performance at LOI was absolutely fantastic. You all really hit it on the money; I just couldn't believe it. [Pause.]

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: Roger. Thanks. Kinda surprised us, too.

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: Uh-uh. I hope you're not getting close to the Earth. We got another corridor to hit, you know.

a08_0962615.speaker: Carr
a08_0962615.text: We haven't quit yet.

a08_0962615.speaker: Borman
a08_0962615.text: Okay.

a08_0963500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0963500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 96 hours, 35 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 now 185,675 nautical miles [343,870 km] away from Earth. Its velocity relative to Earth now reading 4,071 feet per second [1,241 m/s]. During the past several minutes, Jerry Carr has been passing along the second edition of the deep space news round-up. That, along with some earlier conversation, we'll play to you now.

a08_0963500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0963500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 96 hours, 45 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8.

a08_0963500-pao.speaker: Lovell
a08_0963500-pao.text: Jerry, in a little while, I'd like to try out a little P37 exercise based on the minus MA. I'll just run one through, and maybe we can get a solution from the ground and see how they compare.

a08_0964225.speaker: Lovell
a08_0964225.text: We'd like to use the computer now if you don't need it now, we'll [garble] from here.

a08_0964225.speaker: Borman
a08_0964225.text: If you can switch it down there without Verb 64, well, go ahead and do it. [Pause.]

a08_0964225.speaker: Carr
a08_0964225.text: We'll give it a whirl, Frank.

a08_0964225.speaker: Borman
a08_0964225.text: Fans are off. The tanks have all been stirred.

a08_0964642.speaker: Borman
a08_0964642.text: Roger. Are you still using the pitch and yaw for the PTC as 10 and 45, aren't you?

a08_0965329.speaker: Carr
a08_0965329.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston with a battery status report.

a08_0965329.speaker: Borman
a08_0965329.text: Go ahead. We were just talking about the batteries.

a08_0965329.speaker: Carr
a08_0965329.text: Roger. At 96 hours GET, battery A has 38.95 amp-hours; battery B has 36.35 amp-hours; battery C has 38.46 amp-hours. Your total, 113.76 amp-hours. At 97 plus 50, battery A will be fully charged and will have 40 amp-hours, and you can terminate charge at that time. Over.

a08_0970212.speaker: Borman
a08_0970212.text: We'll give you back Verb 64, Houston. [Long pause.]

a08_0970212.speaker: Lovell
a08_0970212.text: We gave you back Verb 64. And I wonder if you could have Guidance figure out a corridor correction at 114 hours for us, with a minus 6.48 gamma.

a08_0970212.speaker: Carr
a08_0970212.text: Okay, Jim. We copy, and we see we've got the Verb 64 back. We'll be back with you in a minute.

a08_0972908.speaker: Carr
a08_0972908.text: Roger. We have a comparison now on your P37. [Pause.]

a08_0972908.speaker: Carr
a08_0972908.text: Okay. Based on your vector, the CMC vector, the ground computes 15.3 feet per second on the midcourse, V EI of 36221, a gamma EI of minus 6.51 so it looks like your P37 program is pretty good. Applying your P37 solution to our MSFN vector, however, we get a gamma EI of minus 10.32. We expect these two solutions to converge with a little more tracking and after you get some Earth horizon sightings. Over.

a08_0972908.speaker: Lovell
a08_0972908.text: Roger. How valuable do you think that the lunar sightings we did just after TEI are, as compared to your MSFN tracking [garble]?

a08_0972908.speaker: Carr
a08_0972908.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Repeat your question, please.

a08_0972908.speaker: Lovell
a08_0972908.text: Roger. I was getting curious of the value of onboard tracking in the P23 close to the Moon, in regards to the MSFN tracking that close to the Moon. I think there might be a trade-off for onboard navigation, and I think it might be a little bit better than MSFN [garble].

a08_0973300.speaker: Carr
a08_0973300.text: Roger. I guess the experts would say that the MSFN data was probably best based on the number of sightings that you've taken. However, that's going to be the subject of quite a bit of evaluation, I think, after the mission. Over.

a08_0973300.speaker: Carr
a08_0973300.text: Roger, Jim. Be advised that we are beginning to read you very weak, and with a rather loud background noise.

a08_0973300.speaker: Lovell
a08_0973300.text: Understand. I think we ought to [garble]. [Long pause.]

a08_0973300.speaker: Carr
a08_0973300.text: Apollo 8, Houston. How do you read now?

a08_0973300.speaker: Lovell
a08_0973300.text: I'm reading - I'm reading you loud and clear.

a08_0973300.speaker: Carr
a08_0973300.text: Roger. Still reading you weak but clearer.

a08_0975455.speaker: Carr
a08_0975455.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You can turn off the battery charger. Over.

a08_0980000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0980000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 98 hours into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8, at the present time, is 182,270 nautical miles [337,564 km] away from Earth. Current velocity relative to Earth now reads 4,100 feet per second [1,250 m/s]. We've had some conversation with the Apollo 8 spacecraft, specifically with Jim Lovell and we'll pass that along now.

a08_0980000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0980000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. What you heard was the ground, via Jerry Carr, talking to Jim Lovell aboard the spacecraft Apollo 8 critiquing the P37 return-to-Earth onboard computer program. Meanwhile, here in Mission Control, we have switched our space digitals display to reference the Moon again. Relative to the Moon, our altitude shows that we're 26,049 nautical miles [48,243 km] away from the Moon, at the present time. And our velocity - this is velocity relative to the Moon - reads 4,871.6 feet per second [1,484.9 m/s]. And 98 hours, 5 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8, this is Apoll

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_0980422.speaker: Lovell
a08_0980422.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Roger. Is this Jim?

a08_0980422.speaker: Lovell
a08_0980422.text: Roger.

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Roger, Jim. Christmas morning around your house was kinda quiet, says Marilyn. She said that they're all thankful that the mission has gone so great. They missed having you around the tree this morning, but they wanted to reassure you that your presents are waiting, and the roast beef and Yorkshire pudding will be on the table when you get home.

a08_0980422.speaker: Lovell
a08_0980422.text: Hey, that sounds good, Jerry - good old roast beef and Yorkshire pudding.

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Yeah, man. Is Frank listening?

a08_0980422.speaker: Lovell
a08_0980422.text: Say hello to them for me, will you?

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Sure will. Is Frank listening?

a08_0980422.speaker: Lovell
a08_0980422.text: Frank's not on the - Frank's not on the line yet; he'll be shortly.

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Okay. How about Bill? Is he still asleep?

a08_0980422.speaker: Lovell
a08_0980422.text: Bill's still asleep.

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Okay. Have Frank give me a holler when he's ready. I've got a message for him, too.

a08_0980422.speaker: Lovell
a08_0980422.text: Okay. Sounds good. How's your Christmas, Jerry?

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Real good, Jim. Santa Claus struck last night before I came in here on the shift, and I guess we'll finish off the unwrapping this morning when I get back.

a08_0980422.speaker: Lovell
a08_0980422.text: Right. He was looking for a chimney on (spacecraft) 103 here, but he didn't see any.

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: [Laughter.] You could have left the hatch unlocked for him. [Pause.]

a08_0980422.speaker: Lovell
a08_0980422.text: I'll think about that one.

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
