a08_0980422.text: Think real hard, Jim. [Long pause.] EECOM says he could have slid down the steam duct. [Pause.]

a08_0980422.speaker: Lovell
a08_0980422.text: Sounds good. About that time, Bill would have been boiling water. [Long pause.]

a08_0980422.speaker: Borman
a08_0980422.text: Hi, Jerry, this is Frank. What's up?

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Hi, Frank. Christmas morning has come at the Borman house. And the boys and Susan and your Mom and Dad all send their love. They say for you to stay in there and pitch. Over.

a08_0980422.speaker: Borman
a08_0980422.text: Okay. Thank you. Please reciprocate for me.

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Sure will, Frank. [Pause.]

a08_0980422.speaker: Carr
a08_0980422.text: Frank, when Bill wakes up, give me a holler. I've got a message for him, too.

a08_0980422.speaker: Borman
a08_0980422.text: Okay.

a08_0981523.speaker: Lovell
a08_0981523.text: Roger. Are the Guidance boys busy this morning? [Pause.]

a08_0981523.speaker: Lovell
a08_0981523.text: I just worked out an answer to move my landing longitude 30 degrees east, and I just want to compare with what they've got based on the same burn time of 114 hours, based on the bias impact longitude determined from the P37 which is wrong. I've indicated that I needed a 600-foot-per-second Delta-V C burn plus, and my Delta-V X changes from a minus 11.6 feet per second. I'd like to have them verify that if I could.

a08_0981523.speaker: Carr
a08_0981523.text: Roger Jim. Stand by, and I'll see if they copied all that. [Long pause.]

a08_0981523.speaker: Carr
a08_0981523.text: The voice isn't too great right now, and the Guidance troops didn't get all of that. How about waiting about 2 or 3 minutes? We'll swap Omni antennas, and then we should get good voice transmissions from you and then repeat it. Would you, please?

a08_0982100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0982100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 98 hours, 21 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 8. Our space digital displays now again referenced to the Earth - are referenced to the Earth. Our distance away for Apollo 8, distance away from the Earth at this time; 181,428 nautical miles [336,005 km]. Current velocity relative to the Earth, 4,108.5 feet per second [1,252.3 m/s]. Capsule Communicator Jerry Carr has just passed along family Christmas messages to two of the Apollo 8 crew members, Jim Lovell and Frank Borman, and we'll let you listen.

a08_0982255.speaker: Carr
a08_0982255.text: Apollo 8, Houston. How do you read? Over.

a08_0982255.speaker: Carr
a08_0982255.text: Roger. We're reading you much better now. Jim can go ahead with his transmission to the guidance troops. They have one question before he starts. They would like to know what his GERU was at T IG , 114 hours. Over.

a08_0982255.speaker: Lovell
a08_0982255.text: Roger. Wait one. The GERU at T IG was plus 07972.

a08_0982507.speaker: Carr
a08_0982507.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. We're ready to copy your data. Over.

a08_0982507.speaker: Lovell
a08_0982507.text: Okay, Houston. Based on the P37 with minus MA solution, I got an impact longitude of minus 160.95. I biased it to get an impact latitude - longitude of 163.75. I wanted to change my impact point 30 degrees to the east, and I tried to determine what my P30 burn parameters would be to do this, and I got a Delta-V X burn of a minus 11.6 and a Delta-V C of plus 600, Delta-V Y of zero. Now that changed my previous Delta-V X burn from minus 50.2. I just want to know whether that meets with their approval.

a08_0982507.speaker: Carr
a08_0982507.text: Roger, Jim. We copy and we'll run it through the mill and give you an answer.

a08_0984935.speaker: Carr
a08_0984935.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston with a Flight Plan update.

a08_0984935.speaker: Carr
a08_0984935.text: Roger. At 100 hours, 30 minutes, change star number 02 from one set to two sets. Over.

a08_0984935.speaker: Borman
a08_0984935.text: Roger. Star 02 from one set to two sets.

a08_0984935.speaker: Carr
a08_0984935.text: Roger. Also, set number 2, set number 2, change star number 11 to star 7. Over.

a08_0984935.speaker: Carr
a08_0984935.text: Roger. Then after star set number 3, initiate PTC again; pitch, 10; yaw, 45. Over.

a08_0984935.speaker: Carr
a08_0984935.text: Roger. Then at 101 hours, 30 minutes; delete the Earth horizon settings. Over. [Pause.]

a08_0984935.speaker: Carr
a08_0984935.text: That's affirmative. The folks here are evaluating the thermal situation. Looks like you'll be out of PTC for a rather extended period of time. That's the reason why we have you initiating PTC again there around 101 as soon as you finish those three star sightings. We're still working on the - about the next 10 hours after 100 hours, we're looking at the thermal situation, and the star sighting situation, and we'll be giving you more updates later on. Over.

a08_0984935.speaker: Borman
a08_0984935.text: Roger. We don't have a thermal problem at all now, do we? All our indications here are normal in here.

a08_0984935.speaker: Carr
a08_0984935.text: Roger. Everything looks okay. I think they're just kinda trying to look down the track aways.

a08_0984935.speaker: Borman
a08_0984935.text: I'm all for keeping it that way.

a08_0985653.speaker: Carr
a08_0985653.text: Roger. Frank, I'd like to talk to you for a minute or two about the auto optics funnies that you've been seeing throughout the mission. Over.

a08_0985653.speaker: Carr
a08_0985653.text: Roger. The problems you've run into so far are due to some unknown source, probably EMI (Electro-Magnetic Interference) or the like loading your CMC trunnion cell which is now 91, so that it doesn't really represent your true trunnion angle. Now this loading problem, we don't feel implies any decrease in the reliability in your CMC at all. We think that the best way to circumvent the problem is to cycle the Optics Zero switch first to Off and then On prior to using the optics for any purpose. And with that procedure, I think you probably won't have any more problem. Over.

a08_0985653.speaker: Lovell
a08_0985653.text: Roger, Jerry. Understand. I do notice one difference. We did two preferred REFSMMATs. The first one we had trouble with; the last one worked out as expected. And I noticed that for the first one that when the option came up, it was for a nominal option, whereas for the very same procedure for this last REFSMMAT change, we got the preferred REFSMMAT option when we called up the program.

a08_0985700-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0985700-pao.text: Roger. Frank, I'd like to talk to you for a minute or two about the auto optics funnies that you've been seeing throughout the mission. Over.

a08_0985700-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0985700-pao.text: Roger. The problems you've run into so far are due to some unknown source, probably EMI (Electro-Magnetic Interference) or the like loading your CMC trunnion cell which is now 91, so that it doesn't really represent your true trunnion angle. Now this loading problem, we don't feel implies any decrease in the reliability in your CMC at all. We think that the best way to circumvent the problem is to cycle the Optics Zero switch first to Off and then On prior to using the optics for any purpose. And with that procedure, I think you probably won't have any more problem. Over.

a08_0990056.speaker: Carr
a08_0990056.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston with a comeback on your entry navigation calculations. Over.

a08_0990056.speaker: Carr
a08_0990056.text: Roger. We went through the charts and got exactly the same answer as you got. It looks like your procedure is very good; looks like it was real good head. You remembered to average out the velocity. We also went ahead and computed the problem to verify the chart and got a good solution. Over.

a08_0990056.speaker: Lovell
a08_0990056.text: Now if we can get our state vectors to agree, we'll be in business.

a08_0990100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0990100-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 98 hours, 57 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. The Apollo 8 spacecraft now 179,989 nautical miles [333,340 km] away from Earth. Current velocity relative to Earth, 4,124.3 feet per second [1,257.1]. Capsule Communicator Jerry Carr has passed along some Flight Plan update information to Apollo 8, and we'll listen to that now.

a08_0990100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0990100-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. Apollo 8 now a bit over 4,000 nautical miles [1,200 km] away from that point in the flight path where it will be recaptured by the Earth's sphere of influence. So at 99 hours, 1 minute into the flight; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0990100-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_0990100-pao.text: Roger. We went through the charts and got exactly the same answer as you got. It looks like your procedure is very good; looks like it was real good head. You remembered to average out the velocity. We also went ahead and computed the problem to verify the chart and got a good solution. Over.

a08_0991938.speaker: Carr
a08_0991938.text: Roger. On your question about the option: Program 40 fits the preferred flag such that the next P52 will come up option 1, subsequent alignments after that come up option 2. Over.

a08_0991938.speaker: Lovell
a08_0991938.text: Rog. Understand. So 40 set up with the TEI burn, put in an option 1 for us.

a08_0991938.speaker: Carr
a08_0991938.text: Roger. Now concerning your restart that happened in lunar orbit, for the peace of mind of the computer people and the MIT folks, we have a question. Did Verb 34 Enter to a flashing Verb 51 in P22 cause your restart? Over.

a08_0991938.speaker: Lovell
a08_0991938.text: Yeah. That sounds like it was it.

a08_0991938.speaker: Borman
a08_0991938.text: That almost caused an unscheduled EVA, too.

a08_0992229.speaker: Carr
a08_0992229.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Biomed switch center. Over. [Long pause.]

a08_0993300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0993300-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 99 hours, 33 minutes into the flight, Apollo 8. Apollo 8 now 178,529 nautical miles [330,636 km] away from Earth. Its current velocity, relative to Earth, now reading 4,141 feet per second [1,262 m/s]. We've had some conversation with Apollo 8, since our last report and we'll play that now.

a08_0993300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_0993300-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston. You heard conversation exchanges between Jerry Carr here in the Mission Control Center and both Jim Lovell and spacecraft Commander Frank Borman. Bill Anders apparently still in a rest period. So at 99 hours, 36 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_0995059.speaker: Carr
a08_0995059.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. It's about time for us to start keeping track of some Command Module RCS temperatures; so when you get a chance, we'd like a reading now, and we'll try to repeat it about every 8 hours or so.

a08_0995059.speaker: Borman
a08_0995059.text: Okay. We'll get them for you right now.

a08_0995059.speaker: Borman
a08_0995059.text: You want the motor off the test meter, right?

a08_0995059.speaker: Borman
a08_0995059.text: So's 5D. [Long pause.] 6A is high; 6B is high; 6C is 5 volts; 6D is pegged high.

a08_0995059.speaker: Carr
a08_0995059.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Roger. Understand. 5C and 5D are pegged high; 6A and 6B are pegged high; 6 Charlie is 5 volts; and 6 Delta pegged high. Over.

a08_0995456.speaker: Carr
a08_0995456.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're showing quad A running a little bit warmer than the other quads. If you remember, I mentioned before that we were coming into a period of time here where we were going to spend a lot of time with no PTC going. We'd like you to try to favor quad A if you can in the shade, and do whatever you can to keep that temperature from getting out of hand. Over.

a08_0995456.speaker: Borman
a08_0995456.text: Roger. I'm only reading 121 on quad A.

a08_0995456.speaker: Borman
a08_0995456.text: Quad C is the highest temperature we have; it's 142. [Long pause.]

a08_0995456.speaker: Carr
a08_0995456.text: Roger, Frank. We're more interested in the tank temperatures than the quad temperatures. Over.

a08_0995456.speaker: Borman
a08_0995456.text: Roger. I understand. Now listen, if you think it is that important, let's just keep PTC-ing it and not even do anything.

a08_0995456.speaker: Carr
a08_0995456.text: Negative. There's no sweat right now. We're watching it, and we just wanted to let you know that this thing is being - being looked at. If we get anywhere near a situation where we feel we ought to change, we'll go back to PTC or cool it.

a08_0995456.speaker: Borman
a08_0995456.text: Okay. Thank you. We'll do our best, but it is kind of hard, though. You are sort of subject of spatial geometry: wherever the stars and the Moon happens to be, that's where you point.

a08_0995456.speaker: Carr
a08_0995456.text: Roger. We understand. We're going to keep an eye on it down here, and we'll keep you appraised.

a08_1000327.speaker: Carr
a08_1000327.text: Roger. Pass the word to Jim that on these marks that are coming up, pretty important that he remember to record his Delta-R and Delta-V and trunnion. We're working low bit rate down here, and so we're not going to be able to record that data from here. Over.

a08_1000327.speaker: Borman
a08_1000327.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Did you read that we are recording all the Delta-R, Delta-V and trunnion [garble].

a08_1001200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1001200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 100 hours, 12 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. Apollo 8 now 176,966 nautical miles [327,741 km] away from Earth. Our current velocity reading relative to Earth is 4,161 feet per second [1,268 m/s]. Let's harken back to one of our earlier air/ground discussions, an earlier reference to restart an unscheduled EVA involved a bit of banter on the part of spacecraft Commander Frank Borman. Apparently, yesterday in lunar orbit, Jim Lovell, working with his computer, got one of his verbs or nouns a bit twisted. The computer reacted predictably by giving a restar

a08_1001356.speaker: Borman
a08_1001356.text: As luck would have it, we got the Sun almost directly on top of us here.

a08_1001356.speaker: Carr
a08_1001356.text: Roger. We understand, but that tank temperature is holding steady, so we're all right.

a08_1001700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1001700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. The reference to quads there dealt with the Reaction Control Subsystem engine quads. From the ground we had a reading, or have a reading on quad A which indicates it's a bit above the temperature level of the other quads, some 7 degrees. And we will be watching this and taking steps to balance the temperatures. So at 100 hours, 17 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_1003058.speaker: Carr
a08_1003058.text: Roger, Frank. The helium tank temperature that we're watching on quad A has only gone up 1 degree in all this work that you're doing, so we don't consider it to be too terribly serious. What we'd like to do, as soon as you've finish this P23 work, is rather than go back into PTC, let's just roll her over 180 degrees and put quad A on the cool side, and hold it that way until your next activity comes up, which is around 102:30. Over.

a08_1004147.speaker: Borman
a08_1004147.text: Okay, Jerry. We're through with Program 23. We're just going to roll here to get the Sun off quad A then, if that's what you want.

a08_1005021.speaker: Borman
a08_1005021.text: It should be getting cool now, Jerry.

a08_1005021.speaker: Carr
a08_1005021.text: Roger, Frank. So far we haven't seen the temperature start back down again. We expect to see it, though. [Long pause.]

a08_1005021.speaker: Borman
a08_1005021.text: Roger. Give us the word if you want us to maneuver back here before that time, will you please.

a08_1005348.speaker: Carr
a08_1005348.text: Roger, Frank. We have some data that was missed on your P23. We'd like you to read it down to us if you have time.

a08_1005348.speaker: Borman
a08_1005348.text: Roger. We will in just a minute.

a08_1005348.speaker: Borman
a08_1005348.text: Go ahead. What do you want?

a08_1005348.speaker: Carr
a08_1005348.text: Roger. On star number 2, the sixth mark, we missed Delta-R and Delta-V.

a08_1005348.speaker: Borman
a08_1005348.text: Sixth mark, that's [pause]. Did Lovell tell you to do this? Come on, Carr; come clean. Did he ask you to ask for this?

a08_1005348.speaker: Carr
a08_1005348.text: Negative. Uh-uh. We really missed it.

a08_1005348.speaker: Borman
a08_1005348.text: It's all zeros, and all zeros.

a08_1005348.speaker: Carr
a08_1005348.text: Roger. All zeros, all zeros. Okay. On star number 7, we missed the trunnion on marks 1, 2, and 3.

a08_1005348.speaker: Borman
a08_1005348.text: On 1, the trunnion was 03235; on 2, it was 03240; and on 3, it was 03241.

a08_1005348.speaker: Carr
a08_1005348.text: Okay, Frank. And then the last one is on star number 1; we missed the trunnion on mark 5.

a08_1005400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1005400-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 100 hours, 54 minutes into the flight of Apollo 8. The Apollo 8 spacecraft at this time, 175,220 nautical miles [324,507 km] away from Earth. At 100 hours, 47 minutes, 47 seconds, the Apollo 8 spacecraft with its crew passed back into the Earth's sphere of influence. Its current velocity relative to the Earth currently reads 4,184 feet per second [1,275 m/s]. At this time, we're in the process of undergoing a change of shift. Cliff Charlesworth and his team now coming aboard. Since our last report, we have had several transmissions from the crew and we're goi

a08_1005400-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_1005400-pao.text: Roger. We will in just a minute.

a08_1005400-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_1005400-pao.text: Go ahead. What do you want?

a08_1005400-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_1005400-pao.text: Roger. On star number 2, the sixth mark, we missed Delta-R and Delta-V.

a08_1005400-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_1005400-pao.text: Sixth mark, that's [pause]. Did Lovell tell you to do this? Come on, Carr; come clean. Did he ask you to ask for this?

a08_1005400-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_1005400-pao.text: Negative. Uh-uh. We really missed it.

a08_1005400-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_1005400-pao.text: It's all zeros, and all zeros.

a08_1005741.speaker: Carr
a08_1005741.text: Was that last number you read down to me mark 2 on star number 1? [Pause.]

a08_1005741.speaker: Carr
a08_1005741.text: Roger. Thank you. That's one gotcha on guidance.

a08_1010310.speaker: Carr
a08_1010310.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You're back under our influence again. Over.

a08_1010310.speaker: Borman
a08_1010310.text: Very good. Things should start speeding up now, huh?

a08_1010310.speaker: Carr
a08_1010310.text: Roger. You've been in for about 20 minutes.

a08_1010310.speaker: Lovell
a08_1010310.text: Find out from the Guidance troops if a midcourse maneuver of minus 4.8 to access [garble] at 14 hours would be better than the 15.2 I came up with first.

a08_1010310.speaker: Carr
a08_1010310.text: We've already started checking it, Jim. I bet you thought you sneaked that P37 past us.

a08_1010500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1010500-pao.text: Now this is Apollo Control, Houston. Since the Black shift is shortly leaving duty, we thought at this time, that we would summarize the activities that we saw during this 9-hour period. When Glynn Lunney's Black Watch came aboard, we were very pleased to see a Christmas tree, a lighted Christmas tree here in the Mission Control Center which we understood was placed up sometime following the Trans-Earth Injection burn. The shift itself was one of relative quiet. When the Black Team of controllers took over, Bill Anders was awake. The - during most of the period, the spacecraft was flying in Pa

a08_1011229.speaker: Borman
a08_1011229.text: Roger. I just wondered how the temperature on quad A tank is doing.

a08_1011229.speaker: Carr
a08_1011229.text: We've seen no improvement as yet, Frank.

a08_1011700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1011700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 101 hours, 17 minutes into the flight, and the Green Team has taken over here in the Control Center. In the last few minutes we have noted down here on the ground that the temperature of quad A, the Reaction Control System 4-way motor on the Service Module called Quad A is showing a slight rise in temperature. It's about 10 degrees above where it should be. The other quads are running 70 to 75 degrees [F, 21 to 24°C]. Quad A is presently reading 86 degrees F [30°C]. So we asked Frank to roll the spacecraft around and put Quad A in the shade for a while. Tryi

a08_1011700-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_1011700-pao.text: Roger. Frank, we're going to establish a range sequence now. We'd like to try to keep silent on the net for about 3 minutes. Over.

a08_1011700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1011700-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control, Houston here at 101 hours, 19 minutes into the flight, and that brings us up to date.

a08_1011728.speaker: Carr
a08_1011728.text: Roger. Frank, we're going to establish a range sequence now. We'd like to try to keep silent on the net for about 3 minutes. Over.

a08_1012121.speaker: Carr
a08_1012121.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Range sequence complete. Over.

a08_1012813.speaker: Borman
a08_1012813.text: Hello, Houston. Apollo 8. How do you read?

a08_1012813.speaker: Carr
a08_1012813.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Loud and clear. [Long pause.]

a08_1012813.speaker: Borman
a08_1012813.text: Houston, how do you read? Apollo 8.

a08_1012813.speaker: Carr
a08_1012813.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Loud and clear. How me?

a08_1012813.speaker: Borman
a08_1012813.text: I wasn't reading you for a while. I read you loud and clear now.

a08_1012813.speaker: Borman
a08_1012813.text: I wanted to know what a range sequence test was, Jerry.

a08_1012813.speaker: Carr
a08_1012813.text: I was afraid you'd ask that. Stand by.

a08_1012813.speaker: Carr
a08_1012813.text: Roger. This range sequence thing is - is a phenomenon we get on down-voice backup; in this mode, the ranging and the voice share the same channel, so we have to periodically check to make sure that they're not interfering with each other. Over.

a08_1012813.speaker: Borman
a08_1012813.text: Thank you. These flights are very educational.

a08_1012813.speaker: Carr
a08_1012813.text: Roger. We are learning a little bit down here, too.

a08_1012813.speaker: Borman
a08_1012813.text: I hope you're not studying re-entry.

a08_1012813.speaker: Carr
a08_1012813.text: No, we're fat on those, Frank.

a08_1013912.speaker: Carr
a08_1013912.text: Roger, Frank. We'd like for you to go back into PTC now. Your helium tank temperature is still holding about the same. And we are going to try PTC to even things out. Over.

a08_1014000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1014000-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 101 hours, 40 minutes. The next television transmission is scheduled for 104 hours and 15 minutes, about 2½ hours from now. Should make it about 3 o'clock Houston time. That's pretty close, and we'll refine that a little later. The rise in quad A, that we noted earlier, is - is not - it's no panic situation at all. It's about 10 degrees above where we plot that it should be. We've rotated the spacecraft around, held it on the dark side for a while. And now the - the crew has been advised to go back to Passive Thermal Control, that gently rolling, barbe

a08_1014000-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_1014000-pao.text: He's off the air right now.

a08_1014000-pao.speaker: Carr
a08_1014000-pao.text: Roger, Frank. Let him know that we've compared his latest P37, and the state vectors have converged to - they're very, very close now.

a08_1014000-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_1014000-pao.text: Your state vector and our state vector are very, very close.

a08_1014000-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_1014000-pao.text: Is that right, Jerry? Okay. I'll tell him. Thank you.

a08_1014049.speaker: Borman
a08_1014049.text: He's off the air right now.

a08_1014049.speaker: Carr
a08_1014049.text: Roger, Frank. Let him know that we've compared his latest P37, and the state vectors have converged to - they're very, very close now.

a08_1014049.speaker: Borman
a08_1014049.text: Your state vector and our state vector are very, very close.

a08_1014049.speaker: Borman
a08_1014049.text: Is that right, Jerry? Okay. I'll tell him. Thank you.

a08_1014049.speaker: Carr
a08_1014049.text: Don't let his head get big, though.

a08_1014049.speaker: Borman
a08_1014049.text: You guys are making it impossible to live with him. It always was pretty hard.

a08_1014700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1014700-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control, Houston again. All caught up. A little quiet period here. Let's run through some of the charts this morning - or this afternoon. The cabin temperature - the cabin pressure is 4.9 pounds per square inch. We're looking at a cabin temperature of 78 degrees [F, 25.5°C]. Yesterday I think we ran between 79 and 77 [F, 25 and 26°C]. Showing presently 29 pounds [13 kg] of waste water aboard. Have 37 pounds [17 kg] of drinking water which means a full tank. And our oxygen quantities are well up there. Oxygen quantity tank 1 is 68 percent, and oxygen quantity in tank 2 is 68

a08_1015103.speaker: Borman
a08_1015103.text: Houston. How do you read Apollo 8?

a08_1015103.speaker: Borman
a08_1015103.text: Hello Michael, we lost lock and Bill hit Command Reset to get the lock back on again, but you're welcome to the antenna.

a08_1020702.speaker: Anders
a08_1020702.text: Houston, Apollo 8. Over.

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Go ahead.

a08_1020702.speaker: Anders
a08_1020702.text: Good morning, Michael.

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: Good morning.

a08_1020702.speaker: Anders
a08_1020702.text: Or is it afternoon? Or is it afternoon?

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: Apollo 8, Houston. You've got a lot of background noise and about unreadable. [Pause.] We're trying to get a better Omni. [Pause.]

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: Apollo 8, Houston. How do you read? Over.

a08_1020702.speaker: Anders
a08_1020702.text: Loud and clear.

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: Okay. You're loud and clear. This Bill?

a08_1020702.speaker: Anders
a08_1020702.text: None other.

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: I got a message for you while you were asleep. Valerie said to tell you that she and the kids are leaving for church about 11:30 and eagerly awaiting your return. She said presents are magically starting to appear under the Christmas tree again so it looks like a double barrel Christmas. Over.

a08_1020702.speaker: Anders
a08_1020702.text: You can't beat a deal like that. [Pause.] How was Christmas at your house today?

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: Early and busy as usual. I told Michael you guys are up there, and he said who's driving?

a08_1020702.speaker: Anders
a08_1020702.text: That's a good question. [Pause.] I think Isaac Newton is doing most of the driving right now.

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: Say again.

a08_1020702.speaker: Anders
a08_1020702.text: I think Isaac Newton is doing most of the driving right now.

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: Rog. We copy. [Long pause.]

a08_1020702.speaker: Anders
a08_1020702.text: Well, give Valerie and the kids a Merry Christmas for me, Mike, and tell them I'll see them there in a while.

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: I sure will, and you might tell Frank if he's got any messages his people are about 10 feet away.

a08_1020702.speaker: Anders
a08_1020702.text: He said "bah humbug."

a08_1020702.speaker: Borman
a08_1020702.text: Howdy, how're you all?

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: You've got a whole row of smiling faces in the back room, Frank.

a08_1020702.speaker: Borman
a08_1020702.text: Very good. Well, they'd be proud of me: I'm using the Exer-Genie right now.

a08_1020702.speaker: Collins
a08_1020702.text: Don't overdo it.

a08_1020702.speaker: Borman
a08_1020702.text: I won't.

a08_1021200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1021200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 102 hours, 12 minutes into the flight. Frank Borman's family; his parents, his wife, his two boys are in the Control Center and they just got a Christmas nod relayed to them from Apollo 8 by Mike Collins. Here's how the conversation went.

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_1021554.speaker: Borman
a08_1021554.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 8.

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: Roger. Quad Able helium tank temperature has dropped very slightly and is looking pretty good to us now.

a08_1021554.speaker: Borman
a08_1021554.text: Thank you, Michael.

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: Righto, and I've got a procedure for Jim which I'd like to read up. It involves bringing the LM and CSM state vectors to the Earth sphere of influence. Over.

a08_1021554.speaker: Borman
a08_1021554.text: All right. Stand by.

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a08_1021554.speaker: Borman
a08_1021554.text: He's getting his hat on now. Whose procedure is this, Michael?

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: Oh, it's the summation of the opinions of all our experts down here. I got it from Mr. Colossus, Gunther Sabionski.

a08_1021554.speaker: Borman
a08_1021554.text: Very good. I want to make sure it wasn't another Aldrin special.

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: I'm sorry you're broken up. Don't say again. [Laughter.] [Pause.]

a08_1021554.speaker: Borman
a08_1021554.text: Merry Christmas, Buzze. [Pause.]

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: Yeah, Merry Christmas up there, Jim. I've got a procedure when you are ready to copy.

a08_1021554.speaker: Lovell
a08_1021554.text: Okay. I just got on the headset; just let me get a pencil and paper here, and I'll copy it.

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_1021554.speaker: Lovell
a08_1021554.text: Okay, Mike.

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: Okay. The purpose is to bring the LM and the CSM state vectors to the Earth's sphere of influence. Step 1: Verb 37 Enter, 23 Enter. Step 2: At Noun 70, at Noun 70, load in register 1, 2, and 3 the following numbers. Register 1, 00002; register 2, five balls; register 3, 00210. Step 3: proceed on Noun 70, Noun 70. Step 4: proceed on Noun 25, 25. Step 5: do not proceed on Noun 18. Wait for 30 seconds; then do Verb 37 Enter, 00 Enter. End of procedure. Over. [Pause.]

a08_1021554.speaker: Lovell
a08_1021554.text: Okay. As I understand it, the reason for this procedure is to bring the LM and CSM state vectors back into the Earth's sphere of influence; is that correct?

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: That's correct.

a08_1021554.speaker: Lovell
a08_1021554.text: Okay. To do it, we go Verb 37 Enter, 23 Enter; and at the Noun 70, we'll load in register 1, four balls 2; register 2, all balls; and register 3, two balls 210. We'll proceed on Noun 70, we'll proceed on Noun 25. We will not proceed on 18. We'll wait 30 seconds, and we'll do a Verb 37 Enter, 00 Enter.

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: That's affirmative. Apollo 8. [Pause.]

a08_1021554.speaker: Lovell
a08_1021554.text: I'm just kinda curious, Mike; I thought this was done for us. I thought the computer took care of this little problem. [Pause.]

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: Roger. Normally, it is done automatically, Jim; and had you done the P23s exactly as scheduled, it would have been, but there was some doubt P23 was stopped about 7 minutes prior to the transition point and just to be absolutely sure, we included this procedure. Over.

a08_1021554.speaker: Lovell
a08_1021554.text: Okay. [Long pause.] Tell Buzz I could sure use his eye-patch.

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: Roger. Understand. I had one on Gemini X. Worked real well.

a08_1021554.speaker: Lovell
a08_1021554.text: Mike, you want me to do this procedure now?

a08_1021554.speaker: Collins
a08_1021554.text: That's affirmative, Jim. Now at your convenience.

a08_1022304.speaker: Unidentified (MCC)
a08_1022304.text: Did you see guidance? Is the flag set? Reset, that's right.

a08_1022450.speaker: Collins
a08_1022450.text: Roger Jim. We copied your DSKY work there, and it's looking just fine to us now.

a08_1022900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1022900-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston here; 102 hours, 29 minutes into the flight. Couple of points we should mention. For one, Quad A, the temperature that we reported earlier up - peaked to 86 degrees [F, 30°C], it's now on it's way down. It's dropped one degree - it's at 85 [°F, 29.4°C]. And that - that drop's taken place in the past 15 minutes. About 15 minutes ago, we went into Passive Thermal Control, a gentle slow roll that should distribute the Sun's heat evenly. Quad B is reading 71 degrees [F, 21.7°C]; Quad C, 76 [F, 24.4°C]; and Quad D, like dog, is 70 [F, 21°C]. This temperature measurement come

a08_1022900-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_1022900-pao.text: You know, one thing you can pass on to the program office - something you might try working on right away is...

a08_1022900-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_1022900-pao.text: Apollo 8, can you stand by? We'll try to get you a better antenna; you're just about unreadable.

a08_1022900-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_1022900-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We are right in between antennas and if you can wait about 5 minutes with your message, we should have better comm then.

a08_1022942.speaker: Borman
a08_1022942.text: You know, one thing you can pass on to the program office - something you might try working on right away is...

a08_1022942.speaker: Collins
a08_1022942.text: Apollo 8, can you stand by? We'll try to get you a better antenna; you're just about unreadable.

a08_1022942.speaker: Collins
a08_1022942.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We are right in between antennas and if you can wait about 5 minutes with your message, we should have better comm then.

a08_1023342.speaker: Collins
a08_1023342.text: Okay. You're Loud and clear now, Frank. Go ahead with what you were saying about the program office.

a08_1023342.speaker: Borman
a08_1023342.text: They ought to get some moving out on some way to fix these windows. The three windows, the hatch window and the two side windows, really it's a shame, the fact that they're almost - excuse me - almost totally unusable, because they got so gummed up.

a08_1023342.speaker: Collins
a08_1023342.text: Roger, I sure agree. We - we copy so far on the windows that 2 and 4 are still in excellent shape and 1 and 5 are sort of mediocre and 3 is just about totally unusable.

a08_1023342.speaker: Borman
a08_1023342.text: Three is totally unusable and 1 and 5 are unusable for any kind of photography.

a08_1023342.speaker: Lovell
a08_1023342.text: And, Mike, that sure puts the CMP in a bad light, you know, when you can't see where you're going.

a08_1023342.speaker: Collins
a08_1023342.text: Yeah, when you're sitting between two guys that won't tell you, too. [Laughter.]

a08_1023342.speaker: Lovell
a08_1023342.text: That's right. You think they'd share a window? No soap. You might also note the optics are very good visibility so far. No coating at all.

a08_1024000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1024000-pao.text: That was Jim Lovell who tagged that one with the statement 'Sure is a shame when the CMP, the Commander - Command Module Pilot can't see where he's going.' It's a reference to the old navigator joke. 'I am the navigator and I have a right to know [where I'm going]. Please tell me.' So, we in - all and all in good shape at 102 hours, 40 minutes into the flight; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_1024232.speaker: Collins
a08_1024232.text: Roger. We copy Jim doing a P52, and I'm standing by with a maneuver PAD for midcourse 5, anytime at your convenience. [Long pause.]

a08_1024232.speaker: Collins
a08_1024232.text: Roger, Jim. This is midcourse maneuver number 5, and it's a RCS/G&N: and it's 31700; not applicable, not applicable. Are you with me?

a08_1024232.speaker: Collins
a08_1024232.text: Good. 103:59:52.86; minus 0005.0, plus all zeros, plus 0000.1; 000, 334, 001; five zeros - 00000, plus 0019.0; 0005.0, 0:14, 0005.0. Are you still with me? Over.

a08_1024232.speaker: Collins
a08_1024232.text: Good. 41, 302.0, 18.3: Shaula, down 06.4, left 0.6; plus 07.47, minus 164.10; 1298.8, 36301, 146:46:40; north set of stars, Sirius and Rigel; roll, 308; pitch, 209; yaw, 357; remarks: use high-speed procedure with minus MA. Over. [Pause.]

a08_1024232.speaker: Lovell
a08_1024232.text: Roger, Houston. MCC-5; RCS/G&N. Are you with me?

a08_1024232.speaker: Lovell
a08_1024232.text: 31700; N/A, N/A, 103:59:52.86: minus 0005.0, plus all zeros, plus 0000.1: 000, 334, 001; all zeros, plus 0019.0; 0005.0, 0:14, 0005.0; 41, 302.0, 18.3; Shaula, down 06.4, left 0.6; plus 07.47, minus 164.10; 1298.8, 36301, 146:46:40; Sirius, Rigel, 308, 209, 357; use high-speed procedure with minus MA.

a08_1024232.speaker: Collins
a08_1024232.text: Roger. And could you go to Accept, please, and we're going to send you a P27 load consisting of a LM state vector and a target load for MCC-5.

a08_1025119.speaker: Collins
a08_1025119.text: Roger. We'd like to dump your waste water tank down to 25 percent; we'd like to do it before the midcourse, for tracking reasons. So if it is convenient with you, if you start right now, we'll dump on down to 25.

a08_1025119.speaker: Borman
a08_1025119.text: Roger. We'll get right with it.

a08_1025520.speaker: Collins
a08_1025520.text: Roger. We got those loads in and verified; you can go back Block at your computer. And George Low says he's working on that window problem at 6, or spacecraft 104. You just happen to have the wrong spacecraft.

a08_1025520.speaker: Borman
a08_1025520.text: That's the wrong statement; we've got the right spacecraft. I'll clue you, if it keeps going this way for 2 more days, we've got not only the right spacecraft, we've got the best spacecraft.

a08_1025713.speaker: Borman
a08_1025713.text: Apollo 8. We're starting the dump now, Houston.

a08_1025713.speaker: Collins
a08_1025713.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_1025713.speaker: Borman
a08_1025713.text: Okay. We're starting the waste water dump now.

a08_1025713.speaker: Collins
a08_1025713.text: Okay, Bill [means Frank]. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a08_1025713.speaker: Borman
a08_1025713.text: That's a blizzard.

a08_1025713.speaker: Collins
a08_1025713.text: Rog. Understand. [Long pause.]

a08_1025713.speaker: Collins
a08_1025713.text: Apollo 8, Houston.

a08_1025713.speaker: Anders
a08_1025713.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a08_1025713.speaker: Collins
a08_1025713.text: Roger. I need a Pop Romeo Dog on all three and a status report on the LMP.

a08_1025713.speaker: Anders
a08_1025713.text: Roger. The LMP's PRD hasn't moved an inch since we took off. And that's the one the CMP used to have, still 0.64. And I just had about 5½ hours sleep, and I'm in the process of scarfing up a meal; and I've been drinking lots of water, feeling good, and that's about it.

a08_1025713.speaker: Collins
a08_1025713.text: Okay. And you got a PRD on the other two.

a08_1025713.speaker: Lovell
a08_1025713.text: Yes. The CMP's PRD is reading point - The CMP's is reading 0.12 rem.

a08_1025713.speaker: Borman
a08_1025713.text: And the CDR: I got stuck with somebody else's, but mine reads now - my new one reads 2.02 rem. I don't know if there is a message there or not.

a08_1025713.speaker: Anders
a08_1025713.text: He's starting to glow in the dark. [Pause.]

a08_1025713.speaker: Collins
a08_1025713.text: Yeah. You should have - you should have hung on to the one you had. It sounded a little bit better. I copy left to right 2.02, 0.12, and 0.64. Over.

a08_1025713.speaker: Anders
a08_1025713.text: Roger.

a08_1025713.speaker: Collins
a08_1025713.text: Thank you, sir.

a08_1025713.speaker: Anders
a08_1025713.text: What have they measured in our [pause] What have they measured on that, I guess you would call it the VABABR, or VABD?

a08_1025713.speaker: Collins
a08_1025713.text: We're sending a boy to the back room to find out.

a08_1025713.speaker: Anders
a08_1025713.text: Find out what it is, or what it's reading?

a08_1025713.speaker: Collins
a08_1025713.text: First one and then the other.

a08_1025713.speaker: Anders
a08_1025713.text: We'll need both answers up here, too.

a08_1030358.speaker: Collins
a08_1030358.text: Roger. Bill's VABR reading that he requested is 0.13. Over.

a08_1030358.speaker: Anders
a08_1030358.text: Roger. Looks like you've got a little discrepancy here.

a08_1030358.speaker: Anders
a08_1030358.text: You ought to give those guys a chance to go back to sleep and calibrate those things. [Long pause.]

a08_1030358.speaker: Collins
a08_1030358.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We just passed 25 percent, and you can terminate your waste water dump, please.

a08_1030358.speaker: Borman
a08_1030358.text: Believe it or not, our gauge is 5 percent behind yours.

a08_1030358.speaker: Collins
a08_1030358.text: Yeah, John Aaron says he's been noticing it.

a08_1030700-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_1030700-pao.text: Yeah. We're going to switch antennas from Madrid to Goldstone in about 3 minutes. You should hear the glitch.

a08_1030700-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1030700-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 103 hours, 7 minutes into the flight. Apollo 8 is 169,750 [nautical] miles [314,377 km] from home. It's moving in a velocity of 4,264 feet per second [1,300 m/s]. You multiply by a 0.68, you get miles per hour. In the last 15 minutes, we've had a good deal of conversation with the crew. And in the course of it, Frank Borman makes a comment, a reference about the windows. He says they are really a shame. We discussed them yesterday, and the message was immediately relayed to George Low. And in the course of the ensuing discussion, Mike Collins suggested perhaps

a08_1030723.speaker: Collins
a08_1030723.text: Yeah. We're going to switch antennas from Madrid to Goldstone in about 3 minutes. You should hear the glitch.

a08_1030723.speaker: Lovell
a08_1030723.text: Rog. Just for information, would the perigee reading and Noun 42 be such a big minus number for such a small burn? We are reading minus 03137 now.

a08_1030723.speaker: Collins
a08_1030723.text: Rog. Understand; Noun 42 perigee reads minus 03137. Over.

a08_1030723.speaker: Lovell
a08_1030723.text: Roger. We're going through Program 30 after you give us the target load, and I didn't think there would be that much of a change for such a small burn.

a08_1030723.speaker: Collins
a08_1030723.text: Roger. Stand by. We'll check into it, Jim.

a08_1031654.speaker: Collins
a08_1031654.text: Roger, Frank. We don't think there's any problem or any funnies in this perigee prediction of minus 03137. It's a Keplerian prediction, and it's not very accurate. Now we've taken your vector from the downlink and run it through a make-believe external Delta-V maneuver down here, and we get precisely the correct answer. Over. [Pause.]

a08_1031654.speaker: Lovell
a08_1031654.text: Roger. Understand that you figure just because of the conics solution that it comes up.

a08_1031654.speaker: Collins
a08_1031654.text: That's affirmative. The Kepler solution is just pretty gross.

a08_1031654.speaker: Lovell
a08_1031654.text: Okay. I was just kind of curious. I could see differences when we were talking about LOI burns, but this being such a short one, I thought it wouldn't be that much difference. I understand.

a08_1031654.speaker: Borman
a08_1031654.text: Y'all are monitoring our - and seeing if we get any inadvertent engine firing all the time, aren't you?

a08_1031654.speaker: Collins
a08_1031654.text: Well, we - we can't tell when you're in low bit rate. When in high bit rate, yes, we are.

a08_1031654.speaker: Borman
a08_1031654.text: Okay. If we crank up high bit rate and just have you take a checkout look at them?

a08_1031654.speaker: Collins
a08_1031654.text: Roger. Since you're on Omni D, Dog, at this time, we're sort of 180 out of phase for the High Gain. As soon as we can get High Gain lock, then we'll, with our high bit rate, be looking at those - be looking for any thruster firings, but we can't do it until then. Over.

a08_1031654.speaker: Borman
a08_1031654.text: Okay. We'll take the antennas and get on the High Gain as soon as we can.

a08_1032100-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1032100-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control, Houston. That catches us up - catches us up to 103 hours, 21 minutes. We are now about 45 minutes away from a - 40 minutes away from the burn, a midcourse correction of 5 feet per second. The spacecraft will have its nose pointed at Scorpio. I do not know exactly what angle that'll be in - along its path of flight, but it apparently will not be in the direct line of flight. It'll be a slight adjustment kind of burn to have the effect to move the spacecraft more to the center of a 35-mile corridor keyhole through which the spacecraft will enter the atmosphere in it's

a08_1032649.speaker: Collins
a08_1032649.text: Roger, Frank. We've done some more checking, and we confirm that that is the correct Keplerian prediction on Noun 42, minus 03137, just like you said.

a08_1033541.speaker: Collins
a08_1033541.text: Roger. We are going to be doing a ranging sequence; if we could eliminate voice for a couple of minutes, we'd appreciate it.

a08_1034241.speaker: Collins
a08_1034241.text: Roger. Our ranging's complete, and we've been monitoring your thruster firings, and they show what appears to be very normal damp activity. Over.

a08_1034241.speaker: Borman
a08_1034241.text: I guess it was associated with the water vent.

a08_1034500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1034500-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 103 hours, 45 minutes into the flight. In the last few minutes we've been looking at the biomed data. The harness is switched to Jim Lovell and his mean heart rate is 57. The high during this sample period was 59; the low is 54. His respiration rate is 13. Jim and Bill Anders are shortly to have Christmas dinner, just after this midcourse correction which is to come at 104 hours into the flight. The 5-foot-per-second burn that'll have the effect of ensuring the spacecraft hits more nearly the center of our entry corridor, rather than the high side of it. We

a08_1034500-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1034500-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control, Houston; 103 hours, 47 minutes into the flight. We'll be back up with the burn in about 12 minutes.

a08_1035708.speaker: Collins
a08_1035708.text: Frank, we've got about 2½ minutes to ignition, and we're still showing some of your SCS switches not set up as per checklist; specifically, rate Low, deadband Minimum, and your BMAG modes at attitude one, rate two.

a08_1035708.speaker: Collins
a08_1035708.text: And your manual attitude switch is in Rate Command.

a08_1035900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1035900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 103 hours, 59 minutes into the flight and Mike Collins has given the crew a standby for their midcourse. 20 seconds to ignition for a burn that - in which the nose will be pointed at a 90-degree angle away - 90 degrees away from a radius vector running out from the center of the Earth. And we'll try to describe the position of the spacecraft a bit more at the change of shift briefing. It's - it's just a very difficult thing to visualize with the cerebral bodies. Present weight is 31,678 pounds [14,369 kg]. We're 167,548 [nautical] miles [310,299 km] from home.

a08_1035900-pao.speaker: Lovell
a08_1035900-pao.text: Rog. We burned on time, 14 seconds, attitude nominal. Our residuals were plus 2 in V GX , minus 1 in V GY nothing in V GZ . Our EMS stopped about 6.2 and was counting up - up to - continued counting after the burn.

a08_1035900-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_1035900-pao.text: Rog. Understand 14 seconds, burn on time, nominal attitude, two-tenths X, one-tenth Y, and nothing minus one-tenth Y, and nothing Z; and you put 6.2 on the EMS, and it continued to count after the burn. Is that affirmative?

a08_1040133.speaker: Lovell
a08_1040133.text: Rog. We burned on time, 14 seconds, attitude nominal. Our residuals were plus 2 in V GX , minus 1 in V GY nothing in V GZ . Our EMS stopped about 6.2 and was counting up - up to - continued counting after the burn.

a08_1040133.speaker: Collins
a08_1040133.text: Rog. Understand 14 seconds, burn on time, nominal attitude, two-tenths X, one-tenth Y, and nothing minus one-tenth Y, and nothing Z; and you put 6.2 on the EMS, and it continued to count after the burn. Is that affirmative?

a08_1040133.speaker: Lovell
a08_1040133.text: No. We put the burn - we put the burn Delta-V in the EMS, and after the burn, it was still counting.

a08_1040133.speaker: Lovell
a08_1040133.text: Okay, Houston. We transferred the state vector to the LM slot.

a08_1040133.speaker: Collins
a08_1040133.text: Roger, Jim. Thank you, and I still don't understand you on this EMS. Counted down from 5 to zero normally and then continued through zero in a negative way, and now it's reading minus 6.2? Is that affirmative?

a08_1040133.speaker: Lovell
a08_1040133.text: Rog. That's right. It was counting up when we shut it off. Last time I saw it, it was 6.9. Now Frank just put it on to Auto again with the Delta-V function switch in Delta-V, and it jumped six-tenths. Then he tried the second time, and it stayed at zero so we really don't know what the story is.

a08_1040400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1040400-pao.text: And that brings us up to the live - up to the present. 104 hours, 5 minutes. 10 minutes from now should start our television acquisition. Let's go back now.

a08_1040400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1040400-pao.text: A reminder to the press in the Building 1 Auditorium area, the big Eidophor will be available for the television pass.

a08_1040548.speaker: Borman
a08_1040548.text: I guess you want us to resume PTC, right? [Pause.]

a08_1040548.speaker: Collins
a08_1040548.text: We'd like you to resume the PTC attitude; pitch, 010; yaw, 045; and then come out of it again for your P23 that you're scheduled for about another hour and 10 minutes, in another hour and 10 minutes.

a08_1040548.speaker: Borman
a08_1040548.text: Mike, this is Frank. Is this TV still scheduled for 104:50?

a08_1040548.speaker: Collins
a08_1040548.text: That's affirmative, Frank, if you can manage it.

a08_1040548.speaker: Collins
a08_1040548.text: How's it going with the TV, Frank? Are we - can the networks count on having it on schedule? Over.

a08_1040548.speaker: Borman
a08_1040548.text: Yeah, we can have it on schedule. We don't have much to do, but we'll perform for you.

a08_1040548.speaker: Collins
a08_1040548.text: Okay. We got a bunch of filter experts standing by if you need any advice.

a08_1040548.speaker: Borman
a08_1040548.text: Well, we're just going to have to just do it inside today because there's no good shots of the Moon and the Earth; the Sun's too darn bright.

a08_1040548.speaker: Lovell
a08_1040548.text: I think it's raining out there.

a08_1040900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1040900-pao.text: Well, until we get acquisition, or until we get closer to the time, 6 or 7 minutes away, we'll just get off the line right now and come back up then. Our present distance, 167,187 [nautucal miles, 309,630 km]; velocity in relation to the Earth, 4,304 feet per second [1,312 m/s]. Our weight is now 31,679 pounds [14,369 kg]. At 104 hours, 9 minutes into the flight; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a08_1040957.speaker: Borman
a08_1040957.text: Roger. On this EMS, when I put it in Delta-V, it's reading zero; then I switched to Auto. Sometimes it'll count to 19 or 20 feet per second. I guess that's what happened.

a08_1040957.speaker: Collins
a08_1040957.text: Rog. Understand when you put it to Auto, it maybe will keep counting up to as much as 19, 20 feet per second.

a08_1040957.speaker: Borman
a08_1040957.text: Just when you put it to Auto; it'll start counting on some occasions, by itself.

a08_1041400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1041400-pao.text: And this is Apollo Control, Houston; 104 hours, 14 minutes. We do not have a picture as yet. We're not particularly trying hard but we do expect it within 45 seconds. Earlier, Frank Borman said only that he'd probably have to keep the camera inside today and made some offhanded reference to the fact that it was raining outside. The Flight Plan shows two crew members, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders would be in an eating period, eating their Christmas dinner. Perhaps we'll see them performing that little chore and also Frank Borman is to be having Christmas dinner. And immediately after dinner, Fran

a08_1041400-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1041400-pao.text: Present velocity is - our present distance from Earth is 166,743 [nautical] miles [308,808 km], moving at a velocity of 4,311 feet per second [1,314 m/s]. It's constantly - it's a constantly increasing value. Present weight of the spacecraft is 31,679 pounds [14,369 kg]. We're standing by waiting for the High Gain Antenna to lock up with our Goldstone antenna. And hopefully the antenna - at the big antenna in Madrid as well. And now our Communications Officer advises he's about - the spacecraft's about 3 degrees from establishing lock, and we ought to just get a picture any second now. For the

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Mike, we're ready when you are.

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: We're ready. [Pause.]

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Say again.

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: Yeah, we're ready, Frank. We're all squared away and eagerly standing by.

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Oh boy. [Long pause.]

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: You got your make-up on?

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Yeah. Have we got a picture?

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: Negative, Frank. [Long pause.]

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: How about now, Houston?.

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: Negative, Frank. [Long pause.]

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: We don't seem to have much luck today, but don't call for a repairman yet. It may be our camera here. [Long pause.]

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Any results yet, Mike?

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: Negative, Frank. It may be that it hasn't warmed up properly.

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Okay. We've had it on for a while. Are you getting our FM okay?

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: Okay, Frank. There - we got it. It's coming in loud and clear. We look like we're looking at your hat and now the MDC. [Pause.]

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Okay. Well, good afternoon. This is the Apollo 8 crew. And how's it focusing now, Houston?

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: It's looking good. If you can hold the thing still, there's sort of a time delay. Any motion at all ruins our picture.

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Tell me if there's any difference in it now.

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: It's looking good now.

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Okay, fine.

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: It looks like you're okay, but somebody else is upside down.

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Okay. That's right. That's Jim Lovell. What we thought we'd do today was just show you a little bit about life inside Apollo 8. We've shown you the scenes of the Moon, the scenes of the Earth, and we thought we'd invite you into our home. It's been our home at least for four days as you can see on the instrument panel. We - we mark off each day on the - on the instrument panel. We're four down, and we're working on the fifth day. Of course, we're all looking forward to the landing on Friday. Down here in the part of the spacecraft that we call the Lower Equipment Bay, we have the President's a

a08_1042126.speaker: Lovell
a08_1042126.text: What do you have today, Bill, for dinner?

a08_1042126.speaker: Anders
a08_1042126.text: Well, here we have some cocoa; should be good. I'll be adding about 5 ounces of hot water to that. [Pause.] These are little sugar cookies, [pause] some orange juice, [long pause] corn chowder, [pause] chicken and gravy, and a little napkin to wipe your hands when you're done. I'll prepare some orange juice here. [Long pause.]

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Okay. You can see that he's taking his scissors and cutting the plastic end off the little [pause] - the little nozzle that he's going to insert the water gun into. The water gun dispenses half-ounce bursts of water per click. [Long pause.] Here we go; Bill has it in now, and the water's going in. [Long pause.] I hope that you all had better Christmas dinners today than us, but nevertheless, we thought you might be interested in how we eat.

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: Rog. I haven't heard any complaints down here, Frank. We'll bring you up to speed on your food when you get back.

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Very good.

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: Looks like a happy home you've got up there.

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Ordinarily, we let these drinks - Ordinarily, we let these drinks settle for 5 or 10 minutes, but Bill's going to drink it right now. Then, to get on with the program, he cuts open another flap, and you'll see a little tube comes out...

a08_1042126.speaker: Lovell
a08_1042126.text: This is not a commercial. [Long pause.]

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: ...and he drinks his delicious orange drink. Maybe I should say he drinks his orange drink. He's usually not that fast. Bill is really in a hurry today. Well, that's what we eat. Now another very important part of the spacecraft is the navigation station or the optics panel. And we - just a minute; Bill wants to say something.

a08_1042126.speaker: Anders
a08_1042126.text: That's good; but not quite as good as good old California orange juice.

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Bill's from Florida.

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Okay. Now if you'll let me have the camera, Jim, and I'll show the people where you do most of your work. Okay. Bill (means Jim), can you explain it?

a08_1042126.speaker: Lovell
a08_1042126.text: If I can clean up some of Bill's food around here, and have it away. [Long pause.] Down in this area is called the LEB or the Lower Equipment Bay, and we have our optics positioning equipment right here. We do all our navigation down here by sighting on stars and on horizons of either the Moon or the Earth. And this is where we find out exactly where we are in space, what direction, and how fast we are traveling. And our computer, as Frank has mentioned, takes information and tells us how to maneuver to get home safely. I work with the scanning telescope and the sextant, and occasionally, if I

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Now that's about all we have for today. I - each and every one of us wish each and every one of you a very Merry Christmas. And, we - I guess we'll see you tomorrow, and we'll be landing early Friday morning. Merry Christmas from Apollo 8.

a08_1042126.speaker: Collins
a08_1042126.text: Roger. Merry Christmas from the ground, Apollo 8, and thank you very much for the guided tour. We really enjoyed it.

a08_1042126.speaker: Borman
a08_1042126.text: Roger.

a08_1042300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1042300-pao.text: Now Borman says 'Mike, we're ready when you are.' and we're certainly ready.

a08_1043300-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1043300-pao.text: We're understanding that the onboard camera takes a minute and a half, two minutes to warm up. At least that's the word of the Communications Officer. Here we go back now.

a08_1043511.speaker: Collins
a08_1043511.text: We're suggesting attitude deadband, Max, and rate, High.

a08_1044529.speaker: Borman
a08_1044529.text: How soon will they tell us what effect that midcourse had on our trajectory, Mike?

a08_1044529.speaker: Collins
a08_1044529.text: Oh, the longer we track, the smarter we'll get; but stand by one for a pertinent answer. [Long pause.]

a08_1044529.speaker: Collins
a08_1044529.text: Roger. Tentatively, your midcourse correction at 122 hours is zero; and in about an hour and a half, we'll have some track data to confirm that. Over.

a08_1044529.speaker: Borman
a08_1044529.text: We're going to have something to eat here, Mike; just taking it easy now.

a08_1044529.speaker: Borman
a08_1044529.text: Did you get another shotgun for Christmas? [Pause.]

a08_1044529.speaker: Collins
a08_1044529.text: No, I'm missing enough with the one I have.

a08_1044529.speaker: Borman
a08_1044529.text: That's what Edwin told me; I thought maybe you might want to try another one. [Pause.]

a08_1044529.speaker: Borman
a08_1044529.text: What was it, 40 shots at four birds?

a08_1044529.speaker: Collins
a08_1044529.text: Oh, negative, Frank. I'm 100 percent, one bird per box.

a08_1044529.speaker: Borman
a08_1044529.text: Then you and I are in the same fix.

a08_1045118.speaker: Lovell
a08_1045118.text: It appears that we did a grave injustice to the food people. Just after our TV show, Santa Claus brought us some - a TV dinner each, which was delicious. Turkey and gravy, cranberry sauce, grape punch; outstanding.

a08_1045118.speaker: Collins
a08_1045118.text: Roger, Jim. Glad to hear it. [Pause.] Now we're down here eating cold coffee and bologna sandwiches.

a08_1045900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1045900-pao.text: Apollo Control, Houston here; 104 hours 59 minutes into the flight. And in between courses of the Christmas dinner, we've recorded this conversation.

a08_1051010.speaker: Borman
a08_1051010.text: Roger. We've got an awful lot of these stars to mark on now, Mike, and we were - they were having some concern about the PTC. Will you let us know if we stay in one position too long, or if we have to knock off and do some PTC?

a08_1051246.speaker: Collins
a08_1051246.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're monitoring your temperatures. The quads all look good. We'll continue to do so, and we expect no difficulty with them during the P23 work.

a08_1051246.speaker: Borman
a08_1051246.text: Our highest tank temperature now is C.

a08_1051246.speaker: Collins
a08_1051246.text: Understand; C is the hot one.

a08_1052600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1052600-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 105 hours, 26 minutes into the flight. A few minutes ago, Frank Borman told us that they had a number of navigational checks to make and their attitude might consequently put certain quads in the Sun for an overlong time. As a result, he asked us to keep an eye - keep an eye on the temperatures. Here's how the conversation went.

a08_1052600-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1052600-pao.text: And our present distance from Earth is 163,838 nautical miles [303,428 km]; velocity, 4,360 feet per second [1,329 m/s]; current weight, 31,679 pounds [14,369 kg]. At 105 hours, 28 minutes into the flight; that's our status.

a08_1054839.speaker: Collins
a08_1054839.text: Roger, Bill. We'd like to talk about your High Gain Antenna sometime when you get a minute.

a08_1055047.speaker: Anders
a08_1055047.text: About 5 minutes, Mike, we'll be done here.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Hi Houston, Apollo 8. About the High Gain Antenna.

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: Okay, Bill. We think it'd be an extremely worthwhile thing to find out how it operates in the Auto Reacq mode, and we propose running a test on it in that mode from 109 to 111 hours GET. Over.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Okay. We'll do that.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: We'll try it on the way out. [Pause.]

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: We have a detailed procedure which we can read up to you anytime you're ready.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Go ahead.

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: Okay. We suggest the start time, 109 hours GET; stop time, 111 hours; and you'll be in a PTC. We're requesting a left roll rate, which we notice you've been preferring, a left roll rate of 1 revolution per hour, and this is in your present PTC attitude (i.e. pitch, 10 degrees, 010 degrees; and yaw, 45 degrees). Procedure is this: step 1, stop at roll angle 150 degrees; acquire - this is step 2 - acquire in Manual mode; 3, switch to Auto Narrow Beam; 4, make sure tracking in Auto mode then switch to Auto Reacq mode; 5, position the High Gain Antenna...

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Wait a minute, Houston.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa.

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: Okay. Whoa, whoa. Standing by.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: I'm still starting. [Pause.]

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Okay. Make sure tracking in Auto and then what?

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: Make sure tracking in Auto, and then switch to Auto Reacq mode. Over. [Pause.]

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Okay. Will do.

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: Okay. Step 5, position High Gain Antenna pitch and yaw control to predicted Earth rise angles, and those angles are yaw, 50 degrees; pitch, minus 40 degrees. Over. [Pause.]

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Okay.

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: Okay. Two more steps. Step 6, remain on High Gain Antenna in this mode for two revs. Do not switch to Omni anytime during these two revs, and maintain mode configuration of voice and data. We expect the loss of track should be no more than 15 minutes per rev. Over. [Pause.]

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Roger.

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: And the final step, 7, if any problem arises, go back to your initial gimbal angles of 10 degrees pitch, 45 degrees yaw, and 150 degrees roll; reacquire and go to Auto mode. Over.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Yeah, let's - I guess there ought to be a step 4A which says start roll again, right? [Pause.]

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: That's affirmative. Excuse me there, that's affirmative.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Okay. If - let's see, if we - I don't understand your last comment. If we get into a problem, you want us to go back to 150 degrees roll?

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: Well, all we want you to do is go ahead and reacquire in the Auto mode, Bill. And it looks like that would be one way of doing it. But all we're saying is, you know, if you want to talk to us about something, or you have any other problems, or you don't like the way it looks, anything at all, just go ahead and reacquire in the Auto mode.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Yeah, why don't we just say if we do have problems, it doesn't pick it up when it's supposed to, give it a good try, and then call you up on the Omnis or position ourselves and we'll talk about it and try for another two revs.

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: That's just fine, Bill.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: Okay. It's worked. We tried it once or twice on the way out, but the one modification is once it did break lock, and go to its manual position, but I switched to the Omnis in between. That sounds fine.

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: Bill, could you run through that again? We're not reading you too loud, and would you say again what you tried on the way out, please.

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: On the right way out, they gave us some Reacq angles which we used, and once it broke lock and repositioned itself, why, it went over to the Omnis and waited till we got to near breaking lock again and switched back and snapped right in there [Pause.].

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: Roger. Thanks. We copy. [Pause.]

a08_1055622.speaker: Anders
a08_1055622.text: We have a few more stars to get, and then we'll give it a try.

a08_1055622.speaker: Collins
a08_1055622.text: Roger.

a08_1061000-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1061000-pao.text: Apollo Control Houston, here; 106 hours, 10 minutes into the flight, and here's what's been going on.

a08_1062315.speaker: Collins
a08_1062315.text: Rog, Bill. We got a bunch of tapes of some of your favorite music down here. You be interested in hearing a little background on the S-band?

a08_1062722.speaker: Lovell
a08_1062722.text: Roger. For some reason, we suddenly got a Program 01 and a 'No Attitude' light on our computer.

a08_1062722.speaker: Collins
a08_1062722.text: Stand by one, Jim. We're working on a procedure for getting you cranked back up again.

a08_1062958.speaker: Collins
a08_1062958.text: Okay. Jim, while we're working on this procedure, we'd like to know did you select 01, did you get a Verb 37 Enter. 01 Enter? [Pause.]

a08_1062958.speaker: Lovell
a08_1062958.text: Let's see, I'm not too sure, Mike. I might have done that, yeah.

a08_1062958.speaker: Lovell
a08_1062958.text: We have star 01 coming up, now that might have been the reason.

a08_1062958.speaker: Collins
a08_1062958.text: Okay. We understand. Why don't you just hold what you've got on your DSKY, and we'll be with you shortly.

a08_1063229.speaker: Collins
a08_1063229.text: Rog. Could you or Bill give us a better Omni antenna, please?

a08_1063753.speaker: Collins
a08_1063753.text: Okay. Frank, our procedure is to select P00, and from P00 go to P51, and get a platform alignment. After you've done that, we will send you up a P27, a REFSMMAT, and then you can do P52 REFSMMAT options, and you'll be back in business. Over.

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: Houston, this is Apollo 8. [No answer.]

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: Houston, Apollo 8.

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Go ahead. [No answer.]

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: Apollo 8, this is Houston. Say again. Over.

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: Okay. We've completed a P51 now. You want us to try a P52, or do you want us to wait till we can put a REFSMMAT in?

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: Stand by one, will you, please, Frank?

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: We're putting together a P27 load for you now, Frank; that's the reason for the delay. We just want to make sure we don't overlook anything before we send it up to you.

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: Okay. We'll just sit tight then. We've got a good P51. We'll just wait till you put in a REFSMMAT, and then, of course, we'll fine align over to that, right?

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: That's right, that's exactly right. Just stand by. [Long pause.]

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: Mike, this is Frank again.

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: Go ahead.

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: I suggest that we go ahead while you're doing that, do a P52 here, and let it do an automatic and just tweak this up. Jim had to use Rigel and Sirius, and they're pretty close together. And although we got a zero difference for the star angle, that might not be a bad idea just to try a 52 here.

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: We'd rather not do that, Frank. Stand by one.

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: All right. We won't do a thing. [Long pause.]

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: Frank, we - we feel that procedure that you're talking about is - is really not required. It's sort of wasting your time. You'd still have to - upon completion of that, we'd have to send you a new REFSMMAT, and you'd have to go ahead and do a P52 to that REFSMMAT in addition. Over.

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: We understand that. Go ahead. We'll wait for your REFSMMAT.

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: Okay. Thank you.

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: Apollo 8, Houston. If you'd go P00 and Accept, we have our P27 ready. We'll send you up a REFSMMAT. Over.

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: Roger. P00 and Accept.

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a08_1064755.speaker: Collins
a08_1064755.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Frank, we'd like to make sure you understand, when you do your P52, you want to select option 1, the preferred option, because those are the registers we're blinking now with this P27.

a08_1064755.speaker: Borman
a08_1064755.text: Roger. Option 1; thank you.

a08_1065200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1065200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 106 hours, 52 minutes into the light - into the flight. We've had a long quiet period this afternoon. The ground - on the ground here, we're working with Jim Lovell. Checking out his computer programs and comparing them against ours, sending him some - some programs so they can be put in and compared. All in all, sort of a feeling of relaxed vigilance, I would say. No major activities going on. Frank Borman should be sleeping, but he's not. He hasn't turned in yet. And a little - before too much longer goes by, we plan to play the crew a little music, perhaps s

a08_1065200-pao.speaker: Collins
a08_1065200-pao.text: Apollo 8, Houston. If you'd go P00 and Accept, we have our P27 ready. We'll send you up a REFSMMAT. Over.

a08_1065508.speaker: Collins
a08_1065508.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We got a good load in; it's your computer. Go to Block.

a08_1065508.speaker: Collins
a08_1065508.text: And you can go ahead with your P52 at your convenience.

a08_1065847.speaker: Collins
a08_1065847.text: Roger. When Jim gets to the end of P52, he's got a flashing Verb 37. We'd like him to not proceed, to hold at that point; we'd like to read some bits and pieces out of the computer at that time. Over.

a08_1065847.speaker: Collins
a08_1065847.text: Apollo 8, if Anders has got time to give us a countdown, could we get the Biomed switch from center to left?

a08_1065847.speaker: Collins
a08_1065847.text: Did you take that 1.7-second time delay into account?

a08_1065847.speaker: Collins
a08_1065847.text: Thank you, Jim. And I'll give you an estimate here on how long we want to hold at this point; it won't be too much longer.

a08_1065847.speaker: Lovell
a08_1065847.text: It was my goof; I must have put in 3701 instead of 3723 and star 01.

a08_1070304.speaker: Collins
a08_1070304.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We have got a Flight Plan suggestion for you.

a08_1070304.speaker: Collins
a08_1070304.text: Go ahead and delete the remainder of these P23s that you're working on now, go back to PTC attitude, and then pick up where it says 108 hours in the Flight Plan to pick up again there with your P23, or if you prefer to slip that time a couple of hours, if you want to get some rest in between.

a08_1070304.speaker: Borman
a08_1070304.text: I think that's a good idea; we'll do that.

a08_1070304.speaker: Lovell
a08_1070304.text: Mike, what does this do to our state vector?

a08_1070304.speaker: Collins
a08_1070304.text: Not a thing. We've looked at your state vector, and it's good.

a08_1070304.speaker: Lovell
a08_1070304.text: So we didn't lose all the nav that we were just - had accomplished, right?

a08_1070304.speaker: Collins
a08_1070304.text: Stand by one on that, Jim. I don't know; I'm checking.

a08_1070544.speaker: Collins
a08_1070544.text: Roger. I say again, your state vector is just fine; it's still tickety-poo, and the reason we're holding here is that we're checking to see whether if any P23 information was lost. That's reason one, and the second reason is that your W-matrix shares some computer memory cells with P01, and we're getting a clarification on the status of your W-matrix before we proceed. Over.

a08_1070544.speaker: Borman
a08_1070544.text: We'll go ahead and start heading over to the PTC attitude.

a08_1070544.speaker: Borman
a08_1070544.text: Do you need the High Gain any more, Mike? [Pause.]

a08_1070544.speaker: Collins
a08_1070544.text: Negative. We don't need it any more.

a08_1071851.speaker: Collins
a08_1071851.text: Roger, Frank. We're coming up on time for an oxygen purge on all three fuel cells. Might be a good time to do it while we're waiting here.

a08_1071851.speaker: Borman
a08_1071851.text: All right. Mike, we're going to purge the three fuel cells, oxygen only.

a08_1071900-pao.speaker: Borman
a08_1071900-pao.text: All right. Mike, we're going to purge the three fuel cells, oxygen only.

a08_1071900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a08_1071900-pao.text: Apollo Control here at 107 hours, 19 minutes into the flight. And the long quiet afternoon continues with Jim Lovell looking at his computer programs and us looking at his computer program, and essentially nothing new to report. Here's the conversation that ensued since our last report.

a08_1072344.speaker: Collins
a08_1072344.text: Apollo 8, Houston. That's enough on fuel cell number 1; if you'd start on 2 please.

a08_1073222.speaker: Collins
a08_1073222.text: Apollo 8, Houston. We're on low bit rate now. Last time we saw you, you were still purging. Over.

a08_1073222.speaker: Collins
a08_1073222.text: You're unreadable, but request that you end your purge.

a08_1073837.speaker: Collins
a08_1073837.text: Apollo 8, Houston. Over.

a08_1073837.speaker: Lovell
a08_1073837.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a08_1073837.speaker: Collins
a08_1073837.text: Roger, Jim. I've got a short procedure I'd like to read up to you on your DSKY, and I'd like to explain what it is. Your W-matrix shared some memory locations with P01; therefore, the W-matrix that you have right now is not a good one, and we would not want you to continue your P23 sightings with that matrix. So this procedure I'm going to give you is going to cause the matrix to reinitialize itself prior to your next P23, when you go into P23. And this will put you back with the value of the W-matrix which you loaded after TEI, you remember, that 3303 thing. And if this has any...

a08_1073837.speaker: Lovell
a08_1073837.text: Roger.

a08_1073837.speaker: Collins
a08_1073837.text: ...further effects on the Flight Plan, we'll - we're in the process of sorting that out, and if need be, we'll send you up a revised sighting schedule later, both for the comm and loss-of-comm case. Over.

a08_1073837.speaker: Lovell
a08_1073837.text: Okay. Stand by, and I'll get something to copy with.

a08_1073837.speaker: Collins
a08_1073837.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a08_1073837.speaker: Lovell
a08_1073837.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a08_1073837.speaker: Collins
a08_1073837.text: Okay. Insert, without releasing the flashing Verb 37, the following: Verb 25 Noun 07 Enter, 77 Enter, 40 Enter, Enter, Verb 37 Enter, 00 Enter. Over. [Pause.]

a08_1073837.speaker: Lovell
a08_1073837.text: Understand. We insert Verb 37 without releasing, is that correct?

a08_1073837.speaker: Collins
